jobs.title: Senior Research Officer - MSNA - Global, Based in Amman
jobs.description:
## **BACKGROUNG ON IMPACT & REACH**

REACH was born in 2010 as a joint initiative of two International NGOs ([IMPACT Initiatives](http://www.impact-initiatives.org/) and [ACTED](http://www.acted.org/)) and the United Nations Operational Satellite Applications Programme ([UNOSAT](http://www.unitar.org/unosat/)). REACH’s **purpose** is to promote and facilitate the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts. REACH facilitates information management for aid actors through three complementary services: (a) need and situation assessments facilitated by REACH teams; (b) situation analysis using satellite imagery; (c) provision of related database and (web)-mapping facilities and expertise.

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis and GIS. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO whose headquarter is based in Paris and is present in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, enabling IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support on its fields of intervention.

## **BACKGROUND ON MULTI-SECTOR NEEDS ASSESSMENT (MSNA)**

Over the past 10 years, REACH has established itself as a leader in the delivery of independent, crisis-wide Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessments (MSNAs). MSNAs respond directly to Grand Bargain commitments by providing impartial, unbiased, comprehensive, context-sensitive, and timely data to inform humanitarian decision-making. In doing so, MSNAs promote a shift in how humanitarian needs are measured and how response planning and prioritization decisions are made. MSNA data enables and promotes needs-based, evidence-based and people-centred decision making when it comes to aid. MSNAs are delivered on an annual cycle aligned with the Humanitarian Planning Cycle (HPC). IMPACT delivers approximately 20 MSNAs each year across some of the world’s most severe humanitarian crises. In 2026, IMPACT embarked on an exciting but ambitious journey to expand and improve the MSNA programme. The goal is to improve the resilience of the data and information system underpinning humanitarian aid policy by streamlining delivery of MSNAs, making them easier, faster and cheaper to deliver by 2028. Delivering on this agenda requires a scale-up of the Global MSNA Team, close coordination with country teams delivering MSNAs, and with our Global Data Team (GDT) based in Amman. This position is therefore based in our Regional Office in Amman.

### **We are currently looking for a Senior Research Officer to join the Global MSNA Team of the Research Systems Unit (RSU).**

**Title:** Senior Research Officer – Research and Development (MSNA)

**Location:** Amman, Jordan, with travel (up to 20% field deployment)

**Line management:** Reports to the MSNA Research and Development (R&D) Specialist; administratively hosted by the IMPACT/ACTED office in Amman

**Contract duration:** 12 months, with possibility of extension.

**Start date:** ASAP

## **POSITION PROFILE**

This position is situated within the Research Systems Unit (RSU) of the Global Programmes Section. Under the overall guidance of the Research Manager, the RSU supports the delivery of core, multi-sectoral research across IMPACT’s countries of operation. Reporting directly to the MSNA Research & Development (R&D) Specialist (based in Geneva), and working closely with the Global Data Team (GDT), the Senior Research Officer will lead and support various initiatives within the R&D workstream of the Global MSNA Team including, among others, MSNA toolkits and methods, the Multi-Sector Needs Index (MSNI), cross-crisis analysis, mortality & nutrition data modules, and digitalization of workflows.

The position is based in Amman in order to keep methodological development close to the responses where MSNAs are implemented at the largest scale, and to strengthen day-to-day technical support to country teams in the region.

## **FUNCTION & RESPONSIBILITIES**

The SAO will support the below core areas of work:

***MSNA toolkit and methods***

- Lead the update of the MSNA sectoral indicator guidance, in coordination with sectoral specialists, and including making guidance notes fit for a public audience.
- Lead the development of the clean dataset template and the analysis tables template, taking account of the capacity of lower-resourced country teams.
- Contribute to the update of the MSNA Global Indicator Bank, the Data Analysis Plan (DAP) template, the KoBo template and checker, and the MSNA sampling guidance, including making relevant resources public.
- Support the coherence and interoperability of the toolkit across the research cycle, and its adaptation for external audiences and partner organisations.
- Fill in the gaps of the toolkit by developing additional resources, as needed.

***MSNA and cross-crisis analysis***

- Develop a revamped Multi-Sector Needs Index (MSNI) guidance note, fit for external audiences, sharing it with other MSNA producers and supporting its uptake.
- Contribute to MSNI lessons learned from the 2026 cycle, any revisions to the framework, and support its presentation to external stakeholders.
- Support the production of cross-crisis analysis, including the consolidation and standardization of large country datasets and the processing of related documentation on data collection and sampling methods across countries.
- Contribute to global MSNA analysis products – quantitative analysis to identify key global trends and findings, and the production of short briefs, dashboards or other similar products for global audiences.
- Support external engagement with global stakeholders, donors and other REACH partners on MSNI and cross-crisis findings, including website articles, webinars and similar activities.

***Digitalization, automation and country support***

- Work with the R&D Specialist and the Global Data Team on reusable analysis pipelines, the consolidated R package environment (including *humind*), and the specification of the MSNA Explorer.
- Contribute to the automation of repetitive MSNA workflows, including support for review of minimum requirements and tool checks.
- Provide technical support and guidance to REACH MSNA country teams at various stages of the research cycle, including research design and sampling methodologies; data collection planning; data processing, cleaning and management; quantitative data analysis; and the reporting and dissemination of inter-sectoral findings.
- Provide ad hoc surge support including country deployment up to 20% – remotely and/or through a field deployment, depending on the extent of support required and the specific needs of the country team.
- Contribute technical content to the Training and Certification Programme, in particular on indicator selection and analysis.

***Country support and quality assurance (approx. 30%)***

- Act as HQ focal point for several MSNA countries according to the MSNA team split per MSNA Cycle. This will involve: monthly check-ins, ad-hoc support throughout the full research cycle ensuring country teams have the resources needed to produce high-quality data and analysis, document reviews, and reporting progress and challenges through the MSNA Info Tracker & HQ MSNA meetings, and proactively flagging issues to the wider MSNA team.
- Support in facilitation of the MSNA CoP and maintaining of the MSNA FAQ and intranet hub.
- Review country outputs against the MSNA minimum requirements at each phase of the cycle – Terms of Reference (ToRs) , Data Anaysis Plans (DAPs), KOBO tools, clean datasets, analysis, MSNI frameworks and bulletins – in coordination with the research quality assurance (RQ) and sectoral (STU) units.

***Key deliverables in the first 12 months***

- Lead the revision and publication of key MSNA toolkit components, including sectoral guidance notes, technical templates and resources, ensuring coherence, usability, and accessibility for both REACH and external MSNA producers.
- Under the guidance of the R&D Specialist, prioritise and implement any methodological revisions to the MSNI Analytical framework, develop internal and external guidance & training materials to support the establishment and implementation of a standardized analytical framework and delivery of key metrics by country teams for the 2027 cycle.
- Support the R&D Specialist with the development, documentation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of a data pipeline that consolidates, harmonizes, validates, and processes MSNA datasets from multiple countries, enabling efficient comparative analysis, global reporting, including year-on-year trends analysis, and integration with the web-based MSNA Explorer.
- Advance the automation of key MSNA workflows, in particular the MSNI, and provide technical support to country teams throughout the research cycle, including research design, sampling, data management, analysis, and reporting, while contributing technical content to the MSNA Training and Certification Programme.

## **REQUIREMENTS**

- Excellent academic qualifications, including Master's degree in a relevant discipline (e.g. development, humanitarian studies, international relations, research methods, social sciences, statistics).
- At least 2 years of experience in the humanitarian sector and/or field-based roles in fragile or development contexts.
- Experience with designing and implementing primary research, in particular large-scale quantitative surveys and/or humanitarian needs assessments.
- Solid understanding of statistical concepts and methods, including sampling.
- Advanced proficiency in R and/or Python for data processing, analysis and reproducible workflows is required for this position; familiarity with version control (Git) and with R package development is a strong asset (please share any public accounts (e.g., Github) with us in your CV).
- Experience developing, testing or otherwise working with multidimensional indices based on quantitative data to summarize multiple data points into easily digestible information an asset.
- Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting, including the ability to explain methodological choices to non-technical audiences.
- Ability to translate programmatic requirements into clear and technically feasible specifications, and to effectively bridge programmatic needs and technical implementation, in collaboration with the Global Data Team and under the R&D Specialist.
- Strong interpersonal skills, including good external engagement and coordination skills.
- Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility.
- Ability and willingness to engage in short term field deployments, including to complex and challenging security environments.
- Fluency in English required; proficiency in Arabic, French, or Spanish an asset.
- Familiarity with the humanitarian system and global humanitarian policy frameworks, in particular the Grand Bargain, the HPC and the JIAF.
- Experience with mortality and/or nutrition survey methods (e.g. SMART) an asset.
- Prior experience leading the design or implementation of MSNAs an asset.
- Familiarity with GIS principles and experience using GIS software an asset (e.g., ArcGIS, R, and/or QGIS).
- Ability to operate InDesign, a strong plus.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 2’580 CHF and 2’640 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
- Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance.
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered).
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’s HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training;
- IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

Working closely with supporters, volunteers and local communities, the postholder will assist with events, campaigns and fundraising activities, whilst building positive relationships that help strengthen Islamic Relief's presence and impact across the region.

- Experience of working in a similar role or within a customer-focused environment.
- Experience of delivering an effective service in support of organisational objectives.
- Proven experience of successfully working under pressure, with multiple demands and in a busy environment.
- Knowledge and understanding of the local region and community.
- Well-developed organisational skills with the ability to coordinate activities and events whilst managing competing priorities.
- The ability to work effectively as part of a team and build strong working relationships with colleagues, supporters and volunteers.
- Excellent communication skills, including speaking, presenting, listening and written communication.
- High standards of numeracy with the ability to accurately record financial information and work within established procedures and regulations.
- The ability to represent Islamic Relief professionally in a wide range of situations.
- Excellent attention to detail and the ability to work accurately under pressure.
- Ability to handle confidential information sensitively and appropriately.
- A proactive and flexible approach to work within a fast-paced and dynamic environment.
- Familiarity with social media platforms including Facebook, Instagram, X (Twitter) and Snapchat.
- Strong motivation and empathy towards the aims and objectives of the organisation.
- A reliable and professional approach to work.
- Willingness to work flexibly, including evenings, weekends and travel when required.

If you are talented, reliable, service-minded, resilient and a highly motivated professional looking for a meaningful career, with a strong commitment to IRW’s mission and values of sincerity, excellence, compassion, social justice and custodianship, please apply by completing our online application form.

jobs.title: Senior Corporate Development Officer
jobs.description:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

Reporting to the Senior Director, Corporate Partnerships, the Senior Corporate Development Officer is responsible for developing corporate partnerships in support of Habitat for Humanity International's (HFHI) mission. The Senior Corporate Development Officer is responsible for identifying, securing, and cultivating corporate partnerships, while also stewarding and expanding existing relationships to deepen engagement and grow support of HFHI's mission. This position will work closely with resource development leadership and key HFHI program stakeholders to maximize fundraising opportunities primarily through strategic partnership with Fortune 500 companies and other major corporations headquartered as assigned. This role will manage a portfolio of prospects representing a revenue range from $5-$10 million annually.

**Key Responsibilities:**

At Habitat for Humanity International, we believe everyone deserves a decent place to live. Reporting to the Senior Director, Corporate Partnerships, the **Senior Corporate Development Officer** will play a key role in advancing Habitat's mission by securing and growing strategic corporate partnerships that generate critical funding and engagement opportunities. This role leads the development, cultivation, and stewardship of corporate partnerships, with a primary focus on Fortune 500 companies and other major corporations.

**Why This Role Matters**

Through strategic relationship building and revenue generation, this role helps expand Habitat's ability to create housing opportunities and strengthen communities. The Senior Corporate Development Officer will manage a portfolio generating approximately $5-$10 million annually while helping position Habitat for long-term growth through innovative, mission-aligned corporate partnerships.

**What You'll Do**

- Develop and execute corporate partnership strategies aligned with partner business objectives and Habitat's mission.
- Identify, cultivate, solicit, and secure new corporate partnerships.
- Grow and steward an existing portfolio of corporate partners to increase engagement, revenue, and long-term impact.
- Build diverse funding streams through corporate philanthropy, sponsorships, employee engagement, workplace giving, cause marketing, gifts-in-kind, and programmatic support.
- Lead collaboration efforts with Habitat Area Offices to coordinate, pursue, and strengthen corporate partnerships.
- Facilitate partnership planning, strategy discussions, proposal development, and donor stewardship activities across Habitat's network.
- Develop compelling presentations, proposals, and partnership opportunities that align corporate social responsibility objectives with Habitat's funding priorities.
- Negotiate partnership agreements in collaboration with internal legal and finance teams.
- Serve as the primary relationship manager for key corporate partners and prospects.
- Work closely with Resource Development colleagues, affiliate leaders, and program teams to maximize partnership opportunities and deliver exceptional partner experiences.
- Track partnership performance, maintain accurate CRM records, prepare revenue forecasts, and provide pipeline and stewardship reporting.
- Mentor and support team members, sharing expertise and fostering collaboration across the organization.

**What You'll Bring**

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
- Minimum of 5 years of experience in fundraising, sales and/or prospect development.
- Demonstrated success securing complex six- and seven-figure multiyear commitments from Fortune 500 companies.
- Experience developing and managing partnership strategies.
- Ability to understand corporate priorities and build mutually beneficial partnership opportunities.
- Excellent communication, presentation, relationship-building, and negotiation skills.
- Strong project management, reporting, analytics, and organizational skills.
- Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in a complex, matrixed environment.
- Highly collaborative, proactive, and solution-oriented approach.
- Strong attention to detail and commitment to excellent customer service.
- Proficiency with business software, databases, spreadsheets, and reporting tools.
- Ability to effectively manage organizational resources, including travel expenses.
- Strong problem-solving and strategic thinking capabilities.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Working knowledge of corporate social responsibility, sales, cause marketing, marketing, public relations, sponsorships, and employee engagement strategies.
- Experience using donor or constituent management systems, including Blackbaud CRM.
- Knowledge of and passion for Habitat for Humanity's global mission.

**What We Offer**

At Habitat for Humanity International, you'll join a mission-driven organization committed to creating impact through partnership, collaboration, and innovation. You'll have the opportunity to work alongside colleagues around the world, build meaningful corporate relationships, and help create lasting change for families and communities globally.

**Ready to help grow transformative corporate partnerships that expand access to affordable housing worldwide? Apply today and bring your expertise, creativity, and collaboration skills to a global organization dedicated to building a world where everyone has a decent place to live.**

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance. For work locations in the US, the hiring range for this position is:

$97,300.00 USD

\-

$144,775 USD

/

Annual

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

**Habitat for Humanity International is an E-Verify employer.**

2 Open Board Positions
jobs.description:
## About the Organization

"Be Aware And Share" (BAAS) is an independent non-profit organization that supports people in need and contributes to social inclusion. Founded in September 2015 in Basel (Switzerland), BAAS primarily focuses on supporting people on the move in Europe. In addition to material and social support as well as educational and recreational opportunities for displaced people, BAAS also carries out awareness-raising and information activities in Switzerland. At the moment, the organization is mainly focusing on supporting refugees in Ioannina in Northwestern Greece at its Community Center. The activities are carried out by volunteers and are financed exclusively by donations. BAAS is a politically and religiously independent organization.

## Positions

We are looking for two new members to join our Executive Board who are passionate about solidarity with people on the move and keen to participate in shaping a dynamic grassroots NGO. The new members will be part of the Executive Board along with the other board members. Board Members work with various professionals in the organization to ensure that BAAS achieves its annual goals and will continue to build a network of supporters to work towards our vision of a peaceful, solidary and mutually inclusive society. We are looking for experienced professionals to take the organization forward by overseeing the operational, financial and technical aspects of Be Aware And Share. The positions are voluntary and require approximately 8 hours of work per week. A minimum commitment of 1 year is expected. The board member will work remotely but is expected to visit BAAS’ Community Center in Ioannina, Greece. The Executive Board is willing to revise the division of responsibilities within the board. However, we are specifically looking for individuals who have a solid background in public relations and project management.

## Overall Responsibilities

● Lead the strategic and executive bodies of the organization

● Coordinate and lead quarterly, and annual operational reviews and periodic forecast updates

● Provide leadership and manage the efforts of all active association members and ensure appropriate support

● Ensure that activities are informed by a resource-based approach through direct contact with working groups

● Represent the organization in Swiss and other humanitarian networks

## Specific Responsibilities PR

● Overviewing the activities of the PR Working Group

● Project management and collaboration on the rebranding process for the digital and graphic identity

● Developing a communication strategy and ensuring its implementation

● Collaboration with the other Working Group on various projects throughout the year

## Specific Responsibilities Project Ioannina

● Overviewing the activities of the Working Group Ioannina

● Biweekly meetings with the project director for updates and coaching sessions

● Monthly Check Ins with the Project Director and the Project Coordinators about their wellbeing and mental health

● Responsible for ensuring the availability of mental health services

● Risk Management focal point

● Overview of the annual budget and assistance in developing it

## Requirements & Skills

● Very good command in spoken and written English. Any other language is an asset

● High level of motivation and a high level of reliability

● Profound knowledge of the social and political situation of people on the move in Europe, especially in Greece

● Ideally professional leadership experience in the nonprofit sector, ideally with a grassroots NGO

● Ability to keep track of the diverse and fast-paced activities of the organization

● Understanding of the current challenges faced by NGOs and willingness to address them innovatively and purposefully

● Strong awareness of how to deal with scarce resources (financial and personnel)

● High resilience, flexibility, team skills and good communication skill

jobs.title: Head of Programs Ethiopia
jobs.description:
ForAfrika is an African-rooted, globally connected organisation dedicated to empowering communities across the continent through sustainable development and humanitarian aid. With over 40 years of operational experience, ForAfrika works in environments that vary from emergency relief settings to long-term development, ensuring that every initiative is contextually aligned with the needs of the people it serves. Through a deep love for Africa and unwavering commitment, ForAfrika delivers programmes that transform lives by embracing an integrated approach to development. This includes enhancing education, health and nutrition, water and sanitation, food security and livelihoods, economic empowerment, and more, building environments where all Africans can thrive.

**Position Summary.**

The Head of Programs is responsible for leading all programmatic functions across the organization's Mozambique operations, ensuring high-quality, accountable, and sustainable programming that aligns with strategic objectives and responds to community needs. This senior leadership role encompasses oversight of program implementation, quality assurance, community integration, Design, Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (DMEAL), and emergency response coordination. The successful candidate will provide visionary leadership to drive program excellence while building organizational capacity and fostering partnerships that amplify impact.

**Reporting Relationships**

The Head of Programs has a solid-line reporting relationship to the Country Director and a dotted-line relationship to the Director of Programs, Global Support Office who provides technical oversight, guidance, and capacity building on programmatic matters. This relationship includes:

Regular program quality reviews and discussions

Technical support and guidance on program design and implementation

Collaborative development of country-specific program strategies

Knowledge exchange on innovative approaches and best practices

Capacity building initiatives for the country program team

**Key Roles and Responsibilities**

1. **Strategic Program Leadership & Quality Assurance**

- Provide strategic direction and oversight for all programmatic activities across multiple sectors including health, education, WASH, food security, livelihoods, and emergency response
- Establish and maintain program quality frameworks ensuring adherence to international standards including SPHERE, Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS), and donor compliance requirements
- Lead the development and implementation of the country program strategy in alignment with organizational mission and donor requirements
- Ensure all programs are designed and implemented in ways responsive to community needs, cultural contexts, and beneficiary feedback
- Champion innovation in program design and implementation methodologies to enhance effectiveness and sustainability

**2. Program Implementation Management**
- Oversee portfolio of programs with collective budgets and ensure efficient resource allocation across initiatives
- Monitor program performance against targets, timelines, and budgetary allocations, implementing corrective measures as needed
- Lead program proposal development processes, ensuring technical quality, contextual relevance, and competitive positioning
- Coordinate with finance team on budget variance analysis (BVA) and financial reporting to ensure fiscal accountability
- Establish and maintain relationships with key donors, government partners, and implementing partners

**3.Community Integration & Partnership Development**
- Ensure meaningful community participation in all phases of program cycle from design through evaluation
- Establish and maintain strategic partnerships with local organizations, government entities, and community leaders
- Lead development of community engagement strategies that promote local ownership and sustainability
- Oversee capacity building initiatives for community-based organizations and local partners
- Ensure cultural sensitivity and conflict-sensitive programming approaches across all interventions

**4. Emergency Response & Humanitarian Coordination**
- Lead organizational preparedness for emergency response including development and regular updating of contingency plans
- Coordinate rapid response to humanitarian crises, ensuring timely and effective assistance delivery
- Represent the organization in humanitarian coordination forums and cluster meetings
- Maintain emergency supply stocks and ensure readiness of response teams and equipment
- Lead needs assessments and response strategy development during humanitarian emergencies

**5. Team Leadership & Organizational Development**
- Provide leadership and mentorship to program managers, MEAL officers, field coordinators, and technical specialists
- Build organizational capacity through staff development planning, training coordination, and performance management
- Foster collaborative work environment that promotes professional growth and high performance
- Establish clear performance expectations and accountability mechanisms for all program staff
- Champion organizational values and ensure adherence to code of conduct and safeguarding policies

**6. External Relations & Representation**
- Serve as primary liaison with donors, government officials, and partner organizations on programmatic matters
- Represent the organization at national and international forums, conferences, and coordination meetings
- Develop and maintain strategic relationships that enhance program effectiveness and organizational profile
- Lead resource mobilization efforts and contribute to fundraising strategy development
- Ensure compliance with government regulations and maintain positive relationships with authorities

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

- Degree in development related studies- Agriculture, Range management, Natural Resource Management, Economics, Social sciences or related field
- Professional certifications in project/program management (PMP, PMD Pro) preferred
- Minimum 8-10 years of progressive experience in international development or humanitarian programming
- At least 5 years in senior management roles
- Demonstrated experience managing complex, multi-sector programs in Sub-Saharan Africa, preferably Mozambique
- Experience in emergency response coordination and humanitarian programming

**Technical Competencies**

- Expert knowledge of program cycle management and quality frameworks
- Strong understanding of international humanitarian and development standards (SPHERE, CHS, HAP)
- Proficiency in DMEAL methodologies, evaluation techniques, and data analysis
- Knowledge of major donor requirements (USAID, EU, UN agencies, bilateral donors)
- Understanding of conflict-sensitive programming and Do No Harm approaches

**Leadership & Management Skills**

- Exceptional leadership capabilities with experience managing diverse, multicultural teams
- Strong strategic thinking and analytical skills with ability to translate vision into operational plans
- Excellent communication and presentation skills in English; local language skills advantageous
- Proven ability to build and maintain relationships with diverse stakeholders
- Experience in organizational development and capacity building

**Personal Attributes**

- Strong commitment to humanitarian principles and development values
- Cultural sensitivity and ability to work effectively in diverse environments
- High degree of flexibility and adaptability to changing circumstances
- Results-oriented with strong attention to detail and quality
- Integrity and commitment to ethical programming practices

**Working Conditions**

- Position based in Ethiopia with regular travel to field locations (up to 40% travel)
- Willingness to work in challenging environments and respond to emergency situations
- Flexibility to work extended hours during crisis response or critical program periods
- Commitment to maintaining security protocols and organizational safety standards

DISCLAIMER: Please note that candidates must have the right to live and work in Ethiopia. The company will not sponsor candidates for this role.

jobs.title: 23649 Regional Financial Comptroller (P)
jobs.description:
Under the overall supervision of the Regional Director and direct supervision of the Deputy Regional Director (Management), with a secondary reporting line to the Comptroller / Director, Department of Financial and Administrative Management (DFM), the Regional Financial Comptroller is responsible for steering, monitoring, and facilitating IOM’s financial and administrative functions across the Region, including facilitating compliance of financial controls and processes adopted by Country Offices (COs) in the Region with IOM’s global financial policies, regulations, and procedures.

In this capacity, the Regional Financial Comptroller delivers strategic financial advisory services and support to COs by promoting the integration of IOM’s financial principles within broader operational frameworks. The Regional Financial Comptroller facilitates the provision of efficient financial and administrative services at both regional and local levels, while also identifying, mitigating, and escalating financial risks as necessary. In addition, the Regional Financial Comptroller champions capacity-building initiatives in finance and administration, driving change and strengthening IOM’s financial workforce, systems, and internal controls. The Regional Financial Comptroller frequently collaborates with DFM Divisions and engages with UN agencies and donor representatives at both regional and country levels.

**Responsibilities**

1. Lead the development and implementation of both short- and long-term financial management plans and strategies at the regional level, aligning with IOM’s global financial policies, regulations, and procedures.
2. Provide strategic financial advice to Regional Office (RO) management and the management of COs in the Region in line with the IOM’s financial policy framework, ensuring effective oversight and compliance with financial controls across the Region in collaboration with Headquarters (HQ), Administrative Centers, and COs.
3. Provide guidance and first-line support to Resource Management Officers (RMOs) and finance staff on financial, administrative, and financial control matters, providing training and guidance on financial and administrative policies, ensuring that processes are efficient and aligned with IOM’s global policies while being adaptable to local contexts.
4. Monitor financial and administrative processes at the Regional and CO levels by facilitating compliance and promoting operational efficiency in coordination with HQ, Administrative Centres, and COs. Conduct periodic visits to CO in the Region to provide guidance, assess capacities, and improve compliance. Communicate the outcomes of these visits to RO management and the Department of Financial and Administrative Management.
5. Strengthen the financial internal control environment across the Region, coordinating with regional global counterparts, particularly with the Regional Risk and Compliance Officer and DFM, to address gaps and prevent fraud or mismanagement. Facilitate the implementation of the Compliance Control Self-Assessment Tool across the Region, contribute to the development of the Risk Register Matrix, and other risk assessment and management-related tools. Monitor and facilitate the segregation of duties within the COs, including but not limited to role assignments in IOM’s Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system.
6. Perform approvals, reviews, or authorizations within the authorities delegated by IOM policies and/or line managers, in close coordination with global counterparts.
7. Oversee comprehensive financial planning, monitoring, and reporting across the Region, including monitoring project financial performance, with an emphasis on promptly identifying changes in the financial health of COs.
8. Identify, assess, and mitigate financial risks in collaboration with Regional and CO management, the Regional Risk and Compliance Officer, and other stakeholders. Escalate significant financial risks and emerging trends to DFM and senior regional management.
9. Oversee the RO budget submission process, monitoring expenditures to ensure adherence to approved allocations and financial policies. Monitor COs budget submissions and periodic forecasts, ensuring financial sustainability and adequate coverage of common costs.
10. Under the guidance of the Treasury Division, facilitate the optimization of cash management and bank account structures across the Region, ensuring alignment with IOM’s global financial strategies. Promote global institutional payment solutions, streamlining processes, and reducing transaction costs across the Region.
11. Monitor compliance with donor financial reporting requirements, facilitate good-quality project financial report preparation by COs and timely submission for internal endorsements.
12. Maintain and monitor audit recommendations and oversight findings, ensuring timely follow-up and resolution by COs.
13. Supervise finance and administrative staff at the RO, ensuring processes are in place to maintain compliance with IOM’s rules and standards.
14. Lead regional finance capacity-building initiatives, focusing on talent development and retention within the financial function. Foster a robust finance community across the Region, encouraging continuous learning, peer collaboration, and alignment with IOM’s global financial strategies. Serve as a key champion of change, facilitating the adoption of technological and policy updates across the region.
15. Represent IOM in inter-agency financial and administrative discussions, including participation in regional and local OMTs, donor meetings, and other external forums.
16. Perform any other duties as assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with ten years of relevant professional experience; and,
- University degree in the above with twelve years of relevant professional experience.
- Professional accounting certification by an internationally recognised professional accountancy body is an advantage.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Demonstrated leadership experience in financial management, with a minimum of ten years of progressively evolving responsibilities for accounting, financial reporting, and financial analysis within an international, decentralized, and/or multinational environment;
- Demonstrated experience in conducting financial analysis and feasibility studies, including trend and ratio analysis. Capable of presenting complex financial matters and experienced in negotiating with member states and donors;
- Excellent knowledge and experience with budgeting, financial, and reporting systems, including ERP;
- Demonstrated understanding and substantial work experience with International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) or International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); and,
- Proven experience in field operations of similar-sized international organizations to IOM is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Demonstrated good communication, exceptional people management, and strong interpersonal skills;
- Demonstrated knowledge of IOM and/or UN financial regulations, policies, procedures and practices is desirable;
- Proven track record in remotely managing teams and functions, including highly decentralized financial and accounting practices;
- Demonstrated skill in operating a complex financial monitoring framework, including policies and procedures tailored to operational needs;

jobs.title: Research Analyst
jobs.description:
**We’re hiring**

**Research Analyst**

**LOCATION: Kampala, Uganda**

**GROSS SALARY RANGE: $2,979 - $4,092(gross monthly)**

Laterite is looking for a new Research Analyst with an understanding of data analysis and a strong motivation to work in social and economic research to join our office in Kampala, Uganda. This role combines research design, data analysis, project management support, data quality analysis, and fieldwork coordination in a collaborative and fast-paced environment.

**WHO WE ARE**

Laterite is a data, research, and analytics firm working on complex development challenges. We partner with universities, global think tanks, international NGOs, multilateral donors, and government ministries. Our clients include the World Bank, TechnoServe, the Mastercard Foundation, and others.

We operate across the Netherlands, Rwanda, Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Sierra Leone, and Peru, with 90+ full-time staff and more than 2,000 enumerators. We believe meaningful impact requires being on the ground, building local teams, and establishing long-term trust. Our office culture is collaborative and gives people autonomy to grow into their roles.

**THE ENVIRONMENT YOU’RE STEPPING INTO**

You will join our team in Uganda in a high-trust environment. We are low on bureaucracy but high on individual accountability. You won’t be micromanaged here—we want you to use your judgment to solve problems, support our fast-paced field teams, and actively improve the systems you work with.

Laterite was founded in 2010 in Kigali, and our office in Kampala opened in 2018. Our project portfolio in Uganda is varied across multiple sectors, and ranges from data collection studies, where Laterite manages data collection for our clients, to full-cycle research projects, where Laterite is responsible for evaluation and sampling methodology, survey design and coding, data collection, data quality and analysis. The Uganda team has managed some of our largest data collection projects and phone surveys on topics spanning coffee agronomy, foundational learning and education, sexual and reproductive health, and renewable energy. Our team in Uganda currently consists of 5 team members.

**TEAM STRUCTURE**

You will report to the Research Manager and Uganda country lead, working closely with the research operations team and data quality colleagues across Laterite. You will have the opportunity to collaborate with research team members in other country offices

**HOW YOU’LL MAKE AN IMPACT**

**1 Supporting research projects**

- Support the ethical approval process, research design, and development of research instruments,
- Conduct quantitative and qualitative data analysis.
- Draft sections of reports and presentations for clients.
- Support communication with clients and internal project teams on project progress.

**2 Contributing to data collection**

- Code survey instruments using SurveyCTO and other ODK-based platforms.
- Collaborate with field teams to develop training materials and support enumerator trainings.
- Participate in field visits to understand and improve data collection processes.

**3 Strengthening data quality and analysis**

- Monitor, clean, and validate incoming survey data (by conducting high-frequency checks, for example).
- Work closely with field teams to resolve data quality issues.
- Support statistical analysis and interpretation of findings.
- Contribute to consultancy-quality reports and data-driven insights.

**4 Contributing to business development (Optional)**

If you are interested, there is also room to contribute to our business development efforts, either through proactive business development or by contributing to the development of technical and financial proposals.

**WHAT YOU BRING**

We are looking for a colleague with strong quantitative data analysis skills and a motivation to work on socio-economic development research. Specifically, you have:

- A completed Master’s degree in Economics, Public Health, Development, statistics, or related fields.
- At least one year of professional experience in similar roles or tasks. (We welcome experience gained through internships, dissertation work, or participation in an academic research group, provided you can demonstrate how this experience meets the requirements of the role.)
- Strong quantitative data analysis skills and proficiency in Stata.
- Excellent written and oral communication skills in English.

*In addition, we welcome:*

- Experience working with ODK-based platforms (e.g., SurveyCTO).
- Previous work experience in Uganda
- Additional software skills, such as knowledge of R or Python.
- Organizational and interpersonal skills, self-motivation and drive to work in a collaborative environment.

**WHAT YOU’LL LEARN AND DEVELOP**

- Technical research design, including sampling and impact evaluation methodologies.
- Project management and client communication.
- Advanced data analysis, statistical techniques, and coding skills.
- Report writing and presentation of findings in a consultancy-quality format.

**WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU**

- **Competitive compensation. $2,979 - $4,092** gross monthly salary (exact grade determined by experience/interviews), medical insurance, pension contribution, and 21 days of annual leave.
- **Professional growth.** We are also committed to supporting our staff’s learning, providing an annual learning budget of up to $1,000 per person and 10 days of time off for professional learning each year.
- **Flexibility.** We also provide remote work options in accordance with Laterite’s remote work policy.

jobs.description:

The Cook is responsible for preparing daily lunch meals, procuring food and kitchen supplies, maintaining kitchen cleanliness, and organizing food stocks. The role also follows up on meal-related accounts and expenses in coordination with staff and the Supply Chain team.

**Work Experience:**

● At least one year of relevant experience in cooking or food preparation, preferably with an NGO, international organization, restaurant, or food-service facility.

● Good organizational, time-management, and multitasking skills.

● Attention to food quality, kitchen cleanliness, and food safety.

Kitchen-based work in an office or guesthouse environment, with regular handling of food supplies, cooking equipment, and cleaning materials.

In line with these values, the IRC implements policies on safeguarding beneficiaries from exploitation and abuse, child safeguarding, prevention of workplace harassment, fiscal integrity, and protection from retaliation.

jobs.title: DRC People Operations & Duty of Care Associate (Fixed-Term)
jobs.description:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

## **About the Role**

The DRC People Operations & Duty of Care Associate will drive the daily execution, administration, and continuous maintenance of health, safety, and duty of care systems for the DRC program. Acting as a crucial operational and staff-facing focal point, this role is responsible for ensuring compliance with staff safety and security protocols across offices, transport, accommodations, warehouses, and field operations in a complex environment. You will ensure that established standard operating procedures (SOPs), incident management processes, and people safety and security systems are practically implemented, clearly communicated, and consistently followed by all staff.

This role has a 12-month fixed-term contract, with the option to renew on business terms.

## **Responsibilities**

Duty of Care & Safety Administration

- Maintain and regularly update foundational risk profiles, movement protocols, and safety logs across all operational locations.
- Serve as the central administrative focal point for incident management, ensuring timely documentation, structured reporting, and tracking of corrective actions.
- Act as the budget administrator for staff well-being, safety, and security expenditures, ensuring resources are tracked and utilized efficiently.
- Oversee the day-to-day implementation and upkeep of established Health, Safety, and Security SOPs (including staff movement, office/warehouse safety, and emergency response).
- Ensure all policies and procedures are practically integrated into daily routines, clearly communicated, and consistently applied across all departments.
- Maintain organized physical and digital filing systems for all compliance, safety, and personnel records.
- Monitor local security developments, political events, and public health situations (e.g., protests, elections, regional conflicts, or health alerts) to proactively provide intelligence updates and advise on necessary operational adjustments.

Training, Onboarding & Capacity Building

- Coordinate the logistics, scheduling, and tracking for staff well-being, duty of care, and basic safety training programs.
- Facilitate thorough administrative inductions for new staff, consultants, and visitors, ensuring they receive, understand, and acknowledge all safety protocols.
- Maintain accurate tracking systems to ensure 100% staff compliance with organizational training requirements.

Incident Management & Support

- Serve as the first-line point of contact for staff reporting workplace incidents, accidents, or health events.
- Maintain up-to-date emergency contact trees, phone trees, and vendor lists to ensure rapid execution of crisis management plans when needed.
- Champion a culture of care, proactively encouraging staff to utilize available resources and reporting systems.
- Serve as the primary operational focal point and key contact for external health and security service providers.

Cross-Functional Execution & Office Management

- Oversee day-to-day office management and facility administration, ensuring workspaces consistently meet foundational health, safety, and duty of care standards.
- Partner closely with HR, Operations, and Supply Chain to embed people-centric systems into broader operational planning.
- Manage administrative relationships with vendors related to office facilities, basic guarding, and staff health services.
- Proactively establish, maintain, and leverage positive working relationships with local authorities, emergency services, police, and traffic departments to ensure rapid support during incidents.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Academic Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Operations Management, Public Administration, Organizational Psychology, or a related field.
- Professional Certifications (Optional but Advantageous):
- HR or administrative certifications (e.g., SHRM-CP, PHR, CIPD, or local equivalents).
- Project management or process improvement certifications (e.g., CAPM, Lean Six Sigma Green Belt).
- Basic safety or trauma-informed care certifications (e.g., Advanced First Aid, Mental Health First Aid).
- Experience: 3–5 years of experience in HR administration, operations, office management, or duty of care, preferably within an NGO, humanitarian, or fast-paced operational context.
- Systems Execution: Proven track record of implementing, maintaining, and enforcing organizational SOPs, policies, and administrative frameworks.
- Process-Oriented: Exceptional organizational skills with the ability to manage documentation, track compliance, and administer budgets accurately.
- People Skills: High emotional intelligence with the ability to act as a trusted "para-HR" figure; capable of championing staff safety while firmly ensuring policy compliance.
- Crisis Competence: Calm under pressure, with the ability to follow established emergency protocols and manage the administrative logistics of incident response.
- Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills; fluency in English and French required.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

## **Contract Duration**

1 year

## **Eligibility**

One Acre Fund can support a work permit for this role. However, nationals of (or those with an extensive professional background and work history in) our countries of operation are preferred.

## **Application Deadline**

17 January 2027. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Subgerencia Nacional de Preparación y Respuesta Humanitaria Perú
jobs.description:
**Plan International** es una organización sin fines de lucro, de Desarrollo y Acción Humanitaria, que promueve los derechos de la niñez y la igualdad para las niñas. Creemos en el poder y el potencial de cada niña y niño, a pesar que muchas veces, se vean limitados por la pobreza, la violencia, la exclusión y la discriminación, siendo las niñas las más afectadas.

En colaboración con niñas, niños, jóvenes, seguidores y socios, apostamos por un mundo justo, abordando las causas profundas de los problemas que enfrentan los niños, niños en situación de vulnerabilidad. Apoyamos a la niñez, capacitándolos para prepararse y responder ante la crisis y la adversidad. Impulsamos el cambio de prácticas y políticas a nivel local, nacional y global gracias a nuestro alcance, experiencia y conocimientos.

Durante más de 85 años, hemos reunido a otros optimistas determinados para transformar la vida de todas las niñas y niños en más de 80 países.

**¡No nos detendremos, hasta lograr la igualdad!**

**LA OPORTUNIDAD**

Es responsable de la preparación y respuesta humanitaria a nivel nacional, responsable de la gestión y coordinación de respuestas de emergencia en el país. Esto implica colaboración para mejorar las capacidades de preparación y respuesta ante desastres. Requiere planificación estratégica e implementación de sistemas efectivos de comunicación y logística. Las acciones incluyen: a) capacitar al personal de emergencia, b) establecer una infraestructura técnica y financiera resiliente, c) mejorar la preparación comunitaria, d) desarrollar alianzas sólidas con donantes y agencias humanitarias para asegurar financiación y apoyo. Estos esfuerzos son vitales para la respuesta inmediata a desastres y la estabilidad a largo plazo en el país.

**LA PERSONA:**

**Experiencia y Conocimientos previos**

- Título universitario en Gestión de Riesgos, Desastres o áreas afines.
- Formación deseable: posgrado (especialización o maestría) en Gestión de Riesgos, Seguridad, Administración de Desastres o Migración
- Experiencia en Respuesta humanitaria y Movilidad Humana (mínimo 4 años).
- Deseable conocimientos y experiencia en Acciones anticipatorias, Cambio Climático (dos años)
- Conocimiento del idioma inglés hablado y escrito.
- Manejo de paquetes informáticos.
- En caso de emergencias se requiere disponibilidad de tiempo completo y disponibilidad para desplazarse.

**Competencias**:

- Compromisos con los Derechos e Igualdad.
- Construcción y Desarrollo de Relaciones.
- Pensamiento estratégico.
- Empoderamiento.
- Orientación a resultados.
- Trabajo en equipo.
- Reconocimiento y previsión de riesgos.
- Liderazgo.
- Iniciativa.

Ubicación: **CO - Perú**

Reporta a: **Representante del País**

Nivel Hay: **16**

Fecha límite para postulaciones: **02 de noviembre 2026**.

La igualdad, la diversidad y la inclusión están en el centro de todo lo que **Plan International** representa. Queremos que Plan International refleje la diversidad de las comunidades con las que trabajamos, ofreciendo igualdad de oportunidades a todos sin importar edad, sexo, etnia, religión o creencia, orientación sexual, identidad de género, estado civil, condición de embarazo, discapacidad.

**Plan International** se basa en una cultura de inclusión y nos esforzamos por crear un ambiente de trabajo que garantice en cada equipo, en cada oficina, en cada país, sea rico en personas, pensamientos e ideas diversas.

Fomentamos una cultura organizacional que abraza nuestro compromiso con la justicia racial, la igualdad de género, los derechos de las niñas y la inclusión.

Plan International cree que en un mundo donde los niños enfrentan tantas amenazas de daño, es nuestro deber garantizar que nosotros, como organización, hagamos todo lo posible para mantener a la niñez segura. Esto significa que tenemos responsabilidades particulares hacia los niños y las niñas con los que entramos en contacto, garantizando las condiciones seguras para evitar daños y riesgos en contra de ellos.

Se llevarán a cabo una serie de controles previos al empleo; de conformidad con la Política de Protección de niños y jóvenes de Plan International.

**Plan International** también participa en el Programa de divulgación de mala conducta entre agencias. De acuerdo con este esquema, solicitaremos información a los empleadores o exempleadores de los postulantes, acerca de hallazgo e incidencias sobre su involucramiento en explotación sexual, abuso sexual y/o acoso sexual durante su temporada de empleo, así como incidentes bajo investigación cuando el postulante dejó el empleo.

Al enviar una solicitud de empleo, el postulante confirma comprender estos procedimientos de contratación.

**Tenga en cuenta que Plan International nunca enviará correos electrónicos solicitando pagos a los/as postulantes. Nuestras oportunidades de empleo se publican en sitios oficiales o redes asociadas al desarrollo y ayuda humanitaria.**

jobs.title: (2) Nutrition Intern
jobs.description:
Organizational Title: One (2) Nutrition Intern

Unit: Programs

Location: Baringo and Kilifi

Reports to: Officer, Nutrition

Grade: None (Internship)

Status: ☒ Full-Time

## Background/Organizational Context

Guided by the remarkable legacy of its co-founder, Helen Keller, Helen Keller Intl partners with communities that are striving to overcome longstanding cycles of poverty. By delivering the essential building blocks of good health, sound nutrition, and clear vision, we help millions of people create lasting change in their own lives. Working in 20 countries – across Africa, Asia, Europe, and the United States – and together with a global community of supporters, we ensure every person has the opportunity – as Helen did – to reach their true potential.

Since 2013, Helen Keller’s Kenya country program has been implemented to improve the health and well-being of mothers, infants, and young children in Kenya, specifically focusing on delivering life-saving health and nutrition interventions such as multiple micronutrient supplements to pregnant women, promotion of early and exclusive breastfeeding, vitamin A supplementation, and community-based treatment for acute malnutrition.

## Scope of the Position

The Nutrition Intern will support the implementation of Helen Keller's First 1,000 Days nutrition interventions in Baringo and Kilifi counties, working under the guidance of the Officer, Nutrition. S/he will help ensure quality project implementation, monitor and document progress and achievements, and strengthen coordination with county and sub-county health management teams and other project stakeholders.

## Key Responsibilities

### General Responsibilities:

1. Ensure quality implementation of the project.
2. Monitor project progress and document the achievements.
3. Strengthen coordination with project stakeholders.

### Specific Responsibilities:

1. **Ensure quality implementation of the project:**

- In liaison with the Officer, Nutrition, develop monthly activity workplans and track progress regularly.
- Support the Officer, Nutrition to prepare quality monthly, quarterly, and semi-annual reports.
- Ensure integration of project plans in the County health and nutrition Annual Work Plans (AWPs).
- Actively participate in county planning and coordination meetings.

1. **Monitor project progress and document the achievements:**

- Track project performance and document achievements.
- Document human-interest stories and best practices from project implementation for learning and replication in other project areas.
- Conduct day-to-day monitoring of the project and provide feedback to improve project performance.
- Plan and implement project data reviews, document findings and recommendations, and work with the counties to implement the agreed actions.

1. **Organize project coordination forums with external and internal stakeholders:**

- Participate in technical working groups and stakeholders' coordination forums in the counties.
- Ensure effective communication and collaboration with the County and sub-county health management teams.

## Required Qualifications & Competencies

### Skills & Experience

- Bachelor's degree in nutrition, public health or equivalent.
- Excellent written and spoken English and Swahili.
- Good knowledge of health and nutrition programs, policies and strategies in Kenya.

### Behavioral Competencies

- Owning Work & Building Trust: Produces honest, well-grounded content and follows through on commitments to program teams, leadership, partners, and external audiences. Takes clear accountability for the quality, accuracy, and brand integrity of communication outputs and addresses gaps directly rather than deflecting.
- Adapting & Navigating Change: Adjusts plans, messaging, and channels in response to evolving program needs, audience feedback, news cycles, and partner-coordination requirements; brings a flexible, problem-solving orientation to short timelines and shifting priorities.
- Getting Work Done: Translates communication strategy into executed outputs by sequencing work, meeting deadlines, holding suppliers and contributors to deliverables, and reinforcing brand and quality standards across every asset that leaves the program.
- Working Together & Growing Others: Builds collaborative relationships across program staff, leadership, partners, media, and global communications counterparts; gives and receives feedback constructively, shares expertise generously, and supports onboarding of new staff and consultants on brand and communication standards.

## Working Conditions

### Travel

This position requires travel up to 20% of the time, primarily domestic travel within Kenya to program sites in Baringo and Kilifi counties, county and sub-county health offices, partner offices, and events.

## Fairness, Belonging and Zero Tolerance to Abuse

As a member of the Helen Keller Family, each employee is expected to:

- Help to develop and maintain an environment that welcomes and develops a multi-cultural workforce with varied lived experiences and identities.
- Foster a work environment where everyone feels valued and included.
- Support employees' evaluation and promotion processes based on skills and performance.
- Promote a safe, secure, and respectful environment for all members of the Helen Keller Family, stakeholders in general, and particularly for the communities we serve.
- Follow Helen Keller Code of Conduct helping to prevent any type of abuse including workplace harassment, sexual abuse and exploitation, and trafficking in persons.
- Adhere to the Organizational Core Values, which include compassion, courage, integrity, and rigor.

jobs.title: Zambia Trial Supervisor (Fixed-Term)
jobs.description:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

One Acre Fund runs a pilot program in Zambia’s Central Province. Our Zambia pilot is exploring ways we can help farmers improve harvests on larger plots of land, which are common in the country. Our office in Zambia is located in Kabwe, the capital of the Central Province.

## About the Role

Seeking a field-based Trial Supervisor to run agronomic trials end-to-end, from plot setup and farmer coordination to season-long data collection, generating the on-farm evidence that shapes our practices and drives more impact per farmer.

## Responsibilities

Field Trial Setup & Protocol Adherence

- Coordinate directly with selected smallholder farmers to establish trial plots, execute baseline soil sampling, and enforce strict adherence to trial protocols throughout the season.

Agronomic Management & Farmer Engagement

- Guide participating farmers on experimental agronomic practices, deliver technical instructions clearly across varying literacy levels, and build strong community trust.

Digital Data Collection & Reporting

- Collect high-quality mobile field data—from baseline through harvest measurements—using digital tools like KoboToolbox or CommCare while conducting routine data integrity checks.

Farm Boundary Mapping & Operational Logistics

- Utilize GPS mapping applications to establish accurate trial boundaries, manage independent field travel across multiple rural sites, and report trial progress to Product Innovations leads.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Certificate or Diploma in Agriculture or a closely related field.
- Valid motorbike license (Class A or A1).
- Strong track record in field trial execution, agronomic management, and ensuring strict adherence to trial protocols.
- Demonstrated ability in farmer engagement, trust-building, and guiding farmers through seasonal trial expectations.
- Proficiency in digital data collection tools (e.g., KoboToolbox, CommCare, or ODK), conducting data quality checks, and timely field reporting.
- Excellent communication skills and fluency in local languages spoken by farmers in assigned trial areas.
- Practical experience using GPS tools/apps to accurately map farm trial plot boundaries is preferred.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Kabwe, Zambia
