**Specific duties of the consultancy**

**Research**

\- Mapping existing data on migration in Iraq and identifying gaps.
\- In consultation with the IOM office, develop a research plan and methodology.
\- Mapping relevant migration stakeholders and data producers in the country.
\- Compiling available data and information on migration in Iraq, including data shared by TWG members, as well as data requested from non-governmental migration actors and experts in the country or internationally; and data available publicly. This includes data on migration trends and impacts and information on policy and legislation.
\- Assess migration trends, migrant stocks and flows, labor migration, return and reintegration, displacement, diaspora engagement, remittances, migrant protection, migration governance, migration and development linkages, and other relevant migration themes.
\- Identify migration data gaps, inconsistencies, coordination challenges, and opportunities for strengthening migration data systems.
\- Conducting interviews with TWG members and other non-governmental migration actors and experts in the country, as coordinated and facilitated by IOM.

**Report drafting**

\- Prepare the inception report.
\- Analyze data and draft report covering migration trends, impacts and governance in Iraq and Draft the National Migration Profile in line with IOM Migration Profile methodology and publication standards.
\- Incorporate feedback from TWG, IOM and other reviewers.
\- Conduct detailed content editing and revisions as needed, including those necessary for the review, endorsement and approval processes by the IOM Research Unit and the Publications Unit.
\- Draft actionable recommendations on migration data system in Iraq and development of evidence-based migration policy or mainstreaming migration into other policy sectors.
\- Finalize the Migration Profile, executive summary, presentation materials, and methodology for future updates.
Capacity development
\- Design capacity development tools for \[enhancing migration data capabilities and systems; and/or utilizing data towards policy development\]
\- Carry out capacity development activities.
\- Contribute to the development of a toolkit to support updating of the MP in future.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

- Timeliness: Delivery of deliverables outlined in these terms of reference within the agreed timeframe.
- Quality of content:
- The MP report incorporates relevant data and information from key national and international stakeholders, aligns with IOM’s guidance on MPs, as well as research and data standards and methodologies.
- Capacity development tools are targeted to the needs of stakeholders (based on a needs assessment), and are considered useful by participants in post-training feedback.
- Collaboration and coordination with IOM project team: Participates in regular meetings with the IOM team as scheduled, as well as ad hoc engagement and coordination depending on the needs of the project.
- Stakeholder engagement: Evidence of consultation with TWG members and other project stakeholders.
- Feedback incorporation: Responsiveness to feedback from IOM the TWG and other partners during the review process.

## **Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

University degree (master’s or equivalent) in Migration Studies, Statistics, Social sciences, International Relations, Political Science, Development Studies, or a related field.
Experience:
• Minimum 10 years of professional experience in migration research or data/statistics, and policy.
• Proven experience carrying out large-scale policy-oriented research / data compilation, ideally in collaboration with government and/or international organizations.

**Skills**

• Strong analytical and writing skills.
• Strong knowledge of migration data systems.
• Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
• Strong knowledge of Iraq’s migration dynamics is an asset.

**Languages**

For this consultancy,

• Excellent proficiency in English, including writing.
• Knowledge of Arabic an asset.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Note: As part of your application, please submit a financial proposal outlining your approach and fees to complete the assignment.**

**Travel required :**
Travel to Iraq required, for stakeholder consultations, meetings, and capacity-building activities, as required by the assignment.
Accommodation and DSA will be covered Separately.

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

**Values** - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

- **Inclusion and respect for diversity**: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- **Integrity and transparency**: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- **Professionalism**: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- **Courage**: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- **Empathy**: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

**Core Competencies** – behavioural indicators

- **Teamwork**: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- **Delivering results**: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- **Managing and sharing knowledge**: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- **Accountability**: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- **Communication**: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

**Notes**

IOM covers Consultants against occupational accidents and illnesses under the Compensation Plan (CP), free of charge, for the duration of the consultancy. jobs.title: Mission France - Responsables des activités de santé mentale F/H
jobs.description:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e Responsable des activités de santé mentale pour son projet au Littoral Nord.

**Contexte:**

Médecins Sans Frontières intervient en France auprès des personnes exilées confrontées aux conséquences sanitaires, psychologiques et sociales des violences liées aux parcours migratoires et aux ruptures de protection. La Mission France combine soins, protection et témoignage pour répondre aux besoins des personnes les plus vulnérables.

Elle concentre aujourd’hui son action sur le Littoral Nord et en Île-de-France, tout en conservant une capacité de réponse rapide aux situations d’urgence. Portée par des équipes pluridisciplinaires, elle développe des activités médicales, psychologiques, sociales et de plaidoyer dans un contexte en constante évolution.

Dans un contexte de forte vulnérabilité des personnes exilées à la frontière franco-britannique, le projet Littoral Nord vise à améliorer l’accès aux soins et à la protection des publics les plus exposés, tout en documentant les impacts sanitaires, psychologiques et sociaux des politiques migratoires. Il constitue un axe stratégique de la Mission France, à l’interface entre action médicale, coordination opérationnelle et plaidoyer.

**Votre rôle :**

Sous la responsabilité du·de la Référent·e du projet pluridisciplinaire Migration, et en lien fonctionnel avec la Référente santé mentale de l’Unité Migration, vous assurerez la coordination, la supervision et le suivi des activités de santé mentale du projet.

Vous encadrerez les psychologues, garantirez la qualité des prises en charge et contribuerez à l’adaptation des interventions aux besoins identifiés sur le terrain.

Votre fonction associera **pilotage opérationnel, supervision clinique, management d’équipe et contribution aux orientations stratégiques du projet**.

**Vos principales responsabilités :**

## **Définir et piloter les activités de santé mentale**

- Identifier et analyser les besoins en santé mentale des personnes accompagnées et contribuer à l’élaboration de la stratégie du projet.
- Planifier, organiser et adapter les activités de soutien psychologique et psychosocial, individuelles et collectives, en fonction des besoins et de l’évolution du contexte.
- Garantir l’application des protocoles et standards MSF, ainsi que la qualité des interventions réalisées dans les structures de soins et sur les lieux d’intervention.
- Participer, avec la Référente santé mentale de l’Unité Migration et le·la Référent·e du projet, à l’élaboration et à l’actualisation des protocoles, outils et supports techniques, conformément aux recommandations sanitaires applicables.
- Superviser la prise en charge des situations complexes et veiller à ce que les personnes nécessitant un soutien psychiatrique bénéficient d’une orientation et d’un suivi adaptés, y compris pour les traitements prescrits.
- Contribuer aux discussions stratégiques et opérationnelles afin d’adapter les interventions aux réalités du terrain.

**Manager, accompagner et développer les compétences des équipes**

- Encadrer les psychologues et organiser leurs plannings entre consultations, activités collectives et interventions d’« aller-vers ».
- Assurer, en collaboration avec les ressources humaines, le recrutement, l’intégration et l’évaluation des membres de l’équipe.
- Identifier les besoins de formation et mettre en œuvre un plan de développement des compétences associant supervision, coaching et partage de pratiques.
- Apporter un appui technique et organiser des formations en santé mentale pour les équipes pluridisciplinaires et les partenaires du projet.
- Veiller à ce que les médiateur·rices et les interprètes intervenant lors des consultations disposent des connaissances et des repères nécessaires pour assurer une communication adaptée.
- Favoriser la coopération, la communication interne et le respect d’une posture professionnelle neutre, indépendamment des convictions personnelles.

**Renforcer les parcours de soins et la coordination pluridisciplinaire**

- Favoriser une prise en charge globale des personnes en collaboration avec les équipes médicales, de travail social et de médiation.
- Participer aux réunions pluridisciplinaires de gestion de cas et accompagner la recherche de solutions pour les situations complexes ou prioritaires.
- Développer et actualiser une cartographie des services de santé mentale, des structures spécialisées, des associations et des partenaires du territoire.
- Renforcer les mécanismes d’orientation internes et externes, en tenant compte de l’accessibilité et des capacités de prise en charge des services existants.
- Entretenir des relations régulières avec les partenaires institutionnels, associatifs et sanitaires afin de faciliter la continuité des accompagnements.
- Identifier et documenter les obstacles à l’accès aux soins, notamment les insuffisances des dispositifs de prise en charge d’urgence après des événements traumatiques.

**Analyser les résultats et garantir la qualité des interventions**

- Superviser la collecte et l’analyse des données relatives aux activités de santé mentale, en veillant à leur fiabilité.
- Définir et suivre les indicateurs, évaluer les résultats et produire les rapports d’activité nécessaires au pilotage du projet.
- Analyser les problématiques rencontrées par les psychologues et les résultats des évaluations rapides des besoins afin d’améliorer les pratiques et les orientations.
- Identifier les problématiques susceptibles d’alimenter les actions de plaidoyer de MSF et les transmettre au·à la Référent·e du projet.
- Contribuer à la planification et au suivi des ressources humaines, matérielles et financières nécessaires aux activités, en lien avec les départements support.
- Veiller à l’utilisation adaptée des ressources et à l’amélioration continue de la qualité des prises en charge.

**Profil recherché :**

**Formation et expérience :**

- Master ou diplôme en psychologie, ou diplôme de médecine avec spécialisation en psychiatrie et inscription obligatoire à l’Ordre des médecins.
- Au moins deux ans d’expérience professionnelle en tant que psychologue ou dans une fonction similaire.
- Expérience dans un projet portant sur la migration.
- Expérience en management d’équipe.

**Compétences et qualités :**

- Solides compétences en santé mentale, en coordination d’activités et en accompagnement des équipes.
- Capacité à superviser les pratiques professionnelles et à développer les compétences des collaborateur·rices.
- Sens de l’écoute, rigueur et exigence de qualité.
- Capacités d’analyse et aptitude à adapter les interventions aux besoins identifiés.
- Esprit d’équipe et capacité à travailler en pluridisciplinarité.
- Gestion du stress, flexibilité et capacité d’adaptation à des environnements difficiles et changeants.
- Adhésion aux principes et aux valeurs de Médecins Sans Frontières.
- Permis B souhaité.

**Langues et outils :**

- Maîtrise du français indispensable.
- Bonne connaissance de l’anglais souhaitée.
- La maîtrise d’autres langues est fortement appréciée.
- Maîtrise des outils informatiques courants : Word, Excel et Internet.

**Conditions d'emploi**

**Mobilité exigée sur le Littoral Nord entre Calais et Dunkerque**

Statut non-cadre : **CDD de 12 mois renouvelable**

**Rémunération et avantages :**

- **3 425,87 € brut mensuel sur 13 mois** 22 jours de RTT par an
- Complémentaire santé prise en charge à 100 % par MSF·
- Titres-restaurant de 12 € (prise en charge MSF à 60 %)·
- Prise en charge à 50 % des transports en commun ou des kilomètres à vélo

**Poste à pourvoir :** 4 janvier 2026.

Islamic Relief Worldwide (IRW) is a faith-based humanitarian relief and development organisation working to save and transform the lives of some of the world’s most vulnerable people. IRUK’s focus is strengthening effective funding, mobilising for change through advocacy and awareness-raising, and strengthening programme development and delivery. IRUK works with various partners and institutions, from governments, non-governmental organisations and local authorities to grassroots communities.

Islamic Relief UK (IRUK) is actively recruiting for the position of Junior Mosque Engagement Officer to be based from one of its regional locations in Whitechapel, Manchester, Bradford, Glasgow, Birmingham or Leicester.

The Junior Mosque Engagement Officer will play an important role in developing and strengthening relationships with mosques, Islamic centres, madrassas and community organisations across their region. Working closely with community leaders, mosque committees, volunteers and supporters, the postholder will help increase engagement, raise awareness of Islamic Relief's work and support the delivery of fundraising activities and campaigns. This is an exciting opportunity for a confident and community-focused individual who is passionate about building meaningful partnerships and making a positive impact within local Muslim communities.

**The successful candidate must have:**

- Previous experience within a community engagement role, particularly involving mosques, Islamic centres or community organisations.
- Experience and confidence in public speaking, delivering presentations and making announcements to audiences of varying sizes.
- Experience of engaging and building relationships with mosque committees, Imams, trustees, board members and community leaders.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
- Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build and maintain productive relationships across diverse communities.
- Experience of supporting or delivering fundraising, engagement or community-based initiatives.
- The ability to represent Islamic Relief professionally across a wide range of situations and settings.
- Strong presentation, networking and relationship-building skills.
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to prioritise workloads, manage competing demands and meet deadlines.
- The ability to work independently, use initiative and remain motivated within a target-driven environment.
- IT literacy with the ability to use Microsoft Office applications, particularly Word and PowerPoint.
- A flexible approach to work and willingness to travel extensively within the region.
- Willingness to work evenings and weekends where required.
- Strong motivation and empathy towards the aims and objectives of the organisation.
- An excellent record of attendance, reliability and professionalism.
- A current full UK driving licence.
- Desirable:
- Competency in a community language such as Urdu, Bengali or Arabic.
- Experience of organising community events and coordinating volunteers.

jobs.title: Senior Subject Matter Expert on Transnational Organised Crime (TOC) & Security Sector Governance (SSG) / Research Lead
jobs.company: Geneva Centre for Security Sector Governance
jobs.description:
At DCAF, we envision a world where democratic sector governance advances sustainable peace and development and human dignity for all.

Our mission is to advance the security of all people through nationally owned, inclusive, and participatory security sector reforms based on international norms and good practices.

DCAF contributes to making peace and development more sustainable by assisting partner states and international actors supporting these states, to improve the governance of their security sector through inclusive and participatory reforms. It creates innovative knowledge products, promotes norms and good practices, provides legal and policy advice and supports capacity‐building of both state and non‐state security sector stakeholders.

**Senior Subject Matter Expert on Transnational Organised Crime (TOC) & Security Sector Governance (SSG) / Research Lead**

**Workplace: Remote / Home-based (with mission travel)**

**Contract type: Consultancy**

**Expected start date: November 2026**

**Estimated level of effort: Up to 40 consultant days (November 2026 - December 2027)**

DCAF is undertaking a study aimed at “Addressing TOC Innovatively Through a Governance Focus” under Phase III of its Enhancing SSG/R Policy & Practice Programme. The project will develop a practical framework to identify governance-focused entry points for addressing transnational organised crime, drawing on research across Latin America and the Caribbean, West Africa and the Western Balkans.

**1. Objectives**

- Lead comparative research, document Latin America and the Caribbean case studies, and guide regional research teams.
- Consolidate cross-regional findings and contribute to expert validation and knowledge-sharing activities.
- Develop an evidence-based Practical Framework for Programming on security sector governance in TOC-affected environments.

**2. Methodology**

- Develop a case selection framework, standardised research protocols and key informant interview guides, incorporating research ethics, risk considerations, gender and intersectional analysis.
- Screen 12–15 potential case settings; conduct desk reviews, field visits and interviews for Latin America and the Caribbean case studies (3 cases).
- Provide methodological oversight and synthesise findings from 6–8 regional case briefs into a draft and final Practical Framework for Programming and synthesis guidance note.
- Provide technical inputs for workshops with partners and facilitate a global expert validation workshop in Geneva.

**3. Your profile**

- Advanced university degree (Masters or PhD) in political science, international relations, law, criminology, security studies or related social science discipline.
- At least 10 years of relevant experience in security policy advisory, empirical research and comparative strategy development, with demonstrated expertise in TOC and SSG/R.
- Proven comparative case study methodology and operational guidance development experience; in-depth knowledge of Latin American security governance and criminal networks, and familiarity with West Africa and/or the Western Balkans.
- Experience engaging donor inter-agency mechanisms and multilateral security advisory missions. Professional fluency in English and Spanish required; working knowledge of French highly desirable. Expert workshop facilitation is an asset.

**4. Assignment details**

- The consultant reports to a Senior Manager in the Africa Americas entity and provides technical guidance to local consultants and regional research teams.
- The contract period runs from November 2026 to December 2027, with deliverables scheduled across Q4 2026–Q4 2027.
- Workshop participation and related adjustments to consultant days are subject to arrangements agreed with DCAF.
- For detailed responsibilities, deliverables and timelines, please refer to the attached [Terms of Reference](https://ats.johdisuite.ch/storage/offers/28xDHXMSwFVKTft6hwCo3j5a77l9Ah8yilwZrCvP.pdf).

jobs.title: Chargé(e) de projet national(e) – Haïti, Amérique latine et Caraïbes
jobs.company: Geneva Centre for Security Sector Governance
jobs.description:
Au DCAF, nous envisageons un monde où la gouvernance démocratique du secteur de la sécurité favorise une paix et un développement durables ainsi que la dignité humaine pour tous.

Notre mission est de promouvoir la sécurité de tous grâce à des réformes du secteur de la sécurité inclusives, participatives et menées à l'échelle nationale, fondées sur les normes et les bonnes pratiques internationales.

Le DCAF contribue à rendre la paix et le développement plus durables en aidant les États partenaires et les acteurs internationaux qui les soutiennent à améliorer la gouvernance de leur secteur de la sécurité à travers des réformes inclusives et participatives. Il développe des outils et analyses innovants, encourage l’adoption de normes et de bonnes pratiques, fournit des conseils juridiques et politiques et soutient le renforcement des capacités des acteurs étatiques et non étatiques du secteur de la sécurité.

Les activités de l'entité Afrique et Amériques du DCAF dans la région Amérique latine et Caraïbes (LAC) visent à soutenir les gouvernements, les parlements, les institutions de sécurité et la société civile en renforçant les capacités et en promouvant les normes et les bonnes pratiques, afin de contribuer à un secteur de la sécurité plus efficace, efficient et transparent, soumis à un contrôle approprié des autorités compétentes, à l'écoute des populations et responsable devant elles.

Afin de renforcer nos activités dans la région LAC, nous recherchons une personne engagée et dynamique pour le poste suivant :

**Chargé(e) de projet national(e) – Haïti, Amérique latine et Caraïbes**

**Lieu : Port-au-Prince, Haïti**

**Date d'entrée en fonction : dès que possible, sous réserve de financement**

**Taux d'activité : 100 %**

**Durée : Contrat à durée déterminée de 12 mois, avec possibilité de prolongation**

**Le poste**

Ce poste joue un rôle essentiel dans la mise en œuvre d'une intervention visant à établir une unité de coordination au sein de la Police nationale d'Haïti (PNH), afin de rationaliser l'aide extérieure et la coordination interne associée. Pour inscrire l'appui à la PNH dans le système de sécurité au sens large et favoriser les synergies avec les initiatives connexes, le projet prévoit également des ateliers techniques et des formations.

La personne titulaire du poste apporte un appui transversal au conseiller international intégré à la cellule de coordination de la PNH (Bureau de Coordination Conjointe – BCC). En étroite coordination avec le siège du DCAF, elle soutient également la mise en œuvre globale du projet, notamment la planification, la réalisation et le compte rendu des ateliers, formations et activités de renforcement des capacités.

**Principaux domaines d'activité**

**Analyse du contexte et conseils**

- Fournir en continu des analyses politiques, des conseils sur le contexte local (notamment sur l'évolution de la situation sécuritaire) et des orientations culturelles au conseiller international et au siège du DCAF.
- Suivre l'environnement opérationnel local et fournir des analyses pour orienter les activités du projet.

**Appui à la mise en œuvre du projet**

- Mener des recherches documentaires ciblées et rédiger des notes d'analyse pour soutenir le travail du conseiller et la mise en œuvre globale du projet.
- Participer aux événements pertinents et en rendre compte conformément aux objectifs définis au préalable.
- Organiser des événements et ateliers stratégiques afin de favoriser les synergies entre les initiatives internationales d'appui au secteur de la sécurité.
- Soutenir les activités plus larges du DCAF en Haïti en identifiant de nouvelles possibilités d'intervention et en contribuant à la conception de nouvelles activités ou de nouveaux projets, en étroite coordination avec le siège du DCAF et le conseiller international.
- Rédiger les principaux livrables du projet, les concepts d'activités spécifiques, les termes de référence, les protocoles d'accord, les conventions, les synthèses contextuelles et les présentations ; collaborer au besoin avec des spécialistes et des consultants.
- Contribuer à la conception, à la planification et à la réalisation des activités de suivi, d'évaluation, de redevabilité et d'apprentissage (MEAL) ; rédiger les rapports du projet en veillant à leur qualité et à leur remise dans les délais fixés.
- Fournir, selon les besoins, un appui administratif souple pour assurer la bonne exécution du projet, notamment en gérant les aspects logistiques, administratifs et de communication liés aux ateliers, formations et missions du DCAF en Haïti (y compris la préparation des ordres du jour et la prise de notes officielles lors des réunions et événements).
- Contribuer au suivi financier des activités et au contrôle du budget.

**Qualifications, compétences et expérience requises**

- Diplôme universitaire de niveau avancé (master ou équivalent) en relations internationales, sciences politiques, études de sécurité, droits humains, droit, études du développement, études des conflits ou domaine connexe.
- La nationalité haïtienne ou un permis de travail valable en Haïti au moment de la candidature est une condition préalable.
- Une parfaite maîtrise professionnelle du français et du créole haïtien, à l'oral comme à l'écrit, est requise. La maîtrise de l'anglais constitue un atout important.
- Au moins trois ans d'expérience professionnelle pertinente dans la coopération internationale ou la gestion de projets, idéalement dans la gouvernance/réforme du secteur de la sécurité (GSS/RSS), l'état de droit ou les droits humains.
- Bonne connaissance démontrée de la gouvernance du secteur de la sécurité, des enjeux liés aux droits humains et du contexte institutionnel et politique en Haïti, notamment grâce à des contacts établis et à une expérience auprès d'acteurs étatiques et non étatiques variés (société civile, médias, institution du Médiateur).
- Compétences avérées en gestion de projets et en recherche ; solides capacités d'appui administratif et maîtrise de la suite Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
- Excellentes capacités d'organisation et de planification, aptitude démontrée à gérer des priorités concurrentes, à travailler sous pression et à respecter des délais serrés.
- Personnalité dynamique, autonome et proactive, capable de travailler de manière indépendante avec un minimum de supervision.
- Excellentes compétences relationnelles et de communication, avec une capacité démontrée à établir et entretenir des relations de travail efficaces dans une équipe multiculturelle évoluant à un rythme soutenu.

**Nous offrons**

- Une expérience professionnelle enrichissante, dynamique et porteuse de sens
- L’occasion de rejoindre une équipe diversifiée, collaborative, respectueuse, engagée et animée par des valeurs communes
- La possibilité de contribuer à renforcer la sécurité de toutes et tous grâce à des réformes du secteur de la sécurité prises en charge au niveau national, inclusives et participatives, fondées sur les normes internationales et les bonnes pratiques

jobs.description:
## **About this role**

Under the line management of the Country Director, the Programme and Grants Coordinator is responsible for the day-to-day coordination of assigned projects across ERC Ukraine’s programme portfolio. The position supports timely and quality implementation, effective collaboration between programme and support teams, donor and partner engagement, proposal development, grant compliance and reporting. The Coordinator identifies implementation risks, facilitates follow-up and escalates issues requiring management decisions.

## **Main tasks**

**Project Management and Coordination**

- Take ownership of the day-to-day coordination of assigned projects, tracking progress against objectives, work plans, budgets, deliverables and donor commitments.
- Maintain oversight of project timelines, milestones, risks, and outstanding actions; identify delays and coordinate timely corrective measures.
- Organise and follow up on project kick-off, review and coordination meetings; support consistent implementation quality and adherence to relevant standards.
- Escalate significant implementation issues and decisions to the Country Director in a timely manner.

**Internal Coordination**
- Coordinate across programme teams and Finance, MEAL, Operations, Procurement, HR and Communications to ensure aligned planning, information-sharing and timely action.
- Work with project and finance teams to monitor budget implementation, identify variances and coordinate adjustments as required.
- Coordinate with implementing partners on project planning, delivery, reporting and follow-up of agreed commitments.

**Donor and Partner Relations**
- Support ongoing donor and partner communication, coordinating responses to requests, clarifications and agreed follow-up actions.
- Coordinate donor meetings, project reviews, monitoring visits and related briefing materials in cooperation with the Country Director and relevant ERC teams.
- Maintain constructive working relationships with relevant external stakeholders within delegated responsibilities.

**Proposal Development and Grant Management**
- Coordinate contributions from relevant teams to concept notes, proposals, budgets, work plans and supporting documents.
- Contribute to proposal narratives and implementation approaches; support the identification and development of funding opportunities.
- Maintain oversight of grant conditions, donor requirements, contractual obligations and submission deadlines.
- Coordinate preparation of grant amendments, budget revisions, no-cost extensions and other donor submissions.

**Reporting, Monitoring and Compliance**
- Coordinate the preparation, quality review and timely submission of donor narrative reports.
- Work with Finance and MEAL to ensure consistency between reported activities, results, indicators and financial information.
- Monitor reporting deadlines, follow up on team inputs and ensure appropriate grant documentation and information management.
- Support compliance with donor agreements, ERC policies and applicable standards; identify gaps and coordinate follow-up.
- Coordinate project reviews, lessons learned and the use of programme evidence in future proposals.

**Other Responsibilities**
- Conduct field visits as required and subject to security conditions.
- Carry out other programme-related responsibilities consistent with the position and agreed with the Country Director.

### **Key competencies**
- At least a Bachelor’s degree in international development, social sciences, management, international relations, project management or another relevant field, or equivalent relevant professional experience.
- At least three years of relevant experience in programme/project coordination, grants management or a related field.
- Demonstrated experience with institutional humanitarian or development donors, including but not limited to ECHO, UN agencies, US State Department (USAID).
- Experience working with local implementing partners, consortia and humanitarian coordination mechanisms.
- Familiarity with humanitarian standards and the operational context in Ukraine.
- Experience coordinating multiple projects and stakeholders, donor reporting and proposal development.
- Good understanding of project cycle management, budget monitoring and donor compliance requirements.
- Strong organisational, analytical, communication and problem-solving skills; ability to manage competing priorities independently and follow through on actions.
- Strong computer skills, including proficiency in MS Office applications and the ability to quickly learn and effectively use internal digital systems and tools.
- Fluency in English (written and spoken); working proficiency in Ukrainian.

**Expected results**
- Assigned projects are implemented in line with agreed plans, budgets and donor commitments.
- Cross-team coordination and follow-up support timely resolution of operational issues.
- Donor communications, reporting and grant submissions are accurate, coherent and on time.
- Implementation risks are identified early and addressed through appropriate action.
- Proposal development is coordinated and supported by timely, quality contributions.

### **What we offer**
- **Collaborative Culture:** We foster a collaborative and inclusive work environment where every team member is valued.
- **Diverse and Inclusive Workplace:** We welcome all people of different races, genders, religions, colours, national or ethnic origins, languages, marital statuses, sexual orientations, ages, socio-economic statuses, (dis)abilities, political convictions, or any other distinguishing feature in our workplace.
- **Good Benefits:** We have a cosy office in the city centre, +4 vacation days, health insurance, and life insurance.

jobs.title: Meal Field Assistant
jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**PROJECT**

Integrated Shelter, Food Security and Livelihoods Support for Safe, Dignified and Sustainable Return in Abul Thohur (Idleb) and Madiq Castle (Hama)

**DUTY STATION**

Idlib, Syria, with regular field visits to Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate, and other project locations as required

**ABOUT THE PROJECT**

IHH is implementing an integrated humanitarian and early-recovery project funded by the OCHA Syria Humanitarian Fund (SHF), supporting safe, dignified and sustainable return in Abul Thohur, Idleb Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate.

The project combines shelter rehabilitation, winterization and Core NFI assistance, cash assistance for food, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread provision, agricultural support for returning wheat farmers, and rehabilitation of community irrigation infrastructure. These complementary interventions aim to address urgent household needs, restore essential infrastructure, protect agricultural livelihoods and strengthen community recovery.

**JOB SUMMARY**

IHH is seeking four MEAL Field Assistants to support the implementation of monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning activities across the project's target locations. Working under the guidance of the IHH MEAL Department, the postholders will conduct field data collection and monitoring, verify beneficiary and activity information, support post-distribution and post-implementation monitoring, document community feedback, and report findings in a timely and accurate manner.

The role involves frequent field visits across the project's multi-sector activities, including shelter rehabilitation, winterization and Core NFI assistance, cash-for-food assistance, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread provision, agricultural support, and irrigation infrastructure rehabilitation. MEAL Field Assistants will use approved tools and methods to collect reliable evidence, check data quality, and help ensure that affected people can safely access information and feedback channels.

The position requires strong attention to detail, impartiality, respectful communication, and strict adherence to informed consent, confidentiality, data protection, safeguarding and PSEA requirements. MEAL Field Assistants support field-level monitoring and data collection under the MEAL team's guidance; they do not independently change project targeting, make programme decisions, or investigate sensitive complaints.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Field Monitoring and Data Collection

- Conduct regular field monitoring visits to project locations in Abul Thohur and Madiq Castle in accordance with the approved MEAL plan, documenting activity progress, implementation quality, access constraints and emerging issues.
- Collect quantitative and qualitative data using approved methods and tools, including KoboToolbox or other digital data-collection platforms, structured questionnaires, observation checklists and approved monitoring forms.
- Support distribution monitoring and post-distribution monitoring (PDM) for cash assistance, winterization, Core NFI and food assistance, including beneficiary interviews and verification of whether assistance was received safely and as intended.
- Support monitoring of shelter rehabilitation, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread activities, agricultural support and irrigation infrastructure works by collecting field observations and beneficiary feedback, without replacing technical inspections or engineering certification.
- Participate in baseline, endline, post-implementation monitoring, market monitoring, needs assessments and other data-collection exercises as assigned by the MEAL Officer.
- Conduct key informant interviews (KIIs), focus group discussions (FGDs) and household surveys when assigned and trained, ensuring that questions are asked consistently and responses are recorded accurately.
- Report delays, access constraints, implementation gaps, safeguarding concerns and other issues through the appropriate reporting lines without delay.

Data Quality and Documentation

- Check completed questionnaires and monitoring forms for completeness, consistency and accuracy before submission, and promptly flag missing data, anomalies, potential duplication or other discrepancies to the MEAL Officer.
- Use approved digital tools and data-collection protocols, including consent procedures, skip logic and validation rules, and seek guidance when a tool or question is unclear.
- Support first-level data cleaning, data entry, coding, verification and organization of quantitative and qualitative information using approved systems and templates.
- Maintain accurate and organized electronic and hard-copy MEAL records, including survey forms, field visit notes, monitoring checklists, attendance records and supporting evidence.
- Prepare clear field notes and concise monitoring updates, ensuring that findings are factual, traceable and submitted within agreed deadlines.
- Collect photographs or other supporting evidence only when authorized and appropriate, and in line with consent, safety and data-protection requirements.
- Support the compilation of indicator tracking information and reporting inputs by submitting complete, timely and verifiable field data to the MEAL team.

Accountability to Affected People and Feedback Mechanisms

- Inform beneficiaries and community members about available feedback and complaints channels and how to access them safely, including during field visits and monitoring exercises.
- Receive, record and refer feedback or complaints through IHH's approved Complaints and Response Mechanism (CRM), following the established procedures and confidentiality requirements.
- Escalate sensitive protection, safeguarding, fraud, corruption or sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) concerns immediately through designated reporting channels; do not investigate such cases independently or share details with unauthorized persons.
- Support follow-up and closure of feedback cases only as instructed by the responsible CRM or MEAL focal point, and contribute to communicating authorized responses to affected people where appropriate.
- Apply impartiality, non-discrimination, accessibility and do-no-harm principles, and report barriers that may prevent women, older persons, persons with disabilities or other vulnerable groups from participating safely.
- Coordination, Reporting and Learning
- Coordinate with the MEAL Officer and relevant programme and field teams to schedule monitoring visits and ensure safe, timely access to project locations, while maintaining the independence and impartiality of MEAL functions.
- Provide timely updates on completed monitoring activities, data-collection progress, field constraints, beneficiary feedback and issues requiring follow-up.

Contribute to periodic monitoring summaries, PDM reports, assessment findings, lessons learned and other reporting products using approved formats.

- Share evidence-based observations with the MEAL team to support corrective action, adaptive management and learning, while respecting confidentiality and need-to-know access.
- Support logistics for surveys, interviews, focus group discussions and monitoring visits, including coordination of appointments and preparation of approved tools and materials.
- Perform other related MEAL duties assigned by the supervisor, consistent with the role and project needs.
- REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE
- Bachelor's degree or diploma in Social Sciences, Statistics, Economics, Development Studies, Public Health, Information Management or another relevant field.
- At least 1–2 years of relevant experience in MEAL, monitoring and evaluation, field data collection, research or accountability activities, preferably with a humanitarian or development organization.

Experience working directly with conflict-affected, displaced or vulnerable communities in Syria is an advantage.

- Practical experience conducting field visits, household surveys, interviews, focus group discussions, beneficiary follow-up or post-distribution monitoring.
- Familiarity with digital data-collection tools such as KoboToolbox, ODK or equivalent platforms is an advantage.
- Basic working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Word, and the ability to organize and check data accurately.
- Understanding of accountability to affected populations, feedback and complaints mechanisms, informed consent, confidentiality, data protection, safeguarding and PSEA principles.
- Ability to follow approved questionnaires and protocols, maintain impartiality, and report data-quality concerns accurately.
- Strong communication, interpersonal and organizational skills, with the ability to engage respectfully with diverse communities.
- Ability to work independently in the field, manage competing priorities and travel regularly to project locations in Abul Thohur and Madiq Castle.
- Fluency in Arabic, both written and spoken, is essential. Working knowledge of English is an advantage.Knowledge of Turkish is also an advantage.

**CORE COMPETENCIES**

- Field monitoring and accurate data collection.
- Data quality checks, verification and documentation.
- Beneficiary communication, accountability and safe referral of feedback.

jobs.title: Trainer and Editorial Mentor - Consultancy
jobs.description:
**Project**: Words That Protect: Gender-Responsive Media and Journalist Networks in Iraq

**Component:** Evidence-Based Gender-Responsive VAW Reporting

**Contract type:** Consultancy

**Location:** Remote, with required attendance at two project workshops in Baghdad and/or Erbil

**Assignment period:** November 2026 – April 2027

## **1. Background**

Words That Protect supports gender-responsive journalism and more responsible media coverage of violence against women in Iraq.

Under Component 2, the project will select and train 30 Iraqi journalists, with equal representation of women and men. Participants will form 15 mixed-gender teams, each consisting of one female and one male journalist, to produce and publish 15 stories addressing violence against women.

The training and production process will be informed by the findings of the project’s baseline media study and by the SEED and Silence and Omissions frameworks. Following the first in-person workshop, participants will enter a structured production and mentorship period covering story development, research, risk assessment, editorial review and publication. Each Trainer and Editorial Mentor will be responsible for supporting seven or eight journalist teams.

## **2. Purpose of the Assignment**

The Trainer and Editorial Mentor will contribute to participant selection, prepare and deliver the project training, and provide structured editorial mentorship to the assigned journalist teams throughout story development, research, production, revision and publication.

The Trainer and Editorial Mentor will support the teams in applying gender-responsive and survivor-centred reporting principles in practice. This includes reviewing story proposals and production plans, supporting the preparation of production budgets, managing the risk-assessment process, monitoring research and production, reviewing stories against the approved standards, and supervising the preparation and implementation of publication plans.

The participating journalists retain responsibility for conducting the research, producing the stories and completing the required revisions. The Trainer and Editorial Mentor leads the detailed editorial mentorship process, provides regular feedback and approves the teams’ submissions before they are delivered to the MiCT project team. MiCT maintains overall oversight of the project and reviews the key editorial and production deliverables.

### **Key Responsibilities**

1. Participate in the participant-selection process by evaluating applications and conducting interviews, with the support and under the management of the MiCT project team.
2. Prepare the required training materials covering the following main topics:
- Gender-responsive journalism principles.
- Survivor-centred approaches to reporting.
- Ethical and legal frameworks for reporting on violence against women in Iraq.
- Appropriate terminology in reporting on violence against women.

- Ethical interviewing practices.
- Ethical use of images and informed consent.
- Violence-against-women support services and safe referral pathways.
- Trauma-informed reporting methods.
- The practical application of the SEED and Silence and Omissions frameworks through reporting scenarios and editorial exercises based on the Iraqi context.

1. Adapt the training materials and mentorship methods in line with the SEED and Silence and Omissions frameworks and the preliminary findings of the study conducted by the MiCT team as part of the project.
2. Deliver the first in-person training workshop and facilitate its practical exercises and editorial activities.
3. Contribute to forming mixed-gender journalist teams, with each team consisting of one female and one male journalist.
4. Provide editorial mentorship to seven or eight journalist teams.
5. Review and approve the story topics and production plans developed by the assigned teams. Review and adjust the proposed production budgets and submit final copies of the story proposals and budgets approved by both the mentor and the participating journalists to the MiCT project team.
6. Manage the risk-assessment process for the assigned teams. Review and approve each team’s risk-assessment file and submit an approved copy to the MiCT project team before the team begins any fieldwork.
7. Closely supervise the research and story-production process and provide regular editorial mentorship. Ensure that each team maintains a complete and properly organised shared research file and task-tracking file.
8. Review each story against the approved standards, oversee the required revisions and grant final editorial approval. Submit the approved version to the MiCT project team by the agreed deadline. The review must ensure linguistic accuracy, factual accuracy, source verification, journalistic quality and integrity, and compliance with the methodological standards for sensitive reporting on gender-based violence.
9. Contribute to selecting publishing outlets and supervise the preparation and implementation of publication plans by the journalist teams. Submit the final publication plans approved by the mentor to the MiCT project team.
10. Update the team-performance tracking sheet monthly.
11. Attend periodic MiCT team meetings, maintain active communication and work in coordination with the project team.
12. Attend the closing workshop in Iraq, to be held in Baghdad or Erbil between the end of March and the beginning of April 2027.
13. Be available for interviews and complete the required evaluation forms.

### **Deliverables**

1. Training materials covering the agreed topics and adapted to the SEED and Silence and Omissions frameworks and the preliminary findings of the project study.
2. Final story proposals and production budgets approved by the mentor and participating journalists.
3. A risk-assessment file for each assigned team, approved by the mentor and submitted to the MiCT project team before the team begins fieldwork.
4. Final publication plans approved by the mentor.
5. Final versions of the journalistic stories approved by the mentor and submitted to the MiCT project team by the agreed deadline.
6. Monthly updates to the team-performance tracking sheet.
7. A progress report covering the period from the beginning of the mentorship phase until the completion of the publication process.

### **Required Qualifications**

1. Extensive professional journalism and editorial experience.
2. Previous experience in similar training, editorial mentorship or supported journalistic production assignments.
3. Demonstrated experience in gender-responsive journalism and survivor-centred journalism.
4. Broad and active professional networks within the media and journalism sector.
5. Experience training and mentoring journalists throughout the research, production, editorial review and publication process.
6. Strong editorial review, fact-checking, source-verification and risk-assessment skills.
7. Ability to manage and follow up with multiple journalist teams while maintaining organised documentation and meeting agreed deadlines.
8. Strong communication and teamwork skills.
9. Fluency in Arabic and sufficient professional English to work with the project frameworks and materials.
10. Previous experience in the Iraqi context, or in projects targeting Iraqi journalists and media institutions, is preferred.

jobs.title: Research Assistant - Consultancy
jobs.description:
**About the Role:**

MiCT is seeking a Research Assistant to support research and media monitoring activities in Iraq, with a particular focus on coverage of violence against women. The position will contribute to mapping and analysing Iraqi media coverage, supporting the development of research findings, and coordinating with trainers, mentors and project staff to integrate these findings into project activities.

**Level of Effort**

50 working days over the assignment period.

## **Key Responsibilities**

1. Monitor coverage of 5–7 cases of violence against women across Iraqi media outlets.
2. Compile a diverse and, as far as possible, comprehensive mapping of Iraqi media outlets and organisations.
3. Contribute to adapting the methodological frameworks under the supervision of the Head of Research.
4. Conduct manual research in Arabic to verify the completeness and breadth of the sample, in accordance with the parameters established by the Head of Research.
5. Participate in analysis and the development of research findings as needed.
6. Coordinate communication between the Head of Research, trainer and mentors to integrate the research findings into participant training.
7. Ensure that mentors and participants apply a consistent analytical framework based on the SEED Foundation guide during the development of their investigations, addressing framing, source selection, omissions, terminology, contextualisation, and survivor safety and privacy.
8. Coordinate with the M&E Coordinator to establish the research findings as a contextual baseline for evaluation and adapt the research content-analysis tool for assessing participant outputs through the peer review activity.
9. Support communication and coordination across project activities, including liaison with project staff, participants, trainers and mentors, follow-up on agreed actions, and coordination of activity arrangements, as required.

## **Required Qualifications**

1. A university degree in journalism, media studies, communication, social sciences, gender studies or a related field.
2. At least two years of relevant professional experience in research, media monitoring, journalism or media development.
3. Familiarity with the Iraqi media landscape and the range of outlets, ownership structures and audiences it comprises.
4. Strong Arabic-language research skills, including manual searches across media websites and social media platforms.
5. Experience in qualitative research or media content analysis.
6. Knowledge of gender-responsive journalism and ethical reporting on violence against women, including survivor safety and privacy.
7. Ability to apply analytical frameworks consistently and maintain organised, traceable research records.
8. Proficiency in spreadsheets and digital tools for organising and managing research data.
9. Strong analytical, organisational and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively within a diverse team.
10. Ability to handle sensitive information confidentially and responsibly.
11. Previous experience with MiCT would be considered an advantage.

## **Reporting and Coordination**

The Research Assistant will work under the supervision of the Head of Research and coordinate regularly with the project team.

Work will be carried out directly in the shared research files maintained by the Head of Research, with contributions and updates reviewed as part of ongoing supervision.

jobs.title: Writing Consultancy: Global Learning Report – Rollout of Gender Transformative and Conflict Sensitivity (GTCS) Guidelines
jobs.description:
**The objectives are:**

The primary objective of this assignment is to synthesize diverse country-level documentation into a structured, analytical global learning report that captures:

1. **The Rollout Process & Feedback:** How the guidelines were introduced, methodology of sensitization workshops, uptake by country offices and partners, and feedback collected from participants.
2. **Topline Initial Findings & Recommendations:** Key insights, operational challenges, adaptations made, and forward-looking recommendations distilled from individual country reports.
3. **Federation & Sector Learning:** Actionable guidance for the federation, and the wider humanitarian/development sector on operationalizing gender-transformative conflict sensitivity in protracted and complex crises.

The deliverables are:

- **Annotated Outline & Analytical Matrix:** Structural outline mapping out the three core sections and cross-country thematic clusters (within 5 working days of start).
- **First Draft Report:** Complete draft of the Global Learning Report, including Executive Summary and synthesis tables.
- **Final Report:** finalizing the draft report after receiving all technical feedback from the designated focal point.

jobs.title: Writing Consultancy: External Impact Paper for Youth Leadership in Crisis
jobs.description:
