jobs.title: Education Project Manager Ethiopia Jigjiga
jobs.description:
**What we’re looking for:**

NRC Ethiopia is seeking an experienced and dynamic **Education Project Manager** to join our team in Jigjiga Area Office. In this role, you will lead the planning, design, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of education programmes across the Somali Region, ranging from emergency education responses to formal, non-formal, and transitional education initiatives, including Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET).

Working closely with Area Office leadership, the Country Office Education team, local authorities, consortium partners, and other key stakeholders, you will ensure the delivery of high-quality, inclusive, and accountable education programmes that meet NRC standards, donor requirements, and the needs of crisis-affected communities. You will also play a pivotal role in resource mobilization, proposal development, budget management, staff coaching, and strengthening safe, child-friendly, and inclusive learning environments.

As the Education Project Manager, you will identify emerging education needs, develop innovative project proposals, and oversee the implementation of emergency and longer-term education interventions that expand access to relevant, quality learning opportunities. Your work will directly contribute to improving educational outcomes for refugees, internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, and vulnerable host-community children and youth, while aligning with NRC’s global education strategy and Ethiopia Country Office priorities.

**Please note:** This opportunity is open to Ethiopian nationals only.

Please download a more detailed[**JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQACgaKxsVIwT5yrNx8C6gSMAXWN3Y8FcSTcK1USVQTR_rs?e=QgmonO) for more specific and generic duties and responsibilities.

**What you will bring:**

- Education- Master’s degree in education planning and management (EDPM), Curriculum Studies, Educational Psychology, Education in Emergencies, or a related field.
- Professional Experience- At least five years of relevant experience in the education sector, preferably in humanitarian, emergency response, or recovery contexts, including a minimum of three years in project management or an equivalent leadership role.
- Technical Expertise- Extensive experience in implementing first-line emergency education responses, formal and non-formal education programmes, and Technical and Vocational Training (TVET) programmes in Ethiopia.
- Experience of working in complex and volatile contexts
- Documented results related to the position’s responsibilities
- Knowledge and leadership skills/profile
- Fluency in English, both written and verbal
- Knowledge of the context in Ethiopia
- Contextual understanding and knowledge of the Education sector and stakeholders in Ethiopia
- Familiarity with Education related minimum standards
- Strong communication skills ensuring good relations and smooth operations with stakeholders.
- Detail-oriented and strong analytical skills
- Strong project management skills.
- Proficiency in Somali language will be an added value.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: Jigjiga, Ethiopia.
- Contract: 12 months.
- Travel: Up to 60%.
- Salary/benefits: grade 8 on NRC’s Resident salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Market Place.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

If you have any questions about this role, please email **ho.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

jobs.title: Especialista de Transferencias Monetarias - Caracas (Staff National)
jobs.description:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Especialista de Transferencia Monetaria** altamente calificado con sede en **Caracas, Venezuela.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**DESCRIPCIÓN GENERAL DEL CARGO:**

El/la Especialista de Transferencias Monetarias brindará apoyo técnico a DRC Venezuela para la preparación, diseño, implementación y mejora continua de programas de asistencia basada en efectivo y cupones (Cash and Voucher Assistance – CVA) en diferentes sectores. La posición contribuirá a consolidar capacidades, herramientas y procesos que permitan implementar CVA de manera segura, basada en mercados, sensible a la protección y conforme a los procedimientos de DRC.

La posición trabajará de manera transversal con Programas, MERA, Finanzas, Supply Chain y equipos territoriales. De manera complementaria y según las prioridades de la operación, podrá apoyar análisis de mercados, inclusión financiera y otras iniciativas de recuperación económica relacionadas con la programación de CVA.

**PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILIDADES**

**Preparación, diseño y calidad técnica de CVA**

- Apoyar el desarrollo, contextualización y actualización de procedimientos, herramientas y flujos de trabajo para la implementación de programas de transferencias monetarias en DRC Venezuela.
- Contribuir al análisis de factibilidad y opciones de respuesta, considerando necesidades y preferencias de las personas participantes, funcionamiento de mercados, riesgos de protección y capacidad operacional.
- Apoyar el diseño de intervenciones de asistencia multipropósito y de transferencias monetarias o cupones vinculadas a objetivos sectoriales.
- Apoyar la definición y revisión de criterios de elegibilidad, mecanismos de registro y verificación, valores de transferencia y frecuencia de asistencia, en coordinación con los equipos técnicos.
- Brindar acompañamiento técnico y control de calidad a los equipos durante el diseño, lanzamiento, implementación, revisión y cierre de proyectos con componentes de CVA.
- Contribuir con insumos técnicos para notas concepto, propuestas, presupuestos, modificaciones e informes de proyectos que incorporen CVA.
- Identificar dificultades técnicas u operativas durante la implementación y acompañar a los equipos en la definición de medidas correctivas.

**Mercados, proveedores financieros y mecanismos de entrega**

- Apoyar y, cuando corresponda, liderar evaluaciones rápidas de mercado y ejercicios de monitoreo de precios, disponibilidad, acceso y capacidad de abastecimiento.
- Traducir los hallazgos de mercado en recomendaciones prácticas sobre modalidad, valor de transferencia, mecanismos de entrega y otras decisiones programáticas.
- Dar seguimiento al mapeo y análisis de proveedores de servicios financieros (FSP) y mecanismos de entrega desarrollados por DRC, actualizando la información cuando sea necesario.
- Dar seguimiento técnico al proceso de procurement de FSP, en coordinación con Supply Chain, Finanzas y Programas, y participar en la evaluación técnica de ofertas y selección del/de los proveedor(es), de acuerdo con los procedimientos de DRC y la segregación de funciones correspondiente.
- Apoyar el establecimiento y prueba de arreglos operativos con el/los FSP seleccionados, incluyendo listas de pago, intercambio seguro de información, confirmación de pagos, pagos fallidos, reintentos, reporting y reconciliación.
- Dar seguimiento al desempeño de los mecanismos de entrega e identificar ajustes para mejorar seguridad, accesibilidad, eficiencia y experiencia de las personas participantes.
- Identificar barreras de acceso financiero y oportunidades de inclusión financiera relacionadas con las poblaciones atendidas.

**Monitoreo, protección y rendición de cuentas**

- Trabajar con MERA para incorporar CVA en evaluaciones, indicadores, monitoreo, PDM y ejercicios de aprendizaje, y asegurar que los hallazgos informen ajustes programáticos.
- Trabajar con Protección para identificar y mitigar riesgos relacionados con modalidad, acceso, exclusión, fraude, seguridad, protección de datos y salvaguardas.
- Promover mecanismos accesibles de información, participación, retroalimentación y quejas para las personas participantes.
- Promover la consideración de género, edad, discapacidad, diversidad, protección y acceso seguro y digno a lo largo del ciclo de CVA.

**Fortalecimiento de capacidades y aprendizaje**

- Identificar necesidades de fortalecimiento de capacidades de los equipos de DRC en CVA y programación basada en mercados.
- Desarrollar y facilitar capacitaciones, coaching, ejercicios de simulación y acompañamiento práctico durante la implementación.
- Mantener organizado y actualizado un repositorio básico de SOP, herramientas, lineamientos y materiales técnicos relevantes para CVA.
- Documentar y compartir buenas prácticas, retos y lecciones aprendidas para favorecer la continuidad y mejora de la programación.

**Coordinación y apoyo complementario de recuperación económica**

- Representar a DRC, según delegación, en espacios técnicos relevantes para CVA y asistencia basada en mercados como el Grupo de Asistencia Basada en Mercados (GABM), y contribuir a análisis, herramientas y recomendaciones conjuntas.
- Mantener coordinación con recursos técnicos regionales y globales de DRC y aplicar lineamientos y estándares relevantes al contexto de Venezuela.
- De manera complementaria y según las prioridades de la operación, apoyar análisis de mercados, inclusión financiera y otras iniciativas de recuperación económica vinculadas o no con CVA.

**Experiencia y competencias:**

- Mínimo 3 años de experiencia profesional relevante en programas humanitarios, sociales o de desarrollo en contextos o con poblaciones afectadas por crisis, desplazamiento o vulnerabilidad socioeconómica.
- Experiencia en una o más áreas relevantes para CVA, como análisis de mercados, seguridad alimentaria, recuperación económica, medios de vida, inclusión financiera, banca o pagos digitales, protección social, focalización de participantes, MERA/gestión de información o asistencia en efectivo.
- Capacidad analítica para interpretar información de necesidades, mercados, servicios financieros o monitoreo y convertirla en recomendaciones operacionales.
- Capacidad para trabajar de manera transversal con equipos programáticos y áreas de soporte, facilitando procesos y acuerdos entre distintas funciones.
- Buenas habilidades de comunicación, facilitación, organización, coordinación y resolución de problemas.
- Conocimiento del contexto venezolano y sensibilidad frente a riesgos de protección, acceso y exclusión.

**Se valorará especialmente**

- Experiencia previa en programas de transferencias monetarias y/o cupones, aunque no es requisito excluyente.
- Conocimiento de estándares, metodologías o herramientas de CVA y programación basada en mercados.
- Experiencia trabajando con proveedores de servicios financieros, sistemas de pago, servicios bancarios, remesas, microfinanzas o mecanismos digitales.
- Formación o certificaciones en CVA, análisis de mercados, inclusión financiera, MERA, protección social, seguridad alimentaria, gestión de proyectos u otras áreas relacionadas.

**Education**

- Título universitario en economía, ciencias sociales, desarrollo, administración, relaciones internacionales, finanzas, ingeniería, u otras disciplinas relevantes.

**Languages**

- Español fluido, oral y escrito.
- Conocimiento intermedio/avanzado de inglés será considerado una ventaja, particularmente para acceder a lineamientos y recursos técnicos globales.

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda G**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**:

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes**: Domingo 08 de Noviembre a las 11:59 pm Hora Local. Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un candidat@ adecuado. DRC se reserva el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez se identifique a un candidato idóneo.

**Fecha de inicio:** Noviembre 2026

jobs.title: Field Finance Officer
jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**PROJECT**

Integrated Shelter, Food Security and Livelihoods Support for Safe, Dignified and Sustainable Return in Abul Thohur (Idleb) and Madiq Castle (Hama)

**DUTY STATION**

Idlib, Syria, with regular field visits to Abul Thohur and Madiq Castle

**REPORTS TO**

Finance Department, IHH Gaziantep Office

**PROJECT DURATION**

1 October 2026 – 30 September 2027

**ABOUT THE PROJECT**

IHH is implementing an integrated humanitarian and early recovery project in Abul Thohur, Idleb Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate. The project combines shelter rehabilitation, winterization and core NFI assistance, cash-for-food assistance, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread, agricultural support to wheat farmers, and rehabilitation of community irrigation infrastructure.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Field Finance Officer will support the day-to-day financial administration and control of project activities in the field, coordinating closely with the IHH Procurement Department and the Finance Department at the IHH Gaziantep Office. The role focuses on reviewing payment documentation, maintaining accurate financial records, supporting timely payments and advances, tracking expenditures, and ensuring that transactions comply with IHH procedures and donor rules.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Financial Transactions and Documentation**

**·** Review payment requests, invoices, receipts, claims, purchase orders, contracts, and other supporting documents for completeness, accuracy, and appropriate authorization before processing.

**·** Support the processing and documentation of approved payments, cash advances, per diems, and other project-related expenses in accordance with IHH procedures.

**·** Maintain well-organized financial files and transaction registers, ensuring that all supporting documents are properly coded, filed, and readily available for review.

**·** Verify that expenses are recorded against the correct project, budget line, and activity, and promptly follow up on missing or inconsistent documentation.

**Cash Management and Reconciliation**

**·** Maintain accurate records of cash received and disbursed, where applicable, and safeguard cash and financial documents in line with IHH cash-handling procedures.

**·** Track cash advances and ensure that they are liquidated within the required deadlines, following up with staff and activity teams on outstanding balances.

**·** Support regular cash counts, reconciliations, and checks of financial records, reporting any discrepancies to the Finance Manager.

**Budget Monitoring and Reporting**

**·** Maintain project expenditure trackers and support periodic budget-versus-actual reviews in coordination with the Finance Manager and Project Manager.

**·** Flag unusual expenses, potential overspending, underspending, or other variances and provide accurate supporting information for follow-up.

**·** Contribute to periodic financial reports, expenditure forecasts, payment plans, and other financial information requested by the Finance Manager.

**·** Support audit preparation and internal or donor financial reviews by retrieving and organizing complete records and supporting documentation.

**Programme and Field Coordination**

**·** Coordinate closely with the IHH Procurement Department and the Finance Department at the IHH Gaziantep Office, as well as programme, logistics, and field teams, to clarify procurement and payment requirements, verify supporting documents, and facilitate the timely processing of approved transactions.

**·** Support financial documentation and field-level verification related to project activities, including shelter rehabilitation, cash assistance, food assistance, bakery support, agricultural activities, and irrigation rehabilitation, as assigned.

**·** Ensure that beneficiary- or supplier-related financial records are handled confidentially and shared only with authorized personnel.

**·** Immediately report suspected fraud, irregular transactions, conflicts of interest, or breaches of financial procedures through the appropriate IHH reporting channels.

**Compliance and Other Duties**

**·** Comply with IHH financial policies, internal controls, anti-fraud and anti-corruption requirements, safeguarding standards, and applicable donor rules.

**·** Maintain accurate, up-to-date, and auditable financial records, both electronically and in hard copy where required.

**·** Perform other finance-related duties assigned by the Finance Manager that are consistent with the position and project needs.

**Qualifications and Experience**

**·** Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field.

**·** At least two years of relevant experience in finance, accounting, or financial administration; experience with an NGO or humanitarian organization is an advantage.

**·** Practical experience reviewing payment documents, maintaining financial records, handling advances, and supporting reconciliations.

**·** Good knowledge of Microsoft Excel and other MS Office applications; experience with accounting or financial management systems is an advantage.

**·** Good understanding of internal controls, supporting-document requirements, and the importance of compliance with organizational procedures and donor rules.

**Skills and Competencies**

**·** High accuracy, attention to detail, and strong organizational skills.

**·** Integrity and ability to handle financial information with discretion and confidentiality.

**·** Good communication and coordination skills, with the ability to work effectively with programme and operations colleagues.

**·** Ability to prioritize tasks, meet deadlines, and work under pressure.

**·** Fluency in Arabic and a good working knowledge of English are required; Turkish is an advantage.

**·** Willingness to travel regularly to project locations in Abul Thohur and Madiq Castle.

**Application Note**

IHH is committed to safeguarding, accountability, equal opportunity, and the prevention of fraud, exploitation, and abuse. The selected candidate will be expected to comply with IHH policies and code of conduct.

jobs.title: Head of Programmes
jobs.description:
The Head of Programmes will play a key role in shaping and strengthening SEED’s programme portfolio, providing leadership, management oversight and technical guidance to our international Programme Managers. The role will support teams to develop and deliver high-quality, impactful programmes that respond to community priorities, reflect good international practice and contribute to SEED’s strategic objectives and commitment to community-led development.

Working across SEED’s programme portfolio, the role will connect international Programme Managers with national Heads of Department and the Director of Programmes and Operations, strengthening collaboration and ensuring that programmes benefit from shared learning and expertise. The Head of Programmes will provide senior oversight while creating space for innovation, reflection and continuous improvement, helping teams to deliver programmes that are effective, responsive and ambitious in their impact.

The postholder will be a programme professional with five to eight years of international development programme design and delivery experience, able to provide practical advice whilst creating a supportive and positive management environment for international Programme Managers.

Candidates without programme management, people management and grant writing experience will not be considered for the post.

This is a new post for our expanding team and is therefore for a six-month period and, after review, has the potential to extend. It is paid at a local salary, with a contribution to flights of £1,200 and insurance of up to £650.

## Key responsibilities

- Provide oversight to SEED’s programmes across Community Health, Education, WASH, Sustainable Livelihoods and Conservation, ensuring an integrated and coherent approach to programme delivery.
- Work closely with Programme Managers, providing expert advice and constructive challenge to ensure programmes are well designed, appropriately resourced and delivered to a high standard in line with SEED’s strategic objectives, policies and values.
- Review programme plans, budgets, proposals, reports and other key programme documentation, providing guidance and quality assurance where required.
- Maintain an overview of programme performance, identifying emerging issues, opportunities, gaps and areas requiring additional management attention.
- Ensure that programmes respond appropriately to community priorities and feedback and remain relevant to changing needs and circumstances.
- Lead on the oversight of SEED’s programme development pipeline, ensuring that future programme opportunities are identified and developed sufficiently in advance of existing projects ending.
- Provide oversight into project budgets, ensuring that financial and narrative reporting is accurate, timely and of a high standard.
- Identify opportunities for programmes to complement and strengthen one another and encourage integrated approaches across SEED’s programme portfolio.
- Provide high-quality line management to SEED’s international Programme Managers through regular supervision, ongoing performance review, annual appraisal and supportive professional development.
- Provide additional management and programme capacity where required to cover staffing gaps or periods of increased workload, ensuring continuity and quality of programme delivery.
- Build a positive, collaborative and accountable team culture in which Programme Managers feel supported while taking ownership of their programmes and responsibilities.
- Work closely with Programme Managers and the MEL Coordinator to ensure that programmes are designed with appropriate monitoring, evaluation and learning processes.
- Ensure that evidence, learning and community feedback are actively used to adapt programmes and inform decision-making.
- Work closely with Malagasy Heads of Department to ensure effective collaboration between international Programme Managers and Malagasy colleagues and that programmes draw appropriately on local knowledge and expertise.
- Work closely with the Director of Programmes and Operations to ensure that SEED’s programmes continually develop in line with organisational strategy, evidence and community feedback.
- Where appropriate, represent SEED’s programmes to donors, partners and other external stakeholders.
- Ensure all of SEED’s policies and procedures are evident throughout the work of the department, including those for safeguarding, whistleblowing and anti-corruption, and undertake continual training to ensure these are promoted at all times

## Person specification

## Experience and qualifications

- At least a first-degree-level qualification or equivalent professional experience in international development or a related discipline.
- Minimum of five years' professional experience in programme management in the Global South.
- Minimum of three years' experience in grant writing, with a proven record of successful funding applications.
- Minimum of five years' professional experience in line management, including supervising, reviewing and mentoring international staff.
- Experience of living and working in the Global South, with the ability and desire to work effectively with teams from different economic and cultural backgrounds and across multiple language barriers.

## Technical and professional skills

- Sound knowledge of international development frameworks and contemporary global issues facing countries in the Global South.
- Familiarity with programme and project management tools, including logical frameworks, Theory of Change models, budgets, activity plans and monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) frameworks.
- Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills, with a demonstrable ability to gather, assess and assimilate facts and data from a range of sources and use these to inform decisions.
- Proven ability to recognise and appropriately manage challenging situations and find practical solutions.
- High degree of written and spoken English, with the ability to edit and produce high-quality English-language documents for donors and publication.
- French language skills to at least B2 level would be highly desirable.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
- Ability to work to tight deadlines in an organised manner and to a consistently high standard.

## Staff management, support and development

- Ability and desire to build capacity within both international and national teams, supporting colleagues to develop their skills and professional confidence.
- Excellent listening and verbal communication skills, combined with a flexible, patient and supportive approach to managing people.
- Ability to provide clear guidance, advice and support to colleagues in relation to SEED's ethos, policies and procedures, helping to protect their safety and the reputation of the organisation.
- Ability to support staff to develop the professional and social attitudes required for living and working in another country and, where necessary, to manage and address aspects of staff behaviour appropriately.
- Demonstrable awareness of and comfort with increased social and professional responsibility, including the ability to exercise sound judgement when supporting and managing others.

## Cross-cultural working

- Strong cross-cultural negotiation skills, with curiosity about and respect for effective ways of working in different cultural contexts.
- Cultural sensitivity and respect, with the ability to build positive and effective working relationships across cultural, economic and professional differences.
- Ability and desire to work collaboratively across multiple language and cultural contexts and to support effective communication between international and national colleagues.

## Communication, teamwork and personal qualities

- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the confidence to give clear guidance while maintaining positive and respectful relationships.
- Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
- Passion, curiosity and motivation for the role, with the ability to enthuse and motivate others.
- Demonstrable commitment to SEED's ethos and approach, with the ability to act as a positive ambassador for the organisation at all times.
- Ability and commitment to work in accordance with, and advocate for, all of SEED's policies and procedures, including safeguarding those with whom SEED works and reporting concerns appropriately.
- A flexible, patient and professional approach, with a strong awareness of the responsibilities associated with working internationally and representing SEED.

jobs.title: Senior Conservation Research Assistant (Madagascar)
jobs.description:
**Position Overview:**

This is a rare opportunity to live and work in Madagascar, one of the world’s most biodiverse and conservation-critical regions, leading long-term, field-based research in a remote setting. We are seeking a highly motivated Senior Research Assistant (SRA) with a relevant MSc and 1–3 years of practical field research experience to lead SEED Madagascar’s conservation research programme on the ground.

As the Senior Research Assistant, you will oversee the day-to-day operations of SEED’s research camp and play a central role in the design, implementation and reporting of our field-based research. Working closely with SEEDs Conservation Research Programme Coordinator and both international and national staff, you will manage data collection, ensure the quality and integrity of research activities and contribute to the analysis and dissemination of findings to donors and the wider conservation community.

Additionally, you will provide leadership and pastoral support to short-term volunteers, ensuring they receive appropriate training, guidance and supervision during their time in the field. This role is integral to advancing SEED’s mission, combining rigorous scientific research with strong team leadership and collaboration in a challenging but highly rewarding field environment.

*Location:* Fort Dauphin, Madagascar

*Timeframe*: 24 months with potential to extend;

*Terms and conditions:* Local salary to support with accommodation and living costs (field-based food/transport provided); contribution to flights and insurance

**Key Duties and Responsibilities:**

- **Research Leadership**
- Lead and manage the research team in the field, ensuring effective data collection and high research standards.
- Lead field-based research on key species and ecosystems, including setting up transects and collecting relevant ecological data.
- Contribute to the development of new research projects and conservation initiatives, helping to identify priority areas for future work.
- Support in the expansion of SEED’s research program by fostering relationships with other conservation organisations and researchers.
- **Data Management & Reporting**
- Ensure data is accurately collected, cleaned and organised in accordance with research protocols.
- Collaborate with the SCRP Coordinator in data analysis and the preparation of research reports for both internal use and external donors.
- Contribute to the development of research papers, presentations, and other publications for the international conservation community.
- Work with the SCRP Coordinator to identify opportunities for research collaborations and funding.
- Assist in the preparation of proposals and reports for research funding and project development.
- **Volunteer Coordination & Training**
- Support in the day-to-day management and pastoral care for short-term volunteers, ensuring their well-being and smooth integration into the field team.
- Lead training sessions for volunteers, ensuring they understand and follow research protocols, data collection methods, and safety procedures.
- **Collaboration & Team Management**
- Work closely with both the international and national research staff to ensure effective communication and team cohesion.
- Foster a positive working environment, promoting collaboration and sharing of knowledge between staff and volunteers.
- Ensure that all fieldwork is carried out in accordance with SEED’s health, safety, and ethical guidelines.
- **Community Engagement & Outreach**
- Support the SEED Madagascar team in engaging with communities, including facilitating meetings, conducting surveys, and helping with outreach initiatives.

jobs.title: IDMC global disaster displacement risk modelling
jobs.description:
IDMC’s disaster displacement risk work complements its monitoring of past and current displacement by providing evidence on where and at what scale displacement may occur in the future. The Global Disaster Displacement Risk Model provides probabilistic estimates of displacement risk associated with different hazards and under current and future climate conditions.

Through its collaboration with UNU-EHS and other technical partners, IDMC has progressively strengthened the model, including, through improvements to hazard and exposure data, vulnerability modelling, geographic resolution and the range of hazards considered. The existing collaboration has also supported the development of new approaches, including impact forecasting.

The next phase provides an opportunity to consolidate these advances. IDMC has recently updated its historical displacement data, including improvements to the geographic specificity of displacement information. This provides a stronger empirical basis for updating and validating the model and strengthening national and subnational risk estimates.

At the same time, methodological work undertaken during the current phase has identified promising areas for further development, including multi-hazard risk modelling and impact forecasting. The impact-forecasting proof of concept, for example, has been tested through hindcasts of 217 historical tropical cyclone events and demonstrated through a live application to Hurricane Melissa. Further testing against observed displacement data and integration of recent improvements to the underlying risk model have been identified as important next steps.

IDMC and NRC seek an agency or consortium to deliver the phased technical work below under a framework agreement. The provider will update and validate the risk estimates, develop a defensible multi-hazard framework, test impact forecasting, document methods and transfer reproducible outputs to IDMC.

- For more details on the scope of work, expected deliverables, and requirements, **please refer to the Terms of Reference (ToR), in the attachment**.
- For more details on the eligibility, **please refer to the Programmes Eligibility (ECPE), in the attachment.**
- For more details on the invitation to bid, **please refer to the Invitation to Bid (ITB), in the attachment.**

**Environmental and Social Monitoring Officer (Environmental Engineer)**

**Organization:** AMAL Organization for Relief and Development

**Duty Station:** As-Suqaylabiyah and Qalaat al-Madiq (Hama based candidates with extensive field travel to project locations in As-Suqaylabiyah and Qalaat al-Madiq could be considered)
**Contract Duration:** 12 months
**Expected Start Date:** asap but no later than 01/01/2027

**Important Note:** This position is being recruited in anticipation of the proposed project. Appointment and contract issuance are subject to final donor approval and confirmation of project funding.

## **About AMAL Organization For Relief& Development**

Amal is a non-profit Syrian non-governmental organization established and registered in Turkey on 6/6/2014, to provide life-saving aid and services to the most vulnerable people, strengthening their resilience, advocating for their basic rights, and also contributing to providing recovery and revitalization programs for societies that war turned

**Position Summary**

AMAL is seeking a motivated Environmental and Social Monitoring Officer (Environmental Engineer) to support environmental and social monitoring of infrastructure and service-delivery activities under the proposed Nabni project.

This is a junior-level position intended for candidates with a good technical foundation who are interested in developing practical experience in environmental and social safeguards.

The successful candidate will support site assessments, environmental and social screening, implementation and monitoring of Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs), contractor compliance, occupational and community health and safety, environmental monitoring and related project documentation.

The position involves regular field visits and close coordination with engineers, contractors, project staff, MEAL colleagues, local stakeholders and service providers.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Environmental and Social Site Monitoring**

- Conduct regular field visits to project sites and monitor implementation of applicable environmental and social requirements.
- Support environmental and social site assessments and screening of proposed interventions.
- Assist in identifying environmental, social, occupational health and safety, and community-safety risks associated with project activities.
- Monitor compliance with site-specific ESMP requirements and agreed mitigation measures.
- Document observations, non-compliance issues and recommended corrective actions.
- Follow up with contractors and project engineers on implementation of agreed corrective measures.
- Maintain organized monitoring records, photographs, checklists and supporting documentation.

**2. Contractor E&S Compliance**

- Monitor contractors’ compliance with environmental, social, health and safety requirements included in tender and contract documents.
- Review the practical implementation of contractor E&S and occupational health and safety measures.
- Check availability and appropriate use of personal protective equipment (PPE).
- Monitor worksite access controls, warning signs, temporary barriers, safe storage and general site housekeeping.
- Support verification that machinery operators and workers performing higher-risk activities have appropriate competencies and safety arrangements.
- Monitor worker welfare and labour-related requirements, including working conditions, age requirements, prohibition of forced labour and non-discrimination.
- Support implementation of requirements related to local recruitment where applicable.

**3. Environmental Monitoring**

- Monitor construction waste segregation, temporary storage, transportation and disposal arrangements.
- Monitor wastewater management and prevention of uncontrolled discharge or contamination.
- Follow up on dust, noise and other temporary construction impacts.
- Monitor the safe handling and storage of paints, fuels, chemicals or other materials where applicable.
- Support identification of environmentally sensitive activities or locations and recommend appropriate mitigation measures.
- Assist the engineering team in considering environmental aspects during implementation and site supervision.

**4. Occupational and Community Health and Safety**

- Monitor occupational health and safety conditions at project sites.
- Check implementation of safe working procedures for activities such as work at height, electrical works, excavation, use of machinery and other relevant construction activities.
- Monitor measures intended to protect community members, school users, pedestrians and other non-workers from construction-related risks.
- Support monitoring of traffic-management and site-access arrangements where required.
- Assist in documenting accidents, incidents and near misses and following up on required corrective measures.
- Immediately escalate serious environmental, social or safety concerns to the Project Manager and relevant technical focal point.

**5. Environmental and Social Documentation**

- Support preparation and updating of environmental and social screening checklists, ESMPs, site monitoring forms and related documentation.
- Maintain environmental and social monitoring records for each intervention.
- Support preparation of periodic E&S monitoring summaries and reports.
- Track corrective actions and maintain a simple action-follow-up register.
- Assist in compiling E&S documentation required for project reporting, donor monitoring or audits.
- Support integration of environmental and social requirements into procurement and contractor documentation.

**6. Community and Social Monitoring**

- Support monitoring of community health and safety and potential temporary impacts on access to services, properties and public facilities.
- Support stakeholder engagement activities where environmental or social issues need to be discussed with affected communities.
- Coordinate with the MEAL team regarding project-related complaints and feedback relevant to environmental or social issues.
- Support monitoring of inclusive access and non-discrimination in relation to supported facilities.
- Assist in documenting ownership, use-right and access information required for project due diligence, under the guidance of relevant project staff.

**7. Mine Action and Other Site-Safety Follow-Up**

- Support administrative and field coordination related to explosive ordnance risk verification where required.
- Maintain records of relevant correspondence, assessments and site-clearance or verification documentation.
- Ensure that unresolved explosive ordnance risks or restrictions are clearly communicated to the project team.
- The officer will not conduct Non-Technical Surveys, clearance or explosive ordnance disposal activities unless separately qualified and formally authorized.

**8. Awareness and Capacity Support**

- Support basic E&S and safety briefings for contractors, workers and project staff.
- Explain applicable site requirements in practical and understandable terms.
- Help contractors and field teams understand corrective actions identified during monitoring.
- Participate in relevant trainings provided by AMAL, Nabni or other technical partners and apply the learning during field monitoring.

**Qualifications and Experience**

**Essential**

- Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Civil Engineering, Occupational Health and Safety, or another closely related technical field.
- Environmental Engineering graduates are particularly encouraged to apply.
- Around 1–2 years of relevant experience is preferred; however, strong junior candidates and recent graduates with limited practical experience may also be considered if they demonstrate sound technical knowledge, field readiness, strong motivation and the ability to learn quickly.
- Basic understanding of environmental management, construction-related environmental impacts and occupational health and safety.
- Ability and willingness to conduct frequent field visits and work around construction and infrastructure sites.
- Ability to prepare clear written observations, checklists and simple reports.
- Good communication and coordination skills.
- Good computer skills, particularly Microsoft Word and Excel.
- Good Arabic communication skills.
- Working knowledge of English sufficient to understand technical guidance and prepare basic project documentation.

**Desirable**

- Previous internship, volunteering or employment experience related to construction, environmental monitoring, engineering supervision, health and safety or humanitarian/development programming.
- Familiarity with ESMPs, environmental and social screening or contractor E&S monitoring.
- Basic knowledge of waste management, wastewater, pollution prevention, occupational health and safety or community safety.
- Experience using field monitoring checklists, GPS/mobile data-collection tools or photographic documentation.
- Familiarity with infrastructure rehabilitation projects.

Who We Encourage to Apply

This position is intentionally designed as an opportunity for a junior environmental or engineering professional to gain practical experience in environmental and social safeguards.

Candidates should not be discouraged if they have not previously held an E&S-specific position. Applicants with a strong technical foundation, attention to detail, confidence working in the field and a demonstrated ability to learn quickly are encouraged to apply.

**Key Competencies**

- Willingness to learn

- Attention to detail

1. Field Supervision & Technical Oversight: Provide daily field supervision for all civil, structural, and finishing works (including blockwork, plastering, tiling, painting, and waterproofing) to ensure strict adherence to the Bill of Quantities (BoQ), approved drawings, and technical specifications.
2. Site Assessment & Planning: Conduct initial site assessments to verify existing conditions (e.g., structural cracks, damaged plaster, existing plumbing/electrical networks) and prepare work plans and technical measurements accordingly.
3. Contractor Performance & Quantity Verification: Monitor contractor activities, verify executed quantities, and measure completed works against the BoQ to certify payment milestones. Document any deviations or non-conforming works and report them immediately.
4. Structural & Finishing Supervision: Supervise and verify the execution of concrete works (footings, columns, slabs), masonry, and precise finishing works such as ceramic/cement tiling, marble installation, and painting to ensure high-quality workmanship.
5. Quality Control & Materials Testing: Verify the quality of all materials delivered to the site (e.g., cement, steel, blocks, tiles, paints, waterproofing membranes) and ensure they match the approved submittals and technical specifications. Witness concrete testing and compaction tests as required.
6. Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) Compliance: Ensure that the contractor strictly adheres to safety procedures during excavation, concrete casting, welding, and other high-risk activities. Enforce environmental regulations regarding dust control and debris management.
7. Reporting & Documentation: Maintain accurate site records, including daily logs, site diaries, and photographic documentation. Prepare periodic progress reports detailing completed works, technical observations, and challenges.
8. Site Handover & Acceptance: Supervise interim and final acceptance of works, ensuring all defects and punch-list items are rectified by the contractor before formal handover. Ensure the sustainability and functionality of the rehabilitated infrastructure.
9. Coordination & Stakeholder Engagement: Coordinate effectively with project teams (Program, Logistics, Procurement), local authorities, and community representatives to resolve technical issues, facilitate site access, and ensure smooth project implementation
10. Perform any other related duties and responsibilities as assigned by the line manager within the scope of work.

**Note: The key responsibilities listed above are indicative and not exhaustive. Additional responsibilities may be assigned to the position in the future, depending on the organizational structure and management requirements.**

**Qualification (Education/Work Experience)**

**Essential Qualifications**

1. Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or a related field.
2. At least 2 years of professional experience in supervising civil works, infrastructure, or construction projects.
3. Practical experience in field supervision of excavation works, concrete foundations, and contractor follow-up.
4. Good command of the English language.

**Desirable Qualifications**

1. Experience working in infrastructure rehabilitation projects, schools, or health centers.
2. Experience in reviewing Bills of Quantities (BoQs), drawings, and technical specifications, as well as measuring and accepting completed works.
3. Proficiency in AutoCAD and Microsoft Office applications.

**Core & Managerial Competencies**

1. **Core Competencies:**

- Communication
- Teamwork
- Planning and organizing
- Accountability
- Creativity
- Stakeholder Orientation
- Commitment to Continuous Learning
- Technological Awareness.

1. **Supervisor/Managerial Competencies:**

- Leadership
- Building Trust
- Vision
- Managing Performance
- Empowering Others
- Judgment/Decision-making.

1. **Technical Competencies:**

- Good knowledge of excavation works, preparation of foundation pits, and casting and construction of concrete foundations.
- Ability to read and interpret drawings, Bills of Quantities (BoQs), and technical specifications, and compare them with the actual implementation on site.
- Good knowledge of civil works quality control methods and monitoring of executed quantities.
- Ability to follow up with contractors, document technical observations, and monitor the implementation of corrective actions.
- Good skills in report writing and field documentation.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.

**Compliance to Anti-Harassment, PSEA, and Child Safeguarding**

- Child abuse in all forms is unacceptable to IYD, which recognizes its responsibility to protect children from harm in all areas of its work. IYD is committed to ensuring a child-safe environment and is applying a zero-tolerance approach towards any kind of child abuse and exploitation.
- IYD employees and related personnel must not under any circumstances take part in any form of discrimination, harassment, or abuse (physical, sexual or verbal), intimidation or exploitation, or in any other way infringe the rights of others inside or outside IYD.

jobs.title: Outreach Officer – Child Protection and Support to Vulnerable Families
jobs.description:
As part of a consortium, Habibi Association is implementing an AICS-funded project under the *Integrated Emergency Programme for Child Protection and Support to Vulnerable Families in Jordan*.The project aims to strengthen the protection and resilience of refugee and Jordanian children and their caregivers through integrated services, income support, capacity building and community mobilisation in Amman, Zarqa, Mafraq and Madaba.Within the consortium, Habibi is responsible for activities aimed at improving access to inclusive, gender-sensitive child protection services and strengthening the economic resilience of vulnerable households through vocational training and support for income-generating activities.To support the implementation of these activities, Habibi Association is seeking an **Outreach Officer** to support outreach, community engagement and beneficiary identification, working under the supervision of the Project Manager and in coordination with consortium partners and relevant local stakeholders.

## **2. Key Responsibilities**

Reporting to the MEAL Officer and/or the Project Manager, the Outreach Officer will be responsible for the following:

**A. Outreach and beneficiary identification**

- Support the development and implementation of the project’s outreach plan in collaboration with consortium partners and local civil society organisations.
- Identify and engage potential beneficiaries in accordance with the project’s eligibility and targeting criteria.
- Conduct beneficiary outreach and data collection using the tools and procedures established by the project.
- Ensure that information collected is accurate, complete and properly recorded, including through the use of tablets or other digital tools.
- Explain the purpose of data collection and obtain informed consent before collecting or recording personal information.
- Identify cases requiring referral and report them to the designated project focal point in accordance with established referral procedures.
- Ensure the confidentiality and secure handling of beneficiary information, in compliance with data protection, safeguarding and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) procedures.
- Submit collected data and related documentation within established deadlines, reporting any challenges encountered during outreach or data collection.

**B. Coordination and organisational support**

- Participate in internal project meetings and coordination meetings with consortium partners, as required.
- Be available to undertake weekly field visits.

## **3. Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- High school diploma required; a degree in Social Sciences or a related field will be considered an asset.

**Professional Experience and Technical Skills**

- At least two years of relevant professional experience in outreach, community engagement or beneficiary identification within development or protection projects.
- Good knowledge of the Jordanian socio-economic context, particularly at the local level.
- Experience working on projects funded by the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS) will be considered an asset.
- Good organisational and planning skills, including the ability to prioritise tasks, manage deadlines and respond to implementation challenges.
- Good command of IT tools and standard office software. Experience with KoboToolbox or other data collection and management software is considered an asset.
- Valid driving licence and ability to drive in Jordan.

**Languages**

- Advanced proficiency in Arabic, both written and spoken.
- Proficiency in English, both written and spoken.

**Personal and Interpersonal Skills**

- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to work constructively with people from diverse backgrounds.
- A proactive, solution-oriented approach and the ability to respond effectively to challenges.
- A strong sense of responsibility, attention to detail and commitment to meeting deadlines.
- Commitment to social inclusion, child protection, gender equality and the rights and dignity of vulnerable and marginalised people.
- Willingness and availability to travel regularly to project locations outside Amman.

## **4. Contractual Conditions**

- **Duty station:** Amman, Jordan.
- **Contract duration:** 15 months.
- **Expected starting date:** December 2026.
- **Gross monthly salary:** JOD 800–950, depending on the candidate’s qualifications and relevant experience.

jobs.title: Advocacy Mobile Implementation Advisor (m/f/x) – MSF Belgium
jobs.description:
**CONTEXT**

In the current landscape of growing humanitarian needs, compounded political, environmental, and economic crises, and shrinking humanitarian space, MSF teams play a key role in maintaining MSF’s relevance and impact and in positively influencing the overall response to communities’ medical and humanitarian needs by authorities and humanitarian actors.

While MSF country programmes have capacity for leverage this potential is often underused due to insufficient analysis and a lack of well-resourced advocacy strategies with clear follow-up mechanisms.

**MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES**

This position is jointly managed by the Operations Department and the Analysis Department, and its main purpose is to provide targeted, time-bound support to country programmes. This includes analysing humanitarian contexts, defining positioning and advocacy objectives, developing data collection frameworks for advocacy, and contributing to the development of advocacy strategies and products.

More specifically, the Advocacy Mobile Implementation Advisor can provide:

**1. Direct support to Operations**

- Support humanitarian analysis, including actor mapping and stakeholders power analysis
- Support the definition or revision of advocacy objectives and priorities, providing input for new or existing advocacy plans, engagement and influencing strategies
- Collect and analyse data and develop advocacy products, such as talking points, briefing notes, reports, and public communication initiatives in collaboration with the Communication Department
- Contribute to external engagement activities at the request of Operations
- Support emergency advocacy during acute or evolving crises by disseminating timely advocacy materials and by providing rapid analysis
- Organise or support learning activities at project level for increased awareness and capacity for humanitarian analysis and advocacy
- Support the recruitment and onboarding of new humanitarian affairs staff, provide guidance and support to existing staff, in complementarity with the Humanitarian Learning and Development Coordinator

**2. Support for the development of knowledge products and learning solutions**

- Contribute to the formalization and dissemination of good practices and the development of new humanitarian affairs tools
- Contribute to the review of advocacy approaches and practices
- Support the development of advocacy methodologies informed by anti-racism, diversity, equality, and inclusion principles
- Contribute to the design and implementation of the learning solutions offered by the Analysis department

**REQUIREMENTS**

**Education & Experience**

- Political, Social Sciences or Public Health degree at postgraduate level
- Minimum 2 years of international MSF experience in humanitarian affairs and advocacy in different contexts
- Experience in data production & management
- Experience in other NGOs is an asset
- Experience in mentoring and/or coaching is a strong asset

**Competencies**

- Strong analytical skills
- Excellent writing skills
- Ability to use data responsibly, safely, and ethically
- Strong mentoring and coaching skills
- Strong communication and teamwork skills
- Flexibility and adaptability to working in diverse settings and with diverse priorities
- Cross cultural awareness
- Strong understanding and ability to promote humanitarian principles

**Languages**

- Proficiency in **English and French**, both written and spoken, is mandatory

**CONDITIONS**

- Expected starting date: January 2027
- Location\*: Brussels (Belgium)

\**Due to administrative constraints, given the duration of the contract, candidates may need to already have the permanent right and/or a valid work permit to work in the mentioned locations.*

*\*Other location/s where there is an MSF entity could be discussed in exceptional cases. The outcome will depend on the candidate's residency, the local legal restrictions (residency, work permit, etc.), and the agreement with the host MSF entity of the location.*

- Type of contract: Fixed-term contract – Full-time
- Duration of contract: 1 year (possibility of extension)
- Mobility: up to 70% of the time in MSF projects worldwide
- Salary according to MSF mobile staff salary grid
- High mobility allowance
- The contractual terms, conditions and salary will be established according to the official residence of the selected candidate and in respect of MSF standard function and salary grid for mobile staff
- Medical insurance 100% covered as per international package; 45 days annual paid leaves
- Not a family position
- *Adhere to the MSF principles and to our managerial values: Respect, Transparency, Integrity, Accountability, Trust and Empowerment*
- *Adhere to the MSF Behavioral Commitments*

**Deadline for applications: 17th of November 2026**

jobs.title: Coordinateur de site et du consortium Fonds Humanitaire (F/H) - République Centrafricaine
jobs.description:
Vous souhaitez intégrer une association militante et agir concrètement pour plus de justice sociale ?

Médecins du Monde agit depuis plus de 40 ans pour soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, dénoncer les entraves à l’accès aux soins et faire évoluer durablement les politiques de santé.

En France et dans près de 30 pays, nos actions s’articulent autour de six combats politiques :

- droits et santé sexuels et reproductifs (dont le droit à l’avortement)
- migration, exil, droits et santé
- réduction des risques
- santé environnement
- droits et système de santé
- espaces humanitaires

## Médecins du Monde en RCA

La République centrafricaine (RCA) demeure confrontée à des conflits armés récurrents, entraînant une crise humanitaire majeure et de nombreuses violations des droits humains et du droit international humanitaire.

Présente dans le pays depuis 2013, Médecins du Monde (MdM) France intervient auprès des populations les plus vulnérables à travers des soins de santé dans les zones reculées, des services de santé sexuelle et reproductive, la prise en charge des survivant·e·s de violences basées sur le genre (VBG) et le déploiement de cliniques mobiles d’urgence. En 2025, ses interventions ont bénéficié à 278 113 personnes.

Récemment, MdM a renforcé sa présence opérationnelle avec le lancement, en novembre 2024, d’un projet à Batangafo dédié à la prise en charge de la malnutrition aiguë sévère chez les enfants et des survivant·e·s de VBG. En mars 2026, une nouvelle base a été ouverte dans la sous-préfecture de Kabo, grâce au financement de la DG ECHO, afin d’appuyer six formations sanitaires, dont l’hôpital secondaire, pour une durée de seize mois.

Pour les prochaines années, MdM prévoit d’accroître ses activités, ses financements et sa couverture géographique, tout en consolidant son positionnement comme acteur de référence dans le domaine de la santé, notamment en matière de prévention et de prise en charge des VBG. L’organisation poursuit également sa collaboration avec les autres ONG internationales afin de renforcer la coordination humanitaire, le partage d’informations et l’efficacité des interventions.

## Pourquoi nous avons besoin de vous

En tant que coordinateur de site et du consortium Fonds Humanitaire (F/H), vous aurez pour principales missions de piloter et de coordonner la stratégie et la mise en œuvre des programmes du consortium Fonds Humanitaire à Batangafo, Bouca, Kabo et Sido, en animant les équipes et les partenaires, en garantissant l'application des procédures MdM et en développant le plaidoyer et les partenariats.

Vous assurerez l’animation du consortium entre MdM et Solidarités International sur la base.

## Vos missions

Plus spécifiquement, vos responsabilités seront les suivantes:

## 1. Coordination, représentation et partenariats

- Représenter MdM auprès des autorités, acteurs humanitaires, bailleurs, partenaires techniques et forces présentes dans la zone d’intervention
- Participer aux mécanismes de coordination, ateliers, conférences et visites institutionnelles afin de renforcer le positionnement de MdM
- Assurer des relations régulières avec les partenaires et veiller à la cohérence des actions menées sur la zone

## 2. Pilotage stratégique et gestion du consortium

- Diriger le consortium, animer la gouvernance, coordonner les membres et garantir une prise de décision efficace et transparente
- Définir, suivre et actualiser les plans d’action, de contingence et de suivi-évaluation (MEAL), tout en veillant à la bonne utilisation des ressources
- Produire des analyses, recommandations et retours d’expérience permettant d’améliorer la qualité des interventions et la coopération opérationnelle

## 3. Supervision opérationnelle et suivi des projets

- Organiser et coordonner les activités de la base de Batangafo, y compris les projets, la construction des infrastructures et les relations avec les partenaires
- Piloter la planification des activités, suivre les indicateurs, les échéances contractuelles et l’exécution des actions afin d’assurer leur qualité et leur conformité
- Contribuer à la définition des orientations stratégiques, assurer le reporting opérationnel et capitaliser les enseignements tirés des interventions

## 4. Gestion de la sécurité et de l’accès humanitaire

- Assurer une veille contextuelle et sécuritaire, collecter et partager les informations nécessaires à l’analyse des risques
- Élaborer, actualiser et faire appliquer les dispositifs de sécurité, tout en sensibilisant les équipes aux procédures et règles en vigueur
- Garantir l’accès humanitaire, gérer les incidents de sécurité et coordonner les réponses opérationnelles et les communications en cas de crise

## 5. Management des équipes et supervision des fonctions support

- Encadrer les équipes de la base : recrutement, intégration, fixation des objectifs, évaluation des performances, accompagnement et développement des compétences
- Favoriser la cohésion d’équipe, gérer les conflits, faire respecter les politiques internes et prendre les mesures correctives nécessaires
- Superviser les volets RH, financiers, administratifs et logistiques de la base, notamment le budget, le suivi des ressources et le respect des procédures internes

## Vos collègues

Sous la responsabilité hiérarchique du coordinateur général (F/H) basé à Bangui, vous collaborez avec l’équipe de coordination de MdM à Bangui et les chefs de base des ONGs membres du consortium ainsi le chef d’Antenne OCHA de Batangafo et tous les responsables des ONGs Internationales et nationales présente à Batangafo. Vous supervisez directement les responsables des équipes support et programmes.

## Vous êtes la bonne personne si…

- Vous êtes diplômé.e d'une formation supérieure en gestion de projet ou généraliste de l’Humanitaire
- Vous avez obligatoirement une expérience réussie de trois ans minimum sur un poste similaire de coordinateur terrain au sein d'ONGi en appui de programmes humanitaires financés par des bailleurs intstitutionnels
- Vous avez une expérience réussie en ouverture de base (fortement souhaité)
- Vous avez une expérience réussie en élaboration, conduite et évaluation de projet de santé d’urgence dans des pays et/ou zones en crise
- Vous avez une expérience réussie dans la gestion de la sécurité et de l'accès dans un contexte sécuritaire volatile
- Vous avez une expérience significative en management d'équipe
- Vous êtes capable d'arbitrer en cas de dilemme de manière structurée et méthodique
- Vous savez faire preuve de proactivité, d'organisation et de planification
- Vous parlez couramment le français et l'anglais
- Vous avez une bonne maîtrise du Pack Office et des outils de travail collaboratifs

## Ce poste n’est pas pour vous si...

- Vous craignez ne pas vous retrouver dans les valeurs et le positionnement militant de Médecins du Monde
- Vous ne vous sentez pas à l'aise pour vivre et travailler dans des conditions de vie relativement simples, voire spartiates
- Vous n'avez pas d'expérience de travail en équipe interculturelle et multidisciplinaire
- Vous ne savez pas faire preuve de patience, diplomatie et pédagogie

## **Les prochaines étapes**

Si votre candidature est sélectionnée, nous vous contacterons rapidement pour vous proposer un entretien RH avec un.e chargé.e de recrutement. Les entretiens, technique et managérial, auxquels des cas pratiques pourront éventuellement être intégrés, auront lieu dans le courant du mois de novembre.

Dans le cadre de la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme, des vérifications d’antécédents sur listes internationales pourront être effectuées. Les données sont traitées de façon confidentielle et sécurisée. Plus d’infos : [http://bit.ly/3CSThBs](http://bit.ly/3CSThBs)

Un extrait de casier judiciaire (B3) sera demandé à toute personne recrutée.

## Nous attendons votre candidature

Nous n’avons besoin que de votre CV et de votre lettre de motivation.

Si vous pensez correspondre à ce poste, postulez !

## Vos conditions d’emploi

**Contrat & statut :**

- Salaire brut mensuel 3 663 €
- CDD à pourvoir à partir du 1er novembre jusqu'au 30/08/2027 (non glissant)
- Départ seul

Cadre de travail :

- Poste basé à Batangafo
- Déplacements à prévoir sur la zone du projet (Sido, Batangafo Kabo et Bouca) et à Bangui

Les avantages :

- 13e mois (pour les salarié.e.s ayant plus de 6 mois d’ancienneté)
- Prime d’expatriation de 10% du salaire brut par mois
- Prise en charge du transport (domicile – mission), des visas, des vaccins
- Hébergement: vous serez hébergé.e en guest house (bon niveau de confort)
- Politique R&R: tous les trois mois
- Assurance santé (participation à 50% de MdM et 50% du salarié)
- Assurance rapatriement
- MdM favorise la formation et la mobilité interne

Les indispensables :

- 5 semaines de congés + 22,5 RTT par an
- Engagement fort en faveur de l’inclusion et de la lutte contre toutes les discriminations
- Plus d’infos : [https://bit.ly/3x5MezL](https://bit.ly/3x5MezL)

Diversité et inclusion

MdM s’engage pour l’insertion des personnes en situation de handicap et lutte contre toutes les discriminations.

Si vous bénéficiez d’une reconnaissance de la qualité de travailleur.se handicapé.e et/ou si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement de poste, n’hésitez pas à nous en faire part.

jobs.title: National Technical Consultant –Electrical Engineer
jobs.description:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Organization:** UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- **VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/207**
- **Position Title**: National Technical Consultant – Electrical Engineer
- **Duty Station:** Dbayeh, Tyr and Adloun with occasional meetings at UNDP offices if need be.
- **Duration:** 4 months (without exceeding 6 working days per month)
- **Vacancy Date of Issue: 27 October 2026**
- **Vacancy Closure Date: 03 November 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1l7n3ymgwhCqXmBtEfHyHwMjbRZk0qOCD/view?usp=drive_link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1l7n3ymgwhCqXmBtEfHyHwMjbRZk0qOCD/view?usp=drive_link)

**BACKGROUND**

UNDP, through its Rule of Law and community security programming, has been supporting national and local institutions in Lebanon to strengthen the delivery of security and public services and promote safer and more resilient communities. This support includes interventions implemented in coordination with the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities (MoIM), the Internal Security Forces (ISF), municipalities, and other relevant local stakeholders. Through consultations, field assessments, and engagement with local authorities and security institutions, inadequate public lighting and unreliable access to electricity have been identified as important challenges affecting the safety, accessibility, and functionality of public spaces and security facilities. These challenges have become increasingly significant in the context of Lebanon's prolonged electricity and energy constraints. In response, UNDP is supporting the implementation of street-lighting and solar-energy interventions in Tyre, Marina Dbayeh, and Adloun ISF Station. The interventions are intended to improve lighting and safety in targeted public areas while promoting reliable and energy-efficient solutions adapted to the operational needs of the respective locations.

Given the technical nature of these interventions, appropriate electrical assessments, technical specifications, and quality control are required to ensure that the proposed systems are suitable for the site conditions, technically sound, safe, and implemented in accordance with the approved designs and specifications.

Accordingly, UNDP intends to recruit an Electrical Engineer Consultant to provide technical support for the interventions in Tyre, Marina Dbayeh, and Adloun ISF Station. The consultant will be responsible for preparing the required technical baseline studies and assessments, including identifying the electrical and lighting requirements of the targeted locations and developing the necessary technical specifications and related documentation.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the supervision of the Senior Project Officer and the Director General of the Directorate of Municipalities and local authorities in Lebanon, the consultant will be responsible for:

- Carry out a site visit and quality evaluation for the condition of the street lighting poles in Tyre.
- Meet with Antelias and Dbayeh municipality to collect the needed information of the street lighting in Marina Dbayeh.
- Submit a detailed plan and specs for installing solar panels for street lighting poles in Marina Dbayeh.
- Conduct site visits to Marina Dbayeh to oversee the implementation of the works.
- Evaluation of finalized works in respect to the public safety regulations and good practice.
- Prepare a BoQ and Technical Baseline study for solar system at Adloun ISF Station.
- Conduct site visits to ADLOUN ISF Station to oversee the implementation of the works.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities, noting that the total duration is 4 months without exceeding 6 working days per month.

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

In addition, any public appearance related to the activity should be coordinated and approved by UNDP.
