jobs.title: Technical Officer – Ocean Observations
jobs.description:
## Description

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Geoscience Energy and Maritime (GEM) Division** provides advice, technical assistance, research and training support to Pacific Island countries and territories (PICTs). There are four (4) areas of scientific programming within this division:

1. **Oceans and Maritime Programme (OMP)** – assists member countries with services that provide applied ocean science and knowledge for evidence-based policy-making and technical solutions for improved ocean and maritime governance, management and capacity development.
2. **Georesources and Energy Programme (GEP)** – assists member countries by applying technical knowledge in the areas of geoscience and sustainable energy use.
3. **Disaster and Water Resilience Programme (DWRP)** – assists member countries to demonstrate strengthened resilience through integrated action on disaster risk management, climate change adaptation, natural resource management and increased access to water and sanitation.
4. **Earth and Ocean Observation Services** – Promoting spatial data and systems analysis and capacity to improve decision-making to improve resilience and sustainable resource management.

The role – **Technical Officer – Ocean Observations** will provide technical hands-on support for SPC’s regional ocean observation and monitoring activities, with a primary focus on wave monitoring systems. The role operates within SPC’s technical workshop capability, supporting the deployment, maintenance, and operational sustainability of wave buoys, while contributing to other in situ ocean observing systems (e.g. ADCPs, water-quality sensors, and multi-sensor platforms) across SPC member countries, including applications relevant to fisheries, maritime, and ocean and climate services.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

**Wave and Ocean Monitoring System – Deployment and Field Operations**

- Plan, coordinate, and participate in deployment, recovery, and redeployment of wave buoys and other in situ ocean observing instruments, in collaboration with SPC teams and national counterparts, including participation in diving operations where required.
- Undertake or contribute to site assessments, mooring design and deployment planning ensuring alignment with local environmental conditions and operational requirements.
- Lead or support offshore and coastal field operations, ensuring compliance with SPC safety and operational procedures, and alignment with mission objectives.
- Prepare mission plans, risk assessments, and field operation reports, documenting technical outcomes, issues encountered, and lessons learned.

**Maintenance, Troubleshooting and Technical Support**

- Provide technical maintenance and troubleshooting support for wave buoys and other in‑situ ocean observing systems, including sensors, telemetry, power systems, and moorings, in collaboration with national counterparts, SPC teams and service providers.
- Plan and coordinate preventative and corrective maintenance activities, to ensure operational availability and longevity of observing systems.
- Diagnose technical faults, recommend corrective actions, and support their implementation by relevant SPC teams, service providers, or national partners.
- Maintain accurate maintenance logs, calibration records, and technical documentation to support asset tracking, audits, and knowledge transfer.

**Data Quality Assurance, Data Management Procedures & SOP Development**

- Support the application of agreed data management and data quality assurance procedures for wave buoys and other in situ ocean observing systems, in line with SPC and country arrangements.
- Support the timely and reliable ingestion of observation data from SPC‑supported systems into SPC and agreed national data management platforms.
- Work with national counterparts to support the sharing and integration of country‑owned observation data in accordance with agreed processes and data governance arrangements.
- Contribute to the development, maintenance, and application of standard operating procedures (SOPs) covering deployment, maintenance, data handling, and incident response.

**Procurement and Asset Management**

- Provide technical input to procurement processes for ocean observing equipment and services, including preparation of technical specifications, participation in evaluations, and engagement with suppliers, in line with SPC policies and procedures.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of ocean observing assets, including inventories, warranties, servicing requirements, and lifecycle status, to support effective planning, maintenance, and sustainability of observing systems.
- Coordinate logistics for ocean observing equipment, including shipping, customs clearance, insurance, and freight documentation, in collaboration with SPC logistics, procurement, and finance teams.
- Ensure asset and logistics documentation is complete, current, and accessible to support audits, reporting, and effective handover between staff and teams.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

## Key selection criteria

**Qualifications**

- Degree in electronics, electrical engineering, marine science or technology, ocean instrumentation, or a closely related technical discipline or an equivalent body of knowledge and experience.
- Open Water Diving certification or equivalent occupational diving certification, and fitness to undertake work‑related diving activities.

**Technical expertise**

- Minimum 4-5 years’ progressive technical experience in marine, oceanographic, environmental monitoring, or related operational fieldwork.
- Demonstrated experience in the deployment, recovery, commissioning, testing, and validation of in situ observation systems, such as wave buoys, moorings, current meters (e.g. ADCPs), or multi‑sensor platforms.
- Practical experience maintaining and troubleshooting marine instrumentation, including sensors, telemetry, power systems, and associated electronics.
- Experience supporting or applying preventative and corrective maintenance practices, including record‑keeping and technical documentation.
- Understanding of marine field operations, including site selection, environmental conditions, operational risks, and safety requirements.
- Experience delivering hands‑on technical training or mentoring to adult learners or technical counterparts.
- Proven ability to work effectively with government agencies, technical services, and regional partners.

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communication skills (oral and written) with a working knowledge of French being an advantage.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

## Salary, terms and conditions

**Contract Duration** – **Until 30 June 2028** – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – The **Technical Officer – Ocean Observations** is a band 8 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of 2,146‒2,683 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 6,632–8,290 (USD 2,876–3,595; EUR 2,595–3,244). An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications.Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews. Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Suva –** SPC provides a housing allowance of FJD 1,500–5,200 per month. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy.

jobs.title: Chief of Party, Food for Peace (FFP)
jobs.description:
**Program: Food for Peace (FFP) Non-Emergency Multi-Year Programming**

**Openings: Two (2)**

**Location: Tegucigalpa, Honduras (1 position); Guatemala City, Guatemala (1 position)**

**Reports to: Global Communities Country Director**

**Please Note: This position(s) is contingent upon award and USDA approval with an anticipated start date of early 2027.**

***\*\*Please note that full professional proficiency in spoken and written English and Spanish is required for these roles\*\****

**Overview:**

*Global Communities champions innovative solutions to complex challenges at the intersection of humanitarian assistance, sustainable development, and financial inclusion. We ensure our approaches are as dynamic and diverse as the communities we serve. We bring together local ingenuity and global insights to save lives and secure strong futures.*

Global Communities is seeking a Chief of Party (COP) for an anticipated multi-year, USDA Food for Peace Non-Emergency project. Authorized under Title II of the Food for Peace Act, USDA’s multi-year Food for Peace Non-Emergency Programming will target people and places that experience recurrent food crises with a Graduation through Agriculture-led Development Approach and by utilizing U.S. agricultural commodities. This approach combines the Graduation model with targeted Market Systems Strengthening focused on agricultural value chains to build resilience, improve food security, and reduce dependence on emergency food assistance.

The COP will lead and oversee the overall implementation of the program, including setting vision and programmatic strategy and providing financial and operational leadership to attain targeted project deliverables and outcomes. The COP will manage a team of senior staff to ensure the quality, timeliness, and efficiency of all products and activities generated under the project. The COP will be responsible for communications with USDA, for publicly representing the project, and for liaising with Government entities and other institutions/stakeholders.

**Responsibilities:**

- Provide program leadership, direction, and supervision, including oversight of staff, consultants, and partners, monitoring and evaluation, and program implementation.
- Ensure implementation of technical interventions, resulting in concrete and on-time and on-target outcomes.
- Serve as primary point of contact for the project with USDA, government counterparts, and other critical in-country stakeholders.
- Lead regular work plan, budget, and implementation reviews to facilitate the cost-effective and timely achievement of deliverables.
- Manage team members, including highly specialized technical staff, to deliver against the annual workplan.
- Ensure project activities maximize impact and are completed in compliance with Global Communities policies, USDA rules and regulations, and local laws, and agreement requirements.
- Lead in adaptive management, achieving peak performance and innovation.
- Oversee timely and high-quality reporting to USDA, effectively and accurately communicating project progress, achievements, challenges, and utilization of funds.
- Ensure establishment and maintenance of systems for project operations.
- Build and maintain strong working relations with key internal and external stakeholders, beneficiaries, suppliers, and partners. Provide effective and timely responses to inquiries and concerns.
- Foster good working relationships with other agencies working on similar or complimentary projects, maximizing visibility and learning.
- Ensure that lessons learned are disseminated and applied.
- Liaise with Global Communities colleagues to coordinate the inputs of gender and inclusion, monitoring and evaluation and other advisory inputs to provide cross-cutting support.
- Collaborate with Global Communities colleagues and projects in-country to ensure effective coordination of Global Communities country operations.
- Undertake all other duties and projects as may be assigned from time to time.
- Frequent travel to project locations required

**Qualifications:**

- Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a discipline related to agriculture, agri-business, economics, international development or other relevant field with a minimum of 10 years of professional experience, including managing multi-sectoral projects with increasing responsibilities and duties; or,
- Bachelor’s degree in a discipline related to agriculture, agri-business, economics, international development, or other relevant field with a minimum of 12 years of professional experience, including managing multi-sectoral projects with increasing responsibilities and duties.
- At least 5 years’ experience as Chief of Party, senior management position, or equivalent, leading implementation of large international donor programs.
- Technical expertise in food security, nutrition, market systems development, value chain development, and/or graduation models.
- Experience working in emerging markets with experience in [USDA’s priority countries](https://www.fas.usda.gov/newsroom/stakeholder-notice-advancing-alignment-america-first-food-assistance-priority-countries) Guatemala and/or Honduras preferred. Experience in Latin America is highly preferred.
- High level of interpersonal, technical, and analytical skills, including a demonstrated ability to interact effectively and collaborate with a broad range of public and private sector counterparts and other key stakeholders.
- Demonstrated knowledge and application of non-emergency Food for Peace, agriculture-led development, resilience or similar programs preferred.
- Ability to develop effective working relationships with government officials, civil society organizations, private sector actors, implementing partners, international donors, and other stakeholders.
- Proven ability to communicate a common vision among diverse partners and the ability to lead multi-disciplinary teams is desired.
- Evidence of effective communication skills, both oral and written, to fulfill the diverse technical and managerial requirements of the agreement is desired.
- Languages: Full Professional Proficiency in spoken and written English and Spanish is required. Must be able to use both languages fluently and accurately and be able to read all styles and forms on all levels pertinent to professional needs.
- A passion for the mission and values of Global Communities.
- Local candidates are strongly encouraged to apply.

*Global Communities positively welcomes and seeks applications from all sections of society. We are committed to a work environment that respects the dignity and worth of everyone and offers equal opportunity. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment.*

*Global Communities holds strict safeguarding principles and has a zero-tolerance policy for conduct of sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment. In the process of recruitment, selection, and appointment, Global Communities will conduct robust reference and background screening checks, including international vetting as a signature of the Global Misconduct Disclosure Scheme to ensure children and vulnerable adults are safeguarded, and abuse is prevented. The incumbent is required to carry out their duties in accordance with Global Communities Safeguarding policy and the Standards of Conduct.*

jobs.title: Deputy Chief of Party II, Technical, Continuity of Integrated Health Services
jobs.description:
CRS is recruiting in anticipation of an award.

CRS is seeking candidates for an anticipated project which will be funded by the Department of State. The overall objective of the project is to deliver cost-effective, high-quality integrated malaria, maternal and child health, health systems strengthening, infectious disease preparedness and response programming, with a clear and time-bound plan to sustainably transition program activities to national and sub-national government and stakeholders.

**Job Summary**

The Deputy Chief of Party II will work as part of the leadership team for the anticipated Continuity of Integrated Health Services (CIHS) project, a multi-country initiative supporting Guinea, Liberia, Mali, and Togo. The Deputy Chief of Party II will provide strategic oversight and leadership for all project technical programming, ensuring the quality, integration, and effectiveness of interventions across malaria, maternal, newborn and child health (MNCH), health systems strengthening, infectious disease preparedness and response, and transition to country ownership.

The Deputy Chief of Party II will directly oversee the project's core team technical advisors and guide implementation of technical strategies aligned with the project's four objectives: (1) strengthening malaria and MNCH service delivery; (2) strengthening health information systems, laboratories, supply chains, and other health systems; (3) improving readiness to detect and respond to infectious disease threats; and (4) accelerating the transition to country-led health programs.

This position will ensure technical approaches are evidence-based, coordinated across countries, and aligned with host-country priorities and the America First Global Health Strategy. The Deputy Chief of Party II's management and technical knowledge will ensure the delivery of high-quality programming and achievement of project results. As a senior leader, the incumbent will proactively manage and mitigate technical risks and support a culture of learning, accountability, and continuous improvement.

**Roles and Key Responsibilities**

- Provide overall technical leadership for the development, implementation and consolidation of the CIHS project across malaria, MNCH, laboratory systems, disease surveillance, health information systems, supply chain strengthening, and other health systems strengthening interventions. Serve as the primary technical point of contact with the Department of State, as well as public, private and non-government stakeholders, when requested.
- Lead the development and execution of an integrated technical strategy that advances the project's objectives and ensures coordination across technical disciplines, countries, and consortium partners. Ensure technical activities achieve high-quality, timely results and are aligned with donor priorities, country needs, and global best practices. Work closely with programmatic and operational leaders to promote effective implementation and ensure CRS program quality standards, MEAL policies, and procedures are consistently applied.
- Effectively manage, supervise, mentor a multidisciplinary team of technical advisors. Foster collaboration across technical areas, manage team dynamics, and staff well-being. Strategically tailor individual development plans and complete performance assessments for direct reports.
- Contribute to the development of staffing plans and the recruitment process of senior technical staff.
- Manage and mitigate technical risks that may affect achievement of project objectives and milestones. Monitor evolving national health priorities, policy developments, and contextual factors that may affect implementation, and support risk mitigation strategies to maintain program quality and continuity. Ensure all staff understand and adhere to CRS staff safety, security, and safeguarding policies and plans.
- Promote, uphold and model responsible stewardship of agency and donor resources. Help ensure technical activities are implemented efficiently and in compliance with donor requirements, while collaborating with CIHS leadership team to support sound budget management, reporting, and accountability.
- Maintain relationships with key staff of consortium partner organizations in areas related to their respective scopes of work. Contribute to coordination of the roles and activities of staff from other consortium member organizations in implementation in line with CRS partnership principles.
- Foster a culture of learning and continuous improvement across the project. Create and maintain an environment that encourages collaborative problem-solving, the sharing of lessons learned, and adaptive management.
- Identify technical capacity gaps among CRS, partner, and government stakeholders and propose targeted training, mentoring, and technical assistance to strengthen institutional and/or technical capacity and advance country ownership.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

- Staff management experience and abilities that are conducive to a learning environment.
- Strong knowledge and experience in budget management.
- Experience in MS Office package (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Visio), Web Conferencing Applications, and information and budget management systems.
- Strong strategic, analytical, systems thinking, and problem-solving skills, with capacity to see the big picture and ability to make sound judgment and decisions.
- Strong relations management abilities. Ability to relate to people at all levels internally and externally, especially with donors and government counterparts. Strategic in how you approach each relationship.
- Team leadership abilities with diverse and multi-disciplinary teams.
- Proactive, resourceful, solutions-oriented and results-oriented.

**Required Languages:** English required, additional proficiency in French preferred

**Travel:** Must be willing and able to travel up to 30%.

**Supervisory Responsibilities:** Yes

**Basic Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in international development, International Relations or a relevant technical area.
- Minimum 5 years’ relevant management and technical experience.
- Minimum 2 years’ experience managing donor funds, including multi-country grants.
- Recognized technical experience and qualifications in sector as demonstrated by peer reviewed publications, conference presentations etc.
- Experience coaching and mentoring project staff.
- Demonstrated experience of successful management, including management of functions of complex, high-value, multi-activity projects and logistics.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Master’s Degree.
- Experience engaging partners and strengthening partnerships. Knowledge of CRS partnership strategy.

**Agency Competencies (for all CRS Staff):**

- **Personal Accountability** – Consistently takes responsibility for one’s own actions.
- **Acts with Integrity** - Consistently models values aligned with CRS Guiding Principles and mission. Is considered honest.
- **Builds and Maintains Trust** - Shows consistency between words and actions.
- **Collaborates with Others** – Works effectively in intercultural and diverse teams.
- **Open to Learn** – Seeks out experiences that may change perspective or provide an opportunity to learn new things.

**Agency Leadership Competencies:**

- **Lead Change** – Continually looks for ways to improve the agency through a culture of agility, openness, and innovation.
- **Develops and Recognizes Others** – Builds the capacity of staff to reach their full potential and enhance team and agency performance.
- **Strategic Mindset** – Understands role in translating, communicating, and implementing agency strategy and team priorities.

- Very strong written and oral communication skills
- Very strong presentation, facilitation, training, mentoring, and coaching skills

**PURPOSE OF THE ROLE**

The Project Officer will lead day-to-day implementation of ICS SP’s child-centred family strengthening, care reform, early childhood development (ECD) and child protection activities in Kisumu or Kakamega County. The role will help families provide safe and nurturing care, prevent unnecessary child–family separation, support safe reintegration and family-based alternatives, and strengthen community protection and referral systems. Working with government services, caregivers and community structures, the Officer will ensure quality field delivery, frontline capacity strengthening, learning and accountability in line with ICS SP policies and project commitments.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Project planning, delivery and community coordination**

- Coordinate ICS SP activities at county and community levels, translating approved project plans into practical schedules, responsibilities and deliverables.
- Prepare activity plans and budgets, track expenditure and outputs, and flag implementation delays or emerging risks for timely corrective action.
- Organize community dialogues, training, field visits and review meetings, ensuring that participants and local actors are meaningfully involved.
- Guide and support community facilitators and frontline personnel through joint planning, supervision, coaching, and regular follow-up.

**2. Family strengthening and care reform**

- Lead community-level family strengthening and positive parenting activities that address the factors driving unnecessary child–family separation.
- Work with authorized Children Services personnel to support family tracing, reunification, reintegration planning and safe follow-up, in accordance with government case-management procedures.
- Link vulnerable children and caregivers to available psychosocial, social protection, livelihood, health and other services that help families remain safe and stable.
- Support government-led transition from residential care and appropriate kinship, foster and other family-based care pathways; statutory placement and certification decisions remain with authorized authorities.

**3. Nurturing care, ECD and child protection**

- Connect parenting and family support with early learning, responsive caregiving, health, nutrition and protection services for young children.
- Strengthen the capacity of caregivers, community child protection volunteers, community health promoters, and other local actors to identify risks and promote nurturing care.
- Promote inclusive access to services for children with disabilities and other vulnerable children and maintain effective referral connections between community and county systems.
- Support safe identification, reporting and referral of violence, neglect, exploitation and other child protection concerns using approved safeguarding and referral procedures.

**4. Evidence, accountability and programme learning**

- Work with the MEAL team to track agreed indicators, validate activity records, gather participant feedback, and use findings to improve delivery.
- Prepare accurate field updates, reports, outcome stories and lessons learned; handle child and household information confidentially and in line with data protection protocols.
- Apply ICS SP safeguarding, child protection and PSEA standards in all activities, and promptly escalate concerns through authorized channels.

**5. Local partnerships and systems strengthening**

- Build strong working relationships with county and sub-county Children Services, health and ECDE teams, community structures, civil society, care institutions and faith/community leaders.
- Contribute to county coordination forums and technical working groups, supporting government ownership and continuity of family- and community-based care.
- Support local partners and frontline actors through joint planning, practical mentoring, referrals, and follow-up on agreed actions.
- Carry out other relevant project duties assigned by the supervisor in line with the responsibilities of the position.

**REQUISITE REQUIREMENTS**

- Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Child Protection, Early Childhood Development, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Public Health or related discipline.
- At least five years of relevant experience in NGO or community-based programming, preferably in child protection, care reform, family strengthening, parenting or integrated ECD.
- Sound understanding of Kenya’s child protection and alternative care systems, family-based care, safeguarding, case management and referral pathways.
- Practical experience working with children, caregivers, frontline workers and government structures to deliver parenting, nurturing care or family strengthening interventions.
- Ability to manage activity plans and budgets, coordinate field implementation, monitor results, and meet organizational and donor reporting requirements.
- Strong community facilitation, partnership management and communication skills, including working respectfully with county government and local service providers.
- Good judgement in sensitive child protection matters, commitment to confidentiality and inclusion, and ability to apply safeguarding procedures consistently.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office; strong written and spoken English and Kiswahili. Knowledge of relevant local languages and ability to travel regularly within project areas are added advantages.

Protecting children, vulnerable communities and our staff is ICS SP’s absolute priority. We have zero tolerance for violence, abuse, and exploitation of children and other people in the communities we serve. Successful candidates must sign and adhere to our safeguarding, child protection and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) code of conduct and policies.

jobs.title: Local Development and Governance Consultant
jobs.description:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Organization:** UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- **VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/206**
- **Position Title**: Local Development and Governance Consultant
- **Duty Station:** UNDP South Area Office (Tyre) with regular field visits to the project sites and with visits to UNDP Country Office in Beirut when and if needed.
- **Duration:** 12 months (without exceeding 18 working days per month)
- **Vacancy Date of Issue: 26 October 2026**
- **Vacancy Closure Date: 02 November 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/16RhrmelwTxxjKSJhV8Hh7Yx7iRKYL-rw/view?usp=sharing](https://drive.google.com/file/d/16RhrmelwTxxjKSJhV8Hh7Yx7iRKYL-rw/view?usp=sharing)

**BACKGROUND**

Lebanon continues to confront an unprecedented financial and economic crisis, exacerbated by a long history of violence, volatility, and social inequality. This crisis has deeply undermined the subsistence capacity of already vulnerable populations. The country remains home to the largest numbers of refugees per capita in the world, with approximately 1.5 million displaced Syrians, 31,400 Palestine refugees from Syria, 35,000 Lebanese returnees, and a pre-existing population of 174,422 Palestine refugees residing in 12 official refugee camps and 156 gatherings. Moreover, the geopolitical environment continues to deteriorate, which poses risks for new displacement waves. This multi-layered crisis has had devastating impacts on Lebanon’s social, economic, and environmental capital, and increasingly threatens the country's social cohesion and stability.

Communities hosting large numbers of displaced populations face compounded challenges due to inadequate institutional capacities, dwindling resources, and a lack of effective collective approaches to managing the crisis. These communities are grappling with the consequences of the Syrian displacement crisis, which has been further exacerbated since 2019 by a severe economic, fiscal, and governance meltdown. Additionally, the increasing pressures from climate change have intensified these vulnerabilities. This state-of-affairs weakens the ability of local communities to cope with the immediate impacts of the crisis, such as service breakdowns, rising poverty, and growing tensions between and within communities. These challenges, in turn, limit their capacity to pursue a sustainable development path, particularly as durable solutions to the displacement crisis remain elusive.

In South Lebanon, these challenges have been further compounded by the impact of recurrent conflict and the escalation of hostilities since 2023, which have caused extensive damage to infrastructure, disrupted livelihoods, displaced populations, and placed additional pressure on already overstretched local services and municipal resources. Despite ongoing returns, many communities continue to face significant recovery needs, including the rehabilitation of basic services, restoration of local economic activities, and support to social cohesion. These pressures underscore the need to strengthen local institutional capacities, enhance coordination among local authorities and development and humanitarian actors, and promote integrated, conflict-sensitive approaches that address both immediate needs and longer-term recovery and resilience.

In response to these challenges, the Lebanon Host Community Support Project – Phase 2 (LHSP 2.0) builds upon the lessons learned from the original LHSP project, which has been implemented since 2014. LHSP 2.0 seeks to anchor stabilization activities within a more integrated local development framework. It focuses on working at the area-based level within clusters and unions, with a strong emphasis on strengthening municipal capacities to enhance the sustainability and impact of stabilization efforts.

At the local level, LHSP 2.0 aims to bolster the coping and sustainable development capacities of host communities. Its key objectives are to create a more enabling environment for mitigating and preventing tensions by:

- Reducing competition over public services, livelihood, and economic opportunities: This is achieved by supporting the maintenance and expansion of service delivery and creating economic opportunities, especially in the context of the significant incapacitation of both public and private sectors.
- Providing conflict-sensitive and inclusive dialogue and decision-making spaces: These spaces allow local communities to engage in peaceful discussions, identify common interests, and collaboratively chart a path towards a sustainable future.

The Local Development for Stabilization (LDP) project aims to enhance local governance and development systems in Lebanon, strengthening their capacity to effectively respond to the challenges posed by Lebanon’s multi-layered crisis. Since 2019, Lebanon has faced unprecedented challenges, including a severe economic collapse, political instability, compounded by the protracted presence of Syrian refugees and other displaced populations. Moreover, Lebanon experienced in the South, unprecedented destruction during the 2024 conflict especially in the South of Lebanon, resulting in the temporary displacement of over one million people.

The absence of central government capacity and the depletion of local resources have left municipalities and local authorities struggling to provide basic services and maintain social stability.

This project addresses these challenges by supporting municipalities and local development actors in enhancing service delivery, promoting resilience, and rebuilding social capital. It aligns with the UNDP Lebanon Country Programme priorities, aiming to foster stabilization, inclusive economic development, and social peace through area-based, integrated local development approaches. The project will focus on:

- Strengthening local governance institutions and capacities to cope with crises and foster long-term development.
- Supporting the creation of decent livelihood opportunities, particularly for vulnerable groups such as women, youth, and displaced populations.
- Promoting access to sustainable and climate-resilient public services, including water, waste management, and energy.
- Enhancing financing mechanisms for municipalities, and empowering local stakeholders through a combination of technical, policy, and financial support.

By leveraging the existing capacities of municipalities, local actors, and UNDP’s portfolio of interventions, the LDP project will foster collaborative, bottom-up solutions that are gender-sensitive and responsive to the urgent needs of communities across Lebanon.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the overall guidance of Project Specialist and day to day management of the relevant Area Manager and close coordination with the LED and Livelihood Specialist, the Local Development and Governance Consultant will be responsible for supporting the assessments, planning, implementation, and monitoring of activities under the LHSP and LDP. The Consultant will ensure proper implementation of livelihood projects under the LHSP and will play a key role in facilitating local coordination among stakeholders in their respective areas, including but not limited to municipalities, unions of municipalities, Social Development Centers (SDCs), Civil Defense units, relevant ministries regional offices and community stakeholders to strengthen participatory local governance and enhance preparedness and service delivery capacities at the local level. To ensure proper implementation of the projects the Local Development and Governance Consultant will perform the following functions related to LHSP and LDP projects:

**Local Development Assessment, Participatory Planning and Coordination:**

- Support the identification and prioritization of community-based interventions based on assessed needs, socio-economic indicators, local development priorities, and available resources.
- Identify opportunities for local economic development, employment generation, livelihood recovery, entrepreneurship, and support to micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs).
- Assess the linkages between local economic activities, productive sectors, value chains, and employment opportunities to inform the design of sustainable interventions.
- Contribute to the drafting of local plans, concept notes, and technical briefs that feed into regional and national coordination mechanisms.
- Contribute to the formulation of integrated interventions that combine basic service recovery with livelihood support, local economic revitalization, and institutional capacity development.
- Ensure that proposed interventions respond to the specific needs and capacities of targeted communities and are aligned with relevant local development plans and national priorities.
- Report to the Area Managers any observations or challenges that may arise during the different phases of the project cycle.
- Coordinate and maintain regular communication with municipalities, unions of municipalities, SDCs, Civil Defense, local committees, relevant ministries regional offices, economic actors (such as private sector, farmers, MSMEs representatives) and community representatives to ensure inclusive and participatory engagement in the local development process.
- Support in the creation of the Local Development Committees that will be created for the LDP project in each respective area and focus zone.
- Coordinate and maintain regular communication with the firm responsible for establishing the area observatories in the targeted focus zones related to LDP project. Support and contribute to community-based assessments and support the identification of local priorities in alignment with the Local Development Plans.
- Facilitate participatory workshops and consultations under the Local Development Platforms (where applicable) to validate findings and support the formulation of local action plans.
- Ensure that all planned interventions are consistent with national frameworks (e.g., MoIM, MoSA, MoA, etc.) and compliant with donor and UNDP requirements (legal, environmental, social, and financial).
- Coordinate with other LDP consultants and area teams to ensure synergies between local governance, livelihoods, and interventions across focus zones.

**Implementation and Coordination**

- Facilitate coordination among local actors during implementation to ensure effective delivery, including local development planning, service improvement, and crisis preparedness.
- Provide ongoing technical support to municipalities, Union of municipalities, SDCs, and Civil Defense to operationalize their local action plans and enhance institutional performance.
- Participate in project monitoring and site visits, ensuring that implementation aligns with quality, inclusiveness, and sustainability standards.
- Support capacity-building activities for local institutions, ensuring the inclusion of women, youth, and vulnerable groups in planning and implementation processes.
- Contribute to the development of knowledge products, case studies, and documentation of good practices emerging from the field.
- Ensure effective follow-up and monitoring of livelihood-related interventions, in close coordination with the LED and Livelihood Specialist and the Area manager.
- Maintain close collaboration with Area Manager, engineers, and the central LHSP/LDP team to ensure consistent quality assurance and alignment across regions.

**Monitoring, Reporting, and Follow-up**

- Support data collection, reporting, and evaluation of local development and governance interventions in coordination with the M&E and reporting teams.
- Document lessons learned, success stories, and challenges to inform adaptive management and future planning.
- Contribute to the preparation of progress reports, communication materials, and visibility products that highlight achievements at the local level.
- Ensure proper archiving and documentation of project-related files, minutes, correspondence, and reports for institutional record-keeping.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The Consultant is expected to submit a monthly progress report undertaking the above tasks and activities under the TOR within 12 months (without exceeding 18 working days per month).

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- With day-to-day management, the Local Development and Governance Consultant will coordinate with the respective Area Manager and the LED and Livelihood Specialist under the overall guidance of Project Specialist.
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.
- Day to Day transportation from home to office (& vice versa) shall be covered by the Consultant’s own means. The Local Development and Governance Consultant will rely on his own means of communication and transportation within and to the South area.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 12 months.

The mission is expected to commence by November 2026.

The time needed to review/comment/approve deliverables and outputs is (5) five working days.

**DUTY STATION**

Local Development and Governance Consultant will be based in their respective Duty Station in UNDP South Area Office (Tyre) with regular field visits to the project sites and with visits to UNDP Country Office in Beirut when and if needed.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** Minimum Bachelor’s degree in local governance, development studies, public administration, economics, or related fields.
- **Experience:** Minimum of Eight (8) years’ experience in local development planning, community engagement, or area-based programming.
- **Language:** Fluency in English and Arabic (both oral and written).

**“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.**

jobs.title: Administrative coordinator (F/M) - Ukraine
jobs.description:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?
For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

**MdM in Ukraine**

MdM International Network has been operating in Ukraine since 2014, improving access to health care, especially providing comprehensive Primary Health Care (PHC), Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) and Mental Health and Psychosocial support (MHPSS) services.

Since February 2022, MdM Spain is leading the country response for the network, while MdM-France is in charge of the operations in Southern Ukraine. The global strategy aims at ensuring the access to quality comprehensive healthcare services for the conflict-affected population in Ukraine.

In Southern Ukraine, MdM-France has set up its country office and a base office in Mykolaiv. An office in Odesa is still running for specific activities monitoring in Odesa. The program consists in supporting various local-based organizations in the delivery of health services for people facing severe constraints to healthcare in Mykolaev and Kherson Oblasts.

The main strategic objectives for the Adminisrative department are, to consolidate the operational process at mission level to strengthen the quality of support services, to transfer competencies to national staff as well as working closer with national partners to build capacities.

Living conditions in Mykolaiv are pleasant (access to restaurants, presence of other organizations, places to relax...).

Expats share modern, well-equiped guesthouse. However, there are strict security rules (curfew imposed by the authorities) and a volatile environment (regular activation of air alerts).

**About the role**

As Administrative Coordinator, you ensure completeness, correctness, timeliness and integrity in your role. As a strategic partner to the operations, you will contribute to the definition and implementation of the mission’s objectives, participate in the sizing of the HR and financial needs and provide technical support to operational staff on the HR and Financial management of the mission.

**What you’ll do**

More specifically, your main responsibilities are the following:

- Supervise the implementation of the mission’s HR set-up
- Define, adapt, plan, and supervise the implementation of the mission’s human resources frameworks, procedures and policies while respecting the local context, local legislation and MdM policies and values (compensations and benefits, recruitment good practices, performance reviews, staff safe guarding, talent management, staff disciplines, career development and learning or team building)
- Plan, centralize, coordinate, and supervise the financial management and administration of the mission (accounting, budget construction and follow-up, internal and external reporting, donor compliance, audits, administrative legal obligations, etc.)
- Follow up the evolution of the legal environment and ensure MdM remains in line with official guidelines and policies in the framework of its principled approach
- Recruit, train, and manage an administrative department team
- Provide technical support to operational staff on the HR and financial management of the mission
- In terms of coordination and representation, you will ensure, when needed and by delegation of the General Coordinator, the representation of MdM in front of donors and liaise with INGOs heads of Admin Departments in-country
- You will provide strong oversight to MDM local Partner activities, including compliance with donor regulations

**Who you’ll work with**

Under the supervision of the General Coordinator (F/M), you will manage the HR and Finance team in the coordination office and functionally support the HR and Finance team in the operational base(s). You will closely interact with the HR and Finance Advisors based in the HQ and the other departments at mission level (logistics, programs etc.)

## REQUIREMENTS

**You are the right match if you:**

- hold a 3 years’ higher education management qualification
- have at least 4 years of experience in administration (HR and Finance) in a humanitarian context (including at least two years’ experience in an international NGO at coordination level)
- have an experience in a conflict setting or challenging environment. like in Ukraine (strong asset)
- have previous experience with MdM (preferred)
- proved your ability to negotiate and build / consolidate a network with authorities in a complex and volatile legal environment
- have a previous successful experience in team management (preferred)
- have a significant experience in PSEA management (an advantage)
- have a solid experience in budget management backed by institutional donors, payroll and accounting in a humanitarian context (prerequisite)
- you proved you are able to understand and interpret the legal administrative framework for staff and the MdM rules
- you have excellent Microsoft Office skills (especially Excel) and knowledge of accountancy software (like Saga or any relevant ERP)
- are fluent in English (mandatory, C1 level minimum), and have some knowledge of Ukrainian and/or Russian (would be an asset

**This role may not suit you if:**

- you are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach
- you are not able to defend the Administrative point of you in front of other actors/leaders
- you are not diplomatic and assertive

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow during the month of November.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

## EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3'392 €
- Fixed-term contract (6 months), starting in beginning of December
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Mykolaiv
- Regular field visits

**Benefits**:

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse managed by the mission
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

**Essentials**:

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.
if you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

jobs.title: Integrante de Equipo de Acción Contra Minas
jobs.description:
El Consejo Danés para Refugiados (DRC por sus siglas en inglés) es una de las principales ONG humanitarias del mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para proporcionar asistencia adecuada con un enfoque basado en derechos para los refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, los desplazados internos, repatriados y migrantes. DRC ha estado presente en Colombia desde 2011, pero 2018 amplía sus operaciones en respuesta a la crisis venezolana. Actualmente DRC Colombia implementa una respuesta humanitaria centrada protección para refugiados y migrantes venezolanos y colombianos retornados en ciudades de Colombia como Riohacha, Barranquilla y Bogotá, actualmente también incorpora actividades en Nariño y en Norte de Santander.

**Objetivo del cargo:**

Ejecutar de manera segura, eficiente y conforme a los Procedimientos Operativos Normales (PON), las Normas Nacionales de Acción Contra Minas y los estándares internacionales aplicables, las actividades operacionales, técnicas y comunitarias requeridas para la implementación de los procesos de liberación de tierras. Bajo la supervisión directa de los responsables operacionales, contribuir al cumplimiento de los objetivos del programa mediante la ejecución de tareas de despeje, estudios no técnicos y enlace comunitario.

Como **Desminador**, realizar operaciones de despeje de forma sistemática, controlada y segura en Áreas Peligrosas Sospechosas (APS) y Áreas Peligrosas Confirmadas (APC), aplicando los procedimientos establecidos para la detección, localización, excavación, recuperación, señalización y apoyo en la destrucción de minas antipersonal, municiones sin explosionar (MUSE) y otros artefactos explosivos, con el fin de garantizar la liberación segura de tierras de acuerdo con los criterios técnicos definidos.

Como **Auxiliar de Estudio No Técnico (ENT)**, apoyar la planificación y ejecución de las actividades de recolección, verificación, análisis y registro de información relacionada con la contaminación por artefactos explosivos, incluyendo la elaboración de actas, diligenciamiento de formatos, levantamiento de información geográfica, georreferenciación, mapeo de áreas peligrosas, gestión documental y mantenimiento de las comunicaciones operacionales, contribuyendo a la toma de decisiones y a la delimitación adecuada de las áreas de intervención.

Como **Enlace Comunitario**, facilitar la comunicación y coordinación entre la organización y las comunidades beneficiarias durante todas las fases del proceso de liberación de tierras, promoviendo la participación comunitaria, la construcción de confianza y el intercambio de información relevante. Asimismo, desarrollar actividades de Educación en el Riesgo de Minas (ERM), orientadas a fomentar comportamientos seguros frente a la amenaza de minas antipersonal, municiones sin explosionar y otros artefactos explosivos, garantizando en todo momento el respeto de los principios de humanidad, neutralidad, imparcialidad e independencia.

**RESPONSABILIDADES:**

**Responsabilidades Desminador:**

- Hacer el mantenimiento, calibración y manejo del detector asignado según el manual del fabricante.
- Garantizar que todas las señales de material metálico han sido investigadas y eliminadas, descartando o confirmando una amenaza, en el carril que le haya sido asignado, señalando el límite de área Reducida/Despejada de acuerdo con el sistema de marcación.
- Seguir las instrucciones del jefe de Equipo para iniciar el Despeje/Reducción del carril.
- Reducir/Despejar el carril asignado siguiendo estrictamente los POA de DRC-ACM y loa EN-AICMA.
- Ante la localización de cualquier objeto sospechoso o componente de MAP/AEI/MSE, debe detenerse, avisar al jefe de Equipo y desde una distancia segura indicarle el indicio a este. En caso de ser confirmado, debe marcar y cerrar el carril.
- Informará al jefe de Equipo el avance de un carril y retornar hasta la Línea Base, retomando la labor en una nueva senda según se le indique.
- Mantener y conservar en buen estado y limpio el equipo asignado.
- Solicitar al jefe de Equipo los elementos que sean necesarios para su labor.
- Cumplir en todo momento las órdenes que indique el jefe de Equipo en el desarrollo de trabajos de ET/D y/o el mantenimiento de las áreas administrativas o alojamiento.
- Responsable de su propia seguridad y autocuidado.

**Responsabilidades Auxiliar de ENT:**

- Estudio y análisis de la información disponible (Expediente Municipal, eventos IMSMA, etc).
- Asistir al jefe de Equipo en la planeación de las tareas de recolección de información en campo.
- Recolectar la información disponible mediante un análisis detallado de la evidencia existente con todas las fuentes de información útil, que refiera de la sospecha o presencia de Artefactos Explosivos, en las zonas asignadas.
- Asistir al jefe de Equipo en el análisis y diagnóstico de las áreas/sectores estudiados, que permita concluir el estado de contaminación o sin contaminación.
- Asistir al jefe de equipo en la marcación de las Áreas Peligrosas o Áreas Peligrosas Confirmadas por medio de la recolección, análisis de información y evidencias.
- Asistir al jefe de equipo en un primer reconocimiento visual de los Artefactos Explosivos localizados en las zonas de investigación.
- Recolectar información relevante para el diligenciamiento de documentos normativos de interés para la organización y sus diferentes programas.
- Asistir al jefe de equipo en la definición de los niveles de priorización de intervención.
- Facilitar el desarrollo de las actividades de DRC-ACM, mediante el correspondiente Enlace Comunitario.
- Seguir los procedimientos operacionales desarrollados por la organización y aprobados por la Autoridad Nacional.
- Apoyar según requerimiento por la gerencia de DRC-ACM, a otros componentes del proceso de liberación de tierras.
- Estar dispuesto a ser traslado de lugar de trabajo conforme a la necesidad de la organización.

**Responsabilidades Enlace Comunitario:**

- Presentar formalmente DRC -ACM, ante las autoridades locales y comunitarias.
- Presentar los objetivos de la presencia de DRC-ACM en las áreas de intervención.
- Incentivar la participación de las autoridades locales y comunitarias en el proceso de ejecución de las tareas de ET/D.
- Obtener información relevante acerca de la comunidad (por ejemplo, el tamaño de la población y sus movimientos, principal medio de subsistencia o fuentes de ingreso principal y cuestiones socioeconómicas).
- Obtener la información sobre el problema de los Artefactos Explosivos en una comunidad específica (historia y dinámica del conflicto / Tipo de Bloqueo / Proyectos de Desarrollo / Priorización, etc.).
- Identificar los grupos de riesgo específicos en la comunidad y entender la toma de riesgos, alcance y los motivos subyacentes para la contaminación por MAP/AEI/MSE.
- Proporcionar información sobre la ubicación y el tipo de Artefacto Explosivo requeridos para el ET/D y la marcación.
- Proporcionar información a la comunidad afectada sobre el ET/D.
- Asegurarse de que los representantes de la comunidad y/o usuarios de la tierra sean consultados y participen en el proceso desde su planeación hasta su finalización.
- Apoyar el desarrollo de la comunidad basado en la participación que implique el fortalecimiento del capital social.
- Informar sobre el sistema de marcación y señalización de las AP/APC, coordinando con la comunidad la existencia de alguna señal que se requiera añadir o quitar por un motivo justificado, buscando la aceptación de las señales oficiales dispuestas AICMA.
- Informar a la comunidad la importancia de la marcación de un área, enfatizando que no se debe quitar ninguna marca o ingresar al área, mientras el trabajo esté en curso y hasta que haya sido entregado por las autoridades.

**Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo**

- Procurar el cuidado integral de su salud.
- Participar activamente en la conformación del COPASST – Comité de Convivencia Laboral –Brigadas de emergencia, así como las actividades que los mismos realicen.
- Cumplir con las normas reglamentos e instrucciones del SG SST.
- Informar oportunamente de los peligros y riesgos latentes con su sitio de trabajo.
- Asistir a las capacitaciones en SST definidas por el programa de capacitación del SG-SST.
- Velar por el mantenimiento del orden y aseo de su puesto y área de trabajo.
- Suministrar información clara, veraz y completa sobre su estado de salud.
- Reportar inmediatamente al área de SST y su jefe inmediato los accidentes de trabajo que se presenten, incidentes (casi Accidentes) y enfermedades diagnosticadas como laborales.
- Reportar al jefe inmediato la necesidad de tomar acciones correctivas o preventivas, que correspondan ante no conformidades reales o potenciales del proceso al cual pertenece.
- Participar en las actividades de capacitación, simulacros y las que sean programadas desde seguridad y salud en el trabajo
- Participar y contribuir con el cumplimiento de la política y los objetivos del SG-SST.

**Soporte médico, Mando y Control:**

- Mantener actualizados las competencias de primeros auxilios y MEDEVAC que la organización le instruya.
- Conocer al detalle los Planes MEDEVAC en su sitio de trabajo, base, campamentos y/o en ruta.
- Asistir al jefe de Equipo o cualquier que sea responsable en cada momento en la ejecución del MEDEVAC en caso de accidente.

**Logística y recursos:**

- Asegurarse que los equipos y medios puestos a su disposición son empleados de manera correcta, manteniéndolos en perfecto estado
- de operatividad (limpieza y cuidado).
- Reportar inmediatamente al jefe de Equipo todos los daños y/o pérdida de materiales/equipos.
- En caso de tener un vehículo asignado, deberá cumplir con las leyes del tránsito, cuidado y mantenimiento del vehículo y cualquier otra norma que vele por el cuidado del vehículo.
- Apoyar en las actividades diarias de mantenimiento de las áreas habitadas por DRC, campamento, áreas de desminado y otras relacionadas con la organización.

**Responsabilidades transversales:**

- Asistir a capacitaciones especiales según se le requiera.
- Aplicar los principios humanitarios y de DRC en el ejercicio de sus funciones.
- Estar dispuesto a realizar otras labores, en que DRC-ACM lo capacite, para el mejor cumplimiento de los objetivos e indicadores del programa, por ejemplo, de conductor de Vehículo.
- Dar cumplimiento al código de conducta de la organización.
- Cumplir con el reglamento interno de trabajo, las normas locales de seguridad y toda disposición de personal y material.

**Se espera que todo el personal de DRC asuma las siguientes tareas generales:**

- Trabajar en el marco de los valores y estándares fundamentales de DRC.
- Estar familiarizado y adherirse a todas las políticas y procedimientos de DRC.

**Experiencias y competencias técnicas:**

- Haber trabajado por turnos extensos en campamentos y conocimiento del medio rural
- Habilidades en herramientas de uso en el campo
- Buen estado físico para trabajo de alta exigencia.
- Capacidad para manejar información sensible y confidencial.

**Educación** (Incluir certificados, licencias)

- Bachiller completo o Técnico o Tecnólogo en alguna área del conocimiento.

**Deseable:**

- Bachiller completo o Técnico o Tecnólogo en alguna área del conocimiento.
- Tener habilidades básicas en uso de herramientas tecnológicas
- Un (1) año de experiencia en trabajo con las comunidades
- Habilidad demostrable en comunicación y socialización de contenidos, para lograr interactuar con la comunidad y autoridades nacionales y locales.
- Manejo de computadores y adquisición de datos.

**Idiomas:**

- Dominio básico de Ingles. (deseable).

**Todas las funciones de DRC requieren que el titular domine las competencias básicas de DRC:**

• Lograr la excelencia: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes

• Colaboración: involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación

• Tomar la iniciativa: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación

• Comunicar: escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad

• Demostración de integridad: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC

**Ofrecemos:**

- Salario: iniciando en $ 1.979.000 según experiencia y competencias del candidato
- Tipo de contrato: Obra Labor
- Horario: Ciclos operativos de seis semanas de trabajo de lunes a sábados de 8:00 a 4:00 p.m., al final del ciclo operativo se disfruta de 2 semanas de descanso (esta información se ampliará en el proceso de entrevistas).
- Fecha de inicio: noviembre 2026
- Medicina Prepagada: al 100% para el trabajador.
- Alimentación: Servicio de alimentación en base.
- Alojamiento: Alojamiento compartido en base
- Lugar de trabajo: Oficina principal Nariño donde inician y finalizan los ciclos operacionales, con disponibilidad de traslado por necesidad programática a los municipios del triángulo del telembi.

**Proceso de solicitud**

Todos los solicitantes deben subir únicamente una carta de presentación (1 página) y una hoja de vida

actualizada (que no supere las 3 páginas) no se reciben más soportes por este medio.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes:** 01 de noviembre de 2026 a las 11:59 am Hora Local.

***Nota: Esta vacante está sujeta a subordinación de fondos por parte del donante.***

**Nota 1:** El postulante que aplique a esta convocatoria autoriza a DRC a validar la información personal suministrada en la hoja de vida. Su identificación será comprobada en las bases de datos públicas y privadas con el uso exclusivo de convalidar la información, de acuerdo con nuestras políticas antifraude, lavado de activos y financiación del terrorismo.

**Nota 2:** El/la postulante que de forma libre y voluntaria deseen hacer parte del proceso de selección para ocupar la posición de la presente convocatoria, deberán observar un estricto apego a las normas que apliquen para la materia (idoneidad en los títulos presentados, ejecución de pruebas de forma personal e individual y veracidad en la información) adhiriéndose a los manuales y Políticas anti fraude de DRC, so pena de declarar descalificado el postulante que incurra en cualquier irregularidad a juicio de la organización, aún por la mera sospecha, e incluso en posibles conductas de tipo penal conforme la legislación colombiana.

**Nota 3:**

¡Queremos que hagas parte de nuestro equipo!

En DRC creemos que la diversidad nos fortalece y que cada persona aporta talentos, experiencias y perspectivas valiosas. Promovemos un entorno de trabajo inclusivo donde todas las personas sean bienvenidas y valoradas por su talento, experiencia y potencial.

Invitamos a postularse a todas las personas que cumplan con el perfil del cargo, sin distinción de género, identidad o expresión de género, orientación sexual, edad, origen étnico o nacional, creencias, condición socioeconómica o cualquier otra característica que contribuya a la diversidad de nuestro equipo.
