jobs.title: WASH Specialist - Mozambique
jobs.description:
**Position Title - WASH Specialist**

**Duty Station - Pemba with travel to districts**

**Reports To - Programme Coordinator**

**Contract Type - Service Provider Consultancy Contract (approx one year)**

**Closing date of applications - 2 November 2026**

The WASH Specialist leads the planning, design, implementation, monitoring and quality assurance of all Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) activities in Mozambique - in both communities and health facilities - ensuring that objectives are achieved on time and in line with technical standards and donor requirements.

Reporting to the Programme Coordinator, the WASH Specialist provides technical and leadership on WASH infrastructure, from design and technical specifications through to construction supervision and operation and maintenance, as well as on hygiene promotion and infection prevention and control.

The WASH Specialist works closely with local authorities, health institutions, communities, partners and contractors to improve access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene, and ensures WASH activities are well integrated with the other programme components.

**Requirements for the role:**

- Degree in Civil Engineering, Water/Environmental Engineering, Public Health or a related field.
- Proven technical expertise in WASH infrastructure design and supervision, including water supply systems, sanitation facilities, drainage, and healthcare waste management.
- Demonstrated experience in WASH within Health Facilities and Infection Prevention and Control (IPC), as well as community-level WASH and hygiene promotion activities.
- Strong experience in construction supervision and contractor management, including technical specifications, Bills of Quantities (BoQs), site inspections, and ESHS (Environmental, Social, Health, and Safety) compliance.
- Familiarity with emergency WASH interventions, climate-resilient designs, and inclusive/accessible infrastructure (gender and disability sensitivity).
- Proven track record in M&E, budget management, procurement coordination, and donor reporting within international NGO environments.
- Excellent representation and coordination skills for active engagement with the WASH Cluster, government health/water authorities, and local partners.
- Experience working in conflict or emergency settings (Experience in Mozambique, particularly Cabo Delgado, is a strong advantage).
- Fluent in Portuguese and English (both written and spoken, essential).

**The main responsibilities of this post include the following:**

**1. Technical Coordination and Programme Management**

- Lead the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all WASH activities.
- Develop annual, quarterly and monthly WASH work plans to ensure programme targets and objectives are achieved.
- Ensure compliance with MENTOR policies, donor requirements, technical standards and national regulations.
- Conduct assessments, technical surveys and programme reviews to identify needs and improve programme quality.
- Support the development of proposals, budgets and donor reports.
- Ensure integration of WASH activities with other programme components where appropriate.

**2. Infrastructure Design and Construction Supervision**

- Prepare designs for water supply systems, sanitation facilities, handwashing stations and waste management infrastructure.
- Ensure designs are climate-resilient, accessible and inclusive (gender, disability).
- Draft technical specifications and bills of quantities; support bid evaluation and contractor mobilisation.
- Conduct regular site inspections, verify the progress and quality of works, manage variation orders and follow up on defect rectification.
- Monitor contractor compliance with Environmental, Social, Health and Safety (ESHS) requirements.

**3. Community WASH Activities**

**Safe Water Supply**

- Oversee activities to improve access to safe and adequate water in targeted communities.
- Supervise the rehabilitation, installation, operation and maintenance of water supply systems.
- Ensure regular water quality monitoring and the implementation of water safety measures.
- Coordinate emergency water supply interventions when required.
- Promote sustainable community management of water infrastructure.

**Sanitation**

- Supervise the rehabilitation, construction and improvement of sanitation facilities in communities.
- Promote safe sanitation and environmental health practices.
- Ensure facilities are accessible and inclusive for all users.

**Hygiene Promotion**

- Lead the design and implementation of hygiene promotion and behaviour change activities.
- Develop and adapt information, education and communication materials.
- Ensure community participation throughout implementation.

**WASH Kits and Supplies**

- Plan and oversee the distribution of hygiene kits, water treatment products and other WASH supplies.
- Ensure transparent and accountable distribution processes, including post-distribution monitoring.

**4. WASH in Health Facilities**

**Infrastructure**

- Conduct assessments of WASH conditions in health facilities.
- Oversee the rehabilitation and upgrading of water systems, sanitation facilities, drainage, handwashing stations and healthcare waste management infrastructure.

**Infection Prevention and Control (IPC)**

- Support the implementation of WASH and IPC standards in health facilities, including healthcare waste management and environmental cleaning.
- Organise training for health facility staff on WASH-related IPC practices.

**Operation and Maintenance**

- Develop operation and maintenance plans for rehabilitated infrastructure.
- Build the capacity of health facility staff to maintain WASH systems and monitor their functionality.

**5. Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning**

- Develop and implement WASH monitoring tools, in coordination with the M&E team.
- Conduct regular field monitoring visits and technical supervision.
- Analyse programme data and prepare technical reports.
- Document lessons learned and good practices.
- Ensure timely and accurate internal and donor reporting.

**6. Staff Supervision and Capacity Building**

- Supervise WASH staff and provide technical guidance.
- Conduct regular performance reviews and support staff development.
- Identify training needs and organise capacity building for staff, contractors, partners and community water and sanitation committees.
- Promote teamwork and a positive working environment.

**7. Budget and Resource Management**

- Prepare and monitor budgets for WASH activities.
- Ensure efficient and accountable use of programme resources.
- Coordinate closely with the logistics, finance, administration and procurement teams.

**8. Representation and Coordination**

- Represent MENTOR in WASH Cluster meetings and technical working groups.
- Maintain effective relationships with government water, sanitation and health authorities, donors and partners.
- Contribute technical inputs to proposals, strategic plans and programme development.

**9. Other**

- Uphold MENTOR's values, policies, safeguarding principles and Code of Conduct.
- Ensure all WASH activities are implemented in line with humanitarian principles and quality standards.
- Undertake any other duties reasonably assigned by the Programme Coordinator.

The MENTOR Initiative is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity in the organisation. We ensure constant non-discrimination throughout the recruitment process.

The MENTOR Initiative is committed to promoting diversity and gender equality and strongly encourages candidates from under-represented backgrounds to apply.

The MENTOR Initiative applies a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation, abuse, mistreatment or harassment, and other types of unethical behaviour including fraud.

The MENTOR Initiative will contact previous employers of applicants to determine if they have any history of violating international standards and codes of conduct relating to such matters.

jobs.title: Somalia - Head of Mission (National Candidates Only)
Functional Lead, Humanitarian ERP
jobs.description:
NGO finance & procurement · Business analysis

**Remote · EuropeContract4 days / week**

Relief Applications is a humanitarian tech company headquartered in Toulouse, France. We build digital tools with and for NGOs, UN agencies and mission-driven organisations, bringing solutions to those changing the world.

We are growing our ERP offer for NGOs: Finance, Procurement and HR modules designed for how humanitarian organisations actually work.

## **About the role**

You will be the business brain of the project. Working side by side with our project manager, you will turn NGOs’ finance, procurement and HR needs into features.

Your work makes our ERP stronger with every deployment and decides whether client teams adopt it. You will run workshops with them, shape the workflows, test what is built and train the users. Occasional travel to clients is expected.

## **Key responsibilities**

### **Requirements & functional design**

- Co-run user-requirement workshops with client Finance, Procurement and HR teams
- Write clear user stories, workflows and acceptance criteria
- Own the functional design of the Finance, Procurement and HR modules: approval chains, budgets and cost codes, data model and reporting
- Flag early when deeper expertise is needed, such as local payroll or HR law

### **Building & testing**

- Prototype and ship features, screens and fixes with AI-supported tools (Claude, Cursor or similar)
- Work through Git with the tech lead and developers, who review your code
- Test features against real NGO scenarios and run user acceptance testing with clients

### **Adoption**

- Review and complete user guides
- Design and deliver trainings for finance, procurement and HR users
- Collect feedback after go-live and turn it into improvements

## **Candidate profile**

### **Additional assets**

- Previous ERP implementation or rollout (Sage, Dynamics, Odoo, SunSystems…)
- Experience with charity finance across several countries
- MEAL or logframe exposure
- Training and documentation experience

### **Experience**

- 3–5+ years in NGO or humanitarian operations, ideally in finance, grants or procurement
- Solid working knowledge of donor rules, budget lines, cost codes, purchase-to-pay flows and grant reporting
- Hands-on experience building with AI

### **Languages**

- Fluent English; French is a plus

### **Skills**

- Business analysis: running workshops, mapping processes, writing user stories
- Comfortable with Git, reading code, and basic data and SQL
- Able to turn rules into working features

### **Soft skills**

- Autonomous and pragmatic
- Confident facing a client’s team
- Honest about what you know and what you don’t

jobs.title: Full-time Programme Internship (New York)
jobs.description:
**About ISHR**

ISHR is an independent, non-profit organisation with offices in Geneva and New York. This internship offers a unique opportunity to view the United Nations human rights system at work in New York. It provides hands-on experience working for an international non-governmental organisation (NGO) as well as the opportunity to contribute to our work supporting human rights defenders, strengthening human rights systems, building and leading human rights coalitions, and responding to significant and systemic human rights concerns. For more information, consult our website [https://ishr.ch/](https://ishr.ch/).

**Internship position**

The Intern will work closely with Programme Officers/Managers and Directors, contributing to our work supporting human rights defenders, strengthening human rights systems, building and leading human rights coalitions, and responding to significant and systemic situations of concern.

Working in a small team, the Intern will have the opportunity to learn at close hand what it means to work for an international human rights advocacy organisation. The Intern will also have the opportunity to collaborate with ISHR staff in all locations and gain hands-on experience on the application of international human rights law in a multilateral human rights system, including advocacy on normative and policy advances for the protection of human rights defenders.

**Training and Opportunities**

Our Interns are fully included as part of the team, including in staff meetings, which provide a comprehensive understanding of the work of an international human rights NGO. Interns also have opportunities to interact and network with human rights defenders, diplomats or other UN and NGO professionals both at the United Nations and at ISHR’s office (or remotely) during meetings.

Where appropriate or necessary for their work, ISHR staff will provide practical sessions and guidance, for example, on monitoring UN mechanisms, drafting reports and advocacy documents, utilising communications technologies, etc. Interns will be supervised by one or two experienced programme managers and supported in achieving their learning objectives through regular check-ins with the Intern Coordinator.

**Key tasks**

- Providing support to programme staff in the implementation of project activities, across ISHR’s strategic programme areas including improving civil society engagement at the UN, addressing reprisals, as well as other projects seeking to enhance protection for human rights defenders;
- Contributing to ISHR’s outreach and communications, including regular online publications;
- Monitoring and reporting on UN human rights meetings, including the ECOSOC’s Committee on NGOs and General Assembly’s Third Committee;
- Approximately 15-20% of the work will be administrative in nature, including assisting with the organisation and preparation of events, training and meetings.

**Internship modalities**

The internship will be in person, in ISHR’s New York Office and will start on 11 January 2027. It is a 6-months full-time (37.5 hours per week) position with no possibility of extension.

**Stipend**

Internships will be compensated with:

- a stipend of USD700/month.
- 25 annual vacation days per calendar year, pro-rated based on start/departure date (12,5 days for six months)

**Requirements**

We expect the successful candidates to:

- be an advanced undergraduate student or graduate student in international relations, law, international public law, human rights or a related field, or have recently completed such studies;
- be motivated to pursue a career in human rights and have a particular interest in the UN and regional human rights systems;
- have **an excellent level of written and spoken English;**
- be detail-oriented and attentive to nuance, in particular in diplomatic environments;
- be motivated, autonomous and a self-starter, and comfortable occasionally working with limited supervision;
- be able to work as a member of an international and multicultural team and willing to participate in a variety of tasks, as required;
- **be authorised to work in the U.S.**

Additional particularly appreciated skills:

- **Advanced to fluent Spanish and/or French and/or Arabic language; Mandarin is also an asset.**
- interest or background, including activism in, corporate accountability, women’s rights, and/or LGBTI rights;
- legal drafting and research including on treaty body jurisprudence;
- interest or background in training/capacity building, including online learning, logistics, travel and event planning;
- be proficient with Google Suite and/or Microsoft tools.

**Equal opportunity**

ISHR is firmly committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity and aims to have a diverse team. ISHR's policy is to practice fair and non-discriminatory recruitment and selection procedures and strive for diverse, international and multicultural personnel. We welcome all kinds of diversity.

Applications are encouraged from all qualified candidates without distinction including on grounds of race, colour, national origin, age, religion, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression or sex characteristics, pregnancy, genetic information, protected veteran status, socio-economic status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We particularly welcome applications from systematically, historically and/or traditionally discriminated against under-represented groups, including women, persons of colour, LGBTIQ+ persons, persons with disabilities and other groups.

To request reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, please contact ISHR’s Human Resources department at hr@ishr.ch

jobs.title: Operations & Finance Coordinator - Mozambique
jobs.description:
**Position Title - Operations & Finance Coordinator (HR, Finance, and Logistics)**

**Duty Station - Pemba (Cabo Delgado, Mozambique) with travel to field bases / districts**

**Reports To - Country Director and HQ Grants Manager**

**Contract Type - Full-time, fixed term approx one year (International Consultant)**

**Closing date of applications - 2 November 2026**

The MENTOR Initiative (‘MENTOR’) is a humanitarian organisation specialising in disease control and improving access to healthcare in emergency settings across countries in Africa, the Middle East and South America. MENTOR is the leading organisation dedicated to the control of malaria and other vector-borne diseases in complex, vulnerable settings.

MENTOR delivers large scale disease control interventions working with communities affected by emergencies such as conflict and natural disasters and at higher risk of diseases. We also help build the technical and operational capacity of local and international partners to incorporate medium- and long-term disease control systems into their operations and country strategy.

**Requirements for the role**

- Education: Advanced University Degree (Master's preferred) in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Logistics, Human Resources, International Relations, or related field.
- Professional background in financial, administrative and operational management is essential.
- Minimum of 10 years of field experience in international NGOs, with at least 5 years in senior coordination roles in emergency or conflict settings.
- Extensive experience managing various departments (HR, Finance, and Logistics), including supply chain, procurement and team leadership.
- Familiarity with Mozambican labour and tax regulations, as well as local legal compliance (Experience working in Mozambique, specifically Cabo Delgado, a strong advantage).
- Extensive knowledge of financial management rules and procurement procedures of major international donors.
- Highly organised with strong coordination and project management skills, proficient in accounting software (preferably SAGA) and advanced Excel.
- Excellent communication and reporting skills for efficient collaboration with HQ and donors.
- Ability to work in a multicultural environment under high pressure, demonstrating strong ethical principles, compliance, and problem-solving skills in volatile contexts.
- Fluent in Portuguese and English (both written and spoken, essential).

**Position Overview**

The Operations and Finance Coordinator (OFC) is a key member of the Country Management Team (CMT) and serves as the primary executive responsible for the leadership, oversight, and integrity of the Human Resources, Finance and Logistics departments of The MENTOR Initiative in Cabo Delgado, Mozambique.

Working in close coordination with the Country Director and the HQ Grants Manager, the OFC ensures financial sustainability, operational supply chain efficiency, and strict compliance with local and international labor, tax and safeguarding policies. The role ensures that all humanitarian interventions are executed with high quality, transparency, and full adherence to donor regulations.

**Main Responsibilities**

**1. Human Resources Management and Leadership (National and International)**

As the primary head of the HR department in Mozambique:

- Legal and Tax Compliance: Lead the rigorous application of Mozambican Labor Law, tax codes (INSS, IRPS), and local regulations, acting as the focal point with the General Labor Inspection and local legal advisors.
- Recruitment and Contract Management: Oversee the complete lifecycle of national staff and community volunteers (job postings, screening, hiring, renewals, and separations), ensuring transparent and auditable processes.
- Payroll Management: Lead and approve the monthly processing of salaries, allowances, and per diems, ensuring accurate and timely payments.
- Team Administration: Oversee the administration of the international team in Cabo Delgado, including work visas, international travel, leave schedules, and direct coordination with HQ HR.
- Performance Management and Staff Development: Implement continuous performance appraisal systems, manage disciplinary procedures, and design capacity-building and training plans for local teams.
- Safeguarding, Code of Conduct, and PSEAH: Enforce zero-tolerance policies and ensure strict adherence to MENTOR’s Code of Conduct by leading briefings, trainings, and in-country complaint/incident handling in coordination with HQ.

**2. Financial Management, Accounting, and Budget Monitoring**

As the primary lead for the mission's financial integrity:

- Accounting Systems: Ensure the proper operation and maintenance of high-quality financial systems using MENTOR’s accounting software (SAGA) and supervise monthly mission book-closing.
- Budget Tracking and Control: Prepare and update monthly Budget Versus Actual (BVA) trackings for all active grants, identifying variances and proposing timely reallocations in coordination with the HQ Grants Manager.
- Treasury and Cash Flow: Lead liquidity management across Pemba and field bases, overseeing local bank accounts, cash safes, fund transfers, and routine Cash Requests to HQ.
- Accountability and Audits: Ensure 100% of financial documentation, invoices, and receipts comply with MENTOR and donor auditability standards; lead preparation for internal and external audits.
- Proposal Development: Collaborate with HQ and the Country Director in developing realistic budgets for new funding proposals.

**3. Logistics, Supply Chain and Transport Management**

As the primary lead for operational logistics support:

- Procurement: Supervise all local and national procurement of goods, equipment, and services, ensuring strict adherence to threshold rules, market surveys, quotation collection, and Procurement Committee processes.
- International Procurement and Customs: Coordinate with HQ on tracking international orders, managing customs clearance processes, and securing VAT/customs duty exemptions with Mozambican authorities.
- Inventory and Warehouse Management: Guarantee rigorous control over central and field warehouses (stock cards, waybills, monthly physical counts), paying special attention to cold chain systems, medical stocks, and WASH supplies.
- Fleet and Transport Management: Oversee the vehicle fleet (owned and rented), ensuring preventive maintenance schedules, fuel monitoring, insurance, logbooks, and safe road, air, and sea transport for staff and cargo to field locations.
- Asset and Facility Management: Maintain an updated master asset register and ensure the functional operational infrastructure of bases and guesthouses (generators, satellite/HF/VHF communications, internet, and utilities).

**4. Security Management Support and Field Operations**

- Serve as the Operational Security Focal Point as delegated by the Country Director.
- Ensure all bases, vehicles, and field teams are equipped with appropriate security equipment (hibernation kits, communications, pre-movement route checks).
- Monitor the evolving security situation in Cabo Delgado in coordination with INSO, UNDSS, and humanitarian partners, supporting updates to evacuation and contingency plans.

**5. Team Leadership, Communication, and External Representation**

- Directly line manage HR, Finance, and Logistics officers/managers in Pemba and field bases.
- Represent The MENTOR Initiative in external coordination forums in Mozambique (Logistics Cluster, NGO HR/Admin Forums, Finance Working Groups).
- Produce regular operational and financial contributions to internal situation reports (sit-reps) and meet all reporting requirements established by the HQ Grants Manager.

jobs.title: Point Focal Suivi-Evaluation- Recherche et Apprentissage (SERA) - Zonal
jobs.description:
**Aperçu de l'organisation**

Tostan est une organisation à but non lucratif 501(c)(3) dont le siège est à Dakar, au Sénégal, et qui opère actuellement dans cinq pays d'Afrique de l'Ouest. Sur le plan stratégique, l'organisation s'est engagée à poursuivre le développement de sa compétence de base, à savoir l'autonomisation de l'éducation, et à documenter et mettre à l'échelle l'impact durable qu'elle crée sur toute une série de questions. Le modèle phare de Tostan, le Programme de Renforcement de Capacités des Communautés (PRCC) de trois ans, a déjà touché des milliers de communautés en Afrique de l'Ouest et de l'Est depuis 1991. Les résultats en matière de gouvernance, d'éducation, de santé, d'autonomisation économique et d'environnement sont actuellement suivis, et Tostan est particulièrement fier d'avoir joué un rôle important dans l'autonomisation à grande échelle des femmes et des filles et dans l'abandon par la communauté de pratiques néfastes telles que l’excision et le mariage des enfants. Dans le cadre de son [plan d'engagement stratégique ](https://tostan.org/tostan-strategy-2023-2030-in-partnership-for-community-well-being/)2023-2030, Tostan se concentre sur la mise à l’échelle stratégique. L'organisation développe de nouvelles stratégies de mise en œuvre pour soutenir le leadership communautaire en débloquant des changements systémiques à plus grande échelle au niveau régional. Elle crée également de nouveaux modèles pour partager et reproduire ses programmes avec d'autres partenaires de développement et étend ses capacités à partager l'approche globale de Tostan pour soutenir et influencer un éventail de publics locaux et mondiaux. Pour plus d'informations, veuillez consulter le site : [www.tostan.org ](http://www.tostan.org/).

**Aperçu du département**

L’équipe de Suivi, Evaluation, Recherche et Apprentissage (SERA) est partie intégrante du Département Programme de Tostan. Elle a pour mission de coordonner et d’appuyer le système de suivi et évaluation des programmes dans les pays où Tostan travaille mais aussi la recherche et l’apprentissage. A travers cette équipe, Tostan suit constamment les performances réalisées dans les communautés partenaires et réalise des évaluations internes impliquant des études de base, des évaluations à mi-parcours et des évaluations finales.

**1. Rôles et responsabilités**

Sous la supervision technique du SERA et la supervision administrative de…………. , Coordonnateur zonal le point focal sera/chargé-e de veiller à la stricte mise en oeuvre de toutes les activités de suivi-évaluation dans sa zone d’affectation

Il/Elle aura pour mission de :

- Soutenir et coordonner les stratégies et les actions de suivi/évaluation mises en œuvre par SERA au niveau des coordinations zonales
- Assurer le contrôle des fiches de suivi
- S’assurer que les données sont collectées ;
- S’assurer que les données collectées sont transmises à SERA national et/ou international ;
- Assurer des missions de suivi en collaboration avec le Coordonnateur zonal et le responsable SERA Sénégal pour s’assurer de l’état d’avancement des activités sur le terrain
- Appuyer la formation des CGC sur les aspects liés au Suivi-Évaluation ;

**2. Résumé de la position**

En tant qu’agent de l’équipe du SERA:

**Responsabilité 1:** ***veiller à l’application stricte du dispositif de suivi mis en place par SERA***

- Connaître le dispositif de suivi - évaluation mis en place
- Partager les composantes du dispositif avec les collègue de la coordination (coordonnateur, superviseurs et autres acteurs concernés)
- Veiller à ce que toute contrainte rencontrée dans la mise en oeuvre du dispositif soit documentée et partagée avec la hiérarchie

**Responsabilité 2:** ***renforcer les capacités du staff de terrain (superviseurs et facilitateurs) en Suivi Évaluation, sur la méthodologie de collecte de données et sur le remplissage des fiches de collecte***

- Former le staff de la coordination en particulier Coordonnateur et superviseurs sur le suivi évaluation ;
- Former les superviseurs sur le remplissage des fiches de collecte.

**Responsabilité 3:** ***s’assurer que les données de suivi sont collectées à temps selon les périodicités convenues***

- Vérifier si les fiches de collectes sont à jour
- S’assurer que les données sont collectées par chaque superviseur dans sa zone
- S’assurer de la complétudes et de la qualité des données collectées
- S’assurer que les données collectées sont transmises au SERA

**Responsabilité 4:** ***appuyer ou piloter la planification et le recueil, des données qualitatives et quantitatives sur le terrain lors des études de milieu, études de base, évaluations à mi-parcours et finales***

- Participer à la planification des études et évaluations ;
- participer et jouer un rôle actif dans la formation sur la méthodologie et les outils pour la collecte de données lors des études et évaluations ;
- Participer à la supervision de la collecte des données ;
- S’assurer de la qualité et de la complétude des données pour chaque étude et évaluation.

**3. Relations clés :**

- ***Superviseur direct (N+1) :*** Coordonnateur zonal
- ***Collaborateurs directs (N-1) :***
- ***Rapports directs (liens fonctionnels directs) :*** superviseurs
- ***Autres collègues :*** staff de la coordination
- ***Localisation :*** Kolda, Tambacounda, Ziguinchor, Kaolack

**4. Qualifications clés requises :**

***L'éducation :***

- Avoir au moins 3 ans d’expérience dans le domaine du suivi évaluation des projets de développement ;
- Avoir un diplôme de niveau licence ou équivalent en développement communautaire/local ou en planification, élaboration et gestion des projets de développement, en Suivi-évaluation des projets.

***Compétences linguistiques :***

- Savoir parler, lire et écrire en français ;
- Avoir une bonne connaissance d’au moins une langue nationale pratiquée dans la zone d’affectation.

***Connaissance et expérience :***

Le point focal zonal SERA doit avoir des compétences et aptitudes avérées dans les domaines suivants :

- Avoir des capacité à coordonner simultanément plusieurs projets différents ;
- Avoir des connaissances et qualifications en matière de développement communautaire ;
- Avoir des connaissances et une expérience avérée dans la conception, la mise en œuvre et le suivi évaluation des projets de développement ;
- Maîtriser l’outil informatique et en particulier savoir utiliser les logiciels courants (Word, EXCEL, Power Point). La maîtrise d’autres logiciels tels que Airtable, Tableau etc serait un atout ;
- Savoir utiliser les tablettes pour une collecte de données électroniques ;
- Avoir l’expérience de travailler en milieu rural avec les populations dans le respect de la dignité humaine, et être apte à supporter le travail sous pression.

***Caractéristiques :***

- Etre ouvert et coopératif ;
- Savoir travailler sous pression et dans un environnement complexe et multiculturel ;
- Avoir d'excellentes compétences en gestion du temps, ainsi que la capacité à mener plusieurs tâches de front et à hiérarchiser les priorités ;
- Avoir le permis de conduire.

***Type de contrat :*** Contrat local

jobs.title: Programme Coordinator - Mozambique
jobs.description:
**Position Title - Programme Coordinator**

**Duty Station - Pemba with travel to districts**

**Reports To - HQ Programme Manager**

**Contract Type - Full-time, fixed term approx one year**

**Closing date of applications - 2 November 2026**

The Programme Coordinator (PC) leads the overall implementation of The MENTOR Initiative's programmes in Mozambique, with a particular focus on Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), ensuring that objectives are achieved on time while identifying needs and opportunities and shaping strategic and operational responses.

The PC provides in-country leadership and representation, with overall responsibility for fundraising, financial and grant management, human resources, technical programme support and logistics.

The PC coordinates the different programmes to ensure consistent, high-quality, accountable and transparent delivery across them all.

**Requirements for the role:**

- Background in programme management in humanitarian settings is essential, with a strong focus on WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) and its integration with public health interventions.
- Extensive experience in in-country operational leadership, including security management in volatile environments, HR supervision, financial management, and logistics.
- Proven track record in grant management and donor relations, including proposal writing, budget tracking, and high-quality reporting to institutional donors.
- Demonstrable experience managing multicultural teams and coordinating across multiple field bases in conflict or crisis-affected regions.
- Familiarity with local labour and tax regulations, legal compliance, and standard NGO operating procedures (Experience working in Mozambique, particularly Cabo Delgado, is a strong advantage).
- Strong understanding of safeguarding and PSEAH policies, with experience in incident reporting, case management and promoting a culture of zero tolerance.
- Highly organised with strong strategic planning, analytical and data management skills, using project log frames as strategic implementation tools.
- Excellent communication, networking and representation skills for active engagement with Health and WASH Clusters, local authorities and donors.
- Fluent in Portuguese and English (both written and spoken, essential).

**The main responsibilities of this post include the following:**

**1. Security Management**

Working closely with the HQ Programme Manager, the PC is responsible for overall security management in a potentially insecure and unstable context:

- Maintain strong networks and regularly collect and analyse information on the security situation.
- Organise regular security updates with MENTOR field bases and report to MENTOR HQ.
- Ensure security-related logistical support is adequate and functional.
- Keep security guidelines current and pragmatic, including evacuation and hibernation plans for all bases.
- Ensure all MENTOR team members strictly follow security rules.
- Provide thorough security briefings to new expatriate team members on arrival.

**2. Programme Management**

- Lead the implementation of MENTOR programmes, in particular water supply, sanitation and hygiene promotion (WASH) activities and their integration with other public health interventions.
- Ensure an efficient data collection and analysis system that meets the reporting needs of all grants.
- Use project log frames as a tool for strategic planning and implementation.
- Work closely with the coordination team to ensure activities are delivered on plan, on objective, and within security constraints.
- Represent MENTOR to external meetings with Clusters (WASH, Health), Authorities, donors, etc.
- Oversee delivery of existing programmes and supervise, develop and support the team.
- Coordinate strategic planning for programme development.
- Ensure quality monthly, quarterly and annual reports are submitted to HQ on time.

**3. Donor Management**

- Oversee grant management, including appropriate expenditure and timely reporting to HQ ahead of donor submission.
- Coordinate and finalise field drafts of donor progress reports for HQ review within required deadlines.
- Carry out exploratory field missions, with HQ, to assess and report on potential new intervention areas.
- Liaise with current and prospective donors, in consultation with HQ, to advance programme ideas and secure funding and support.

**4. Financial and Administrative Management**

Working closely with the in-country Finance team and the HQ Grants Manager, the PC is responsible for the financial integrity of the programme and the cost-effective use of resources in line with available budgets and MENTOR standard procedures:

- Ensure appropriate security precautions around cash management.
- Keep budget tracking for all grants up to date, in collaboration with the Finance Coordinator.
- Ensure monthly finance documents (expenditure reports, cash requests, payroll, budget plans) reach HQ on time.
- Ensure expenditure documentation meets MENTOR standard requirements.
- Ensure compliance with local taxation and labour regulations.
- Finalise and endorse official mission documentation (MOUs, contracts, agreements).
- Track proposal and administrative requirements relevant to the country context.
- Secure HQ authorisation for all new grants.

**5. Human Resource Management**

- Directly manage MENTOR Coordinators and oversee their management of programme and operational support staff.
- Participate in recruitment and final selection of consultant team members.
- Lead in-country briefings for incoming consultants and debriefings for those completing contracts.
- Ensure timely performance reviews for all consultant staff and conduct reviews for direct reports.
- Oversee and approve recruitment of national staff in line with national labour law.
- Review internal HR policies with the Finance and HR team, in line with national labour law.
- Ensure consistent application of national contract formats and per diem policies.
- Lead weekly and ad hoc team meetings, and senior programme management meetings.
- Ensure contracts, the Code of Conduct, and MENTOR policies are respected by all staff.
- Implement MENTOR's Safeguarding/PSEAH policies, training and briefings for staff and volunteers.
- Support in-country Safeguarding Focal Points, in collaboration with the HQ Safeguarding focal point.
- Lead on safeguarding matters, ensuring effective support and appropriate case management.
- Ensure timely incident reporting to HQ on any policy or Code of Conduct violations and support ongoing cases.

**6. Logistics**

Working closely with the logistics team:

- Ensure adequate logistical support for security management.
- Oversee timely procurement in line with budgets, programme needs and guidelines.
- Oversee stock management of assets, WASH materials, medicines and prevention materials.
- Maintain logistical filing systems, including equipment manuals, maintenance schedules and waybills.
- Oversee fleet renewal and maintenance per HQ instructions.
- Oversee procurement, maintenance and use of communications equipment (HF, VHF, satellite phone/internet).
- Coordinate daily transport activities by road and air.

**7. Communication**

**Internal**

- Ensure regular communication within programme teams and hold regular general team meetings.
- Organise regular management meetings for all coordinators.
- Produce regular internal situation reports.
- Brief HQ (PM and GM) regularly.

**External**

- Ensure MENTOR's participation in relevant external meetings.
- Organise and join technical meetings with health and WASH stakeholders.
- Maintain transparent, efficient data and information exchange with stakeholders.
- Build strong working relationships with partners, donors and stakeholders; identify development and emergency funding opportunities through forums and conferences.

**8. Other**

- Share best practice across the organisation as required.
- Undertake any other duties assigned by the HQ Programme Manager.

The MENTOR Initiative is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity in the organisation. We ensure constant non-discrimination throughout the recruitment process.

The MENTOR Initiative is committed to promoting diversity and gender equality and strongly encourages candidates from under-represented backgrounds to apply.

The MENTOR Initiative applies a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation, abuse, mistreatment or harassment, and other types of unethical behaviour including fraud.

The MENTOR Initiative will contact previous employers of applicants to determine if they have any history of violating international standards and codes of conduct relating to such matters.

jobs.title: Responsable Analyse Médicale et Plaidoyer - Est de la RDC (h/f/x) - Médecins Sans Frontières
jobs.description:
**CONTEXTE**

En République Démocratique du Congo (RDC), Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) travaille en collaboration avec le Ministère de la Santé afin de fournir des soins médicaux aux victimes des conflits et des violences, aux personnes déplacées ainsi qu'aux personnes affectées par des épidémies ou pandémies telles que le VIH/SIDA, la tuberculose, le paludisme, la malnutrition, entre autres. Ces situations sont souvent associées à la faiblesse des institutions étatiques, aux capacités limitées du système de santé public et à une compréhension insuffisante des besoins et des lacunes réels sur le terrain. La contribution de MSF s'appuie sur ses projets réguliers ainsi que sur ses équipes de réponse d'urgence, prêtes à intervenir sur l'ensemble du territoire en cas d'épidémie, de catastrophe naturelle ou de conflit.

En 2023, face à l'intensification de la violence dans l'est de la RDC, qui a entraîné le déplacement d'un nombre record de civils, MSF a renforcé ses activités afin de répondre à l'augmentation des besoins humanitaires. Depuis l'année dernière, l'ensemble des missions MSF au Nord-Kivu est confronté à d'importants défis liés aux ruptures de stocks de médicaments contre la tuberculose, le VIH et le paludisme, ainsi qu'à des pénuries d'intrants médicaux (cartouches GeneXpert, tests VIH et paludisme, etc.) et à une capacité limitée de réponse face à l'augmentation des cas de violences sexuelles, de malnutrition et d'épidémies. Le nombre élevé de déplacements de population complique également l'accès aux soins de santé. Les réductions de financement du Fonds mondial ainsi que le conflit en cours dans l'est de la RDC contribuent à ces perturbations.

En tant que **Responsable Analyse Médicale et Plaidoyer - Est de la RDC**, vous êtes responsable de l’analyse médicale et du développement des activités de plaidoyer liées à l’accès aux soins et aux services de santé dans l’est du pays. Placé(e) sous la supervision hiérarchique du Représentant Médical du BALI (Bureau administratif et de liaison intersectionnel de MSF) et en lien fonctionnel et technique avec les Conseillers en politiques de santé suivant la RDC, vous contribuez à l’identification, la documentation et l’analyse des principaux obstacles à l’accès aux soins ainsi qu'à l'élaboration des positionnements et messages de plaidoyer de MSF. Vous travaillez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes projets et les Coordinateurs Médicaux des différentes sections MSF présentes au Nord-Kivu afin de collecter et consolider les informations issues du terrain. Vous collaborez également avec le Responsable Plaidoyer VIH/TB basé à Kinshasa afin de relayer les enjeux identifiés dans l'Est auprès des autorités nationales, des bailleurs et des autres acteurs de santé concernés. En tant que membre de l'équipe de coordination, vous assurez le lien entre les réalités opérationnelles observées dans les projets et les initiatives de plaidoyer menées aux niveaux provincial, national et international.

**RESPONSABILITES PRINCIPALES**

**Analyse des obstacles à l'accès aux soins**

- Collecter, centraliser et analyser les informations relatives aux barrières d'accès aux services de santé, notamment dans les domaines du VIH, de la tuberculose, du paludisme, de la vaccination, de la nutrition et de la prise en charge des violences sexuelles. Produire des analyses permettant de mieux comprendre les défis rencontrés par les populations et d'orienter le positionnement de MSF

**Suivi des financements et cartographie des acteurs**

- Assurer une veille sur les financements des programmes de santé et sur les évolutions du paysage humanitaire et sanitaire. Analyser l'impact des financements sur la disponibilité des services de santé et maintenir une cartographie actualisée des acteurs intervenant dans les zones couvertes par MSF

**Consolidation et analyse des données issues des projets**

- Consolider les données et informations remontées par les projets MSF concernant les ruptures de stocks, les difficultés d'accès aux traitements et diagnostics, les tendances épidémiologiques, la malnutrition ou les violences sexuelles. Transformer ces informations en analyses permettant d'identifier les principales lacunes et risques pour les populations

**Suivi de la disponibilité des intrants médicaux**

- En collaboration avec les équipes pharmacie et supply, suivre la disponibilité des médicaments, tests diagnostiques et autres intrants de santé essentiels. Participer aux mécanismes de coordination concernés et contribuer à l'identification précoce des risques de rupture ou de difficultés d'approvisionnement pouvant affecter les activités médicales

**Développement et mise en œuvre du plaidoyer**

- Contribuer à l'élaboration et à la mise en œuvre des stratégies de plaidoyer de MSF en documentant les besoins, les insuffisances de réponse et les conséquences pour les populations. Participer à la rédaction de messages clés, notes de briefing, analyses et autres documents destinés aux autorités, bailleurs de fonds et partenaires

**Coordination et collaboration intersectionnelle**

- Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les équipes médicales, opérationnelles et de plaidoyer des différentes sections MSF intervenant au Nord-Kivu. Participer aux discussions internes visant à développer des analyses communes, harmoniser les positionnements de MSF et renforcer la cohérence des actions de plaidoyer aux niveaux provincial, national et international

**PREREQUIS**

**Education & Expérience**

- Diplôme universitaire en santé publique, politiques de santé, sciences de la santé, affaires humanitaires ou dans un domaine connexe. Une spécialisation en plaidoyer, sciences politiques ou communication constitue un atout
- Minimum 2 ans d’expérience internationale dans différents contextes humanitaires ou de santé publique est requis
- Expérience du secteur de la santé publique ainsi qu’une bonne compréhension des mécanismes de financement de la santé et du fonctionnement des systèmes de santé est un atout important
- Une expérience au sein de MSF ou d’une autre INGO médicale est indispensable
- Une expérience en plaidoyer auprès des autorités sanitaires, des bailleurs de fonds ou d’autres acteurs de la santé constitue un atout
- Un intérêt marqué pour la région ainsi que pour les enjeux humanitaires est attendu

**Compétences**

- Capacité à analyser et à synthétiser des données médicales, épidémiologiques et opérationnelles
- Capacité démontrée de représentation, du réseautage, et de négociations
- Forte sensibilité interculturelle et aptitude à travailler dans des environnements multiculturels
- Résistance au stress
- Travail d’équipe et coopération
- Agilité et diplomatie
- Excellente maîtrise du Pack Office 365 est obligatoire

**Langues**

- Très bonne maitrise orale et écrite du **Français**
- Bonne connaissance d’Anglais est un atout

**CONDITIONS**

- Date de début : **Dès que possible**
- Localisation : **Béni**, Est de la RDC
- Mobilité : **mobilité importante dans les projets et les coordinations**
- Type de contrat : Contrat à durée déterminée – Temps plein
- Durée du contrat : **9 mois** (prolongeable)
- Salaire selon la grille salariale internationale de MSF
- Les termes contractuels, les conditions et le salaire seront établis en fonction de la résidence officielle des candidats sélectionnés et dans le respect des grilles standard de fonction et de salaire de MSF
- **Pas de poste en famille ou couple**
- ***Adhésion aux valeurs managériales de l’organisation : Respect, Transparence, Responsabilisation, Intégrité, Confiance, Autonomisation***
- ***Adhésion aux engagements pour un comportement responsable***

**Date limite pour postuler : 15th of November 2026**

***Les femmes sont encouragées à postuler.***

jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.description:
**OB DESCRIPTION**

**PROJECT**

Integrated Shelter, Food Security and Livelihoods Support for Safe, Dignified and Sustainable Return in Abul Thohur (Idleb) and Madiq Castle (Hama)

**DUTY STATION**

Idlib, Syria, with regular field visits to project locations

**ABOUT THE PROJECT**

IHH is implementing an integrated humanitarian and early-recovery project funded by the OCHA Syria Humanitarian Fund (SHF), supporting safe, dignified and sustainable return in Abul Thohur, Idleb Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate.

The project combines shelter rehabilitation, winterization and Core NFI assistance, cash assistance for food, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread provision, and agricultural and irrigation-related interventions. Through these complementary activities, the project aims to address urgent household needs, restore essential infrastructure and support agricultural livelihoods and community recovery.

**JOB SUMMARY**

IHH is seeking an experienced Project Manager to lead the overall planning, implementation, monitoring and closure of the project, ensuring that all activities are delivered effectively, on time, within the approved budget, and in compliance with IHH policies and OCHA SHF requirements.

The Project Manager will oversee the implementation of integrated Shelter/NFI and Food Security and Agriculture/Livelihoods (FSAL) activities, providing leadership to the project team and ensuring effective coordination between technical teams, support departments, local authorities, community representatives and relevant humanitarian stakeholders.

The role requires strong project management and organizational skills, sound financial oversight, and the ability to manage multidisciplinary teams and address operational challenges in the Syrian humanitarian context. The successful candidate will ensure that project activities achieve their intended results while maintaining high standards of programme quality, accountability, safeguarding and donor compliance.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Project Planning and Implementation**

**·** Lead the planning, implementation and closure of the project in accordance with the approved proposal, logical framework, work plan, budget and donor requirements.

**·** Develop and regularly update detailed implementation plans, activity schedules, procurement plans and resource requirements in coordination with relevant technical and support teams.

**·** Oversee the implementation of shelter, NFI, food security, agriculture and livelihoods activities, ensuring that project outputs, targets and milestones are achieved within the approved timeframe.

**·** Monitor progress against the approved work plan and indicators, identify implementation delays and operational challenges, and implement appropriate corrective measures.

**·** Ensure effective integration and complementarity between project components to maximize impact and avoid duplication of assistance.

**·** Conduct regular field visits to assess implementation progress, verify the quality of activities, engage with project teams and communities, and address implementation challenges.

**·** Ensure that project documentation, implementation records and supporting evidence are complete, accurate and maintained in accordance with organizational and donor requirements.

**Technical Oversight and Programme Quality**

**·** Coordinate with engineering staff to ensure the effective implementation of shelter rehabilitation activities, including household assessments, preparation and review of Bills of Quantities (BoQs), contractor supervision, quality assurance and verification of completed works.

**·** Oversee winterization and Core NFI assistance, ensuring transparent beneficiary selection, appropriate verification, clear communication of assistance modalities and coordination between SHF-funded and IHH-funded caseloads.

**·** Supervise the implementation of cash assistance for food, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread activities, ensuring compliance with approved targeting criteria, delivery arrangements and monitoring requirements.

**·** Coordinate with agriculture and field teams to support the effective implementation and monitoring of agricultural assistance, irrigation-related interventions and activities supporting farming livelihoods.

**·** Ensure that project activities comply with approved technical specifications, implementation procedures and relevant quality standards.

**·** Work closely with technical staff to identify implementation gaps, address quality concerns and ensure that interventions respond to identified household and community needs.

**·** Promote coordination across technical components to ensure consistent implementation and efficient use of project resources.

**Team Leadership and Coordination**

**·** Provide day-to-day management, supervision and guidance to project staff, ensuring clear responsibilities, effective communication and accountability for results.

**·** Coordinate closely with engineering, FSAL, finance, procurement, logistics, monitoring and other relevant teams to ensure timely and effective project delivery.

**·** Monitor staff performance, identify capacity-building needs and support professional development and continuous improvement.

**·** Maintain effective working relationships with local authorities, community representatives, contractors, service providers and relevant humanitarian actors.

**·** Represent IHH in relevant coordination meetings and external engagements related to the project, as delegated by senior management.

**·** Organize regular project review meetings to assess progress, discuss challenges, agree on corrective actions and follow up on outstanding issues.

**·** Ensure that field teams receive the guidance, information and resources required to perform their responsibilities effectively.

**Budget Management and Donor Compliance**

**·** Monitor project expenditure against the approved budget and implementation plan in coordination with the finance team.

**·** Review budget utilization, expenditure forecasts and financial progress, identifying variances and proposing corrective actions when required.

**·** Coordinate with finance, procurement and logistics teams to ensure that project expenditures, procurement processes, contracts and payments comply with IHH procedures and donor requirements.

**·** Ensure that project activities and expenditures remain within the approved scope and budget and that any proposed changes follow established authorization procedures.

**·** Monitor financial and operational risks, identify potential overspending or implementation bottlenecks, and take timely action to address them.

**·** Ensure that financial and programme documentation is accurate, complete and available for internal reviews, audits and donor verification.

**·** Escalate significant financial, contractual, operational or compliance issues to senior management in a timely manner.

**Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Reporting**

**·** Ensure systematic monitoring of project implementation against approved indicators, targets, milestones and means of verification.

**·** Coordinate with monitoring and evaluation staff to support data quality, activity monitoring, post-distribution monitoring and other required assessments.

**·** Ensure that beneficiary selection, registration and verification processes are transparent, properly documented and consistent with approved eligibility criteria.

**·** Oversee household-level de-duplication and the separate tracking of SHF-funded and IHH-funded assistance, where applicable.

**·** Ensure that feedback and complaints mechanisms are accessible to affected communities and that feedback is documented, referred and addressed through established procedures.

**·** Prepare, review and submit timely, accurate and evidence-based donor reports, internal progress updates and other required project documentation.

**·** Maintain effective project management systems and ensure that implementation records and indicator-tracking tools are regularly updated.

**·** Document implementation challenges, lessons learned and good practices, using monitoring findings to improve programme quality and inform management decisions.

**Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement**

**·** Maintain effective coordination with relevant local authorities, community representatives, service providers and other stakeholders in the targeted locations.

**·** Coordinate with relevant humanitarian coordination mechanisms and sector actors to promote complementarity, information sharing and alignment with identified needs.

**·** Facilitate communication between field teams, technical specialists and support departments to resolve implementation challenges.

**·** Support coordination with relevant stakeholders involved in shelter rehabilitation, food security, agricultural livelihoods, bakery operations and irrigation-related activities.

**·** Ensure that community engagement is conducted transparently and that beneficiaries receive clear information about project objectives, eligibility criteria, assistance modalities and feedback channels.

**Protection, Safeguarding and Risk Management**

**·** Ensure that protection mainstreaming, gender sensitivity, disability inclusion, accountability to affected populations and the principle of do no harm are integrated throughout project implementation.

**·** Work with the designated GBV Programme Focal Point to identify and mitigate potential gender-based violence risks associated with project activities.

**·** Ensure compliance with IHH safeguarding policies, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), the organizational code of conduct and relevant reporting procedures.

**·** Promote safe, dignified and non-discriminatory access to project assistance, with particular attention to vulnerable and marginalized groups.

**·** Identify and monitor operational, security, access, financial, procurement and implementation risks, and develop appropriate mitigation measures.

**·** Ensure that safeguarding concerns, protection risks and other incidents are reported and referred through established organizational channels.

**·** Promote a culture of accountability, integrity, transparency and responsible use of humanitarian resources.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE**

**·** Bachelor's degree in engineering, agriculture, economics, business administration, project management, international development or another relevant discipline. A master's degree is an advantage.

**·** At least five years of progressively responsible experience in similar positions within the humanitarian sector, including project planning, implementation, team management, budget monitoring and donor reporting.

**·** Demonstrated experience in at least one of the following sectors: Shelter and Non-Food Items (SNFI) or Food Security and Agriculture/Livelihoods (FSAL). Experience in both sectors is highly preferred.

**·** Proven experience managing donor-funded humanitarian projects and ensuring compliance with organizational policies, approved budgets and donor requirements.

**·** Experience in work planning, indicator tracking, financial monitoring, risk management and preparation of donor reports.

**·** Demonstrated ability to supervise multidisciplinary teams and coordinate effectively with technical and support departments.

**·** Experience working with local authorities, community representatives, contractors, service providers and humanitarian coordination mechanisms in Syria.

**·** Experience with OCHA or the Syria Humanitarian Fund (SHF) is highly desirable.

**·** Familiarity with shelter rehabilitation, cash-based assistance, food security, agricultural livelihoods or early-recovery programming is an advantage.

**·** Strong organizational, analytical, leadership, communication and problem-solving skills.

**·** Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Word. Familiarity with project monitoring and digital data-collection tools is an advantage.

**·** Fluency in Arabic and excellent proficiency in English, both written and spoken, are essential. Knowledge of Turkish is an advantage.

**CORE COMPETENCIES**

**·** Project planning, implementation and results-based management.

**·** Team leadership, staff supervision and multidisciplinary coordination.

**·** Budget monitoring, financial accountability and donor compliance.

**·** Analytical thinking, risk management and problem-solving.

**·** Effective communication, negotiation and stakeholder engagement.

**·** Monitoring, reporting and evidence-based decision-making.

**·** Accountability, integrity, confidentiality and commitment to humanitarian principles.

**·** Adaptability and the ability to manage competing priorities in a complex operational environment.

**WORKING CONDITIONS**

The position will be based at the IHH Idlib Office, with regular field visits to Abul Thohur, Idleb Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate, as required by project implementation needs. The successful candidate must be able to coordinate effectively with field teams and travel to project locations when required.

jobs.description:
**DEADLINE FOR APPLICATIONS**

10 November 2026-23:59-GMT-05:00 Eastern Standard Time (Panama)

*WFP celebrates and embraces diversity. It is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all its employees and encourages qualified candidates to apply irrespective of race, colour, national origin, ethnic or social background, genetic information, gender, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, religion or belief, HIV status or disability.*

**ABOUT WFP**

The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of extreme weather shocks.

At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP's values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves.

To learn more about WFP, visit our website: [https://www.wfp.org](https://www.wfp.org/) and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/c/worldfoodprogramme), [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/unwfp/), [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/worldfoodprogramme/), [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/WorldFoodProgramme/), [Twitter](https://twitter.com/WFP?ref_src=https://reliefweb.int/twsrc%5Egoogle%7Ctwcamp%5Eserp%7Ctwgr%5Eauthor), [TikTok](http://www.tiktok.com/@worldfoodprogramme?lang=en).

- WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate.
- WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment.
- WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities.

This position is based in Panama and reports to Deputy Regional Director.

**THE ROLE**

To deliver a wide range of business support processes and activities for a specific professional area of work, to facilitate effective service delivery.

2\. Respond to standard queries and provide timely and accurate guidance.
3\. Process and manage routine administrative and financial tasks in various functional areas, to contribute to the effective and timely management of resources
4\. Manage and maintain records and databases, to ensure information is organized and readily available for staff.
5\. Maintain relationships with a range of individuals through provision of business support to assist in information sharing and service delivery to staff.
6\. Proof-read reports, documentation, correspondence, etc., making changes in line with established guidelines where appropriate.
7\. Contribute to improvement of business procedures and processes.
8\. Collect and perform basic analysis of data to contribute to quality business information management.
9\. Provide guidance to junior colleagues in performing their duties.

**ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES:**

- Support the planning and execution of events organized by the Regional Director´s Office, including Leadership meetings and government fora.
- Support business processes related to the implementation of programs and projects led by the Regional Director Office.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE:**
**Education:** Completion of secondary school education. A post-secondary certificate in the related functional area is desirable.

**Experience:** Five or more years of progressively responsible work experience in the relative business stream with experience in general administrative work.

**Knowledge and Skills:**
• Knowledge of specialized common business practices and methods, gained through relevant technical training and experience.
• Ability to develop and maintain relationships with a range of individuals in order to provide a high-quality support service.
• Ability to carry out basic data analysis and independently rectify problems requiring attention.
• Ability to monitor and record financial transactions.
• Good communication skills required to give and receive information and work with a variety of individuals.
• Ability to maintain confidentiality

**Language:** General Service (Headquarters): Fluency (level C) in English language. Fluency (level C) or intermediate knowledge (level B) of another official language may be required depending on the location of the post or area of responsibility.

General Service (Field): Fluency in both oral and written communication in the UN language in use at the duty station and in the duty station’s language, if different.

**TERMS & CONDITIONS:**

Number of openings: 1

Based in: Panama City, Panama

Type of Contract: General Service

Level: 5

Duration: 12 months
This position is open to Panamanian citizens or residents with a permanent visa.You can consult the UN Salary Scale for Panama page for your reference. Fixed-Term appointments are for a continuous period of one year or more and shall have a specified expiration date. The initial appointment is subject to a probationary period of one year.Successful candidates will be placed in a roster for two (2) years.

WFP is committed to supporting individuals with disabilities by providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process. If you require a reasonable accommodation, please contact: global.inclusion@wfp.org

jobs.title: GRANT MANAGER, Bangui, CAR.
jobs.description:
## The Role

**Job Title:** Grants Manager

**Location:** Bangui, Central African Republic

**Position Type:** International or national position

**Contract Type and Duration:** 12-month renewable fixed-term contract, subject to a probationary period.

**Reporting Line:** Regional Director

**Supervision:** The role has no line-management responsibilities but will work closely with Support Services and Programme teams.

**Salary and Leave:** 3200-3600EUR before tax. 33 days of annual leave to include all public and religious holidays

### Roles and Responsibilities:

Under the supervision of the designated Regional Director and in close collaboration with the Country Managers, Regional Head of MEAL, and Programme Development Manager, the Grants Manager will be responsible for the following key areas:

### Grants Management and Compliance

- Maintain oversight of donor contracts and grant agreements throughout the grant lifecycle.
- Develop and maintain a grants and compliance tracker; communicate obligations, responsibilities and deadlines; coordinate follow-up with Programme, Finance, MEAL and partner teams; maintain complete records; and escalate significant risks, gaps or delays to the appropriate managers.
- Coordinate grant requirements at project kick-off, review and closeout, ensuring that staff understand approved plans, budgets, deliverables, compliance obligations and deadlines.
- Support Project Managers to monitor implementation, prepare and track justified amendment requests, manage authorised donor communication, complete closeout requirements and document lessons for future programme design.
- Proactively identify potential donor compliance issues, and work with the team to develop appropriate and timely responses.

### Donor Reporting and Information Management

- Together with the Regional Head of MEAL, lead the donor reporting process, maintaining a clear reporting calendar and coordinating timely inputs from Programme, Finance, MEAL and other teams.
- Develop and maintain appropriate templates for reporting and other donor documentation requirements.
- Review narrative and financial reports for accuracy, consistency, evidence, compliance and alignment with approved plans and results frameworks; secure required approvals; follow up on gaps or delays; archive final submissions and supporting evidence; and guide colleagues on donor reporting standards.
- Establish and maintain an organised system for managing grant-related documentation throughout the grant lifecycle.
- Ensure that grant agreements, approved proposals, budgets, amendments, donor reports, correspondence, monitoring reports, evaluations, and closeout documents are properly filed and archived in designated organisational systems.
- Conduct periodic reviews of project files to verify the completeness, accuracy, and accessibility of grant documentation.
- Coordinate with Project Managers and relevant colleagues to ensure that project documentation is uploaded and maintained in accordance with organisational procedures.

### Communication, Donor Engagement, and Visibility

- Coordinate with Programme and Communications colleagues to identify achievements, results and lessons for donor briefings, success stories, case studies and other communication products.
- Ensure that all materials meet donor visibility requirements and Concordis standards for safeguarding, confidentiality and approval, and maintain an accessible record of key donor communications and products.

### Capacity Building and Internal Coordination

- Provide practical guidance to Project Managers and Programme, Finance and MEAL colleagues on grants management, donor compliance, proposal development and reporting.
- Promote consistent systems and standards across the regional programme, address implementation or capacity gaps, share good practice and lessons, and maintain effective coordination with Country Managers, the Regional Director and relevant UK colleagues.

### Safeguarding, Conduct and Confidentiality

- Comply with Concordis safeguarding, anti-fraud, anti-corruption, conflict-of-interest and code-of-conduct requirements.
- Maintain strict confidentiality regarding staff, financial, supplier and organisational information.
- Immediately report safeguarding, fraud, corruption, exploitation, abuse or other serious concerns through the appropriate reporting mechanisms.
- Ensure administrative and logistical arrangements support safe and dignified participation of staff and programme participants.

### Other Duties and Responsibilities

- Contribute to the continuous improvement of grants management systems, tools, and procedures to strengthen efficiency, accountability, transparency, and compliance across the regional programme.
- Support the Regional Director, Country Managers, and Programme Development Manager in other grant-related activities that contribute to effective programme implementation, resource mobilisation, and organisational development.
- Perform other duties reasonably assigned by the Line Manager that are consistent with the objectives and scope of the position.
- Ensure a comprehensive and timely handover of outstanding responsibilities, grant documentation, reporting deadlines, contractual obligations, and pending actions before the end of the assignment.

### Required Qualifications and Competencies

#### 1. Education and Qualifications

- Bachelor or Master’s degree in International Development, International Cooperation, Economics, Social Sciences, Project Management, or another relevant field.
- Additional professional training or certifications in grants management, project cycle management, fundraising, compliance, or donor reporting will be an advantage.
- Professional qualifications in accounting, finance, or related fields will be an asset.

#### 2. Professional Experience

- At least four (4) years of relevant professional experience in international cooperation, international development, humanitarian assistance, or peacebuilding programmes.
- At least three (3) years of demonstrated experience in grants management or a similar position.
- Proven experience independently coordinating proposal development, donor reporting, and grant compliance processes, including consolidating contributions from multiple stakeholders.
- Demonstrated experience working with institutional donors. Experience implementing European Union funded interventions is an advantage.
- Experience managing grants throughout the project cycle, including proposal development, contract management, reporting, grant amendments, compliance monitoring, and closeout.
- Experience preparing and reviewing narrative reports, financial reporting packages, proposals, budgets, and supporting documentation.
- Experience coordinating with Programme, Finance, Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL), and other support teams to ensure compliance with donor requirements.
- Previous experience working in conflict-affected, fragile, or complex operating environments will be an asset.

#### 3. Technical Competencies and Knowledge

- Strong knowledge of institutional donor regulations, contractual requirements, proposal development procedures, reporting standards, and compliance frameworks.
- Demonstrated ability to coordinate complex proposal development and donor reporting processes, ensuring quality, consistency, and timely submission.
- Good understanding of project cycle management, grant administration, budget monitoring, risk management, and donor compliance.
- Strong analytical, organisational, planning, and coordination skills, with attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple deadlines and competing priorities.
- Advanced practical knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word, and Outlook, as well as online collaboration and document management tools such as SharePoint.
- Excellent writing, editing, reviewing, and information consolidation skills, particularly for donor proposals, narrative reports, and institutional communications.
- Ability to work independently while coordinating effectively with multidisciplinary and geographically dispersed teams.

#### 4. Languages

- **English:** Fluency in written and spoken English, with excellent report-writing, editing, and communication skills.
- **French:** Fluency in written and spoken French, with excellent report-writing, editing, and communication skills.

#### 5. Key Stakeholders

#### Internal Stakeholders

- Regional Director.
- Country Managers.
- Programme Development Manager.
- Project Managers and Programme teams across Cameroon, Chad, CAR, and Darfur in Sudan.
- Finance and Support Services teams.
- Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) team.
- Communications teams.
- UK Team

#### External Stakeholders

- Institutional donors, including the European Union (EU) and other current or potential funding partners.
- Implementing partners and local organisations.
- External auditors and other relevant compliance or verification bodies.
- Other relevant stakeholders involved in programme implementation, donor coordination, and resource mobilisation.
