DDD retains the discretion to re-advertise the vacancy, to cancel the recruitment, to offer a contract with a modified job description or for a different duration, or to offer a contract at a lower grade.

jobs.title: Climate Resilience Senior Adviser
jobs.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Climate Resilience Senior Adviser**, you will provide strategic and technical support to World Vision’s National Offices (NOs) in the South Asia Pacific (SAP) region to strengthen climate adaptation and resilience, with particular emphasis on environmental degradation and livelihoods. You will also lead efforts to identify opportunities to influence policy, secure funding, and establish new partnerships.

**Provide technical support and build capacity of Field Offices**

You will develop a Regional Environment and Climate Change Action Plan aligned with WVI’s global commitments and strengthen Field Offices’ technical capacity to implement it. You will drive the development of impact-focused programme models that improve the well-being and resilience of vulnerable children and households to economic, conflict, and climate shocks.

You will guide Field Offices in strategic planning, programme implementation, environmental safeguarding, and greenhouse gas emissions accounting and reduction. You will also strengthen regional and global partnerships, develop capacity statements and case studies, support access to Green Climate Fund (GCF) and other climate financing opportunities, and monitor and report progress against relevant WVI regional and global KPIs.

**Coordinate regional engagement and represent the South Asia-Pacific Regional Office as CCA technical expert both internally and with external partners**

You will promote World Vision’s Climate Action and Resilience programmes to private and institutional donors and provide thought leadership to identify policy influence, funding, and partnership opportunities. In collaboration with the Regional Office and Field Offices, you will identify funding opportunities, facilitate cross-project learning and knowledge sharing, support research dissemination, and provide technical and strategic support for regional and global engagements, including UNFCCC Conferences of the Parties (COPs) and other climate policy and advocacy forums.

**Showcase WV as a thought leader and technical specialist – 20%**

You will engage government officials, UN bodies, faith-based organizations, media, and development partners across South Asia Pacific to promote the integration of climate change mitigation and adaptation into World Vision programming, particularly regarding climate impacts on natural resources. You will identify and implement measures to assess climate vulnerability affecting child well-being in alignment with WVI’s Our Promise 2030 strategy and develop position papers to influence donor policies and government interventions.

**Research and Knowledge Management**

You will research and evaluate promising global and regional climate action practices, ensure the technical quality of climate-related programmes, projects, policies, practices, and guidance, and participate in research and analysis supporting relevant technical areas.

**Requirements include:**

- At least 7 years multi-country experience working in Climate Adaptation in program development, in the country/resource-constrained contexts.
- Master’s degree and/ higher professional qualifications in Forestry, Environment, Climate Change or relevant field.
- Experience in working with the UN system, donors , academia and research organisations preferred.
- The candidate is expected to have knowledge and experience particularly around Blue economy, mangrove restoration and bio-diversity programming, Environmental safeguarding experience (use of CEDRIG/NEAT+), GCF/GEF/AF experience and carbon emission reduction experience.
- Additionally, certification on NEAT +, CEDRIG, SOLSTICE and working knowledge of ECHO Minimum Environmental Requirements.
- Proven track record in securing funding in the field of climate change and adaption, and/or livelihoods.
- Demonstrated leadership and management experience in technical sectoral teams
- Understanding of resilience building and climate action approaches
- Ability to appropriately commission, interpret, and apply research and evaluation activities
- Ability to influence strategies and plans of partners; both WV entities and any external partners

jobs.title: Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Officer – ARCH
jobs.description:
*Help shape how ARCH measures progress, learns, and grows. Join a new cultural cooperation program connecting Denmark and Africa, and turn evidence into stronger programs and partnerships with lasting impact.*

**NOTE:** This position is based in Nairobi, Kenya, and requires working from the Nairobi office two to three days per week. Applicants must be based in Nairobi and have the right to work in Kenya. Professional working proficiency in French is strongly desired.

## **About ARCH and the role**

ActionAid Denmark manages ARCH – the Fund for African-Danish Relations through Exchange of Culture and Arts. Funded by the Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, this new program supports equitable cultural partnerships between Denmark and up to fourteen African countries through grants, exchange, and shared learning.

As ARCH’s MEL Officer, you will be based in Nairobi and join a Secretariat team working across Denmark and several African countries. You will report to the Head of Secretariat in Denmark.

You will join as ARCH moves from inception into implementation. Building on the MEL framework established during the inception phase, you will operationalise and manage practical systems for monitoring, evaluation and learning, ensuring that results and lessons are captured, understood and used to improve the programme. A key part of the role is making MEL useful and accessible for grantees, including small cultural organisations and collectives with limited MEL experience, so they can plan, track and report on results with confidence.

## **Your main responsibilities**

### **Monitoring, evaluation and results management**

- Operationalise, maintain and continuously improve ARCH’s MEL framework, monitoring tools, reporting templates and data collection systems, building on the Inception Report.
- Conduct ARCH’s media-coverage baseline study using the inception-phase methodology and maintain ongoing media monitoring for this indicator.
- Track progress against ARCH’s Results Framework: outcomes, outputs, indicators, baselines and targets.
- Apply and maintain a tiered partner-monitoring approach, ensuring requirements are proportionate to grant size.
- Maintain, verify, consolidate and analyse quantitative and qualitative data across the grant portfolio, including through ARCH’s digital grant management platform.
- Ensure that youth engagement, gender equality, disability inclusion, cultural diversity and human rights-based approaches are captured systematically in data and reporting.
- Quality-assure partner and grantee narrative and results reporting in English and French, and maintain organised, audit-ready MEL records.
- Support monitoring visits, spot checks and verification activities together with Secretariat colleagues, Local Liaison Officers and partners.

**MEL training and support to grantees**

- Design and deliver practical MEL training, onboarding and webinars for grantees and partners, adapted to grant tier, language and experience; develop accessible tools and provide hands-on follow-up.
- Brief and support Local Liaison Officers to help grantees with basic monitoring and data collection.

**Reporting, learning and adaptive management**

- Prepare results data, indicator updates and draft MEL sections for reports to the Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs and ARCH governance bodies.
- Organise structured reflection after calls for proposals and regular portfolio-wide learning harvests.
- Capture and share lessons and good practices through the Annual Learning Report, Grant Learning Notes, case studies and other knowledge products.
- Identify trends, challenges and opportunities in programme data and translate them into practical recommendations that strengthen programme planning, strategic dialogue, governance, decision-making and adaptive management.
- Support learning processes linked to the ARCH Strategic Dialogue Forum and other learning events.
- Prepare data, evidence and documentation for the external Mid-Term Review in 2028 and the internal end evaluation.

## **About you**

We are looking for a structured, curious and collaborative MEL professional with a practical approach and strong analytical skills. The role is particularly suited to an early-career candidate who can explain MEL concepts clearly, support others to build their skills and turn evidence into useful insights.

### **Essential requirements**

- A relevant degree in monitoring and evaluation, development studies, social sciences, statistics, economics or a related field.
- Up to three years of relevant professional experience is preferred. Candidates with up to five years of experience are also welcome to apply.
- Hands-on experience designing or implementing MEL systems for donor-funded programmes, including collecting, analysing and reporting on indicator data against a results framework or logframe.
- Working knowledge of results-based management and theory of change approaches.
- Good quantitative and qualitative analysis skills, including experience developing indicators, data collection tools and reporting templates, and preparing clear analytical or donor reports.
- Experience designing and delivering training, workshops or coaching for partners, community groups or colleagues, with the ability to explain MEL concepts in simple, practical terms.
- Excellent written and spoken English.
- Strong organisational, problem-solving and communication skills, with integrity and close attention to detail.
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively across teams and cultures and to build constructive relationships with diverse stakeholders.
- Professional working proficiency in written and spoken French is strongly desired.

### **Additional advantages**

- Familiarity with institutional donor results and reporting requirements, such as those of bilateral agencies, the EU or UN agencies.
- Experience with MEL in grant-making or sub-granting programmes across multiple organisations or countries.
- Experience with digital data collection, analysis and visualisation tools such as KoBoToolbox, ODK, Excel or Power BI.
- Experience with participatory or qualitative learning methods, such as outcome harvesting or Most Significant Change.
- Experience with media monitoring or communications analytics.
- Knowledge of the arts, culture or creative sectors.

## **Practical information**

**Location and working arrangements**
This is a full-time position based in Nairobi, Kenya. You will work from the Nairobi office alongside the Senior Admin and Financial Management Specialist two to three days per week, with the option to work from home on the remaining days. Some travel within ARCH countries and internationally may be required.

**Salary and benefits**
The salary range is fixed at a junior level and informed by Kenyan NGO and INGO market benchmarks. The gross cash salary includes amounts equivalent to a 10% pension contribution and an allowance for health and life insurance, which employees arrange themselves. Salary, benefits and employment conditions will be discussed with shortlisted candidates.

jobs.title: Chargé-e de Communication
jobs.description:
**Organisation overview**

Tostan is a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization based in Dakar, Senegal, currently operating in five West African countries. At the strategic level, the organization is committed to continuing to develop its core competency of empowering education, and to document and scale the sustainable impact it creates on a range of issues. Tostan's flagship model, the three-year Community Empowerment Programme (CEP), has already reached thousands of communities in West and East Africa since 1991. Results in governance, education, health, economic empowerment, and the environment are currently being monitored, and Tostan is particularly proud to have played an important role in the large-scale empowerment of women and girls and in community abandonment of harmful practices such as female genital mutilation and child marriage.

As part of its strategic engagement plan 2023–2030, Tostan focuses on strategic scaling. The organization is developing new implementation strategies to support community leadership by unlocking broader systemic changes at the regional level. It also creates new models for sharing and replicating its programs with other development partners and expands its capacity to share Tostan's global approach to support and influence a range of local and global audiences. For more information, please visit: [www.tostan.org](http://www.tostan.org).

**Role overview**

The Communications team shapes Tostan’s narrative, advocacy, brand identity and donor visibility at community, national, regional and global levels. Tostan is part of a four-year regional programme on young women’s economic leadership in climate-resilient horticulture in Senegal and The Gambia. Within it, Tostan leads the community governance and social transformation component in partner communities across both countries.

The Communication Officer will show how changes in community governance and social norms open economic pathways for young women. The officer will turn field evidence into stories, public narratives and policy arguments, and will bring young women’s experience into the spaces where decisions on investment, finance and markets are made. Young women and community actors are the authors of this change. The officer’s job is to document it accurately and amplify their voices, never to speak in their place.

**Roles and responsibilities**

The Communication Officer reports to the Head of Communications and works in close operational coordination with the Senior Programme Manager.

1. **Programmatic Communication (35%)**

● Plan and conduct regular field missions to partner communities to document change through interviews, written stories, photography and short video, working with young women, community leaders, local authorities and producer groups.

● Work with the MEL and programme teams to turn monitoring data and evaluation findings into impact stories and case studies that show how community governance and norm change translate into economic opportunity.

● Contribute to the production of documentary films at country and regional levels, from story research and field coordination to review of edits.

● Produce local-language safeguarding communication materials in coordination with the Safeguarding Focal Points.

● Support the selection, training and mentoring of young women community storytellers, and edit their stories for publication.

● Maintain a well-catalogued multimedia library with documented consent for every image, recording and quote. ● Co-draft the communication sections of donor narrative reports with the MEL and programme leads.
2. **Digital Communications 20%**

● Produce regular content for Tostan’s and partners’ social media channels, newsletters and websites in French and English

● Feed and update the programme’s shared online knowledge platform and impact dashboard with stories, data and multimedia, in coordination with partner web teams.

● Run digital campaigns around programme milestones and international days related to women’s economic rights, food systems and climate.

● Track digital performance and report regularly on what works, what does not, and why.

● Apply co-branding, attribution and visibility guidelines across all digital assets.
3. **Advocacy (25%)**

● Contribute to policy briefs and thematic reports that turn field evidence into recommendations on public investment in women-led rural enterprises, on the integration of community-led models into national programmes, and on access to finance and markets.

● Support the preparation of the annual learning and advocacy forum, including content, speaker preparation and the meaningful participation of young women and community representatives.

● Prepare briefing notes, talking points and toolkits for Tostan leadership and programme staff attending policy dialogues, consortium meetings and regional events.

● Identify opportunities for young women and community leaders to speak directly in national, regional and global forums, and prepare them for these appearances with their informed consent.

● Monitor national policy processes, budget cycles and public debates in Senegal and The Gambia, and flag openings for advocacy to the Head of Communications.
4. **Media Relations (20%)**

● Build and maintain working relationships with journalists, editors and radio producers in national, regional and community media.

● Support the selection, training and mentoring of journalist fellows, including solutions-journalism workshops, and follow their reporting on women-led rural enterprise.

● Draft, translate and distribute press releases, media advisories and op-eds in French and English.

● Organise press trips to partner communities and coordinate media presence at key moments, including community engagement days and public declarations.

● Apply the media engagement protocol, prepare spokespeople and contribute to crisis response when needed. ● Monitor media coverage of young women’s economic rights and rural development, and report on how framing changes over time.

**Key relationships**

***Direct line Manager:*** Head of Communications

***Localisation :*** Thiès. Senegal

**Key Qualifications Skills, Education, and Experience**

● Bachelor’s Degree in Communications, Master’s degree, or similar advanced degree in relevant discipline preferred

● More than five years communications experience;

● Experience working in a development context and/or social sector organization

● Professional experience using and leading others on key communications technology tools such as web-based project and content management systems, social media tools as well as search engine optimization

**Characteristics**

● Ability to build relationships and work effectively within a complex, multi-stakeholder environment.

● Expertise using and overseeing the production of websites, online communities, videos, webinars, infographics and other multimedia web content

● Excellent analytical, written and verbal communication and presentation skills

● Ability to quickly distill complex concepts into interesting and digestible pieces

● Passionate belief in and commitment to Tostan’s mission to empower African communities to bring about sustainable development and positive social transformation based on respect for human rights

● Ability to work in a collaborative, co-creative team, bringing value to the team’s outcomes

**Language**

● High levels of English

● French as a minimum

● Other languages that Tostan works in would be an advantage – especially Wolof or Portuguese

> Our team is made up of people who strongly believe in Tostan’s mission to empower communities to develop and realize their vision for the future and inspire large-scale movements towards dignity for all.

jobs.title: AFGHANISTAN - Gender Responsive WASH Program Manager (F/M) -KABUL
jobs.description:
## About us

**Desired start date: 1st November 2026**
**Duration of the mission: 6 months**
**Location: Kabul**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONAL activities are implemented in Bamyan, Herat, Helmand, Nimroz and Farah provinces, with emergency activities that can be deployed all over the country. Operational bases are in Zaranj (capital of Nimroz Province), Farah, Herat and Bamyan city.

The team is now made of 125 national and 9 international employees with an annual budget of around 5.5 M EUR. SI currently implements WASH and Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR)/Natural Resource Management (NRM) programs.

There are currently 3 grants under implementation:

\- CDCS (French MoFA): covering emergency response interventions across several provinces.

\- ECHO consortium: In consortium with SCI (lead), INTERSOS and HI, the project responds to the returnees crisis at informal settlements and areas of return. SI response focuses on WASH, MPCA and winterization.

\- ECHO consortium: In consortium with INTERSOS (lead), and MdM, the project provides integrated Health, Nutrition, and WASH interventions in white areas. SI response focuses on WASH.

## About the job

**GENERAL OBJECTIVES**

-Lead the implementation of a strategic assessment and programme quality initiative aimed at strengthening the meaningful inclusion of women in WASH programming, ensuring delivery of agreed objectives, workplans and budgets.Oversee technical assessments, evidence generation, data analysis and production of operational recommendations to strengthen gender-responsive WASH programme design and service delivery.

-Coordinate technical engagement with implementing partners and relevant stakeholders throughout implementation.

-Build and maintain effective working relationships with women organisations, implementing partners, technical institutions and other relevant stakeholders to support project implementation and technical collaboration.

-Represent SI in technical meetings, workshops and coordination forums related to gender-responsive WASH programming, ensuring consistent communication and follow-up with external stakeholders.

-Support the development of practical tools, technical guidance and organisational learning to improve the integration of women's priorities into WASH programmes, and the inclusion, wellbeing and development of female colleagues within the organisation.

-Ensure activities are delivered in compliance with SI procedures, donor requirements and the evolving operational context, while maintaining appropriate communication and risk management.

**ISSUES AND SPECIFIC CHALLENGES**

-Working in a highly sensitive and changing operational environment affecting programming related to women and gender inclusion.
-Coordinating assessment activities across several provinces and with multiple partners.
-Managing large amounts of qualitative and quantitative data and translating findings into practical recommendations for gender-responsive WASH programming.
-Balancing operational realities with the objective of strengthening the meaningful participation and inclusion of women in WASH programmes.
-Ensuring effective coordination between programme, MEAL, grants and support departments.
-Frequent travel to project locations is required to support field activities, partner coordination and quality assurance in line with the security context and organizational procedures.

**PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS**

-Complete the ongoing assessment, including supervision of data collection, quality assurance and analysis.
-Finalize the assessment report and related technical products.
-Coordinate review and validation of findings with SI teams and external partners.
-Develop practical guidance and tools to strengthen the integration of women's priorities into WASH programme design and implementation.
-Support the integration of assessment recommendations into ongoing and future WASH programmes.
-Strengthen collaboration with women's organizations, technical partners and other stakeholders supporting the initiative.
-Ensure effective planning, reporting, external coordination and overall project management throughout implementation.

**SECURITY CONSTRAINTS**

Volatility of the context, but access to the field is possible for all areas of intervention

## Your profile

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

Bachelor's degree in a relevant field, such as Social Sciences, Public Health, Engineering, Development Studies, International Relations, Political Science, Management or another related discipline.

- Experience in the humanitarian sector : 3-4 years
- Experience on a similar position : 0-2 years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1\. Project management: Experience planning, coordinating and monitoring projects, assessments or research activities.

2\. Analysis and reporting: Ability to analyse information and produce clear reports, recommendations and other technical documents.

3\. Digital and data management: Good computer skills (Microsoft Office); experience with Kobo or other digital data collection tools is an asset.

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1\. Communication and stakeholder engagement: Strong interpersonal skills and ability to build effective relationships with partners and stakeholders.

2\. Organisation and problem-solving: Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently and adapt to changing circumstances.

3\. Leadership and teamwork: Ability to coordinate teams, facilitate collaboration and support capacity building.

**LANGUAGES**

1\. Proficiency in English is mandatory

2\. Proficiency in Dari

3\. Pashto is a plus

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2365 gross per month (2150 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 600.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every two months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

Guest House conditions: Well furnished Guest House is vailaible with the needed services. Electricity is limited but the guesthouse will be supported by the solar system and as well as generator. A small GYM is also available in the Guest House for maintaining routine excercises

Internet and telephone network: The staff will have dedicated SIM & Mobile for his/her communication 24/7

Restaurant & social life: Social life is limited to authorized restaurants and locations, and contact with other INGO staff, with a curfew.

jobs.title: Project Director (f/m/d) (100%)
jobs.description:
***Time Commitment***: The initial contract duration is until July 2027, with the possibility of an extension depending on project funding. A long-term commitment is preferred.

***Location***: Ioannina, Greece

**About the Organization and the Project**

Be Aware And Share (BAAS) is an independent non-profit organization that supports people affected by forced displacement and oppressed communities and stands against fortress Europe. Founded in 2015 in Switzerland, BAAS is primarily engaging in working with and for people on the move in Europe. Currently, the organization mainly focuses on its Community Center in Ioannina, Greece where a variety of services are offered. BAAS also carries out awareness-raising activities in Switzerland. All BAAS work is financed exclusively by donations.

**Job Description**

We are seeking a dedicated Project Director who will ensure the smooth and efficient running of our operations in Greece. In this dynamic role, you'll oversee project implementation, manage human and financial resources, take the lead for strategic steering, handle logistics, establish and maintain a comprehensive risk management system and support the project team in delivering high-quality services to people on the move. Your leadership will help BAAS navigate the complexities of solidarity work and drive our vision forward. You will be the key link between the operations in Greece and the organization in Switzerland, responsible for driving the Greek legal entity of BAAS and acting as its representative internally and externally. The Project Director reports to the Executive Board of Be Aware And Share.

**Main Responsibilities**

● Guide the strategic development of the project in alignment with the organization’s goals

● Handle all tasks related to the Greek legal entity and act as its representative

● Manage and support the project team, promoting a positive work environment

● Ensure sustainable human resource management, incl. recruitment processes

● Establish and maintain effective monitoring and evaluation systems as per donor requirements

● Conduct regular risk assessments, implement mitigation strategies, and ensure the safety of operations for staff, participants, and the organization

● Ensure adherence to organizational policies and carry out regular policy reviews

● Assist in the preparation and management of the project budget, ensuring financial accountability and sustainability

● Act as Safeguarding Focal Point for incident management and compliance

● Build and maintain relationships with local and regional partners, stakeholders, and communities to enhance project effectiveness and outreach

● Manage all logistical aspects, including apartments, transportation and related resources

**Requirements**

● Minimum 3 years of experience in operations management, preferably within the humanitarian or NGO sector

● Proven track record of managing projects effectively ● Strong understanding of logistics, budgeting, and compliance in non-profit operations

● Familiarity with data management and reporting systems

● Excellent leadership and team management abilities

● Ideally knowledge of Greek legal entities or experience with legal entities in other contexts

● Knowledge of project cycle management, including project identification, planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation

● Strong administrative and organisational skills, with the ability to work and manage autonomously, while also leading a team

● Ability and willingness to work in a dynamic and highly challenging environment

● Category B driver's license, manual transmission and willingness to drive in Greece

**Compensation and Benefits**

● EUR 1,300 net per month

● 21 days of annual leave (excl. public holidays)

● Wide scope for independent work structure and participation in organizational development

● Access to diverse networks and partnerships

● The opportunity to take on a responsible position in a committed and dynamic team and to make a crucial contribution to the realization of the BAAS operations in Greece

jobs.title: Country Operations Manager – Ukraine
jobs.description:
**Place:** Kiev or Kharkiv, Ukraine
**Starting date:** 1st December 2026
**Duration of contract:** 12 months

**Due to the urgency of this recruitment, we encourage interested candidates to submit their applications as soon as possible. We will be reviewing applications on an ongoing basis.**

Humanity & Inclusion is an independent and impartial aid organisation working in situations of poverty and exclusion, conflict and disaster. The organisation works alongside people with disabilities and vulnerable populations, taking action and bearing witness in order to respond to their essential needs, improve their living conditions and promote respect for their dignity and fundamental rights.

Since its creation in 1982, HI has run development & humanitarian projects in more than 55 countries and responded to numerous emergencies. Today, we have a budget of approximately 200 million euros, with 4,000 employees worldwide

At Handicap International-Humanity & Inclusion, we truly believe in the importance of inclusion and diversity within our organisation. This is why we are engaged to a disability policy to encourage the inclusion and integration of people with disabilities.

Please indicate if you require any special accommodation, even at the first interview. [For more information about the organisation.](https://www.hi.org/en/index)

**JOB CONTEXT:**

From February 2022, HI has re-opened a Country Programme in Ukraine to respond to the humanitarian needs triggered by the full-scale invasion of Ukraine by the Russian Federation.

In 2024, HI pillars of interventions are:

- Health: HI aims to improve access to quality physical rehabilitation and mental health and psychosocial support services (MHPSS) for conflict-affected vulnerable population.
- Protection: Given the scale of humanitarian and protection needs, HI intervenes at various levels to ensure that vulnerable conflict-affected populations have access to multi-sectoral services tailored to their needs. In addition, HI aims to foster a disability-inclusive humanitarian response.
- Humanitarian Mine Action: Ongoing attacks dangerously exacerbated Explosive Ordnance (EO) contamination in Ukraine.
- EORE/CPP: HI is conducting a multi-pronged approach to EO Risk Education (RE) and Conflict Preparedness and Protection (CPP).
- Advocacy
- NTS: HI is implementing Non-Technical Survey activities in Kharkivska Oblast since 2025.
- VA (Victim Assistance)

HI has 2 hubs, one in the East (based in Dnipro), one in the North East (based in Kharkiv), and the coordination office is in Kyiv.

**YOUR MISSION:**
Under the responsibility of the Country Director Ukraine, as Operations Manager you contribute within the country where you are based to the implementation of the mandate and the 10-year strategy of Humanity & Inclusion. You ensure optimal quality and impact of the projects implemented in the country, through a delegation system with appropriate control mechanisms. You share with all HI managers the responsibility of sound management and successful functioning of the global organization, through paradigm changes.

**Responsibility 1: Management**

1.1: Be the manager (direct report) of the 3 Project Managers in the country of assignment

- Foster team spirit and team functioning guaranteeing synergies and exchange of good practices between Project Managers and with head office colleagues.
- Recruit and contribute to the professional development, autonomy and well-being at work of the Project Managers: in link with the corresponding professional channels, set formalized individual objectives, ensure coherence between HI’s needs and competencies and motivation of his/her teams, develop and monitor competence development plan, evaluate individual performance, contribute to career evolution.

**Responsibility 2: Contribution to the Programme’s Operational Strategy and HI frameworks & regulations**

2.1: Contribute to the development of the Programme’s Operational Strategy, and to its implementation and annual monitoring

- With assessment of ongoing projects, contribution to context and sectorial analysis, contribution to fundraising strategy, to resource sizing, to M&E tool.
- Contribute, with his/her portfolio of projects and donors’ data, to the annual monitoring of the StratOp.
- In case of crisis/emergency, implement the framework and set-up determined by HI Operations Director.
- Actively lead to the development of opportunities, partnerships and strategy in new potential areas of implementation.
- Actively support start-up of new programmes and operations in current areas of implementation (education and preparedness).

2.2: Implement the project part of the Programme’s Operational Strategy

- Contribute to size and plan necessary resources, recruitment of the Project Managers (ensure the fit between competencies and the projects’ challenges and ambitions), develop and monitor their competence development plan, in link with the corresponding professional channels and with the Human Resources Manager.
- Develop regular contacts with current and potential donors at field level and liaise with the Programme Director, Project Managers and Technical Unit to check coherence with overall Programming and fundraising strategy.
- Within the operational framework defined in the StratOp, identify and transform funding opportunities in new potential areas, conduct the design and writing of new projects with relevant colleagues in new potential areas of operations.
- In link with the Technical Unit Manager, identify and develop local partnerships and/or consortia with NGOs, institutions, companies, on technical priorities or important topics at National Level and in new potential areas of intervention.

2.4: Ensure sound management and monitoring of projects under his/her responsibility (New potential areas of intervention)

- In link with the Technical Unit Manager and the MEAL Unit, ensure that HI technical quality standards are applied in the projects, and monitor the implementation of recommendations from support missions, evaluations and donor audits.
- Ensure compliance with project donors’ rules and regulations, including visibility.
- With the support of the MEAL Manager, deploy all adequate tools that will allow financial control and project monitoring, compliance with HI policies and frameworks, and the respect of contractual obligations towards donors: consolidation, control and reporting to the Ops Manager operational and organizational elements (dashboards and corrective measures, unrestricted funds consumption, beneficiaries’ data…).
- Facilitate internal audits (operational, financial and organizational), and ensure the implementation of their recommendations on his/her responsibility area with relevant colleagues.

2.5: With both operational opportunities and risks in mind, contribute to the monitoring and analysis made by HAS, Operations and CD, and propose mitigation measures when relevant in new potential areas of intervention.

- Implement analysis and monitoring of risks & opportunities related to HI presence and activities; implement risk mitigation actions at his/her level; and ensure the implementation of a humanitarian watch.

**Responsibility 3: Influence**

3.1: Support develop external influence of HI (forums, operational & strategic alliances, etc.) and the external representation of the organization (events, media) at the National Level

- Can represent HI vis-à-vis local, national, traditional, political, military and diplomatic authorities and bodies; and international organizations and coordination mechanisms & system.
- Take on the messages of HI global advocacy to all relevant external parties.
- Develop local partnerships.

**CHARACTERISTICS OF THE POSITION:**

- The security situation in Ukraine remains relatively stable, although air alert is frequently active. However, markets, restaurants and cafes are open, and life continues as normal. There is a strict curfew, the hours depend on the region.

**YOUR PROFILE:**

- You have at least 5 years of professional experience in humanitarian / early recovery contexts,
- You have at least 3 years of experience in management of field bases and/or programs,
- A solid work experience in one or more of the core sectors is a strong asset: health (physical rehabilitation, P&O, psychosocial support), protection, disability mainstreaming / inclusion, and/or livelihoods, or education,
- Previous experience in designing and managing programs with local partners is a strong asset.
- You demonstrate strong teal management and organizational skills, a high level of autonomy and initiative,
- Fluency in oral and written English is compulsory.

**CONDITIONS:**
At HI, the conditions offered are up to your commitment and adapted to the context of your mission: [Join the team](https://hi.org/en/join-the-team)

- 12 months International contract starting from **1st December 2025**;
- The international contract provides social cover adapted to your si2uation:
- Unemployment insurance benefits for EU nationals;
- Pension scheme;
- Medical coverage with 50% of employee contribution;
- Repatriation insurance paid by HI;
- Salary from 2869 € gross/month upon experience;
- Perdiem: 597 € net/month - paid in payroll
- Hardship: 500 € net/month paid with your salary;
- Paid leaves: 25 days per year;
- R&R: 5 days every 8 weeks + possible transport/package support;
- Position unaccompanied:
- Payment for travel costs (air ticket & visa) and transport of your personal effects;
- Mission of more than 12 months: a child allowance of 100€ per month, per child (from the second child) paid in payroll
- Housing: Collective taken in charge by HI;
- If you are resident in the country: local package.

jobs.title: Senior QA Tester (Maternity Cover)
jobs.description:
**Senior QA Tester (Maternity Cover)**

**6-month Fixed Term Contract. Full Time. Working hours may need to be aligned to UK working hours time zone**

**The start date for this role will be January 2027**

**Location: New Delhi, India**

**Salary: INR 17,70,337 per year (pro rata)**

*If we receive a high volume of applications, we reserve the right to close the advert before the scheduled closing date. Therefore, we encourage interested applicants to apply at their earliest convenience.*

**About us**

Christian Aid exists to create a world where everyone can live a full life, free from poverty. We are a global movement of people, churches and local organisations who passionately champion dignity, equality and justice worldwide. We are the changemakers, the peacemakers, the mighty of heart.

We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace, and recognise the value this brings in forming strong, creative and high performing teams. We welcome applications from all sections of the community, and from those with experience from outside of the voluntary sector. And no, you don’t have to be Christian to work here – we encourage people of all faiths and none to apply. We just ask that everyone lives out our values of dignity, equality, justice and love. We value a good work-life balance, so we’re open to part-time and flexible working. We also offer hybrid working for our office-based colleagues.

**About the role**

Reporting in to the Digital Product Owner, the **Senior QA Tester** will take ownership of Quality Assurance (QA) within Christian Aid’s core Digital Team, ensuring the delivery of high-quality, reliable, and user-friendly websites that are consistent and coherent.

This strategic role will embed agile testing practices, streamline QA processes, and foster a culture of continuous learning and improvement within the Digital Team and the CRM Team, with an equal division of time between the two teams based in different divisions.​

Some of the main responsibilities of the **Senior QA Tester** will include:

- Identify, manage and mitigate risks related to both digital and CRM projects ensuring high quality work that is impactful.
- Collaborate with the Digital Product Owner and CRM Technical Lead to verify that all designs and technical outputs meet quality standards and align with project goals and wider organisational values and goals.
- Collaborate with the Digital Optimisation Analyst and CRM Technical Lead to ensure all test results are properly tracked, analysed, and shared to support continuous learning, feedback and optimisation.
- Design, write and execute visual regression and behaviour-driven testing for every code release, identifying and reporting any issues to the development teams to support a culture of continuous learning and improvement.
- Report and track defects: Log defects, provide clear information for developers to fix them, and retest to verify the issues are resolved.
- Manage continuous improvement and optimise testing processes to enhance efficiency, effectiveness, consistency and coherency.
- Utilise relevant analytics tools to measure feature performance against expected outcomes and provide actionable feedback to guide future development.
- Create and execute manual scripts/scenarios, implementing a consistent standard across all CRM developments supporting with quality and consistency.
- Manage 3rd party conformance with QAT & UAT standards by proactively raising identified issues and putting forward suggested improvements supporting with a culture of continuous learning and improvement.
- Provide daily progress reports through stand-ups and parking lot meetings building relationships based on trust and openness.

**About you**

**Who we are looking for**

**Essential:**

- Higher education or equivalent experience obtained in a relevant subject area.
- Substantial experience working with content management systems (CMS), particularly Drupal.
- Developed ability in application of usability, accessibility and security standards.
- Understanding of cross browser limitations and work arounds.
- Understanding of optimisation techniques (both in file weight and perceived/actual rendering speed) and performance measurement.
- Developed ability to interpret complex communications briefs from others.
- Highly developed communication and collaboration skills and ability to work in an Agile team environment.
- Highly developed interpersonal, negotiation and influencing skills.
- Experience of Dynamics 365 CRM CE.
- Experience with Cypress / Percy / PlatformSH / SEMRush
- Competency in test automation, test-driven development (TDD), and exploratory testing, along with a general understanding of development principles, programming languages
- Experience of working with developers to unit test key use case scenarios

**Further information**

*At Christian Aid we strive to be an inclusive and diverse employer and recognise the value that this brings in helping to build strong, creative and high performing teams.*

*We are actively encouraging racialised minorities, LGBTQ+, people with disabilities, returning parents or carers who are re-entering work after a career break, people with caring responsibilities, people from low socioeconomic backgrounds, women, and older workers to apply. This is because these groups are under-represented within our teams, especially at senior level, and we recognise and value the contributions members of these groups make to strong, creative and high performing teams.*

*We have a strong Christian ethos and we encourage applications from all faiths. Applicants will be expected to demonstrate an understanding of and sympathy with Christian Aid’s faith identity.*

*All successful candidates will require a DBS/police check appropriate to the role and location and a Counter Terrorism Sanction check as part of your clearance for commencing your role with us. We also participate in the* [***Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme***](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/)*. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.*

*This role requires applicants to have the right to live and work in the country where this position is based and undertake the role that you have been offered.
