jobs.title: Security Officer (remote)
jobs.description:
**Position Title:** Security Officer

**Location:** Home-based, providing remote support to HQ and the Gaza team

**Reporting to:** Programme Manager

**Duration:** Six-months

**Closing date of applications**: 2 November 2026

**Requirements for the role**

- At least five years’ experience in humanitarian security.
- Sound knowledge of NGO operating environments, security procedures and duty-of-care requirements.
- Familiarity with donor procedures and reporting expectations.
- Proficiency in English and French; knowledge of Arabic is an advantage.
- Experience using security information, incident-reporting and analysis platforms.
- Good understanding of governance and compliance requirements.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills

The MENTOR Initiative (‘MENTOR’) is a humanitarian organisation specialising in disease control and improving access to healthcare in emergency settings currently across countries in Africa, the Middle East and South America. MENTOR is the leading organisation dedicated to the control of malaria and other vector-borne diseases in complex, vulnerable settings.

MENTOR supports large scale disease control interventions working with communities affected by emergencies such as conflict and natural disasters and at higher risk of diseases. We also help build the technical and operational capacity of local and international partners to incorporate medium- and long-term disease control systems into their operations and country strategy.

**Overall job purpose**

The Security Officer (Gaza) provides dedicated, security advice and remote coordination support to MENTOR’s Gaza team. The role focuses on the safe planning and delivery of large-scale medical-supply distributions across Gaza and related staff deployments.

Working remotely in support of HQ, the postholder supports senior and line managers through timely security analysis, review of context-specific arrangements, staff preparation, contingency planning, and incident and crisis-management support. Gaza remains the primary focus, although HQ management may request proportionate support for other MENTOR country programmes.

The role is advisory. Accountability for security management and operational decisions remains with the relevant line managers and designated HQ managers.

**Task and responsibilities**

**Security analysis, planning and advice**

- Monitor security threats affecting Gaza through reliable security platforms and networks, analyse their operational implications, and share timely and relevant information to HQ and field teams.
- Advise senior managers and relevant line managers on security policy, risk, security procedures, and the implications of the Gaza context for planned activities.
- Develop, review and update the Gaza Security Plan, risk assessments, standard operating procedures, movement protocols, communications arrangements, hibernation, relocation and evacuation contingencies, and other context-specific security documentation, in coordination with the Gaza team and HQ management.
- Review security arrangements for the distribution of medical supplies and other projected activities, and provide documented advice to HQ on feasibility, risk-reduction measures, required resources, and conditions for implementation.
- Support HQ’s preparation of deployment, suspension, relocation and evacuation decisions by providing current analysis, clearly defined risk thresholds, options and recommendations; final decisions remain with the designated HQ managers, except where delegated emergency authority applies.
- Define and support appropriate security briefing, induction, training and debriefing for personnel working on or deploying to Gaza, including the development and delivery of Gaza-specific training packages and, where appropriate, training of trainers.
- Advise on the suitability and procurement of security-related equipment and services, including communications equipment, insurance, specialist training and external consultancy, and identify financial or human-resource gaps affecting safe implementation.
- Produce and coordinate security-incident reports when required, ensuring compliance with organisational, legal, insurance and donor reporting protocols, and maintain accurate security records for accountability purposes.
- Collate and analyse security incidents and identify lessons learned, and recommend updates to policies, procedures, training and operational plans.
- Assist managers during security incidents and support the activation and functioning of MENTOR’s crisis-management arrangements for serious or high-profile incidents affecting Gaza.
- Coordinate with the HQ Programme Manager, the Gaza team and other relevant departments on projected activities, ensuring that appropriate security assessments, preparedness measures and duty-of-care considerations are addressed in advance.
- Assist, when requested, with the recruitment or technical assessment of security-related personnel and with the review of security plans produced by field teams.
- Contribute to monitoring the effectiveness of security management, promote a positive security culture, and support departmental and organisational working groups as required.
- Provide proportionate remote security advice or technical support to other MENTOR country programmes only when needed and specifically requested by HQ management, while ensuring that Gaza remains the primary operational priority.

**Other duties**

- Carry out other security-related tasks assigned by the Security Officer or designated HQ management, consistent with the advisory nature of the role and the priority requirements of the Gaza response.

The MENTOR Initiative is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity in the organisation. We ensure the constant non-discrimination throughout the recruitment process.

The MENTOR Initiative is committed to promoting diversity and gender equality and strongly encourages candidates from under-represented backgrounds to apply.

The MENTOR Initiative applies a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation, abuse, mistreatment or harassment, and other types of unethical behaviour including fraud.

The MENTOR Initiative will contact previous employers of applicants to determine if they have any history of violating international standards and codes of conduct relating to such matters.

jobs.title: NIGERIA - FIELD COORDINATOR (M/F) - NORTH WEST
jobs.description:
## About us

**Desired start date: 15/01/2027**
**Duration of the mission: 6 months**
**Location: Gusau**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

SI has been present in Nigeria for 10 years - since 2016 in Northeast Nigeria and 2020 in the Northwest.

SI’s coordination office is in Abuja and there are 2 regional base: In Maiduguri for the NE, including 2 sub base in Monguno and Ngala. In Gusau (Zamfara state) for the NW programs inclusing 1 sub offices in Birnin Kebbi (Kebbi State).

In the Northeast, SI operates in 3 LGAs of Borno state (Monguno, Ngala and Konduga). SI has also intervened in other LGAs includingJere, Maiduguri MMC, Dikwa, Gwoza and Bama in the recent past.as well as emergency operation in Adamawa State.

In the Northwest, SI intervenes in 5 LGAs of Zamfara state: Gusau, Anka, Talata Mafara, Zurmi and Kaura Namoda. SI also newly opened a base (2026) in Birnin Kebbi, to operate in 6 LGAs of Kebbi State related to an INTPA project. SI also carry out emergency interventions in Sokoto and Katsina States.

The annual volume of the Nigeria mission is between 6 and 7 million USD.

SI's mission in Nigeria responds to the critical needs of populations affected by conflict, natural disasters and epidemics in the North East and North West of the country, through its traditional sectors of intervention, namely WASH, FSL and Shelter. SI is currently funded by a number of institutional donors, including ECHO, CDCS, INTPA, SIDA RRM and NHF (US funding), with the possibility of further funding depending on the development of the mission's projects.

The mission also relies on a partnership approach, localization and good coordination to strengthen its intervention in the country. It works closely with local partners and participates actively in existing coordination platforms.

Mission staff : 165
Northwest staff : 40

## About the job

**General objective:**

The Field Coordinator is the representative of the organization at field level.
Context
To maintain SI positioning known as one of the main WASH actor in the NW and in particular in Zamfara and Sokoto State.
To maintain SI active participation in all foras in the NW and keep a close relationship with MDAs, local authorities, other humanitarian organizations and the NIF as well.
Security
To monitor the security situation in the NW and in particular within SI program implementations areas : Zamfara, Sokoto and Kebbi.
In Kebbi State the security situation is very volatile hence there is a need for a close monitoring of the context for a better understanding of the dynamics of opposite groups to minimize the risk of SI in the area ;
Logistics
To ensure framework agreement are in place both for log and program
To encourage suppliers to comply with national laws for collaboration with SI
To ensure old furniture and equipment are identified for replacement or auctioning
Working closely with the coordination to ensure laptops and other equipment are included in all new proposals
To ensure that experienced electricians and plumbers are identified for framework agreements signing in Gusau.
Admin
To ensure regular budget follow up meeting (monthly) and share any alert to coordination
To ensure budget tools (OFU/LFU) are regularly updated and forecasted until the end of every project.
Programs support
To support the program Managers to ensure close monitoring of their projects implementation and timely delivery of the project with the required quality
To ensure use of standards SI tools such as distribution list and timely delivery of reports : internal and external : APU, consortium partners reports and donor reports .etc.

**The main challenges:**

Humanitarian sector in transition and with challenging funding perspective
Dynamic security context requiring strong analysis capacity and decision taking
Multiple bases in different geographical area requiring strong management follow up and support

**Security constraints:**

Position based in Gusau which remain a secured area but with strict security procedure to follow up (level 3). Movement outside GH/office has to be made by SI vehicle, no walking policy and some area are restricted to go.
The city of Gusau is implementing a curfew from 10 PM to 6 AM.
FC NW is also supervising the sub base in Birnin Kebbi (Kebbi state) requiring frequent movement to support the team accordingly - movement are linked to security approval.

## Your profile

**Diploma and experiences :**

Diploma : Master Degree in humanitarian/development studies, social sciences, management or other related discipline

EXPERIMENT IN THE HUMANITARIAN SECTOR : 5 years and more

EXPERIMENT ON SIMILAR POSITIONS : 3/4 years

**SKILLS :**

**Technical skills :**

1. Substantial experience in a similar or senior management position in an overseas INGO environment, Experience in SI sectors of expertise (WASH, FSL, Shelter, Emergency)
2. Experience of strategic planning and Team management
3. Capacity to deal with a multiplicity of issues, to self - update and learn very quickly from a highly and constantly evolving environment / ability to analyze information quickly and accurately / ability to manage and prioritize a high workload and multiple tasks with tight deadlines / ability to communicate clearly internally and externally to represent SI (MoUs, negotiations, governance…) / good understanding of security management / proven ability to deal with local authorities and Local partners.

**Transversal skills :**

1. Proven experience in managing teams notably in complex ethnic and/or religious contexts or sensitive environments, Willingness to work in a volatile security context
2. Good knowledge of the humanitarian project cycle management, and operational management
3. Diplomacy and strong communication skills, ability to take initiatives, good problem-solving skills in day to day and crisis situations,. Understanding of and commitment to SI’s mission and values.

**Languages :**

1. English (fluent - mandatory)
2. Hausa (an asset)
3. French (an asset)

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3080 gross per month (2800 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 600.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

Accomodation in Guest House in Gusau with a comfortable environment, in spite of limited movements outside of the compound for security reasons (movement by car only - curfew in city from 10 PM) . The Guest House offers good living conditions, with private bedroom and bathroom and shared & comfortable common spaces. Electricity and internet are available at the office and at the GH at all times. All essential good (food, hygiene etc..) can be bought locally in the supermarkets in Gusau and restaurant are also available. Sport centers (gym, football, tennis, swimming pool for leisure ... etc) are also accessible in some secured part of Gusau.

Periodically passing through Abuja (Coordination office) to meet with coordination. Abuja is comfortable and safe. Abuja has good markets, high standard medical services, and additional social or sport gathering that ca be used while visiting.

jobs.title: SOUTH SUDAN - GRANTS MANAGER (M/F) - JUBA
jobs.description:
## About us

**Desired start date:** 08/02/2027
**Duration of the mission: 6** months
**Location:** Juba - South Sudan

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in some twenty countries, the SI teams – 2500 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONAL (SI) has been operating in South Sudan since 2006, conducting activities in emergency and post emergency context.

\- Food insecurity is one of the highest in the world due to recurring shocks (consecutive years of widespread flooding, conflict-based displacement), and an ongoing protracted macro-economic crisis.
\- The country also faces cholera outbreaks on a yearly basis, has very limited sanitation coverage and safe water access remain a challenge for most of the population.
\- On top of these chronic situations, South Sudan has been highly impacted by the war that started in Sudan in April 2023. As of mid 2026, more than 1,300,000 people have entered South Sudan, the vast majority entering through the Joda/ Wunthow border point in Renk County, Upper Nile State (northern part of South Sudan).
\- In 2025 internal tensions increased at government level and have led to wide spread conflicts within the country. Elections at the end of 2026 may not happen as planned.
\- An Ebola outbreak is currently at its doors in DRC and Uganda.
As a result, 10 million are in need of humanitarian assistance as of 2026.

**SI sectors of intervention:**
\- The portfolio includes both WASH & FSL activities. SI's expertise in running emergency WaSH intervention is highly acknowledged by all WaSH actors and donors. SI has also been one of the first responders of the cholera response. Recent fundings have allowed increasing significantly the FSL component on the mission
**Areas of operation:**
**SI is present:**
\- In Upper Nile, SI has an office in Renk and a sub-office in Malakal. The response has focused on cholera and drought while maintaining life saving WASH services for returnees and refugees in the two main transit centres of the country.
\- SI has opened a base in Ulang in 2025 (State of Upper Nile but under another base/Field Coordinator)
\- In addition, SI has a rapid emergency team (ERRM) based in Juba, who is being deployed following Rapid Needs Assessment in flood, epidemic or conflict induced displacement in the country.
**Size of operations:**
In 2026, the mission’s estimated budget is around USD 10 million, and 140 employees following an ongoing scale up on the last quarter of 2025.
The mission is currently funded by ECHO (3 grants), DoS, CDCS, FIFSAN, SSHF, Norway MoFA, FCDO.

## About the job

**General objective:**

Under the supervision and with the support of the Grants and Partnership Coordinator, the Grant Manager role on general Grant Manager tasks and on supporting project development and diversification of funding sources.

Specifically, he/she is in charge of:

• Contributing to the mission’s strategic development.

• Monitoring and identifying funding opportunities in line with SI country and global strategy.

• Overseeing compilation of timely and high-quality proposals, reports and contract modification requests for submission to donors and consortium partners.

• Monitoring compliance with donor procedures throughout the grant cycle and building capacity of new and existing staff on internal accountability tools and donor procedures.

• Proactively following-up on donor contractual obligations, from contracting to closing and archiving, and ensuring contractual obligations are known and understood by relevant staff/departments.

• Developing partnerships with national partners and reinforcing SI localization strategy (tools, partner identification)

• Managing the partnership with other partners of consortiums

**The main challenges:**

• Contributing to the mission’s strategic development.

• Diversifying fundings sources in line with SI country and global strategy.

• Increasing the quality of reporting and proposal development.

**Priorities of the 2-3 first months:**

• Finalize the back and forth with the donors on the proposals, especially the ECHO HIP proposals

• Follow-up on donor contractual obligations on the current and future donor contract

• Management and capacity building of the Reporting and Communication Officer under the direct management

## Your profile

**Education / academic background:**

- Master Degree in humanitarian/development studies, social sciences, management or other related discipline.
- 3-4 years in the humanitarian sector
- 1-2 years on a similar position

**Specific skills and experience:**

- Experience in developing proposals for institutional donors.
- Experience in capacity building of staff.
- Experience in developing concept notes and strategy papers.
- Excellent writing skills & Excel usage.
- Experience in managing audits and compliance risks.
- Experience in budget follow-up.
- Experience in developing localization strategies.
- Good organization skills. Rigorous & detail-oriented profile
- Good coordination and diplomacy.
- Good stress management.
- Experience working with SI (or a similar organization) is an asset.
- Prior experience in South Sudan would be considered as an asset.

**Language:**

- Fluent in English, written and spoken.
- Arabic is an asset.

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**

**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2150 gross per month (2150 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 700.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

- The Grants Manager is living in a shared guesthouse with the other international staffs.
- Individual room, with electricity 24/7.
- Internet and Phone network available
- Restaurants and international food are available

There is an internal curfew at night for international staffs - different zones are set (6-8-10PM). Curfew can be reduced based on security updates
There is one driver available on evenings for movements out of office hours, 2 drivers during weekends daytime.
Access to activities is possible for all (and encouraged!).
In coordination, movements outside of Juba town (besides intervention location) for leisure are not permitted.

jobs.title: Research, Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) Officer
jobs.description:
**Research, Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) Officer**

LOCATION: Kakamega, Kenya (with field travel as required)

REPORTS TO :MEAL Coordinator

**Employment type: Full-time | Application deadline: October 30, 2026**

**ABOUT ICS SP**

For over 30 years, ICS SP (Investing in Children and their Societies) has worked across Africa to build safe and nurturing environments for children and families. Our programming spans Violence and Exploitation, Early Childhood Care and Development, Inclusive and Safe Education, and Sustainable Livelihoods. Visit [www.icsafrica-sp.org](http://www.icsafrica-sp.org) to learn more about us.

**PURPOSE OF THE ROLE**

Reporting to the MEAL Coordinator, the Research, Monitoring & Evaluation Officer will lead day-to-day implementation of results-based monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning activities for ICS SP programmes supported from Kakamega. The Officer will work with programme teams and partners to develop and operate robust M&E systems, generate credible evidence of results, strengthen reporting and use learning to improve programme quality and effectiveness.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Results-based monitoring, evaluation and programme quality**

- Develop, implement and regularly refine results-based M&E systems, results frameworks, indicator definitions, monitoring plans and practical data-collection tools in collaboration with the MEAL Coordinator and programme teams; align these with ICS SP and donor requirements.
- Monitor project activities, outputs and progress against approved plans and targets, identify performance gaps and implementation of bottlenecks, and recommend corrective actions to project management.
- Plan and undertake routine field monitoring and data verification visits; prepare clear findings, action points and follow-up reports for programme teams and management.
- Coordinate field-level inputs to baseline assessments, evaluations, research and other studies, ensuring sound methods, reliable evidence and follow-up on recommendations.

**2. Data management, analysis and quality assurance**

- Maintain accurate, timely, and secure indicator-tracking systems, project databases and supporting records, with consistent data collection and documentation procedures.
- Conduct data quality checks, cleaning, verification and analysis; reconcile figures across field tools, databases and reports, and strengthen completeness, accuracy and timeliness of project and partner submissions.
- Analyze quantitative and qualitative data, including appropriately authorized child protection case-management, capacity-strengthening and awareness-raising data, and present findings responsibly and with relevant disaggregation.
- Produce dashboards, evidence briefs and data visualizations to communicate project results and inform operational decisions, donor reports and programme improvements.

**3. Planning, reporting and M&E capacity strengthening**

- Prepare annual and quarterly M&E component plans and budgets and contribute to consolidated project work plans, target-setting exercises, and annual programme reviews.
- Prepare and consolidate monthly, quarterly and annual results reports, key-result summaries, M&E reports, and evidence-based inputs to management and donor reporting.
- Organize and facilitate M&E trainings, review meetings and workshops, including concepts, agendas, tools and learning materials; coach programme staff, partners and community structures in using the M&E framework.
- Support project coordinators to prepare performance reviews and planning workshops, using verified results to identify challenges, lessons, and recommendations.

**4. Accountability, safeguarding and responsible data management**

- Strengthen community feedback and accountability mechanisms and support appropriate documentation, referral and escalation of concerns in line with ICS SP procedures.
- Ensure ethical data collection, informed consent, confidentiality, child safeguarding and data protection standards in monitoring, research, case-related data and dissemination of findings.
- Promote safe, inclusive and participatory M&E approaches, with particular care in engagement with children and vulnerable communities.

**5. Research, knowledge sharing and coordination**

- Identify and document evidence-based success stories, achievements, lessons learned and good practices and translate findings into practical recommendations for programme improvement.
- Compile and disseminate relevant information from project data systems to programme management, donors and other authorized stakeholders in accessible formats.
- Facilitate learning exchanges, periodic reflection, and the integration of evaluation and research findings into organizational knowledge management, planning, and strategy.
- Collaborate with government agencies, NGOs, research actors and M&E networks; represent ICS SP in relevant technical forums as delegated by the MEAL Coordinator.

**REQUISITE REQUIREMENTS**

- Bachelor’s degree in Monitoring and Evaluation, Statistics, Economics, Social Sciences, Community Development or related field.
- Minimum five years of progressively responsible M&E experience in NGO, child-focused, community development or related social-impact programming.
- Demonstrated ability to develop and implement results-based M&E systems, indicators and tools, conduct field monitoring and data quality assessments, and prepare high-quality results and donor reports.
- Proficiency in Excel and digital data collection (such as Kobo Toolbox or ODK); experience using statistical analysis or data visualization tools is an added advantage.
- Understanding quantitative and qualitative research, evaluations, case-related data analysis, and ethical monitoring approaches.
- Strong planning, organization, communication, report writing, facilitation, analytical judgement and stakeholder engagement skills; ability to coach programme teams and partners.
- Commitment to safeguarding, confidentiality and responsible handling of personal and case-related data.
- Excellent written and spoken English and Kiswahili; ability and willingness to travel regularly to project sites.

ICS SP’s absolute priority is protecting children, vulnerable communities and our own staff. We have zero tolerance of incidents of violence, abuse and exploitation of children and other people in the communities we serve, whether committed by our staff or others connected to our work. Successful applicants will be required to sign and adhere to our safeguarding, child protection and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) code of conduct and policies.

jobs.title: Supervisory Board Members
jobs.description:
**Provided by: GP MENA ELECTION COMMITTEE**

**Deadline: November 9, 2026**

**For: Potential Supervisory Board candidates**

**Targeted Countries: Morocco, Tunisia & Jordan**

Greenpeace Middle East and North Africa is seeking senior, values-driven leaders to join its Supervisory Board and help guide the organization through its next phase of impact and growth.

Operating in a region shaped by accelerating climate impacts, environmental pressures, conflict, economic uncertainty and rapid change, Greenpeace MENA needs strong, independent and forward-looking Supervisory Board members to remain resilient, relevant and impactful.

**About Greenpeace MENA**

Greenpeace MENA is part of the global Greenpeace network, working across the Middle East and North Africa to advance climate and environmental justice and a greener, fairer and more peaceful future.

Our vision is a MENA region where its natural richness and communities are protected and where future generations can thrive with dignity in a peaceful, sustainable and just future.

**Who we are looking for**

Greenpeace MENA is a dynamic, high-functioning regional organization seeking Supervisory Board members who can complement our current mix of competencies and help us navigate emerging organizational, environmental and regional challenges.

We are seeking candidates who bring a combination of:

- Board-level or senior leadership experience
- Strong strategic leadership and sound judgement
- A strong understanding of the MENA region and its cultural, social, economic, political and environmental context
- Experience leading or governing organizations through complexity, uncertainty, growth or transformation
- The ability to provide independent oversight and strategic perspective
- Commitment to Greenpeace MENA’s mission, independence and values
- Strong networks and exposure across MENA and/or internationally
- The capacity and commitment to contribute actively to an engaged and accountable Supervisory Board
- Residence in, or a strong connection to, the MENA region is highly desirable.

**Specific skills and experience**

We are particularly interested in candidates who bring one or more of the following:

- Strategic leadership and Board governance
- Board-level or senior executive leadership
- Organizational development, transformation and change leadership
- Risk, resilience and crisis governance
- Fundraising, philanthropy and resource mobilization
- Legal, regulatory or institutional governance
- Climate, environment, sustainability or climate justice
- Strategic communications, media, public engagement or movement building
- Strong regional and international networks and exposure, particularly across civil society, philanthropy, and relevant institutions

**Role of the Supervisory Board**

The Supervisory Board safeguards Greenpeace MENA’s mission, integrity, independence, accountability and long-term sustainability, providing strategic oversight while maintaining a clear distinction between governance and day-to-day management.

Key responsibilities include:

- Overseeing Greenpeace MENA’s strategic direction and long-term organizational development
- Approving organizational strategy and major strategic decisions
- Approving multi-year and annual budgets and annual financial statements
- Overseeing organizational risk, resilience and good governance
- Overseeing key governance and organizational policies
- Recruiting the Executive Director, setting their remuneration, and overseeing performance and accountability.
- Safeguarding Greenpeace MENA’s independence, values and organizational integrity

**Independence and eligibility**

Supervisory Board members must exercise independent judgment and avoid actual or perceived conflicts of interest.

Candidates cannot:

- Be current employees of Greenpeace or have left Greenpeace employment within the previous year
- Have a vested interest that conflicts with Greenpeace’s objectives or independence
- Be directly employed or contracted by governments, ministries or embassies
- Hold a material financial interest in an industry, company or entity that is a target of Greenpeace campaigns

**Commitment and term**

This is a voluntary, non-remunerated governance role.

Board members are expected to participate actively in Board and committee work, including approximately four Board meetings per year, committee responsibilities and occasional ad hoc engagement, requiring around 15–20 hours per quarter.

Supervisory Board members are appointed for a three-year term, renewable once for one additional three-year term.

**Interested in helping shape Greenpeace MENA’s future?**

If Greenpeace MENA’s mission resonates with you and you believe your leadership experience, expertise, perspective and networks can contribute to our next chapter, we would be pleased to hear from you.

Please download and complete the [**Expression of Interest form**](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1J6Geq-sohq93EhvV8irhumhdvS-TMIil/edit), outlining your relevant Board or senior leadership experience and the contribution you could make to the Greenpeace MENA Supervisory Board. Once completed, please upload the **Expression of Interest** form along with your **CV** and **Cover Letter** through this [**link** ](https://gpmena.bamboohr.com/careers/112)no later than **November 9, 2026**.

Shortlisted candidates will be invited to meet with the Greenpeace MENA Election Committee. All applications will be treated with appropriate confidentiality.

jobs.title: Finance & Administration Officer
jobs.description:
**Finance & Administration Officer**

LOCATION:Kisumu, Kenya (supporting Western Kenya offices; field travel required)

REPORTS TO :Finance & Operations Manager

Employment type: Full-time | Application deadline: 30 October 2026

**ABOUT ICS SP**

For over 30 years, ICS SP (Investing in Children and their Societies) has worked across Africa to build safe and nurturing environments for children and families. Our programming spans Violence and Exploitation, Early Childhood Care and Development, Inclusive and Safe Education, and Sustainable Livelihoods. Visit [www.icsafrica-sp.org](http://www.icsafrica-sp.org) to learn more about us.

**PURPOSE OF THE ROLE**

Based in Kisumu and reporting to the Finance & Operations Manager, the Finance & Administration Officer will provide financial management, grants compliance, accounting and administrative support to ICS SP operations and programmes across Western Kenya, including Kisumu, Kakamega, Nyamira and other field locations as required. The Officer will support budgeting and grant management throughout the project cycle, ensure accurate and timely accounting and financial reporting, maintain effective internal controls, and enable efficient office and field operations in line with ICS SP policies and donor requirements.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Financial accounting and transaction management**

- Ensure complete, accurate and timely recording of transactions in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, with proper coding to projects, budget lines, donors and offices, and adequate supporting documentation.
- Review payment requests, staff accountability and supplier documentation for completeness, accuracy, authorization and compliance; coordinate timely processing of approved payments and maintain orderly electronic and physical records.
- Maintain and reconcile bank, petty cash, mobile money, advances, receivables, payables and other assigned ledger accounts; monitor outstanding balances and follow up on timely settlement and liquidation.
- Support month-end and year-end close, including journals, accruals, prepayments, fixed-asset and depreciation records, balance-sheet schedules, account reconciliations and resolution of posting errors.

**2. Budget management, grants and donor compliance**

- Support programme teams in proposal budgeting, project set-up, annual and activity budgeting, cash-flow forecasting, budget revisions and grant close-out, ensuring alignment with funding agreements and organizational procedures.
- Monitor budgets and expenditure against approved work plans, identify variances and funding gaps, and advise budget holders on expenditure trends, cost allocations and timely corrective actions.
- Review programme and partner financial submissions, including activity budgets, cash requests, supporting documents and liquidations, for compliance with donor conditions, procurement rules and ICS SP policies.
- Support grant and sub-grant financial monitoring, partner financial reviews and preparation of donor financial reports and supporting schedules; escalate compliance concerns and material exceptions promptly.

**3. Internal controls, financial reporting and statutory compliance**

- Prepare accurate and timely monthly project and management reports, cash-flow updates, budget-versus-actual analyses, reconciliations, donor statements and other financial reports as assigned.
- Maintain robust financial controls covering segregation of duties, payment approvals, procurement documentation, advance management, supporting evidence and retention of financial records; identify control weaknesses and recommend improvements.
- Support payroll inputs and statutory compliance, including preparation and reconciliation of applicable payroll deductions, tax and other regulatory returns, in coordination with the Nairobi finance and HR teams.
- Maintain complete audit files and schedules; support statutory, project and donor audits, spot checks and due-diligence reviews, and track resolution of audit findings.

**4. Office administration, logistics and HR support**

- Coordinate day-to-day office administration across Western Kenya, including supplies, utilities, service providers, travel and accommodation arrangements, meeting logistics, office records and facilities follow-up.
- Support procurement planning and documentation, supplier coordination, asset and inventory registers, physical verification, asset movements, and disposal processes in accordance with ICS SP policies.
- Support HR administration, including onboarding documentation, leave and timesheet follow-up, staff benefits coordination, employee advances and confidential personnel records, working closely with the designated HR focal point.

**5. Capacity strengthening and operational coordination**

- Provide practical guidance to programme staff, field teams and implementing partners on budgets, accountability, financial procedures, documentation standards and donor requirements.
- Monitor partner and field-level financial management practices, identify training needs, deliver or coordinate refresher sessions and follow up on agreed improvements.
- Liaise with programme teams, logistics colleagues, suppliers, banks and relevant county or other stakeholders to resolve operational and financial issues while maintaining professional working relationships.
- Undertake regular support visits to field offices, promote cost-conscious use of resources, and carry out other related duties assigned by the Finance & Operations Manager.

**REQUISITE REQUIREMENTS**

- Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, Business Administration or a related discipline from a recognized university.
- Professional accounting qualification (CPA, ACCA or equivalent); current membership of a relevant professional body is desirable.
- At least five years of relevant post-qualification experience in finance and administration, preferably within an NGO or donor-funded development organization.
- Demonstrated experience in grant and project financial management, budget monitoring, donor compliance, reconciliations, financial reporting, and audit support.
- Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and Office 365. Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central is an added advantage.
- Working knowledge of Kenyan statutory and payroll obligations, procurement controls, staff advances and office administration procedures.
- Sound analytical judgement, attention to detail, integrity, confidentiality, strong written and verbal communication, and ability to manage competing deadlines.
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively across offices; willingness to travel regularly within Western Kenya.

ICS SP’s absolute priority is protecting children, vulnerable communities, and our own staff. We have zero tolerance of incidents of violence, abuse or exploitation against children or other people in the communities we serve, whether committed by staff or others connected to our work. Successful applicants will be required to sign and adhere to ICS SP safeguarding, child protection and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) codes of conduct and policies.

jobs.title: DMEAL Adviser - Pacific
jobs.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **DMEAL Adviser - Pacific**, you will provide strategic and technical DMEAL support, capacity strengthening, and advisory services to World Vision’s four Pacific Field Offices within the SAPO region, promoting quality DMEAL practices, evidence use, and learning. You will provide technical leadership for grant DMEAL across SAPO, including non-Pacific Field Offices, through the DMEAL for Grants Community of Practice (CoP), strengthening grant DMEAL quality, capacity, and cross-country learning while developing evidence and impact briefs. You will also provide matrix supervision and technical guidance to the DMEAL leads in Papua New Guinea and Solomon Islands, as agreed with the respective Field Offices, and report to the Regional Evidence and Impact Senior Adviser.

**Technical Assistance**

You will support Pacific National Offices in applying DMEAL and programme quality standards, guidelines, tools, and methodologies, including reviewing programme designs, baselines, evaluations, Annual Impact Measurement (AIM), and programme reports. You will provide technical guidance on iMPAQ, monitoring and MEAL systems, data quality, analysis, reporting, and evidence-based decision-making. You will also help communicate programme impact for income and influence goals and promote knowledge sharing and lessons learned to improve programme and organizational performance.

**Capacity Building**

You will assess DMEAL staff competencies, processes, structures, and approaches, identify gaps, and develop capacity-building interventions for National Offices and partners. You will facilitate workshops, peer learning, and individual support, lead regional MEAL capacity-strengthening initiatives, support the regional M&E Community of Practice, and strengthen Field Office teams’ use of monitoring data and evidence for programme quality, adaptive management, learning, and reporting.

**Strategic Management Support**

You will support the development and refresh of Pacific Field Office strategies, ensuring DMEAL and programme quality priorities are integrated. You will support Partnership and DMEAL initiatives, strengthen collaboration with donors and Support Offices, contribute to organizational programme quality strategies and standards, lead the regional AIM process and support quality Annual Child Results Reports. You will also provide technical support to relevant Pacific Field Offices in developing and implementing Integrated Programme Frameworks (IPFs), including in Solomon Islands.

**M&E Leadership**

You will develop professional networks and partnerships with universities, private-sector organizations, donors, and non-profit entities, contribute to organizational M&E discussions and guideline development, and coordinate with Support Offices and major donors to align monitoring and evaluation requirements. You will also collaborate with the Regional Grant Acquisition team to provide DMEAL and programme quality inputs and support, including participation in grant Go/No-Go decision-making.

**Requirements include:**

- Minimum of 5-7 years of experience in monitoring and evaluation at a national level (or large program level).
- Proven ability to facilitate working groups, communities of practice or other similar learning mechanisms
- Proven ability to collaborate with all levels of staff and to motivate and mobilize individuals outside their reporting line to achieve agreed strategic plans.
- Knowledge of the monitoring and evaluation requirements of one or more institutional donors (USAID, DFAT, DevCo, etc.)
- Bachelor’s degree and post-graduate certification or master’s degree in the social, statistic or related field.
- Qualitative and/or quantitative research and evaluation skills, including but not limited to study design, survey instrument design and use, establishing and measuring outcome and process indicators, sampling, data analysis plans, data cleaning, and statistical analysis.
- Demonstrated ability to report, present and communicate results, written and verbal in modern standard English.
- Master’s degree in social sciences, statistics or related field.
- Evidence of the ability to facilitate M&E capacity building approaches (workshop facilitation, 1:1 coaching, etc.)
- Business process improvement (Lean Six Sigma)
- Experience in working in pacific countries

jobs.title: NIGERIA - GRANTS & PARTNERSHIP HEAD OF DEPARTMENT (M/F) - ABUDJA
jobs.description:
## About us

**Desired start date: 15/12/2026**
**Duration of the mission: 12 months**
**Location: ABUJA**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

**Solidarites International** launched its operation in Nigeria in 2016 as a consequence of the humanitarian needs of displaced populations and host communities caused by the current crisis with conflict and the ongoing violence in the North-East of Nigeria led by Armed Opposition Groups since 2009. The security situation and epidemics/outbreaks continue to affect millions of lives in Northeastern and North Western parts of Nigeria. As of June 2022, according to IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix, an estimated 2.2 million people are displaced within Borno State which remains, for a major part, inaccessible to humanitarian actors.

The targeted sectors of intervention are WASH, Shelter, RRM, Food Security & Livelihoods. The annual budget of the mission is around 8.3 million euros in 2022.

The mission is organized with a coordination office in Maiduguri and 3 bases located in Ngala, Dikwa and Monguno managed remotely from Maiduguri for the North-East. In the North-West, Solidarites International is conducting activities on 3 bases located in Gusau, Anka and Taleta in Zamfara State. Abuja is the representative for the mission Nigeria.

Mission staff : 165
The Grants and Partnership HOD will directly manage the Grants coordination team composed of :
\- A Reporting & Communications Officer
She/he will closely work with all Departmental Heads, Field Coordinators and Project Managers of the mission.
The Grants and Partnership HOD will report to the Country Director and be in link with Grants & Partnership department in HQ.

## About the job

**General objective:**

Working closely with the programmes and support departments, the Head of Grants and Partnerships Department is responsible for managing relations with donors, as well as developing and monitoring the country office's funding strategy. They supervise, adapt and optimise working methods and tools dedicated to managing donor accountability.
They validate contractual documents (project proposals, reports, requests for amendments, partnership agreements, etc.) before they are submitted.
They play a key role in defining the country office's partnership strategy and coordinates relations with the various implementing partners (see the partnership implementation framework). Ensures effective coordination between departments for grant management and provides strategic support to the country office in relation to donor relations, external representation, management of implementing partners, external compliance and accountability to donors.

**The main challenges:**

\- Access challenges and remote management due to security contraints in some areas of intervention
\- Strategic positionning in a global trend of funding decrease
\- Focus on partnership and localization in all areas of intervention. This requires adapted operational modalities and a support to local partners.

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

\*Support the programmatic strategy (2027-2032) and PROG 2027 implementation
\*Monitoring of partnerships and capacity building plan in coordination with other Department (Programs, E & C, etc.)
\*Follow up on the advancement of the financing contracts
\*Finalize partnership management/localization strategy
\*Coordinate proposals
\*Continue developing relationship with donor representatives and engage internally/ externally with different interlocutors to identify new funding opportunities

**Security constraints:**

No walking policy everywhere in the country / Security situation calm in Abuja, level 2 (out of 5), Maiduguri is level 3 and level 4 in other bases/sub-bases.

## Your profile

**Diploma and Experience :**

Diploma : Bachelor or masters in a related degree: humanitarian response, international cooperation

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 5 years and more

Experience on similar positions : 3/4 years

**SKILLS :**

**Technical skills**

1. Excellent reporting, writing and proof reading skills
2. Strong knowledge of main donors (ECHO, French donors, SIDA etc) and their respective policies / guidelines
3. Previous experience and achievements in developing strategic partnerships with other NGOs (MoUs, negotiations, governance, capacity building ...)
4. Proven ability to deal with donors and operational partners

**Transversal skills**

1. Critical thinking skills and the ability to adapt to fast-paced environments, while working independently to meet tight deadlines with minimal supervision
2. Good knowledge of the humanitarian project cycle management;
3. Excellent communication, networking skills, organizational and prioritization skills, ability to multi-task, Capacity to adapt and show organizational flexibilit
4. External representation

**Languages :**

1. English (fluent - Mandatory)
2. French (an asset)

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2860 gross per month (2600 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

The Grant & Partnership HOD will be based in Abuja with frequent field visit expected in the regional offices (Maiduguri. Birnin Kebbi and potentially Gusau or Sokoto).
In Abuja, living condition are good and all commodities and goods (local or imported) can be found (supermarket, restautant, cinema, sport centers ...). Abuja GH is Comfortable with private bedroom and bathroom, 24/7 electricity and internet. GH is located in the same estate as the office, avoiding taking the car every morning but still clearly separated from working area (not the same building). Estate where GH/Office is located is providing Gym room, Swimming pool and squash court.
At base level, (Maiduguri, Birnin Kebbi and Gusau), the bases offers a comfortable environment, in spite of limited movements outside of the compound for security reasons. The Guest House offers good living conditions, with private bedroom and bathroom and shared & comfortable common spaces. Electricity and internet are available at the office and at the GH at all times. Ping pong, pool table and some gym equipment are available in the GH in Maiduguri. All essential good (food, hygiene etc..) can be bought locally in the small shops around the office, or in the pre-validated supermarket. Visits to other NGOs are possible, as well as some pre-validated places (hotel and restaurants).
Occasional field visit in NE sub bases, to ensure a correct program overview depedning on the security context and validation. No Overnight are possible in NE sub bases, only daily round trip with UNHAS are possible.

jobs.title: Emergency Response Manager Sudan
jobs.description:
**Background:**

The Emergency Response Manager (ERM) will oversee the overall country emergency response programme.

The ERM will lead on the coordination, quality response, management, and reporting of emergency response activities including those under the ECHO-funded Emergency Response consortium (FaSER) and UN pipelines. The ERM will support and provide technical supervision of emergency response teams in the field to respond to rapid onset crises related to conflict displacement and natural disasters, coordinating all emergency preparedness plans, minimum prepared actions (MPAs), and supervise emergency activities across NRC’s geographical spread in Sudan.

This will include pre-planning, assessment, coordination, leadership and overseeing emergency responses, in collaboration with Area Managers, Programme Specialists and other relevant programme and support departments, including safety and security and cash and market-based programming.

The role will also play a crucial function as surge capacity and will be deployed to hotspot locations across Sudan to reinforce critical emergency response programming depending on the needs of the operation.

**What you will do:**

Generic responsibilities:

1. Ensure adherence to NRC policies, handbooks, procedures and SOPs/guidelines;
2. Overall oversight, strategic development, and operational management of emergency response interventions across the Country Office;
3. Development of robust emergency set-ups based on appropriate needs analysis with an integrated programme approach;
4. Development of emergency response strategies and technical SOPs/guidelines;
5. Development and management of funding proposals, project budgets and donor reports;

Specific responsibilities:

1. **ERM Consortium Programme Management:**

- Overall responsibility for effective and efficient coordination of the emergency preparedness and response projects consistent with the project management cycle *(including reporting to the desired quality and standard)*;
- Overall budget management for FaSER projects/portfolio implemented and ensure appropriate burn-rates are maintained and that solutions to over/under expenditure are applied;
- Develop strategies, set-ups, and continuous review of technical guidance, tools, and SOPs for the overall emergency response

**2. Emergency Surge Support**

- Provide general programme support to key Area Offices during emergency responses including directly overseeing cash and other distributions.
- Lead and develop Emergency Response plans to coordinate NRC’s overall response to an emergency and provide inputs for use in fund raising, advocacy and programme development
- Lead coordination meetings with Programme, Support and Area Office colleagues.

**3. Coordination and Representation:**

- Liaise and coordinate with UN and I/NGO partners, local authorities, and beneficiaries in planning and response to emergencies, preparedness, and contextual understanding of areas of operations;
- Represent the RRM Consortium to external stakeholders - donors, government, coordination bodies, and local and international NGOs. Include the Steering Committee and other consortium staff in representation as much as possible and as appropriate. Network with relevant actors to help achieve consortium objectives;
- Conduct senior representation at state level and promote strong working relationships with government counterparts;

Please refer to the detailed [Job Description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQBuZJQ-ramxQq178rbecg-aATvc50YqX3Sjy3I3YrYyE9A?e=NEqRjT) as the above enlisted responsibilities are just a snapshot.

**What you will bring:**

1. **Generic professional competencies:**

- At least five years in a humanitarian programming environment, including three years’ experience in project management position;
- Previous working experience in implementing emergency programme cycle in complex, fragile, and volatile contexts;
- Must have experience in cash-based programming, specifically cash distribution modalities;
- Emergency Response expertise, including Rapid Response Mechanisms (RRM) or Emergency Response Mechanisms (ERM);
- Technical expertise in one of NRC’s Core Competencies (Shelter/NFI, WASH, ICLA, Education, Camp Management/Protection from Violence), is added advantage;
- Documented results related to the position’s responsibilities;
- Fluency in English, both written and verbal;
- Computer literacy in Microsoft Office, including strong skills in Excel.

1. **Context/ Specific skills, knowledge and experience:**

- Keen interest and knowledge of the context in Sudan, previous experience in Sudan is very valuable;
- Arabic language skills is an advantage;
- Previous experience working with/ in consortiums and multi-agency projects;
- Specific experience in camp-contexts, distributions, cash programming and shelter/NFI
- Strong skills in analysis and coordination
- Experience in needs assessment, project monitoring and evaluation, and programme development;
- Strong leadership skills and a supportive management style;
- Experience of a flexible approach to managing and prioritising a high and diverse workload;
- Proven ability to work effectively across cultures, in sensitive environments and with stakeholders at all levels.

- **What we offer:**
- Duty station: Al-Geniena, Darfur, Sudan
- Contract: 12 Months (renewable based on funding and performance)
- Travel: 80%
- Salary/benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s either **national or international** salary scale.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- *For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity MarketPlace.*
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Applicants who do not fill in the required information will not be considered for the role.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Mandatory to submit the below when applying:
- **Your most updated English CV and remove all previous outdated CVs.**
- **Your most updated Cover Letter**
- **Do not attach certificates or any other documents apart from the two mentioned above.**
- **Incomplete applications will not be considered.**
- **This position is open for both national and international candidates. Internals might be assessed first if the pool is competitive.**
- We receive many applications for each vacant position. Therefore, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email **esa.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.
- [Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)
- [Learn more about Sudan](https://www.nrc.no/countries/africa/sudan/)

jobs.title: Global Surge Team Roster: Emergency Grants Coordinator
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**IRC Global Surge Team:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s most severe humanitarian crises, helping people survive, recover, and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC delivers life‑saving assistance and long‑term recovery services to people affected by conflict and disaster. Today, the IRC works in over 30 countries and 22 U.S. cities, restoring safety, dignity, and hope to millions worldwide.

The IRC’s Global Surge Team (GST) is a roster of highly qualified humanitarian professionals who deploy on short notice to emergency and non‑emergency contexts to support the IRC’s mission. GST members provide specialized, time‑bound support where capacity gaps exist, typically for deployments of up to three months.

**The GST is a flexible, occasional employment opportunity. Deployment needs vary based on demand. Staff can take on additional deployments as opportunities arise and if they are interested.** Deployment opportunities depend on organizational and operational requirements and may vary over time; as such, deployments cannot be guaranteed. Staff supporting emergency responses must be prepared to deploy within 72 hours as needs arise.

**French speaking candidates are currently being prioritized.**

**Job Summary:**

The **Emergency Grants Coordinator, Global Surge** plays a critical role in supporting emergency humanitarian responses by leading grant management, donor compliance, proposal development, and reporting functions in rapidly evolving crisis settings. As part of surge deployments, this position ensures the timely mobilization and stewardship of donor funding through the development of high-quality proposals, robust monitoring and reporting systems, and effective coordination with program teams, partners, donors, and headquarters. The role provides strategic guidance on donor regulations and compliance requirements, strengthens grants management capacity through staff training and mentorship, and supports strong information management practices to ensure accountability, program quality, and operational effectiveness. Working in complex emergency environments, the Emergency Grants Coordinator helps secure and manage resources that enable the delivery of impactful humanitarian assistance to affected populations.

**Responsibilities:**

- Ensure high quality and timely submission of funding proposals through development of timelines, coordinating technical and financial input, writing overviews, editing and formatting proposal documents, and liaison with HQ on approval and submission processes.
- Work with program and management staff to promote and ensure development of strong data collection andmonitoring & evaluation process, detailed collection and analysis of program data.
- Hire and train in-county grants staff as the need arises to efficiently support the scale and scope of the program
- Establish and ensure maintenance of comprehensive grant files and related information management processes including issuing reporting formats and schedules, maintaining donor and external contact information/files and protocols and establishing a photo library.
- Participate in and/or lead grant opening and review meetings; ensuring all required information is circulated in advance, meetings are fully documented and action items completed.
- Provide advice on donor grant compliance issues, visibility and reporting requirements; proactively engaging with program teams to ensure appropriate IRC and donor visibility
- Coordinate partner subgrant processes including preaward assessments, subgrant development, HQ review and approval processes, related partner reporting and compliance training to promote an encouraging and constructive relationship and effective oversight of subgrant activities and results.
- Prepare high quality and timely donor and management reports on grants and sector activities in close collaboration with program staff.
- Represent IRC and coordinate with other agencies, local government, donors and other partners to promote deliver of best practice humanitarian assistance and coordination of efforts.
- Support media and communications activities as requested by the emergency response team.
- Provide a comprehensive handover to successor, including ensuring transfer of all related documentation, program monitoring data and staff performance information.

**Requirements:**

- Significant experience in grants management, humanitarian program management, or a related field, including work in emergency and conflict-affected settings.
- Strong knowledge of major humanitarian donor regulations and compliance requirements, including UN agencies, USAID/BHA, ECHO/EC, and FCDO (formerly DFID).
- Proven experience coordinating donor proposals, grant management processes, reporting, and compliance across multiple stakeholders.
- Excellent English writing, editing, and communication skills; additional language skills are an asset (French fluency required).
- Strong understanding of monitoring, evaluation, and data management systems, with experience supporting program quality and accountability.
- Experience developing project budgets and working closely with finance teams on donor financial requirements.
- Demonstrated ability to build partnerships, facilitate collaboration across departments, and provide training and guidance on grants management and donor compliance.
- Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet tight deadlines in fast-paced environments.
- Ability to work independently, adapt quickly to changing circumstances, and perform effectively in high-pressure emergency response contexts.
- Willingness and ability to deploy internationally on short notice to support humanitarian emergencies.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Compliance Coordinator - Syria Aleppo or Idleb
jobs.description:
Established in 1977, GOAL is an international humanitarian and development agency, committed to working with communities to achieve sustainable and innovative early response in crises, and lasting solutions to poverty and vulnerability. GOAL has worked in over 60 countries and has responded to almost every major humanitarian disaster. We are currently operational in 18 countries.

GOAL began operations in Syria in 2013 responding to the acute needs of conflict-affected communities. GOAL's areas of operations include but not limited to Aleppo, Idleb and Damascus Programmes focus on Food and Nutrition Security, WASH, Shelter, Livelihoods/ERMS and Emergency Response with an emphasis on cash and voucher modalities. GOAL Syria implements its programmes directly, with staff based in Syria, and through Syrian NGO partners. GOAL's programme works at the household and community levels to improve community resilience and household coping strategies

**Job purpose:**

The Compliance Coordinator “CC” will oversee the Compliance Department, ensuring annual compliance plans are developed/followed and are appropriate to the context and management requirements. CC will manage the Compliance team who work across all departments, including programs, finance, procurement, logistics, and human resources, providing timely advice on donor regulations and feedback on the effectiveness of the internal controls in place in ensuring adherence to those regulations.

Provide leadership and oversight of the GOAL Syria Compliance Department ensuring that all responsibilities of the Compliance Department are fulfilled in a timely and effective manner, making best use of GOAL’s resources and ultimately ensuring compliance with donor and GOAL procedures and policies

**Duties, objectives and competencies:**

- Lead and manage the Compliance Department, including staff supervision, planning, and performance management.
- Develop and implement annual compliance plans and monitor compliance across all functions.
- Identify, assess, and mitigate compliance risks, ensuring timely escalation of significant issues.
- Provide guidance on donor regulations, organizational policies, contracts, partnerships, and grant management.
- Deliver compliance training and build staff and partner capacity.
- Oversee compliance reviews, audits, reporting, and follow-up on corrective actions.
- Ensure donor compliance, due diligence, sanctions screening, and regulatory requirements are effectively implemented.
- Support and monitor implementing partners to strengthen compliance systems and accountability.
- Coordinate donor audits, compliance investigations, and reviews, while escalating fraud, misconduct, or other significant breaches.

**Requirements (essential):**

- Bachelor’s degree in relevant subjects (such as Business Administration, Law, Finance, Accounting, Risk Management, international trade, or a related field).
- At least 3 years’ experience in leading compliance, audit, risk management, governance, or donor compliance within NGOs or Business Sector.
- At least 6 years professional experience in INGOs or NGOs in related fields.
- At least 5 years’ previous experience in team management.
- Proven ability to develop staff and provide training on systems and procedures.
- Any previous experience in implementing organizational internal control, SOPs and donor policies.
- Strong knowledge of donor regulations, internal controls, and risk management practices.
- Experience in compliance monitoring, risk assessment, audit follow-up, and corrective-action tracking.
- Ability to manage and priorities a varied workload in a rapidly changing work environment.
- Previous Experience in reviewing donor agreements, partnership agreements, procurement processes, waivers, exceptions, and organizational procedures.
- Willingness and ability to undertake some travel for work purposes, as required.
- Ability to work under pressure to pursue multiple tasks simultaneously to successful conclusions.
- Excellent leadership, analytical, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
- Excellent attention to detail.
- Trustworthy and honest.
- Fluency in Arabic and English

**Requirements (desired):**

- At least two years previous work experience as head of department.
- Diplomacy and negotiation skills.
- Master’s degree in related field.
- Previous experience in Anti-Terrorist Sanctions check systems.
- Previous experience in the U.S.G Vetting System "PVS".
- Data Analysis skills, including knowledge of Power BI and advanced Microsoft Excel

**General terms and conditions**

**Safeguarding**

Children and vulnerable adults must be safeguarded to the maximum possible extent from deliberate or inadvertent actions and failings that place them at risk of abuse, sexual exploitation, injury and any other harm. One of the ways that GOAL shows this on-going commitment to safeguarding is to include rigorous background and reference checks in the selection process for all candidates.

**Safeguarding Statement**
GOAL has zero tolerance for safeguarding violations. All staff are expected to adhere to GOAL’s Code of Conduct and Safeguarding policies, including the prevention of sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (PSEAH). Recruitment is subject to safeguarding checks, including reference verification

**Accountability within GOAL**

Alongside our safeguarding policy, GOAL is an equal opportunities employer and has a set of integrity policies. Any candidate offered a job with GOAL will be expected to adhere to the following key areas of accountability:

- Comply with GOAL’s policies and procedures with respect to safeguarding, Code of Conduct, health and safety, data protection and confidentiality, do no harm principles and unacceptable behavior protocols.
- Report any concerns about the welfare of a child or vulnerable adult or any wrongdoings within our programming area.
- Report any concerns about inappropriate behavior of a GOAL staff or partner.

This means that we will close adverts as soon as we have found the right candidate and this may be before the published closing date. We would therefore advise interested applicants to submit an application as early as possible.*
