UNDP is the UN’s global development network, an organization advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience, and resources to help people build a better life. UNDP works in about 170 countries and territories, working with national counterparts on solutions to global and national development challenges. In Bhutan, over the last 50 years, UNDP has been supporting the Royal Government to attain its national priorities. In 2024, UNDP started implementation of the Country Programme Document 2024-2028, aligning to the country’s 13th Five Year Plan (13th FYP).

In 2023, Bhutan graduated from the UN list of Least Developed Countries (LDCs). Over the past decades, the country has made remarkable progress in reducing income and multidimensional poverty, aligned with its commitment to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Despite the impressive progress, the country is grappling with critical socio-economic challenges such as large-scale emigration of the productive and skilled labor force, youth unemployment, declining fertility rate, increasing trade deficit, and shrinking fiscal space. These challenges take place amidst a slow post-pandemic economic recovery and against the broader backdrop of structural challenges, such as limited economic diversification, a still-nascent private sector, absence of robust regulatory and institutional framework.

Bhutan’s 13th FYP (2024-2029) sets out the ambitious target of doubling the size of the country’s economy within the next five years and then doubling it again over the subsequent five years, reaching USD 10 billion by 2034, a target year that Bhutan plans to reach the high-income status. Recognizing the challenges and potential opportunities in Bhutan’s 21st-century economy, the Royal Government of Bhutan aims to accelerate and foster a robust economic recovery and growth. It is in this context that the Royal Government of Bhutan requested UNDP’s policy advisory assistance to support the Prime Minister’s Office in a high-level consultation and the subsequent development of a development roadmap for the realization for the government’s development vision as outlined above.

In June 2025, the Royal Government endorsed the Bhutan 21st Century Economic Roadmap, which sets the ambitious target of growing Bhutan’s economy tenfold (10X) by 2050 or earlier and transforming the country into a high-income, inclusive and sustainable economy. Recognising that achieving this 10X ambition requires a fundamentally different delivery architecture — one centred on performance, execution and accountability — the Royal Government established a dedicated Delivery Unit (DU) under the Prime Minister’s Office, anchored within the Office of the Cabinet Affairs and Strategic Coordination (OCASC), to drive the implementation of the 21st Century Economic Roadmap and the 13th Five Year Plan.

The Delivery Unit forms part of a wider 10X Implementation Governance Structure that comprises a National Steering Committee (NSC) chaired by the Hon’ble Prime Minister. The DU will serve as the secretariat to the NSC and report directly to the Hon’ble Prime Minister. It will be composed of a multidisciplinary team with expertise in planning, economic and financial analysis, project and performance management, data analytics, investment facilitation and public–private partnerships.

The Delivery Unit’s mandate spans the full delivery cycle: (i) designing and formulating detailed sectoral roadmaps with defined interventions, milestones, KPIs and implementation pathways in close coordination with lead agencies; (ii) developing investment frameworks and financing strategies, structuring bankable projects, and engaging investors and development partners in coordination with the Economic Development Board (EDB); (iii) facilitating and negotiating public–private partnerships and coordinating implementation across ministries and agencies; (iv) rigorously monitoring progress through dashboards, field reviews and structured delivery assessments, and providing regular updates to the NSC and the Hon’ble Prime Minister; and (v) conducting annual evaluations of agencies implementing projects under the 21st Century Economic Roadmap. In doing so, the DU will institutionalize the missing link between strategic ambition and on-the-ground delivery, embedding a culture of performance, foresight and accountability across government and accelerating Bhutan’s journey towards high-income status by 2034.

To support this initiative, UNDP seeks to recruit a Delivery and Performance Specialist to be embedded within the Delivery Unit. The Delivery and Performance Specialist will serve as the core engine of the Delivery Unit’s performance management and analytical functions, translating the 10X ambition into measurable KPIs, real-time dashboards and structured delivery routines that enable evidence-based decision-making by the National Steering Committee.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the overall guidance of the Director General, Office of the Cabinet Affairs and Strategic Coordination and Director, Office of the Prime Minister, and supervision of the Programme Analyst, Governance and Advocacy at UNDP CO, the Delivery and Performance Specialist will lead the design, operation and continuous improvement of the Delivery Unit’s performance management system, data analytics and dashboards for priority projects identified in the Bhutan 21st Century Economic Roadmap and other strategies and projects which are priority for the Delivery Unit. The Delivery and Performance Specialist will also support the Delivery Unit’s work in tracking implementation progress, surfacing bottlenecks, and equipping the National Steering Committee, Technical Steering Committees and lead agencies with the data, evidence and insights required to course-correct in real time.

Design and operationalize the Delivery Unit’s performance management framework

- Design and operationalize the Delivery Unit’s performance management framework, including KPIs, milestones, trajectories and delivery scorecards for priority projects under the 21st Century Economic Roadmap.

- Support the development of sectoral 10X project blueprints and contribute performance-management inputs to detailed sectoral roadmaps, KPIs and delivery plans.

- Work closely with the Bhutan Innovation Lab (BIL) to support the transition of Entry Point Project (EPP) blueprints into implementation, translating strategic recommendations, delivery pathways, milestones and KPIs developed by BIL into operational delivery plans, performance monitoring frameworks and implementation tracking mechanisms.

Develop and maintain dashboards, data pipelines and analytical tools

- Build and maintain live dashboards and visualization tools, including Power BI, Tableau or other relevant platforms, to track progress of 10X priority projects, with regular reporting to the National Steering Committee, Technical Steering Committees and the Hon’ble Prime Minister.

- Establish data pipelines and reporting protocols with line ministries, agencies and lead implementers to ensure timely, accurate and reliable data flow into the Delivery Unit.

- Conduct data analysis and diagnostics to identify implementation bottlenecks, delivery risks and early warning signals, and propose evidence-based course corrections.

Support structured delivery routines, reporting and evaluation

- Organise and facilitate structured delivery routines, including stock takes, problem-solving sessions and monthly performance reviews between the Delivery Unit, lead agencies and the Hon’ble Prime Minister, and document agreed actions and follow-ups.

- Support the annual evaluation of agencies implementing projects under the 21st Century Economic Roadmap, and contribute to the preparation of progress reports, briefing notes and presentations for the National Steering Committee and the Hon’ble Prime Minister.

- Contribute to the design and facilitation of 10X Labs and stakeholder clinics, providing data-analytics inputs to detailed sectoral roadmaps, KPIs and delivery plans.

Ensure gender-responsive analysis and programming

- Ensure the systematic integration of gender perspectives into policy analysis, recommendations, and programming, informed by sound gender analysis that incorporates sex-disaggregated data and addresses differentiated needs, priorities, and impacts across diverse groups.

Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing, and advocacy relevant to the assigned thematic areas.

- Identify capacity building needs and opportunities. Ensure appropriate training, project workshops and other relevant activities are organized and implemented in a consultative manner, involving technical experts and stakeholders that may include the government, private sector, NGOs, donors, and/or academia.

- Ensure project reports capture results, lessons learned and good practices for possible wider application.

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP is the leading United Nations organization fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and planet. The Fiji multi-country office covers ten countries including Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, Kiribati, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Republic of Naoero, Palau, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu as well as provides support to regional initiatives.

UNDP in the Pacific has developed its Multi-Country Programme Document (MCPD, 2023-2027) to guide its interventions in the next five years in full alignment and directly to contribute to the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF, 2023–2027). The Office covers 10 countries in the Pacific with an extensive portfolio which has grown over time. The UNSDCF and UNDP MCPD are designed in full alignment with the 2030 agenda, Samoa Pathway, and 2050 Strategy for the Blue Pacific Continent, which is endorsed by the Pacific Island Countries (PICs) among others. The UNDP Pacific Office next five-year plan strategic priorities are encapsulated under three outcome areas: (i) Planet, (ii) Prosperity, and (iii) Peace. Following a strategic review process which was completed in June 2022, UNDP Pacific office structure is aligned to the emerging priorities of the office. In this regard, the programme portfolio will include mutually reinforcing work streams crafted around two clusters (i) Resilience and Climate Change; and (ii) Inclusive Growth and Effective Governance, supported by a policy and innovations team, operations team, management programme and oversight team, which provides strategic guidance on results management and compliance entrusted with the corporate alignment, programme finance management and quality assurance, and a strategic communications team, which provides knowledge management and communication support to all programme interventions.

Fiji is among the most disaster-prone countries in the Pacific and is exposed to tropical cyclones, floods, storm surges, landslides, droughts, earthquakes, tsunamis, volcanic hazards, disease outbreaks and the increasing impacts of climate change. These hazards continue to affect lives, livelihoods, infrastructure, ecosystems and national development.

The National Disaster Management Act 2024 establishes the National Disaster Risk Management Office (NDRMO) as the lead agency responsible for coordinating disaster risk management, disaster risk reduction, disaster preparedness, response, and recovery and resilience-building across Fiji. The Act further provides for the establishment of Divisional Disaster Risk Management Offices to strengthen sub-national coordination and implementation of disaster risk management.

To support implementation of the National Disaster Management Act 2024, the National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2018–2030, the National Disaster Risk Management Plan, the Early Warnings for All (EW4All) Initiative and the Multi-Hazard Early Warning System (MHEWS) Roadmap, the Government of Fiji, through the UNDP Green Climate Fund Programme, will recruit a Communications & Public Relations Assistant to lead strategic communications, public information, media engagement and awareness activities that promote disaster risk reduction, climate resilience and the objectives of the GCF EW4All Project and the NDRMO.

Working under the technical direction of the Manager Emergency Planning Coordination (NDRMO) and the Project Manager - EW4All, the Project Communications & Public Relations Assistant will ensure timely, accurate, and accessible disaster information, strengthen public confidence, and support the implementation of Fiji’s Multi Hazard Early Warning System (MHEWS) and Common Alerting Protocol (CAP).

Duties and Responsibilities

Summary of Key Functions:

The incumbent will serve as the primary focal point for:

- Strategic Communications: develop and implement communication strategies, annual plans, and public education campaigns.

- Disaster Risk Communication: lead awareness initiatives, risk communication strategies, and behaviour change campaigns.

- Media & Partnerships: build strong partnerships with broadcasters, telecoms, and digital platforms to ensure rapid dissemination of alerts.

- Emergency Public Information: coordinate official messaging during National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) activations, ensuring consistency and accuracy.

- Digital Engagement: manage NDRMO’s website, social media, and digital channels with inclusive, multilingual content.

- Trust & Feedback: establish mechanisms to counter misinformation, strengthen transparency, and capture community feedback for continuous improvement.

1.Provide strategic and risk communications:

- Strategy & Planning: develop and implement NDRMO’s Communication Strategy, Annual Communication Plan, and national public awareness campaigns supporting disaster risk reduction (DRR), preparedness, response, and recovery.

- Risk & Emergency Communication: lead proactive risk communication to promote accurate and consistent public information before, during, and after disasters.

- Programme Integration: coordinate communication strategies for key NDRMO initiatives, including the Green Climate Fund (GCF) Early Warnings for All (EW4All) Project, Fiji’s Multi-Hazard Early Warning System (MHEWS), and the National Common Alerting Protocol (CAP).

2.Disseminate emergency operations & public information:

- NEOC Coordination: serve as the focal point for public information during National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) activations, ensuring real-time, accurate, and consistent official warnings and situation reports.

- Direct Dissemination: leverage the National CAP Platform to coordinate multi-channel public warnings across broadcasters, mobile networks, social media, websites, and community channels.

3.Facilitate media engagement & stakeholder partnerships:

- Partner Collaboration: build and maintain strong working relationships with the Ministry of Information, Ministry of Communications, broadcasters, telecommunications providers, and digital platforms.

- Misinformation & Public Trust: monitor media channels to detect misinformation/disinformation, issuing rapid clarifications and official myth-busting updates to preserve public confidence.

- Media Management: lead media relations, issue press releases, organize briefings, and prepare speeches, advisories, and official statements.

4.Lead in digital engagement, content creation & inclusion:

- Digital Platforms: manage NDRMO’s official website, social media, and digital channels with accurate, timely, and engaging content.

- Accessible Content Development: produce diverse content (infographics, short videos, podcasts, newsletters) ensuring products are culturally appropriate, multilingual, and fully accessible to persons with disabilities and vulnerable groups.

5.Gauge community feedback, and support M&E & knowledge management:

- Feedback Loops: establish and manage community feedback mechanisms (including post-event evaluations) to measure public trust, warning comprehension, and information reach.

- Analytics & Performance Reporting: monitor media analytics, track campaign effectiveness, and prepare periodic performance reports with actionable recommendations for continuous improvement.

- Documentation & Donor Visibility: oversee photography, videography, and documentation for key events, ensuring full compliance with donor visibility and reporting requirements (including GCF).

6.Manage flagship campaigns and initiatives:

The incumbent will directly drive and manage the following core campaigns:

- “Know Your Risk Fiji” Campaign: a year-round, multi-media national awareness initiative promoting disaster risk reduction across traditional and digital platforms.

- Monthly Hazard Awareness Calendar: targeted seasonal campaigns aligned with Fiji's primary hazards (cyclones, flooding, drought, tsunamis, and fire).

- Disaster Ready Fiji Schools Initiative: tailored communication packages, educational toolkits, and interactive preparedness activities for primary and secondary schools.

- Community Champions Programme: training and equipping community leaders, faith-based organizations, women's clubs, and youth ambassadors to amplify life-saving preparedness messages.

- Rapid Myth-Busting & Rumour Management Unit: an active monitoring mechanism to identify public confusion during disasters and publish instant, verified clarifications.

- Multi-Platform Public Warning Framework: operational coordination with telecoms, media houses, and local networks to guarantee automated, seamless alert delivery through the CAP platform.

7.The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core Competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Demonstrate focus on achieving quality results and impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Look beyond conventional approaches and established methods

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Actively pursue opportunities for learning and self-development professionally and personally

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Be flexible in handling change, and adopt new ideas, approaches and ways of working

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Pursue everything with motivation and drive

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Act in a way that demonstrates empathy and emotional intelligence, showing consideration for the needs and feelings of others

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Treat all individuals with respect, consider ethical implications and respond sensitively to all differences among people

- Strategic Thinking : Develop effective strategies and prioritised plans in line with UNDP’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight.

Business Management

- Partnerships Management: Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

- Communication: Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Digital

- Social Media : Knowledge of social media and ability to advise the use of social media for development outcomes.

External Relations & Advocacy - General (across the functions)

- Public Relations : Ability to build and maintain an overall positive public image for the organisation, its mandate and its brand, while ensuring that individual campaigns and other communications and advocacy initiatives are supported in reaching the public.

- Digital Literacy: Ability to apply terms and concepts from digital communications in daily work.

- Multimedia writing/editing: Ability to create and/or edit written content for multimedia.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Secondary education is required, OR

- A University Degree (Bachelor’s degree) in communications, journalism, public relations, or another related discipline would be given due consideration but not a requirement

Experience:

Minimum of 5 years (with high school diploma) or 2 years (with bachelor’s degree) of demonstrated experience in strategic communications, media relations, and public awareness campaigns is required.

Required Skills

Experience in the use of computers, office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and web-based management systems, and advanced knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages.

Desired Skills

- Demonstrated experience in strategic communications, public awareness campaigns, and public relations within disaster risk management, climate change, or development programs.

- Proven excellence in professional writing, editing, and content creation for diverse platforms, including articles, social media campaigns, newsletters, blogs, press releases, and public multimedia materials.

- Hands-on experience in supporting public safety messaging, emergency communications, or multi-hazard early warning dissemination channels.

- Proven Familiarity with Fiji’s Disaster Risk Management Framework, the National Disaster Management Act 2024, the Fiji National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2018–2030, and the Early Warnings for All (EW4All) initiative.

- Demonstrated ability in translating complex technical information (such as Multi-Hazard Early Warning Systems and Common Alerting Protocols) into accessible, clear public outreach materials.

- Working knowledge of the local languages Fiji Hindi or iTaukei is desirable.

Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

Background

The Philippines' recent transition to upper-middle-income status has increased the importance of aligning economic growth with sustainability, digital transformation, and human rights accountability. As sectors such as mining, renewable energy, agribusiness, tourism, infrastructure, and digital platforms expand, governance challenges related to community grievances, land and resource disputes, labor rights, environmental impacts, and stakeholder participation persist, often disproportionately affecting women and marginalized groups.

To address these challenges, the Philippines initiated work on a National Action Plan on Business and Human Rights (NAP-BHR), led by the Presidential Human Rights Committee Secretariat (PHRCS). While several ASEAN countries have already institutionalized their NAPs, the Philippines remains in the development stage. Recent efforts have accelerated under the 4th Philippine Human Rights Plan 2024-2028, including the establishment of a multi-agency technical working group to develop a NAP-BHR focused on responsible business conduct, Indigenous Peoples' rights, and ancestral domains.

The FAIR BHR Project seeks to strengthen Business and Human Rights (BHR) governance by promoting more integrated, participatory, and evidence-based approaches that connect sustainability, human rights, accountability, conflict sensitivity, and stakeholder engagement. The project will support the Philippine government in building evidence, raising awareness, strengthening coordination, and fostering inclusive dialogue to inform BHR reforms.

The initiative will also promote stronger collaboration among UN agencies, leveraging complementary expertise and positioning UNDP as a strategic convener. As an initial pilot, the project will generate evidence and lessons to inform longer-term programming and the development of a comprehensive Project Document supporting the institutionalization of BHR in the Philippines.

UNDP is looking for a Project Coordinator who will lead the Project Management Unit (PMU). The post involves working under the overall guidance of the UNDP Institutions and Partnerships (I&P) Programme Team and various key stakeholders to ensure that the project will achieve its intended objectives.

Duties and Responsibilities

Ensure strategic management of the project and provide day-to-day financial and administrative management for the delivery of the project’s activities focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Lead the preparation and updating of the project’s annual work plan, human resources plan, procurement plan and M&E plan;

- Ensure effective implementation of the project work plan, in keeping with UNDP’s Project management guidelines;

- Manage project funds, maintain financial integrity, and ensure effective use of project resources;

- Effective application of UNDP financial oversight through the Quantum enterprise management system;

- With support from project staff, provide quality and timely financial reports, as per UNDP financial rules and regulations as well as Donor requirements;

- Ensure delivery of outputs and contribution to outcomes through an effective implementation plan and close coordination with UNDP management and technical teams and other key stakeholders;

- Provide overall coordination and oversight of all project activities;

- Ensure accountability by leading the preparation and submission of comprehensive reports (monthly, quarterly, annual, and donor), aligning results with project objectives, addressing challenges, and providing insights to drive strategic decision-making and enhance overall project performance; and

- Work closely with CO programme and finance teams to ensure efficient and transparent use of project resources in line with approved budgets and within UNDP rules and regulations.

Develop and maintain effective working relationships and coordination with key counterparts to ensure the strategic positioning of the project focusing on the achievement of the following results:

- Build and maintain an effective working relationship with key partners and stakeholders;

- Work closely with the project team and stakeholders to ensure that the project outputs are delivered on time, meet set standards of quality, and are useful to stakeholders;

- Promote coordination, dialogue, and good practice knowledge sharing among stakeholders; and

- Ensure effective collaboration with the UN agencies and other development partners.

Support resource mobilization focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Identify and collaborate with potential partners to leverage Project funds and results to formulate new interventions and identify new resource mobilization opportunities;

- Develop concept notes, project proposals, and project document to support pipeline development and resource mobilization.

Support human resources management focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Supervise personnel members under the PMU and provide necessary guidance and coaching; and

- Set performance parameters for staff members under the PMU, assess their performance, and provide feedback.

Ensure facilitation of communications, knowledge management, and advocacy focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Identification and synthesis of best practices and lessons learned directly linked to project goals; and

- Sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Project Coordinator will lead the Project Management Unit (PMU) based in UNDP Country Office in Metro Manila and is expected to lead the implementation and monitoring of the activities under the project.

Under the direct supervision of the Institutions and Partnerships (I&P) Programme Team Leader, the Project Coordinator is expected to work closely with the I&P Programme Analyst – Governance and Rule of Law that provides programme assurance for the project, and collaborative with other UNDP Country Office Programme and Operations teams. S/he is also expected to collaborate with relevant government agencies, UN agencies, and other key stakeholders.

Competencies

Core Competencies:

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Background

Under the direct supervision of the Project Manager, the Project Assistant will support the implementation of the Green Transition Portfolio Pillar 1 – Decarbonization (hereinafter, “GTP - Pillar 1”), funded by Sweden.

The Portfolio aims to contribute to a just green transition in Bosnia and Herzegovina by empowering policymakers, businesses, communities, entrepreneurs, and scientists to devise and implement policies and solutions driving significant decarbonization and CO2 reduction. Key focus areas include transitioning from fossil fuels to clean energy (aiming for the most vulnerable to escape energy poverty), eliminating waste and pollution, combating environmental harms, introducing circular and climate-neutral business models, and protecting natural resources. The portfolio supports effective, fair, and sustainable development through policy dialogue, regulatory improvements, capacity building, and incentives in energy sustainability, waste management, sustainable business models, green chemistry, and environmental protection, driving system-level changes for Bosnia and Herzegovina’s green transition.

The intervention is an integral part of a wider set of reform and investment interventions in Bosnia and Herzegovina guided by the Portfolio “Catalysing the Green Transition in Bosnia and Herzegovina”. This Portfolio is a 5-year programmatic framework of UNDP in Bosnia and Herzegovina, which leverages new development thinking and aims to anchor and catalyse a broader just transformation towards a green and zero-carbon Bosnia and Herzegovina. Interventions elaborated in this Concept Proposal cover a three-year period, while potential continuation of activities will be determined in 2027.

Under the overall guidance of the Project Manager, the Project Assistant will provide support services ensuring high quality, accuracy, and consistency of work. Project Assistant will be responsible for technical and logistical assistance to the Project Manager while implementing activities under the GTP - Pillar 1.

The incumbent will be based in UNDP BiH office in Sarajevo.

- Participate in the planning, organizing and execution of Project activities;

- Organize and coordinate seminars, training activities, workshops, site visits and other exchange and facilitation events for stakeholders;

- Organize and coordinate information exchanges both internationally and between participating institutions;

- Maintain the Project files and supporting documentation for payments;

- Draft routine official correspondence and assists in the preparation of various reports.

Support to the Project teams in implementation of Project business processes:

- Support drafting of the terms of references for international and local consultants and experts to be hired for the implementation of the Project;

- Provide support to the Sector Procurement Associate(s) and the Project team in the preparation and processing of procurement actions for goods, services and supplies required by the Project, including compiling and preparation of the procurement documentation, and tracking procurement requests;

- Support the payment requests authorized by the Project Manager;

- Organize translation and interpretation services in accordance with business processes.

Support to Business Process Quality Assurance:

- Facilitate that business processes followed by the projects are in line with the UNDP rules and regulations, policies, and internal control framework;

- Assist in timely reporting and participate in the drafting of the reports;

- Prepare administrative, technical, and financial reports;

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

General Assembly Resolution 2186 (XXI) decided to “bring into operations the United Nations Capital Development Fund as an organ of the General Assembly which shall function as an autonomous organization of the United Nations. The UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) assists developing countries, especially least developing countries, in the development of their economies by supplementing existing sources of capital assistance by means of grants, loans, and guarantees. UNCDFs vision is to help mobilize and catalyze an increase of capital flows for SDG impactful investments to Member States to address the most pressing development challenges facing vulnerable communities in these countries and thereby contribute to sustainable economic growth and equitable prosperity.

As a Flagship Catalytic Blended Financing platform of the UN, UNCDF utilizes its unique capability in the UN system to deploy grants, loans and guarantees to crowd-in finance for the scaling of development impact. UNCDF focuses on where the needs are greatest, a deliberate focus and capability rooted in UNCDF’s unique investment mandate to support the achievement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the realization of the Doha Programme of Action for the least developed countries, 2022–2031.

As per its Strategic Framework, UNCDF works to deploy its functions as a hybrid development organization and development finance institution. UNCDF responds to Member States requests for assistance by providing targeted technical and financial advisory services on investments for development outcomes, designing bespoke financial structuring solutions, undertaking financial derisking of investments, and enhancing investment readiness of SDG aligned projects in partnership with private sector, United Nations Organizations, International and Local Finance Institutions, Development Finance Institutions as well as Foundations and Philanthropy, among others. UNCDF works to develop local financial systems, new markets and mobilize and crowd in capital from public and private sources. UNCDF is driven by a partnership mindset which enables it to deploy its different capital capabilities in highly tailored and responsive ways in order to mobilize investments flows from other sources, in particular from the private sector. By structuring transactions which are highly impactful, but also recognize the need for multiplying the impact of its own capital, UNCDF seeks to position itself as a preferred partner for different stakeholders. UNCDF’s work is focused on three priority areas, including:

• SME Finance

• Sub-National Finance

• Digital Finance

UNCDF’s organizational set up includes an Investment and Implementation Division (IID), Investment and Finance Oversight Division (IFOD), Operations and Oversight Division (OOD) and a Directorate of the Executive Office. UNCDF staff and personnel are located in regional hubs based in Dakar (Senegal), Nairobi (Kenya) and Bangkok (Thailand) with sub-regional presence in a number of locations in the Caribbean and Pacific Regions. UNCDF is led by an Executive Secretary based out of New York, USA. Pursuant to General Assembly resolution 2321(XXII, para 1.a), the Administrator of the UNDP performs the function of the Managing Director of UNCDF. UNCDF is overseen by an Executive Board comprised of UN Member States.

The Digital Transformation and Innovation Unit (DTI) leads UNCDF's enterprise-wide digital transformation, including the integration of artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies into UNCDF's investment, programmatic, and operational workflows, while also ensuring compliance with UN AI policy and guidelines. Under UNCDF's Strategic Framework 2026–2029, DTI is responsible for operationalizing a portfolio of AI agents and emerging-technology pilots that strengthen the quality of catalytic capital deployment, accelerate programme delivery, and expand financial inclusion in Least Developed Countries (LDCs), Small Island Developing States (SIDS), and fragile settings.

The Information Technology Analyst - AI and Emerging Technologies will work on the implementation and scaling of the AI portfolio, building on the foundational AI actions and the first deployed AI system (Strategic Alignment Intelligence, or SAI). The position is central to helping to translate UNCDF's strategic AI commitments into a mature, governed, and institutionally embedded ecosystem of digital solutions serving UNCDF's catalytic mandate, while aligning with UN and UNDP AI frameworks.

Duties and Responsibilities

The AI and Emerging Technologies Integration Analyst will work under the direct supervision of the Head of Digital Transformation and Innovation Unit, UNCDF. The incumbent will collaborate closely with the Executive Secretary, Regional Team Leads (RTLs) and the Digital Transformation and Innovation Unit.

Under the overall guidance and direct supervision of the Head of Digital Transformation and Innovation Unit, the Information Technology Analyst : AI and Emerging Technologies will be responsible for the following key result areas:

1. Operation and continuous development of UNCDF's enterprise AI agent portfolio

- Operate, maintain and improve the portfolio of AI agents deployed across UNCDF's investment, programmatic and operational workflows, including agents supporting investment pipeline analysis, investment proposal review and stress-testing, programme document drafting, donor reporting, market analysis, internal guidance on roles and workflows, and other operational processes..

- Design, prototype, test and deploy new agents on the enterprise AI platforms in use or under institutional adoption, including Google Gemini Enterprise, Salesforce Agentforce, agent development frameworks such as the Google Agent Development Kit, and additional frontier large language model providers and agentic platforms as they are integrated into UNCDF's technology stack, ensuring compliance with broader UN policy on AI governance and related technology.

- Support in identification and prioritizing of new use cases through structured discovery with teams at Headquarters and in Regional Offices, and translate them into technical designs and delivery roadmaps.

- Extend deployed agents beyond retrieval and analysis toward document generation, forecasting and workflow action, including production of analytical outputs and presentation materials directly from institutional data.

- Conduct iterative validation of agent outputs against historical institutional decisions and documented outcomes, record performance metrics, and refine agent reasoning logic and system instructions accordingly.

- Maintain version-controlled technical documentation and user guidance for each deployed agent, and coordinate onboarding across Headquarters and Regional Offices.

2. Enterprise AI architecture, data integration and institutional knowledge infrastructure

- Develop, test and maintain assigned components of the shared technical layer connecting UNCDF AI agents to institutional and external data, including interoperable connectors (Model Context Protocol servers or equivalent) that can be reused across enterprise AI platforms.

- Develop and maintain retrieval and grounding capabilities over UNCDF document repositories, enabling agents to use relevant institutional documentation, results, evaluations and lessons learned with appropriate source attribution.

- Integrate approved external development-finance, macroeconomic and credit-risk data sources into AI-agent workflows, including sources such as the World Bank, OECD, IMF and commercial risk-data providers.

- Contribute technical analysis to UNCDF’s enterprise AI initiatives, including assessment of platform capabilities, licensing approaches, costs, and user-access requirements, to inform management decisions on the multi-platform architecture.

- Work with UNCDF ICT, enterprise-systems teams and relevant UNDP counterparts to implement interoperability, authentication and security requirements, and identify potential duplication across platforms.

3. Integration of emerging technologies beyond AI

- Contribute to UNCDF’s technical exploration and integration of emerging technologies relevant to development finance, including distributed ledger technologies (e.g., Hyperledger Fabric), digital public infrastructure (DPI), digital identity and eKYC systems, tokenization, and programmable-finance applications.

- Design and implement defined feasibility assessments, technical pilots and proofs of concept demonstrating how emerging technologies may accelerate capital deployment, reduce transaction costs and enhance financial inclusion in LDCs, SIDS and fragile settings.

- Translate, when assigned, defined use cases from UNCDF’s priority financial, programmatic and operational areas into technical requirements, implementation options and draft roadmaps, in line with agreed strategic direction and technical architecture.

- Research selected emerging technologies relevant to development finance—such as CBDCs, blockchain-based financial infrastructure and interoperable payment systems—and prepare concise analysis on possible uses for UNCDF.

4. AI governance, responsible deployment and risk management

- Contribute to the development and implementation of UNCDF’s internal AI governance framework, in alignment with the UN’s policies and governance framework, including model-selection criteria, prompt governance, data-handling protocols, human-in-the-loop requirements and escalation procedures for higher-risk use cases.

- Review proposed AI use cases and deployments against applicable UN-system guidance, including the UN Principles for the Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence, the Global Digital Compact, and relevant UNDP/UNCDF data-protection and cybersecurity policies.

- Support the preparation and maintenance of responsible-AI monitoring documentation and basic evaluation materials, including benchmark results, limitation disclosures and validation records.

- Identify and document potential risks associated with AI integration, escalate significant issues to the supervisor, and contribute to practical mitigation measures and management briefings.

5. Partnerships, capacity building and knowledge management

- Support the Digital Transformation and Innovation unit in engagement with external AI and emerging-technology providers, including research, meeting coordination and follow-up related to potential partnerships and collaboration with relevant UN-system entities.

- Contribute to development and delivery of practical user-orientation, prompt-engineering and role-specific training sessions and materials to help UNCDF personnel use approved AI tools effectively.

- Prepare and maintain technical and programme documentation, including architecture diagrams, decision logs, reports, and updates to UNCDF’s AI priorities.

- Participate in relevant internal UN-system forums on AI for development finance, and support the preparation of materials presenting UNCDF’s work.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Background

The UNDP Country Office success in its delivery of UNDP programmes is dependent on ensuring an adequate security framework is in place. The Host Government has primary responsibility for the security and protection of personnel employed by United Nations Security Management System organizations, their eligible family members, and property.

The UN House Security Team provides security coverage for UN House personnel, visitors, premises and assets, including 24/7 coverage of designated security posts and daytime coverage during UN House working hours.

Position Purpose

This position serves a dual function, supporting both the UN House/Common Services security arrangements, while also supporting UNDP's broader operational and programmatic objectives.

Under the guidance and supervision of the UNDP Operations Manager, the UNDP- UN House Security Associate supports the activity of the UN House Security Team and provides reliable security services for UN House Agencies. The assignment will include supporting the security arrangement with an outsourced security service, including preparation of technical requirements, technical support to related procurement process and monitoring of contractor performance. Further to support UNDP as required in the implementation of security and safety management in Moldova

The incumbent will work in close coordination with the UN House Management Committee, UNDP Procurement and other relevant functions for the outsourced security services transition and contract implementation. He/she will also work in close coordination with the UNDSS Security Associate for technical security guidance on UN House related matters as well as with UNDP Security Office, through the RSA/SRSS for technical guidance on UNDP related security matters.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

Performance monitoring of the security company (Guards team):

- Monitor and coordinate the outsourced security services, aimed at ensuring uninterrupted security coverage of UN House.

- Support induction and briefing of the selected company’s deployed personnel on UN House security procedures, access control arrangements, control-center functions, CCTV and access-control systems, fire and emergency procedures, incident reporting requirements, confidentiality and standards of conduct.

- Draft and/or coordinate post instructions, relevant SOPs, logbooks, access arrangements and operational information required for the UN House security service.

- Check, against contractual requirements, that deployed contractor personnel meet the required qualifications, training and documentation requirements and that the contractor has the required staffing/replacement arrangements in place.

- Monitor service delivery against the contract, technical specifications and agreed KPIs, including staffing levels, attendance, post coverage, response to incidents, reporting, replacement arrangements and compliance with UN House security procedures.

- Maintain regular operational communication with the contractor’s designated supervisor/team leader and promptly escalate performance gaps, security incidents or non-compliance with the UNDP Operations Manager, with technical coordination with UNDSS as appropriate.

- Monitor the performance and conduct of Security Guards and ensure compliance with applicable SOPs and security instructions and support follow-up on corrective actions and prepare periodic performance observations/reports as required.

- Support verification that the contractor operates in accordance with applicable Moldovan legislation and contractual obligations, while referring legal or contractual compliance issues to the responsible UNDP functions for determination.

Monitor the Access Control and Control Center:

- Control admission of authorized personnel and movement of United Nations property into and out of the premises.

- Ensure that unauthorized personnel and prohibited items do not gain access to UN House facilities.

- Conduct patrols and physical security checks of the compound, offices, perimeter and parking areas, and report irregularities.

- Use relevant technical screening and access-control equipment and maintain control of the emergency key system and related records.

- Maintain and/or supervise operation of the security control center.

- Prepare, print, issue, activate/deactivate and replace UN House access cards for personnel, as required, and maintain accurate records of cards issued, returned, lost, damaged or cancelled.

- Monitor and control, as applicable, the UN House Emergency Line and Panic Button, video surveillance system, fire safety and suppression system, electronic door locking/access-control system and VHF working channel.

- Ensure familiarity with and compliance with established procedures for operation of security systems.

Assist in supporting CO in Emergency Response:

- Be familiar with emergency procedures, Security Standard Operating Procedures and contingency plans and support their implementation.

- Know how to use firefighting equipment and support emergency response measures on the premises.

- Respond to emergencies affecting the safety and security of UN House personnel, visitors, assets and facilities in accordance with authorized procedures.

Overall security support to UNDP management and personnel:

- Provide support in keeping UNDP management informed of security matters affecting UNDP programmes and its personnel.

- Assist in implementing the Country Security Plan, Contingency Plans, and Business Continuity Management.

- Provide support to the UNDP Operations Manager on implementation of relevant security arrangements, including Warden System support, maps, security routes and related documents, as requested.

- Gather information for inclusion in Country Office security reports;

- Respond to and assist in reporting safety and security incidents affecting UNDP personnel and eligible dependents by gathering and verifying security information relevant to analyzing the situation;

- Maintain information of UNDP security contact details;

- Assist UNDP OM with the preparation and updating security aspects of procedures for dealing with emergencies involving UNDP staff and operations;

- Provide support in organizing training courses on security awareness and preparedness for UNDP personnel and provide security briefings to newly recruited employees;

- Assist UNDP OM during emergencies, incidents and security-related events;

- Monitoring news/information with potential impact on the security environment through different external and internal sources and providing information to OM on possible effects to UNDP personnel, programs and assets;

- Contribute to knowledge networks and professional communities.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is a global organization that is part of the broader United Nations System, dedicated to promoting sustainable development. Established in 1965, UNDP plays a pivotal role in supporting nations in their efforts to eradicate poverty, reduce inequality, and advance socio-economic development. With a focus on inclusive and equitable growth, UNDP provides technical expertise, mobilizes financial resources, and delivers policy and other services to support the formulation and implementation of effective development strategies and solutions that align with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP operates in over 170 countries and territories, collaborating with local partners, governments, and other stakeholders to build resilient communities and foster sustainable development. UNDP's initiatives span a wide range of areas, including climate change, gender equality, governance, and crisis response, embodying its commitment to creating a better and more sustainable future for people across the globe.

Under the overall guidance of the Operations and Finance Specialist, the Finance Associate supports the highest efficiency in People Programme operations, as well as other programmes and partnerships within the PPP team, including timely and accurate donor reporting, financial resources management and the provision of accurate, thoroughly researched and documented financial information. He/she analyzes operational rules and regulations and provides solutions to a wide spectrum of complex operational issues. The Finance Associate promotes a collaborative, client-oriented approach consistent with UNDP rules and regulations.

Under the guidance and direct supervision of the Finance Specialist, the Finance Associate provides support in execution of financial services in the BMS/OHR/PPP Team ensuring effective and transparent financial management

The Finance Associate works in close collaboration with the BMS/OHR New York, BMS/Office of Financial Resources Management (OFRM)/Corporate Financial Reporting and Agency Services Team, BMS/Information and Technology Management Office (ITM), as well as the transactional part of HR and finance services ensuring successful operations, human resources management, financial resource management, and client-orientation of the People Programmes.

Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Ensures implementation of the People Programme financial management strategies

- Ensure People Programmes financial activities, financial recording/reporting system, and follow-up on audit recommendations are in full compliance with UNDP Programme and Operations Policies and Procedures (POPP) and strategies.

- Support implementation of effective internal controls and proper functioning of a client-oriented financial resources management system.

- Assist in supporting office management to articulate the framework and conditions of contributions to People Programmes.

- Assist in monitoring People Programme financial resources, reconcile donor accounts and prepare forecasts.

- Support in monitoring of financial exception reports for unusual activities, transactions and investigation of anomalies or unusual transactions. Provision of information to management on the results of the investigation when satisfactory answers are not obtained.

- Support in reviewing and approving cost estimates, including update and development of tools for calculation of JPO/SDP/Seconded expert costs and continuous alignment with UNDP finance policies.

- Assist in monitoring and follow up on contributions from donors to the JPO Programme positions.

- Support in organization of cost-recovery mechanisms for services provided by UNDP to JPO Programmes of UN agencies.

- Assist in controlling and monitoring of co-financing arrangements and processes

- Support in controlling and monitoring of Centrally Management Costs arrangements and processes

- Support end-year reversal of UN Organisations JPO Programme financial transactions from UNDP books.

Ensure implementation of timely and accurate financial reporting on People Programmes

- Support implementation of JPO Programme financial management model and suggest improvements as applicable.

- Assists in preparation of reports containing analysis of the People Programme financial situation.

- Support in monitoring and preparation of People Programmes financial reports to donors and UN Agencies on a timely and quality basis.

- Support in facilitation of JPO travel requests, including organization of air tickets and monitoring of Duty Travel and Training Balances

- Support in designing, developing and maintaining Business Intelligence (BI) and Data Analytics tools such as Power BI, while leveraging advanced Excel capabilities to analyse complex data from multiple sources into user friendly reports and summaries to support daily operations as well as strategic decision making.

- Support in designing, refining and developing emerging HR, financial and operational oversight tools such as UN All, Power BI, Dashboards.

- Synthesize lessons learned and best practices in financial management.

- Provide sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Background

Afghanistan for more than 50 years on climate change and resilience, gender, governance, health, livelihoods, and rule of law.

Following the power shift in August 2021, the situation for the country remains largely uncertain and fragile, with approximately seventy percent of the population facing multifaceted vulnerabilities affecting their well-being, human security and long-term development while nearly a third of the population are estimated to be acutely food insecure. Over the recent years, international assistance has played a vital role in averting a socioeconomic collapse by providing lifesaving, resilience-building and livelihoods-sustaining assistance to millions of people, hundreds of critical healthcare and educational centres, and tens of thousands of small and medium enterprises, often owned and managed by women. Nevertheless, the humanitarian challenge in Afghanistan is one of the biggest in the world, and basic human needs and priorities remain extremely high. In 2024, 95 percent of households experienced at least one shock of an economic or natural disaster nature such as floods, droughts and others.

To help tackle the pressing challenges for enduring livelihoods and climate resilience, UNDP is designing fit-for-purpose portfolios of programs to create new livelihoods, income opportunities, basic services and to build resilience against climate-induced natural calamities that continue to haunt millions of households in the country.

Afghanistan remains one of the most gender-unequal countries in the world, with women facing systemic challenges hindering their access to education and employment opportunities in the public sector and restricting their participation in public life. UNDP remains committed to women's empowerment through capacity-building initiatives, livelihoods and self-employment/employment support, enhancing gender-responsive decision-making at community level, and supporting local communities to include women, in line with UNSCR 1325 (Women, Peace, and Security).

To support UN joint programming in the provision of basic human needs, a Special Trust Fund for Afghanistan (hereinafter referred as the Fund or STFA) was established on 20 October 2021.

The Fund serves as an inter-agency mechanism to enable donors to channel their resources and coordinate their support to the UN joint programmes in support of the UN Strategic Framework for Afghanistan (UNSFA) which serves as the strategic planning framework for the United Nations in Afghanistan. The Steering Committee is the decision making structure for the Fund while the Multi-Partner Trust Fund Office (MPTF Office) acts as the Administrative Agent. The Trust Fund Management Unit (TFMU) is the Fund Secretariat for STFA and is the entity responsible for the operational functioning of the Fund and provides technical and management support to the Steering Committee. The STFA will be directly supervised by the Resident Coordinator while UNDP will provide administrative support to the Secretariat, TFMU.

Under the direct supervision and overall guidance of the Resident Coordinator and matrix reporting of the UNDP Resident Representative, the Trust Fund Manager supports the Trust Fund governance structures to engage with relevant stakeholders (donor community and development partners) through the Trust Fund Steering Committee and Technical Coordination Working Group (TCWG) mechanism. The Trust Fund Manager leads the Project Management, Finance, Communications as well as Monitoring and Evaluation teams housed in the Trust Fund Management Unit. The team composition shall be adjusted over time as and when approved by the Steering Committee. The Trust Fund Manager will report administratively to the UNDP Resident Representative.

Job Purpose and Organizational Context

The Trust Fund Manager performs functions related to (1) management and coordination of the activities financed by the Trust Fund and advice to the Steering Committee on the Fund strategic priorities; (2) advocacy and building strategic partnerships; (3) knowledge management and impact analysis of the activities financed by the Trust Fund; and (4) management and oversight of the TFMU.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Management and coordination of the activities financed by the Trust Fund and advice to the Steering Committee on the Fund strategic priorities

- Provide strategic advice to the STFA Steering Committee on Fund related matters.

- Support the Resident Coordinator, donors and Participating UN Organizations in the review and redesign of the governance arrangements; strategies and coordination arrangements, as needed, ensuring alignment to Agenda 2030 as well as national sectoral and cross-cutting priorities.

- Ensure the development of the Fund’s strategic planning documents.

- Oversee the review and updating of the Fund ToR and the Operations Manual.

- Ensure effective technical and administrative support to the Steering Committee and TCWGs’ processes and follow-up of on decisions.

- Liaise and ensure close coordination with the Fund Administrative Agent (MPTF Office in New York).

- Guide the Participating UN Organizations on the programming processes and requirements as laid out in the TF Operations Manual.

- Implement call for proposals in line with the Fund procedures and Resource Allocation Criteria.

- Ensure quality control of the MPTF funded projects, including coherence, risk management and application of cross-cutting approaches within the Fund.

- Ensure Fund monitoring through the Fund-level Results Management System.

- Ensure the development and implementation of the Fund Risk Management Strategy.

- Ensure and oversee the production of the Fund annual reports and other updates.

2. Advocacy and Building Strategic Partnerships

- Develop and ensure implementation of the Fund's communication strategy and visibility plan.

- Develop and ensure implementation of the Fund's resource mobilization strategy.

- Liaises and coordinates with donor focal points and other TF stakeholders.

- Establishes and maintains strategic partnerships with additional potential donors, and identify and initiates key resource mobilization opportunities.

- Facilitates UN multi-agency engagement in the programming.

- Ensures linkages and consistency between the MPTF and other related initiatives.

- Lead outreach efforts vis-à-vis civil society actors, foundations, and the private sector and facilitate the identification of collaboration arrangements as appropriate.

3. Lead Knowledge management and impact analysis of the activities financed by the Trust Fund

- Analysis and management of Fund's knowledge, including knowledge systematization, establishment of good practices and lessons learned and proposals of recommendations.

- Commission assessments, studies, surveys as instructed by the Steering Committee and the TCWGs.

- Contribute to strategic and policy discussions with the MPTF stakeholders.

- Identification and synthesis of best practices and lessons learnt directly linked to country policy goals.

4. Management and Oversight of the Trust Fund Management Unit / Team

- Oversee the activities of the TFMU and its team.

- Prepare and monitor the Annual Work Plan(s) and budget for the TFMU.

- Prepare job descriptions and vacancy announcements, and identify, hire and supervise staff and consultants.

- Ensure monitoring and control of operational risks of the TFMU.

Other

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: Supervises the Trust Fund Management Unit

Competencies

Core:

Achieve Results:

- Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact. ​

Think Innovatively:

- Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems. ​

Learn Continuously:

- Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences.​

Adapt with Agility:

- Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands. ​

Act with Determination:

- Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results​.

Engage and Partner:

- Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration​.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

- Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity​.

Cross-Functional & Technical

Partnership management - Relationship management:

- Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding.

Partnership management - Multi-stakeholder engagement and funding:

- Knowledge and ability to forge multi-stakeholder partnerships, and remove any obstacles to Resource mobilization and multi-stakeholder funding platforms.

Business management - Risk management:

Business Development - Integration within the UN:

- Ability to identity, and integrate capacity and assets of the UN system, and engage in joint work.

- Knowledge of the UN System and ability to apply this knowledge to strategic and/or practical situations.

Business Direction & Strategy - Negotiation and Influence:

Business direction & strategy - System Thinking:

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- A first level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above-mentioned fields, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Experience in resource mobilization and partnership development is required.

- Demonstrated in-depth experience in providing policy advice and developing programmatic solutions, tools and methodologies for the attainment of the SDGs is required.

- Experience in the use of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, Teams, etc.), and advanced knowledge of web-based management systems such as ERP and advanced programmes for statistical analysis of data is required.

Background

Job Purpose and Organizational Context

As the lead United Nations agency on international development, UNDP works in 170 countries and territories to eradicate poverty and reduce inequality. UNDP helps countries develop policies, leadership skills, partnerships and institutional capabilities to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

As outlined in the UNDP Strategic Plan 2026-2029, UNDP’s work is guided by four strategic objectives that together define the organization’s contribution to human development: expanding prosperity for all, strengthening effective governance, safeguarding a healthy planet and building crisis resilience. These objectives are enabled by three accelerators that drive transformative impact across the portfolio: digital and AI innovation, gender equality and sustainable finance. Through this integrated approach, UNDP supports countries to deliver tangible improvements in people’s lives and to advance sustainable development at scale.

In alignment with the UNDP Strategic Plan, the Regional Programme for Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) 2026-2029 outlines UNDP strategic offers and priorities for the next four years in the LAC region and identifies sustainable finance as a key accelerator. At the Fourth International Conference on Financing for Development (FfD4), UNDP also launched the LAC Facility for Financing Resilient Human Development (LAC Facility), which is a multi-stakeholder platform focused on enhancing the region’s capacity to mobilize public and private investments. The LAC Facility will be an essential mechanism to support the roll-out of the Regional Programme 2026-2029 in LAC.

UNDP, through its Sustainable Finance Hub (SFH) (https://sdgfinance.undp.org/), supports partners in promoting financing for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). As an accelerator of the UNDP Strategic Plan, sustainable finance strengthens countries’ ability to mobilize, align and deploy finance at scale for national priorities. UNDP supports international and country level policy reform as a catalyst for system-wide change, stronger policy environments, better-functioning markets and more coherent financing strategies for sustainable development. SFH work is delivered through three interconnected portfolios: 1) Public Finance for the SDGs; 2) Private Finance for the SDGs; and 3) Global & Country Financing Policy Frameworks.

SFH Public Finance for SDGs (PF4SDGs) portfolio supports governments to strengthen public finance systems for sustainable development. Operating across 99+ countries with a portfolio exceeding $200 million, the portfolio provides integrated technical assistance across four core pillars: 1) Tax/Domestic Resource Mobilization, 2) Public Expenditure Efficiency and Effectiveness, 3) Fiscal Policy Coherence, and 4) Digital Fiscal Governance. The portfolio works with Ministries of Finance, Planning, and line ministries to align fiscal policies, tax systems, debt strategies and public expenditure with national development priorities and the 2030 Agenda. UNDP’s comparative advantage in public finance stems from its unique position at the nexus of fiscal policy and development outcomes. Rather than focusing on isolated technical reforms, UNDP empowers governments to adopt whole-of-government and whole-of-society strategies that link fiscal instruments directly to sustainable development impact. This includes facilitating cross-ministerial policy dialogue, building coalitions for reform, integrating governance, climate, gender, health, and resilience priorities into fiscal frameworks, and supporting countries in translating SDG ambitions into fiscally viable implementation pathways.

The Regional Public Finance for SDGs Specialist will report to the Head of Public Finance for SDGs, SFH (Madrid), with a matrix reporting line to the Regional Advisor, SDG Finance – Latin America and the Caribbean, in the Regional Hub for LAC (Panama), while maintaining strong working relationships with the relevant teams/experts from the global SFH, Regional Hub, and Global Policy Network (GPN), as well as the OECD TIWB Secretariat in Paris. The position will be responsible for contributing to the delivery of activities under UNDP’s Public Finance for SDGs initiative in the region, hosted within the Regional Hub for LAC in Panama and the activities will contribute to the implementation of UNDP’s Regional Programme for LAC (2026-2029) and the LAC Facility for Financing Resilient Human Development.

- Provide strategic and technical support to the Regional Hub and SFH for PF4SDGs implementation in the region, working closely with Country Offices, Regional Hub and SFH teams.

- Support Country Offices to provide policy advice to Ministries of Finance, Planning, and matincluding by connecting and building on existing work on the Integrated National Financing Frameworks (INFFs) and financing strategies for SDGs/NDCs/NBSAPs.

- Work with Regional Hub and global SFH teams to provide technical support to the County Offices for the country-level implementation of PF4SDGs related interventions, drafting/reviewing ToRs and concept notes/FPC related materials, technical reporting, and backstopping.

- Guide research and analysis to identify public finance reforms, drawing on PF4SDGs analytical tools and the fiscal policy coherence process.

- Support the Regional Hub and Country Offices to facilitate dialogue and coalition building with government, donors, civil society, and private sector stakeholders.

- Develop/refine frameworks, methodologies, and tools for PF4SDGs implementation.

- Support the design and implementation of TIWB (Tax Inspectors Without Borders) initiatives in the region, including coordination with COs and relevant partners, and ensuring alignment with PF4SDGs objectives.

Advise and support knowledge, Evidence, and Learning

- Conduct horizon scanning and original research on tax, fiscal policy, public financial management (PFM), debt management and related topics.

- Produce policy papers, case studies, and knowledge products for expert and non-expert audiences based on ongoing CO work and regional level initiatives.

- Contribute to UNDP flagship publications, policy briefs, and working papers

- Document lessons learned, innovations, and impact from PF4SDGs interventions, promoting global uptake.

- Support the Regional Hub to facilitate South-South and triangular cooperation for peer learning.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments
