- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

At the country level, UNV Field Units (FUs) and designated UNV personnel are responsible for promoting volunteerism through the mobilization of UN Volunteers across the UN system in the areas of peace, development, human rights and humanitarian assistance. FUs represent and position UNV within the respective countries, particularly within the UN country team, adopting a client-oriented and solutions-based approach.

As UNV is the systemwide service administered by UNDP, FUs are hosted within relevant UNDP offices, collaborating closely with the UNDP resident representative and the UN resident coordinator system. The UNV country coordinator ensures compliance with UNV and UNDP policies, rules, and regulations.

Under the overall guidance of the regional manager and direct supervision of the portfolio manager or specialist in the Regional Office (RO), the country coordinator manages the FU and leads UNV’s engagement at the country level.

The role’s primary purpose is to ensure that UNV effectively anticipates and responds to the needs of the UN system and partners by mobilizing qualified volunteers and promoting volunteerism across sectors. This includes strategic positioning, partnership building, advocacy, and contribution to UNV’s Strategic Framework implementation.

The country coordinator works under the general guidance of the UN resident coordinator to position UNV and its services within the UN system and liaises regularly with the UNDP resident representative for support. The incumbent also collaborates closely with the UNDP country office for administrative matters, participates in UN country team activities as invited (including joint UN programme, operations, communications teams and other subsidiary groups of UNCT), and may represent UNV in joint coordination mechanisms with government and non-government stakeholders.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Lead volunteer mobilization

• Position UNV as a system-wide service provider supporting UN partners to achieve their programmes and UNSDCF goals.

• Develop and implement country-level volunteer mobilization strategies aligned with UNV’s Strategic Framework and partner demand.

• Participate in UN collective planning processes (CCA, UNSDCF, humanitarian response plans, thematic task forces) to integrate volunteerism in their implementation.

• Present UNV’s value proposition to maximize contributions of UN Volunteers, and guide partners in developing volunteer assignment descriptions.

• Support local talent outreach and acquisition efforts in alignment with corporate strategies.

• Promote Online Volunteering as a core component of UNV’s offer.

• Monitor mobilization trends, track key performance indicators, and use corporate tools (CRM, BI reports, UVP) for informed decision-making.

• Facilitate executive, operational, and partnership missions by UNV.

2. Manage partnerships

• Build and sustain effective relationships with UN partners to promote UNV’s mandate and services.

• Analyze country strategies (UNSDCF, agency strategies) to identify opportunities for volunteer mobilization.

• Maintain business intelligence on UN programming, funding and workforce trends to diversify partnerships and forecast volunteer demand.

• Engage regularly the heads of agencies, their management teams and senior programme and operations staff to support volunteer mobilization, collaborating proactively to identify opportunities

• In coordination with the RO and ERCS, map and pursue SVF mobilization opportunities.

• Engage with government, civil society, private sector, and development partners in close coordination with other UN entities as may be required to realize agreed objectives.

3. Ensure Duty of Care

• Support host entities with guidance and best practices to ensure successful volunteer assignments.

• Work closely with UNDSS, the UN Designated Official for security, and host agencies to ensure the safety, security, and inclusion of UN Volunteers. Provide timely support during security evacuations.

• Ensure volunteers receive appropriate briefings, orientation, and guidance from host entities on arrival and benefit from appropriate supervision throughout their assignment.

• Brief the volunteer on expected code of conduct and other relevant factors for a successful experience; be available to answer questions.

• Conduct regular field visits to volunteer locations and monitor volunteer well-being and provide guidance on critical administrative aspects.

• Facilitate regular engagement with and among volunteers (e.g., town halls, networking, and community activities) to strengthen volunteer experience and well-being.

4. Lead advocacy on volunteerism

• Align communications with volunteer mobilization and talent acquisition goals, develop impactful volunteer stories in collaboration with the RO and External Relations and Communications Section (ERCS), promote UNV at national, regional and global levels.

• Stay informed of national volunteer initiatives, policies and strategies, including those supported by the UN system, and share relevant updates with Volunteer Advisory Services Section.

• Stay informed of host countries’ aspirations to promote national volunteer talent through fully funded UNV assignments domestically and abroad, share relevant updates with ERCS on emerging demand for UNV solutions, and support their implementation if needed.

• Stay informed of the International Volunteer Day and other volunteer recognition efforts by national counterparts and, where appropriate, collaborate around respective activities in close coordination with UN country teams and upon advice from the RO and ERCS.

• Encourage volunteers to act as advocates and disseminate their experiences as advocates and ambassadors of volunteer action.

5. FU Management

• Lead and coordinate the FU to ensure effective and efficient service delivery and a collaborative work environment.

• Supervise, empower and ensure performance and accountability of FU team members. Provide coaching and oversight to ensure consistency and client orientation in the FU’s communication with all clients.

• Develop, monitor, and manage the FU’s annual work plan and budget in compliance with performance targets and UNDP regulations.

• Liaise with UNDP programme and operations teams to ensure administrative support, alignment with local protocol, and facilitate cooperation on critical issues such as visas for international volunteers.

• Ensure that the FU undertake assigned transactions in the Volunteer Management Cycle in accordance with corporate SOPs.

• Escalate operational and reputational risks and other significant issues promptly to the RO.

Competencies

Core Competencies

Achieve Results:

- Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work

Think Innovatively:

- Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking

Learn Continuously:

- Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning

Adapt with Agility:

- Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process

Act with Determination:

- Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously

Engage and Partner:

- Is facilitator/integrator, bring people together, build/maintain coalitions/partnerships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

- Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making

People Management

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

System Thinking

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgment to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact other parts of the system

Integration within the UN System

- Ability to identify and integrate the capacity and assets of the UN system and engage in joint work. Knowledge of the UN System and ability to apply this knowledge to strategic and/or practical situations

Results-based Management

- Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus on improved performance and demonstrable results. Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools

Partnerships Management

- Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies

Knowledge Generation

- Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need

- Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations

Digital Awareness and Literacy

- Ability to monitor new and emerging technologies, as well as understand their usage, potential, limitations, impact, and added value

- Ability to rapidly and readily adopt and use new technologies in professional activities, and to empower others to use them as needed. Knowledge of the usage of digital technologies and emerging trends

Event planning and execution

- Ability to plan, manage and execute public and private events to ensure that they support and amplify individual communications and advocacy initiatives, as well as UNV's overall brand and mandate

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent), or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience in humanitarian, development and/or peace-related fields.

- Experience in partnership building and management is essential.

- Experience in advocacy, public relations, or communication is an asset.

- Experience in programme reporting, monitoring and evaluation is an asset.

- Experience in volunteer management and/or promotion of volunteerism is an asset.

- Experience in working in digital platforms and tools, including CRM and ERP systems is an asset.

Office/Unit/Project Description

The Volunteer Services Centre (VSC), part of UNV’s Management Services, supports a growing global portfolio of over 15,000 UN Volunteers (2025), delivering timely and high-quality services across the full volunteer lifecycle. This includes recruitment, pre-assignment processing, contract administration, payroll, separation, and evacuation support for UN Volunteers serving with UN agencies, funds, programmes, and missions. With a presence in 13 locations worldwide, VSC ensures consistent and compliant service delivery across diverse operational contexts.

Under the guidance and supervision of the Operations Associate/Team Leader (G7) for the duty station, the Operations Associate supports the delivery of end-to-end volunteer lifecycle services within the VSC. The role contributes to timely onboarding, contract administration, and accurate management of benefits & entitlements, and lifecycle events.

The incumbent ensures the integrity, transparency, and accuracy of service delivery in line with the UN Volunteers Conditions of Service (COS), policies, and procedures, while maintaining high-quality outputs and consistency across multiple countries and stakeholders.

VSC collaborates closely with the Volunteer Solutions Section (VSS), headquarter units, Regional Offices, Field Units, the UNDP Global Shared Services Centre, and other UN partners to deliver coordinated services. The Operations Associate advises stakeholders on policies and procedures, promotes a collaborative and client-focused approach, and supports the timely implementation of the VSC work plan.

Scope of Work

The Operations Associate supports the delivery of end-to-end UN Volunteer lifecycle services, ensuring timely, accurate, and compliant execution of operational processes from onboarding through separation across multiple countries and stakeholders.

3.1 Provision of Volunteer Lifecycle Services

- Facilitae processing of assignments from offer issuance through entry on duty and separation, including offer and/or contract generation and management, benefits & entitlements, life events, separations, verification of documentation and required clearances.

- Review, validate and follow up on pre-assignment requirements, including PII updates, mandatory courses, beneficiary information, banking details, medical clearance, etc.

- Administer volunteer contracts and manage lifecycle processes, including benefits, entitlements, claims, and life events in line with the UNV Conditions of Service.

- Handle complex and sensitive cases, including medical and security evacuations, contract amendments, resignations, terminations, and recovery of overpayments, ensuring confidentiality and compliance.

- Administer and certify processing of benefits in full compliance with applicable provisions of the UN COS.

3.2 Data Management and Compliance

- Review validate, and record supporting documentation and transactions in corporate systems to ensure accuracy for payroll processing, reporting, and audit purposes.

- Support payroll-related administration by reviewing payment requests, ensuring completeness and alignment with the COS, following up on HR data corrections, and coordinating on payroll and banking exceptions, including returned or rejected payments where applicable.

- Maintain accurate and up-to-date records and case history in relevant systems, ensuring full traceability and proper documentation of all actions.

- Ensure all activities are compliant with applicable policies, procedures, and internal control frameworks.

3.4 Coordination and Client Service Delivery

- Liaise with Regional Offices, Field Units, UN entities, and internal teams to coordinate service delivery and resolve operational queries and ensure consistent application of policies and procedures.

- Provide guidance to stakeholders, including UN Volunteers, on lifecycle processes, documentation requirements and service-related matters, and ensure timely follow-up on pending actions and exceptional case.

- Support handling, follow=up, and escalation of operational queries and cases in line with established workflows, ensuring appropriate communication and resolution.

3.5 Monitoring, Issue Resolution and Risk Management

- Monitor the progress of lifecycle cases and service transactions across deployment, contract administration, payroll and separation.

- Identify risks, delays, or inconsistencies and escalate issues as appropriate.

- Support timely resolution of operational issues, coordinating with relevant teams and service providers where required.

3.6 Knowledge Management

- Contribute to the review and continuous improvement of workflows, standard operating procedures and templates by identifying bottlebecks and operational gaps.

- Provide inputs for preparation of knowledge articles, frequently asked questions (FAQ) and best practices. Support knowledge sharing through development of training materials, guidance notes, and lessons learned.

- Participate in knowledge networks and communities of practice.

3.7 The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation.

The Operations Associate will report to the Operations Associate/Team Leader (G7) for the location under the substantive guidance of the P3 Operations Specialist and overall leadership of Deputy Chief, Volunteer Services Centre (VSC).

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The country programme document, 2025-2030, aligns with the 2030 Agenda, the African Union Agenda 2063, and the UNDP Strategic Plan, 2022-2025. It represents UNDP contributions to the National Development Plan and the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework.

It focuses on two pillars: (a) People-centred sustainable development and resilience, prioritizing people’s well-being and planetary health (aligned with Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework outcomes 1 and 2 and UNDP signature solutions 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6); and b) Inclusive governance, peace, and prosperity, embodying harmonious development, effective resource management, and equitable governance (aligned with Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework outcomes 2 and 3 and UNDP signature solutions 2, 3 and 6).

The role of the Country Office Communications & Partnerships Unit is to adopt UNDP’s global communication strategy to a local context and the Country Office development priorities. Through the production of high-quality communication materials and innovative use of relevantly targeted communication channels (internal and external), the communications team works collaboratively to position UNDP as a leader in the development arena, promote visibility of UNDP program outcomes/development results, mobilize support for Sustainable Development Goals in the country, and practice delivery as one UN.

Under the guidance and direct supervision of the Resident Representative, with support from the Deputy Resident Representative, the Communications and Partnership Specialist serves as Head of the Communication and Partnership Unit and provides office-wide strategic leadership for communications, partnerships, external relations, advocacy and resource mobilization. As a member of the Country Office senior advisory structure, the Specialist provides authoritative advice to senior management, shapes institutional positioning and engagement with senior government, development partner and private-sector counterparts, and leads the design, governance and oversight of integrated strategies aligned with corporate, regional and Country Office priorities.

The Communications and Partnership Specialist will maintain a regular working relationship with the Regional Communications Adviser. The Communications and Partnership Specialist would also work in close collaboration with the Programme and Operations teams, staff of other UN Agencies, will be an active member of the UN Communications Group, the UNDP Communications Regional and HQ staff, government officials, international and local media, subject matter experts, donors, and civil society to ensure successful implementation of UNDP’s communication strategy in the Country Office.

We are seeking a highly experienced and dynamic Communications and Partnership Specialist to lead the Communication and Partnership Unit at a senior strategic level. The incumbent will translate corporate and Country Programme priorities into an integrated communications, partnership and resource mobilization agenda; exercise judgement on complex and sensitive issues; advise senior management on strategic positioning and reputational risk; and ensure accountable, coherent delivery across the Country Office.

The successful candidate will be responsible for leading the Country Office's communication and visibility initiatives, cultivating strategic partnerships, strengthening external relations, and overseeing the development of compelling multimedia content that enhances organizational reputation, supports resource mobilization efforts, and engages a wide range of audiences.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

Providing strategic leadership and oversight for communication, advocacy and visibility initiatives that strengthen UNDP positioning and reputation, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Lead the formulation, approval and periodic review of an integrated Country Office communications, advocacy and visibility strategy and annual plans, establishing priorities, governance arrangements, performance standards and accountabilities for implementation by the Communications Analyst and unit personnel;

- Set strategic messaging and ensure quality assurance and compliance with UNDP branding standards across all platforms and major products;

- Provide authoritative strategic advice on media relations, high-level press engagements, crisis and sensitive communications, political context recommend response options to senior management and coordinate implementation of agreed risk-mitigation measures;

- Draft and review press releases, speeches, newsletters, success stories, and other communication products;

- Provide strategic oversight and quality assurance for the Country Office website, social media platforms and digital campaigns, with day-to-day management led by the Communications Analyst;

- Establish performance, audience and influence metrics; commission or lead periodic analysis; and use evidence to advise senior management on corrective action, investment priorities and strategic adjustments.

Leading strategic partnerships, senior stakeholder engagement and external relations in support of Country Office priorities and leading the substantive development and negotiation of partnership frameworks focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Lead the identification, cultivation, negotiation and strategic stewardship of high-value relationships with senior government counterparts, donors, UN entities, international financial institutions, civil society and private-sector partners, with accountability for advancing Country Programme priorities and UNDP positioning;

- Develop partnership engagement strategies and collaboration frameworks;

- participate in senior-level policy dialogues, donor consultations, forums and negotiations; prepare strategic advice, briefing and engagement options for the RR/DRR; and secure follow-up on institutional commitments;

- Lead the substantive development and negotiation of partnership frameworks, Memoranda of Understanding, financing arrangements and other collaborative initiatives, ensuring strategic fit, due diligence, risk management and clear institutional accountabilities;

- Maintain a stakeholder database and engagement plan;

- Strengthen networking opportunities for organizational growth and influence.

Leading communication and partnership support to resource mobilization, quality assurance of donor agreements, donor relations and the identification of new funding and collaboration opportunities, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Lead or provide final strategic quality assurance for major funding proposals, investment cases and concept notes, ensuring a compelling value proposition, programme coherence and alignment with partner priorities;

- Prepare communication materials for donor engagement and fundraising campaigns;

- Lead development and implementation of the Country Office partnership and resource mobilization strategy; direct senior-level intelligence and opportunity analysis; prioritize prospects; and maintain management oversight of a diversified pipeline, targets, risks and conversion performance in coordination with Programme teams;

- Provide office-wide governance and quality assurance for donor engagement, visibility, reporting and stewardship commitments; resolve cross-unit bottlenecks; escalate material risks; and hold responsible teams accountable for consistent and timely follow-up;

- Develop promotional materials highlighting organizational achievements and impact.

Providing strategic direction and quality assurance for high-quality communication and knowledge products that showcase organizational achievements and lessons learned, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Set priorities and provide strategic direction and final quality assurance for multimedia content, publications and digital campaigns produced under the day-to-day leadership of the Communications Analyst;

- Document project results, beneficiary stories, and best practices;

- Develop case studies, factsheets, annual reports, and impact reports;

- Ensure quality control and consistency of all communication materials;

- Facilitate internal knowledge-sharing initiatives.

Lead in strengthening the organization's digital presence and public engagement.

- Set strategic direction, risk parameters and performance expectations for social media and digital engagement, with operational management and content calendars led by the Communications Analyst;

- Monitor online engagement, media coverage, and public perception;

- Coordinate digital campaigns to promote organizational initiatives;

- Respond to media inquiries and coordinate public information activities;

- Analyze communication metrics and prepare performance reports.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement:

Under the overall guidance and direct supervision of the Resident Representative, with support from the Deputy Resident Representative, the Communications and Partnership Specialist serves as Head of the Communication and Partnership Unit and exercises delegated authority for its strategic direction, integrated planning, budget and resource prioritization, workforce management, quality assurance, risk management and performance. The Specialist supervises and develops Unit personnel, establishes accountabilities, makes recommendations on resource allocation and service delivery, and is accountable for the quality and timeliness of office-wide communications, partnership and resource mobilization results. The Communications Analyst leads day-to-day operational coordination of communications personnel and consultants under the Specialist's direction and delegated framework.

jobs.description:

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

General Assembly Resolution 2186 (XXI) decided to “bring into operations the United Nations Capital Development Fund as an organ of the General Assembly which shall function as an autonomous organization of the United Nations. The UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) assists developing countries, especially least developing countries, in the development of their economies by supplementing existing sources of capital assistance by means of grants, loans, and guarantees. UNCDFs vision is to help mobilize and catalyze an increase of capital flows for SDG impactful investments to Member States to address the most pressing development challenges facing vulnerable communities in these countries and thereby contribute to sustainable economic growth and equitable prosperity.

As a Flagship Catalytic Blended Financing platform of the UN, UNCDF utilizes its unique capability in the UN system to deploy grants, loans and guarantees to crowd-in finance for the scaling of development impact. UNCDF focuses on where the needs are greatest, a deliberate focus and capability rooted in UNCDF’s unique investment mandate to support the achievement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the realization of the Doha Programme of Action for the least developed countries, 2022–2031.

As per its Strategic Framework, UNCDF works to deploy its functions as a hybrid development organization and development finance institution. UNCDF responds to Member States requests for assistance by providing targeted technical and financial advisory services on investments for development outcomes, designing bespoke financial structuring solutions, undertaking financial derisking of investments, and enhancing investment readiness of SDG aligned projects in partnership with private sector, United Nations Organizations, International and Local Finance Institutions, Development Finance Institutions as well as Foundations and Philanthropy, among others. UNCDF works to develop local financial systems, new markets and mobilize and crowd in capital from public and private sources. UNCDF is driven by a partnership mindset which enables it to deploy its different capital capabilities in highly tailored and responsive ways in order to mobilize investments flows from other sources, in particular from the private sector. By structuring transactions which are highly impactful, but also recognize the need for multiplying the impact of its own capital, UNCDF seeks to position itself as a preferred partner for different stakeholders. UNCDF’s work is focused on three priority areas, including:

• SME Finance

• Sub-National Finance

• Digital Finance

UNCDF’s organizational set up includes an Investment and Implementation Division (IID), Investment and Finance Oversight Division (IFOD), Operations and Oversight Division (OOD) and a Directorate of the Executive Office. UNCDF staff and personnel are located in regional hubs based in Dakar (Senegal), Nairobi (Kenya) and Bangkok (Thailand) with sub-regional presence in a number of locations in the Caribbean and Pacific Regions. UNCDF is led by an Executive Secretary based out of New York, USA. Pursuant to General Assembly resolution 2321(XXII, para 1.a), the Administrator of the UNDP performs the function of the Managing Director of UNCDF. UNCDF is overseen by an Executive Board comprised of UN Member States.

Duties and Responsibilities

Working under the guidance and supervision of the UNCDF Executive Secretary, the Head of Impact Measurement Verification and Learning (IMVL) leads in the generation, verification, and use of high-quality impact intelligence to support investment decisions, portfolio performance management, accountability to stakeholders, and organizational learning particularly in fragile, climate-vulnerable, and underserved markets typical of LDCs and SIDS.

Under the Leadership of the UNCDF Executive Secretary, the Head of IMVL coordinates and oversees the work of the Impact Measurement Verification and Learning Unit, established in the UNCDF front office, composed of Strategic Intelligence, Impact Measurement and Evaluation.

The overarching purpose of the IMVL unit is to determine whether and to what extent, the work of UNCDF is achieving positive intended impacts, and to provide data-driven recommendations on strategic and systemic actions that strengthen performance. This includes assessing whether UNCDF programming in digital finance, SME finance and sub-national/municipal support, is achieving development objectives. Insights and lessons from IMVL research, field reconnaissance and evaluations should enable UNCDF to expand pathways for replication, scalability, crowding in public and private investors and improving the conditions enabling market transformation in developing countries.

The Head of IMVL will provide key contributions as part of the senior management team. In addition to taking the lead role in impact management and assessment, the Head of IMVL will be expected to significantly contribute to other strategic areas, including transaction structuring, pipeline development, risk analysis and knowledge sharing.

The Head of IMVL will be based in New York, United States and will be required to travel occasionally.

UNCDF staff may be periodically redeployed to different regional hubs or headquarters as needed, subject to capability, consent, and due process.

UNCDF adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNCDF personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

1) Lead Strategic Impact Intelligence, Portfolio Insight, Knowledge Management, Thought Leadership, and IMVL Data Systems and Digital Tools:

- Lead development and provision of forward-looking intelligence that informs investment strategy, pipeline development, and portfolio performance.

- Lead development of impact intelligence products to support strategy and investment decisions.

- Lead analysis of sectoral, geographic, and thematic trends relevant to blended finance and impact investing.

- Lead development of impact theories aligned with organizational priorities as defined in the UNCDF Strategic Framework.

- Lead development, production and dissemination of portfolio-level impact insights to inform resource allocation and risk management.

- Lead institutionalization of learning and contributions to sector-wide knowledge.

- Lead development of internal guidance materials and technical notes.

- Oversee and ensure development and maintenance of repositories of lessons learned and best practices.

- Lead production of thematic briefs and research outputs and ensure support and contributions to publication of case studies.

- Promote innovation in impact methodologies.

- Ensure reliable infrastructure for collecting, managing, and analyzing impact data and coordinate with Corporate IT on the development and maintenance of impact data platforms.

- Lead definition of system requirements for data collection and reporting and ensure data interoperability across programs and investments.

- Lead support to visualization tools and dashboards.

- Oversee and ensure IMVL data governance standards.

2) Lead the Impact Verification, Measurement and Assurance function

- Ensure robust, standardized, and practical measurement of impact across UNCDF investments and programs.

- Lead development of impact intelligence products to support strategy and investment decisions. Analyze sectoral, geographic, and thematic trends relevant to blended finance and impact investing.

- Lead development of impact theses aligned with institutional priorities (e.g., climate resilience, financial inclusion, gender equality).

- Lead development and production of portfolio-level impact insights to inform resource allocation and risk management.

- Lead integration of contextual intelligence (fragility, climate vulnerability, market gaps) into decision frameworks.

- Ensure support to due diligence by assessing theory of change coherence, environmental and social safeguards adherence and expected development outcomes.

- Safeguard the credibility, integrity, and reliability of reported impact results.

- Lead verification of impact data reported by investees and partners.

- Oversee and ensure periodic data quality audits, spot checking and validation exercises.

- Lead development and consistent organization-wide implementation of impact assurance protocols.

- Manage relationships with external verification partners where applicable.

- Lead identification of risks related to impact overstatement or data gaps.

- Oversee and ensure traceability from reported outcomes to source evidence.

3) Lead Evaluation and Learning (MEL)

- Lead development and dissemination of actionable learning through structured evaluation of UNCDF investments and programs.

- Oversee the UNCDF evaluation function.

- Lead development of evaluation frameworks suited to blended finance models.

- Oversee the carrying out of midterm, final and ex post evaluations.

- Commission and supervise external evaluators.

- Ensure integration of learning loops into program and investment design.

- Lead translation of evaluation findings into practical recommendations.

4) Lead Governance, Reporting and Stakeholder Engagement

- Ensure accurate, credible reporting to internal leadership and external stakeholders.

- Lead preparation of impact reports for senior leadership, donors, and investors.

- Lead support to reporting against development and Strategic Framework commitments.

- Ensure alignment between reported results and verified evidence.

- Lead IMVL contributions to UNCDF annual reports, impact disclosures, and strategic reviews.

- Lead development of briefing materials on impact results for the UNCDF Executive Secretary, Managing Director, and Executive Board.

- Ensure productive relationships with internal and external partners contributing to impact outcomes

- Coordinate with investment teams to integrate impact into decision-making, including participation in the UNCDF Investment and Disbursement Impact Committee, to ensure that the approval of new projects/programs meet expected standards for impact measurement and evaluation.

- Liaise with investees to strengthen their measurement capacity.

- Engage donors, development partners, and co-investors on impact matters.

- Represent the organization in technical working groups.

5) Provide Effective IMVL Team Leadership & Coordination

- Lead a small team of staff and consultants delivering high-quality analytical and technical outputs.

- Develop and manage the IMVL annual work plans, ensuring that all planned deliverables are meeting time and quality expectations

- Supervise and mentor IMVL team, assigning workloads and ensuring efficient task management.

- Set performance expectations and development plans.

- Build team capacity in evaluation methods and data analytics.

- Maintain a collaborative, results-oriented team culture.

El PNUD es la principal organización de las Naciones Unidas en la lucha para poner fin a la injusticia de la pobreza, la desigualdad y el cambio climático. En Panamá trabaja a nivel nacional, nivel municipal y comarcal. El PNUD hace parte de las Agencias, Fondos y Programas de las Naciones Unidas en Panamá aportando al logro del Marco de Cooperación de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo Sostenible (UNSDCF en inglés).

El PNUD en Panamá está organizado en tres grupos programáticos que coordinan más de 40 proyectos en todo el territorio nacional: Igualdad e inclusión social, económica y ambiental Gobernabilidad, paz y derechos humanos Cambio climático, gestión integral ambiental y reducción de riesgos y desastres

El proyecto “Latidos del Barrio: Cultura que Transforma Comunidades” es una iniciativa impulsada por el Ministerio de Cultura con apoyo del PNUD, orientada a fortalecer la inclusión social, la cohesión comunitaria, la participación ciudadana, el acceso a servicios culturales y formativos, la activación deportiva y la economía creativa en territorios priorizados. El proyecto operará mediante una Unidad Coordinadora del Proyecto, con enfoque territorial, gestión basada en resultados, articulación interinstitucional, acompañamiento comunitario y cumplimiento de los procedimientos aplicables del PNUD.

Alcance del trabajo

El/la Asistente de Logística brindará apoyo operativo y administrativo a la implementación del proyecto, mediante la organización y ejecución de las actividades logísticas, la gestión de inventarios, el apoyo a eventos, el control de materiales y el funcionamiento de los centros del proyecto, contribuyendo al desarrollo oportuno y eficiente de las actividades programáticas y comunitarias.

Las actividades específicas incluyen:

Brindar apoyo operativo durante la ejecución de las actividades, contribuyendo a su desarrollo conforme a la planificación establecida.

Registrar los movimientos de inventario y mantener actualizados los controles establecidos. Verificar la disponibilidad de materiales e insumos antes del desarrollo de las actividades y reportar oportunamente las necesidades de reposición. Colaborar en la recepción y verificación de bienes adquiridos, asegurando que correspondan a las especificaciones y cantidades solicitadas.

Dar seguimiento al uso adecuado de los materiales y equipos asignados a las actividades del proyecto. Mantener organizados y actualizados los registros físicos y digitales relacionados con la gestión logística. Apoyar en el cumplimiento de los procedimientos administrativos, logísticos y de control interno establecidos por la organización.

- Apoyar la creación, el intercambio y el fortalecimiento del conocimiento, así como el desarrollo de capacidades relevantes para el proyecto. Participar en capacitaciones y organizar sesiones informativas sobre procedimientos internos para el personal del proyecto. Brindar apoyo en la difusión e intercambio de datos relevantes y lecciones aprendidas dentro de la oficina de país y a nivel regional. Mantenerse al tanto de las mejores prácticas emergentes a nivel nacional, regional e internacional relacionadas con el trabajo del proyecto asignado. Realizar contribuciones valiosas a redes de conocimiento y comunidades de práctica. Apoyar la recopilación y sistematización del conocimiento, los productos y las herramientas del proyecto, así como su amplia distribución a los socios.

jobs.title: Driver-Security Clerk, NPSA-4, DS - Dnipro (4 posts), Kharkiv (1 post), Poltava (3 posts), Mykolaiv (3 posts)
jobs.description:
Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) works in about 170 countries and territories, helping eradicate poverty, reduce inequalities and exclusion, and build resilience. It thereby helps them sustain progress and achieve the Sustainable Development Goals. In Ukraine, UNDP operates with three programme priorities: Democratic Governance and Inclusive Social Fabric, Inclusive and Sustainable Economic Recovery and Growth, and Sustainable Environment and Energy Transformation.

Since the start of hostilities in 2014 and the full-scale invasion in 2022, UNDP in Ukraine has been present on the ground through its hubs across the country, supporting regional and local authorities and civil society partners in their emergency response and crisis management efforts.

Lessons from the past years informed the development of UNDP’s Country Programme Document (2025-2029) and the scale-up of the Area-Based Recovery (ABR) Framework. The Framework’s programmatic pillars of Reconstruction, Returns, Resilience, and Reforms focus on ensuring community recovery and creating conditions for the return to a development pathway in Ukraine.

Addressing the country’s complex reconstruction and recovery requires a holistic, systems-based response that empowers all parts of society, including government, local authorities, the private sector, and citizens, with the capacity and resources to respond effectively. To ensure a whole-of-society approach, the framework offers an integrated, participatory, and inclusive methodology to advance recovery in communities most affected by the war.

In this context, the Driver-Security Clerk provides reliable, safe driving services, ensures high accuracy, and supports the Administrative Unit in general premises management, demonstrating a client-oriented approach, a high sense of responsibility, courtesy, tact, and the ability to work with people of different national and cultural backgrounds.

Duties and Responsibilities

Safe Driving and Transportation

• Provide timely, reliable, and secure transportation using soft skin and armoured vehicles within the city and to the regions, including overnight trips where required, under conditions of increased security threats. Transport UNDP/UN personnel, consultants, guests, and visitors as authorized by the UNDP Country Office (CO) and UNDSS.

• Ensure that all instructions regulating safe driving behaviour, Rules of the Road, and UN Security policies and procedures for Ukraine, particularly in relation to transportation of UN personnel, are strictly followed.

• Ensure that the vehicle is not left unattended while on mission and conduct a 360-degree vehicle sweep before and after any movement.

II. Vehicle Maintenance and Safety

• Ensure that the assigned vehicles are in good operational condition: conduct daily checks (oil, fuel, brakes, tyres, battery, tool kits, etc) on all assigned vehicles before the commencement of any trip/mission and report any defects to the Transportation Assistant and Administrative Associate for immediate repairs and maintenance.

• Perform routine daily vehicle maintenance and carry out minor emergency mechanical repairs, as required.

• Maintain daily vehicle logs (mileage, fuel consumption, travel routes, signature of passengers) and submit logs to the direct supervisor on a timely basis.

• Ensure that repair and maintenance services of armoured/soft vehicles are performed on a timely basis and with authorization from the direct supervisor.

• Ensure that the vehicle has valid insurance and a first aid kit.

• Ensure that the vehicle is equipped with sufficient Personal Protection Equipment (PPE) for all the passengers and the driver, at least one trauma bag, and, where required by the applicable Security Risk Management (SRM) measures, at least one operational satellite communication solution (e.g. VHF radio, a satellite phone or Starlink).

• Assist in vehicle history records preparation, collecting all vehicle-related documentation (scanned copies of invoices, receipts, acts, insurance certificates, etc.)

III. Logistical and Field Support

• Assist in the organization of logistical preparation of field trips, visiting missions, etc.

• Provide a full range of logistical support, including all necessary provisions for large VIP missions.

• Provide transportation-related support to official personnel and visitors arriving at the train station and facilitate their field travel arrangements.

• Assist in reviewing records related to in-country missions and field trips.

• Raise security clearance requests in the TRIP system for field missions in accordance with applicable security procedures.

• Load/unload light cargo delivered by the vehicle.

IV. Office, Administrative and Security Support

• Support emergency and contingency planning for UNDP road movements and participate in the assigned security capacity-building events and trainings.

• Conduct security briefings for missions if a security professional is not present in accordance with UN Travel SOPs.

• Assist in general maintenance of the office premises.

• Provide clerical support to operational and project activities.

• Drive UNDP vehicle for delivery and collection of mail, documents, pouches, equipment, and other administrative tasks upon request of the direct supervisor.

• Demonstrate respect for gender equality in professional interactions, identify and address sexism and gender discrimination.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Driver-Security Clerk is directly supervised and guided by the Administrative Associate, under the matrix supervision of the Field Security Specialist who provides direction on security-related duties and defines security-related work objectives. The Head of the Area-Based Recovery and the Field Operations Manager provide the overall oversight.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results:

LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility:

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination:

LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:

LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Thematic Area

Definition

Business Management

Communication

Ability to communicate in a clear, concise, and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media, and other appropriate channels.

Administration and Operations

Vehicle management

Knowledge of policy & procedures on fleet management.

Business Management

Customer Satisfaction/Client Management

Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs.

Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests.

Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Administration and Operations

Documents and records

management

Overall document (hard or electronic) management.

Registry and retention policy, including storing and archiving

2030 Agenda: People

Gender and Crisis

Required Skills and Experience

Min. Education requirements

- Secondary Education is required; OR

- University Degree (Bachelor’s degree) in Logistics, Transport, Security or other related fields will be given due consideration, but it is not a requirement.

- Valid Ukrainian driving license categories B and C/C1 (valid for driving both soft skin and armoured vehicles up to 5,500 kg) is required.

Min. years of relevant work experience

- Minimum 4 years (with Secondary Education) or 1 year (with Bachelor’s degree) of professional driving experience is required.

Experience, Knowledge, and Skills

- A safe driving record.

- Proven track record of sound knowledge of driving rules and regulations and skills in minor vehicle repair.

- Proven knowledge of radio procedures and radio equipment use.

- Experience in the use of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel).

Desirable Criteria

- Experience of driving armoured vehicles.

- Experience of driving in conflict-affected areas.

- Experience in providing logistical support, including all necessary arrangements for large-scale VIP missions conducted in convoy.

- Experience of working with international organizations/projects.

- Experience of working with and knowledge of protocol and customs issues.

- Demonstrated prior experience in supporting security logistics and administrative work.

Required Language(s)

Fluency in Ukrainian and English is required

Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. El PNUD es la principal organización de las Naciones Unidas en la lucha para poner fin a la injusticia de la pobreza, la desigualdad y el cambio climático. Trabajando con nuestra amplia red de expertos y socios en 170 países, ayudamos a las naciones a construir soluciones integradas y duraderas para las personas y el planeta.

El proyecto “Inclusión social a través de la Música: La Red Nacional de Orquestas y Coros Infantiles y Juveniles de Panamá como instrumento de transformación Social” busca contribuir al desarrollo inclusivo y sostenible de Panamá al mejorar los niveles de cohesión social mediante la inclusión activa de niños, niñas y adolescentes en procesos colectivos de enseñanza musical. Se basa en un modelo innovador de enseñanza colectiva de la música, a través de orquestas y coros infantiles y juveniles, que trasciende lo artístico y se convierte en una política pública transformadora que promueve ciudadanía, sentido de pertenencia, equidad de género y el respeto a la diversidad, al tiempo que ofrece nuevas oportunidades de vida para jóvenes en contextos de alta vulnerabilidad.

II. Alcance del trabajo

El/la Asociado/a de Proyecto brindará apoyo al fortalecimiento de la gestión del proyecto, contribuyendo a su implementación efectiva y oportuna, asegurando que los productos y entregables se desarrollen conforme al cronograma, presupuesto, estándares de calidad y procedimientos del PNUD.

Las actividades específicas incluyen:

1. Apoyo a la Gestión y seguimiento del proyecto:

• Apoyar a el/la Coordinador/a de Proyecto en la planificación, coordinación y seguimiento de la implementación de las actividades del proyecto.

• Apoyar a el/la Coordinador/a de Proyecto y a el/la Especialista de Monitoreo y Evaluación del PNUD y del proyecto en la coordinación de los procesos relacionados con el monitoreo, evaluación y la gestión de los recursos del proyecto.

• Apoyar en la elaboración de términos de referencia (TdR), especificaciones técnicas y otros documentos requeridos para la contratación de consultores, contratistas y servicios del proyecto.

• Gestionar y dar seguimiento a las solicitudes de viaje, procesos de adquisiciones, microcompras, contrataciones y demás procesos administrativos del proyecto, velando por el cumplimiento de los procedimientos del PNUD y los cronogramas establecidos.

• Coordinar con las áreas de operaciones y otras unidades de apoyo el procesamiento oportuno de las transacciones administrativas y operativas del proyecto.

• Consolidar la información requerida para la preparación de informes semestrales, anuales, planes operativos anuales y otros reportes de gestión del proyecto, asegurando la calidad, consistencia y oportunidad de la información presentada.

2. Gestión Documental y Aprendizaje:

• Velar por la integridad, actualización y disponibilidad de la documentación técnica y programática del proyecto, en coordinación con el personal de apoyo administrativo.

• Dar seguimiento al control y organización de la documentación técnica y administrativa del proyecto, asegurando que se encuentre completa y disponible para procesos de monitoreo, auditoría y rendición de cuentas.

• Recopilar las lecciones aprendidas durante la ejecución del proyecto.

jobs.title: Project Procurement Analyst [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

1. Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP’s Rule of Law Programme in Pakistan is working to strengthen the rule of law and to ensure equal access to justice and security services, particularly for women and marginalized groups across Pakistan in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) including the merged districts (MDs), Balochistan, and Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT). In close collaboration with a range of government, rule of law and justice sector institutions, the overall Programme aims to enhance and sustain peace and stability for the longer-term in Pakistan.

The Programme activities and interventions therefore directly correspond with the government of Pakistan’s strategies and commitments to rule of law and justice reforms, as well as improving the efficiency and effectiveness of institutions to deliver accountable and affordable security and justice services to the public.

The Rule of Law Programme implementation is guided by the following four strategic objectives:

- Policy, legal and regulatory frameworks strengthened to warrant people-centered, equitable, timely, affordable justice and security delivery to all people with an emphasis on women, marginalized and vulnerable groups, and digital technologies.

- Capacity of justice and security stakeholders (duty bearers) enhanced to deliver inclusive, timely, and accessible services to all people with an emphasis on women and digital technologies.

- Capacity of women, and the most vulnerable and marginalized (rights holders) strengthened to access referral pathways to justice and security.

- Justice and security sector institutional facilities enhanced to deliver inclusive, timely, and accessible justice and security services, through women friendly and gender-responsive infrastructure development support with an emphasis on flood resilience and green energy.

Against this backdrop, UNDP actions and interventions are aimed at restoring public confidence and service delivery in the formal justice and rule of law sectors through a range of initiatives i.e. policy development and reform, fostering justice and security sector governance, as well as oversight and accountability at an institutional level with emphasis on inclusive and gender-responsive programming. The overall engagement strategy, therefore, involves both federal and local levels. The Programme is implemented in partnership with the Judiciary, Police, Prosecution, Prisons, Probation and Reclamation, Bar Associations, Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and the academia both at federal and provincial levels.

The Project Procurement Analyst will provide dedicated procurement planning, coordination and management support for programme activities. The Analyst will facilitate transparent, competitive, timely and value-for-money procurement of goods, services, works and specialized technical expertise in accordance with UNDP procurement policies, procedures and applicable programme requirements.

The Analyst will support procurement planning, solicitation and evaluation processes, contract award and administration, vendor performance monitoring, procurement compliance and reporting, including technically complex requirements relating to infrastructure, refurbishment, ICT equipment and digital solutions. S/he will coordinate closely with designated other team members and relevant Country Office colleagues while maintaining appropriate segregation of duties and institutional controls.

2. Scope of Work

Under the supervision of the Project Operations and Finance Analyst, the Project Procurement Analyst will plan, coordinate and manage procurement processes for programme activities. The Analyst will work closely with technical and operations colleagues to ensure that procurement requirements are appropriately planned, documented, processed, monitored and administered in accordance with UNDP procurement policies and procedures and applicable programme requirements.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

I. Lead procurement planning and provide procurement advisory support.

- Prepare, consolidate, regularly update and monitor the programme procurement plan in coordination with designated other team members and relevant Country Office colleagues.

- Review planned procurement requirements for goods, services, works and consultancy contracts and advise on appropriate procurement strategies, methods, sequencing, timelines and documentation requirements.

- Support early identification of procurement needs and dependencies to ensure procurement actions are initiated in sufficient time to meet programme implementation schedules.

- Provide guidance on procurement processes, lead times, applicable policies and documentation requirements and support consistent application across programme activities.

- Analyse procurement pipelines and identify potential delays, risks, bottlenecks and opportunities for consolidation or efficiency, recommending appropriate follow-up actions.

- Coordinate procurement planning with financial and operational planning to ensure resource availability and alignment with approved workplans and programme priorities.

II. Coordinate preparation and implementation of solicitation and evaluation processes.

- Coordinate preparation and quality review of procurement documentation, including requisitions, solicitation documents, evaluation criteria, schedules and other required procurement records.

- Coordinate with designated other team members to ensure that terms of reference, statements of work, technical specifications, bills of quantities and other technical requirements are complete, clear and suitable for competitive procurement.

- Manage and/or facilitate solicitation processes for goods, services, works and consultancy requirements in accordance with applicable UNDP procurement procedures.

- Coordinate responses to bidder queries, pre-bid meetings, site visits and other procurement-related communications, ensuring fairness, transparency and appropriate documentation.

- Support and coordinate bid/proposal evaluation processes, including establishment of evaluation panels, preparation of evaluation documentation and timely completion of technical and financial evaluations.

- Prepare and/or coordinate procurement submissions, recommendations for award and supporting documentation required for relevant review and approval processes.

- Maintain appropriate segregation of duties, confidentiality, fairness and transparency throughout procurement processes.

III. Support contract award, administration and vendor performance management.

- Coordinate contract-award and related procurement actions following completion of required reviews and approvals.

- Maintain a systematic overview of programme contracts, purchase orders, procurement milestones, expiry dates, deliverables and other key contractual requirements.

- Support contract administration in coordination with designated other team members and relevant Country Office colleagues, including amendments, extensions and other contractual actions as required.

- Monitor procurement and contractual timelines and follow up on pending actions that may affect programme delivery.

- Support vendor and contractor performance monitoring and maintain appropriate documentation of performance issues, corrective actions and lessons for future procurement.

- Facilitate timely resolution or escalation of procurement and contract-administration issues in accordance with UNDP procedures.

- Support orderly contract completion and closure, including confirmation that required procurement and contractual documentation is complete.

IV. Support specialised and technically complex procurement requirements.

- Coordinate procurement processes relating to infrastructure and refurbishment works, ICT equipment, digital justice solutions, specialized technical services and other complex programme requirements.

- Coordinate with designated other team members responsible for technical requirements to ensure appropriate procurement approaches and complete technical documentation, while preserving clear segregation between procurement and technical responsibilities.

- Support market research and sourcing approaches, where required, to inform procurement strategy, competition, value for money and availability of suitable suppliers or service providers.

- Advise on procurement packaging, market approaches, solicitation methods and timelines for complex or interdependent requirements.

- Promote environmentally and socially responsible procurement considerations, accessibility and sustainability where relevant and consistent with UNDP procurement requirements.

- Identify procurement risks associated with technically complex requirements and recommend appropriate mitigation measures and sequencing.

V. Ensure procurement compliance, monitoring, records and reporting.

- Ensure procurement actions are conducted in accordance with UNDP procurement policies, procedures, delegated authorities and applicable programme and donor requirements.

- Maintain complete, accurate and audit-ready procurement files, trackers and records for programme procurement actions.

- Monitor implementation of the procurement plan and provide regular updates to programme management on procurement status, timelines, risks, delays and required decisions.

- Provide procurement information and supporting documentation for programme reviews, audits, spot checks, donor reporting and other assurance processes, as required.

- Support implementation and follow-up of procurement-related audit or review recommendations and strengthen controls where required.

- Coordinate with relevant Country Office procurement and operations colleagues on institutional processing, committee reviews, contracting and other corporate procurement requirements.

- Contribute procurement inputs to programme workplans, progress reports, management updates and other programme documentation, as required.

- Keep abreast of changes in UNDP procurement policies, procedures, systems and good practices and support their consistent application within the Programme.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

3. Institutional Arrangement

The Project Procurement Analyst will be based in the UNDP Pakistan Country Office in Islamabad, with travel to programme implementation locations, particularly Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, as required.

Under the supervision of the Project Operations and Finance Analyst, the Project Procurement Analyst will provide dedicated programme-level procurement planning, coordination and management support for activities.

The Project Procurement Analyst will work closely with relevant programme colleagues and relevant UNDP Country Office procurement and operations units, to ensure timely, transparent, competitive and compliant procurement. Technical specialists will remain responsible for substantive and technical requirements and acceptance of specialised deliverables, while the Procurement Analyst will manage and coordinate the applicable procurement processes.

4. Competencies

Core Competencies

Achieve Results

LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously

LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination

LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner

LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion

LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Thematic Area

Name

Definition

Procurement

Procurement Management

The ability to acquire goods, services or works from anoutside external source

Procurement

Contract Management

Knowledge of contract management concepts, principles and methods, and ability to apply this to strategic and/or practical situations

Business Management

Risk Management

Ability to identify and organise action around mitigating and proactively managing procurement, contractual and operational risks.

Business Management

Project Management

Ability to plan, organise, prioritise and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

Business Management

Customer Satisfaction / Client Management

Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and

deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs.

Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond

clients' immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns

Business Direction & Strategy

Systems Thinking

Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Business Management

Communication

Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication ; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience.

Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

Please refer to the competency framework site for the entire list of competencies and further

explanations.

5. Minimum Qualifications of the Successful NPSA

Min. Academic Education

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Business Administration, Public Administration, Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Finance, Economics, Management or a related field OR

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience, will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

- CIPS level 3 is highly desirable for this position and candidates holding this level at the time of application will have a distinct advantage. If the desired certification is not available at the time of recruitment, it should be obtained within one year of recruitment. Candidates holding a CIPS certification at any level below at the time of application will have a proportionate advantage

Min. years of relevant Work experience

- Applicants with Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience.

- Applicants with a Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of two (2) years of relevant experience in procurement, supply chain management, contract management or related areas.

Desired additional skills and competencies

- Experience in procurement planning and implementation for goods, services and/or works is desired.

- Experience preparing and/or coordinating solicitation documents, tendering processes, bid/proposal evaluations and contract-award documentation is desired.

- Experience in contract administration, procurement tracking and vendor or contractor performance management is desired.

- Experience applying procurement policies, procedures, ethical standards and internal controls is desired.

- Experience with procurement of infrastructure works, ICT equipment, digital systems or specialised technical services would be a strong advantage.

- Experience conducting market research, sourcing or procurement analysis to support competition and value for money is desirable.

- Experience maintaining procurement records and supporting audits, reviews or other assurance processes is desired.

- Experience with procurement in donor-funded programmes or international development settings is highly desirable.

- Proven Knowledge of UNDP procurement policies and procedures would be an advantage.

- Experience using enterprise resource planning, e-procurement or procurement-management systems is desirable; familiarity with UNDP Quantum or comparable systems would be an advantage.

- Experience coordinating with technical, finance and programme teams on complex procurement requirements is desirable.

- Previous work experience with UN agencies or international organisations would be an advantage.

- Strong analytical, organisational, communication, negotiation and stakeholder-coordination skills and experience are desired.

- Proven Ability to manage multiple procurement actions and deadlines while maintaining accuracy, transparency and compliance is desired.

Required Language(s) (at working level)

Fluency in English and Urdu languages (spoken and written) is required

Professional Certificates

Professional certification or specialised training in procurement, supply chain management, contract management, public procurement or related areas will be an added advantage.

7. Travel:

The Procurement Analyst will be based in Islamabad and is expected to travel to programme implementation locations, particularly Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, as required for procurement planning, market assessments, pre-bid or site visits, contract monitoring, coordination and other programme-related assignments.

References may also include peers.
