jobs.title: Project Coordinator [Open to Tier 1 & 2 applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP Albania works in partnership with national and local institutions, the private sector, civil society and development partners to advance Albania’s sustainable development and European Union accession priorities. Through its Inclusive Growth portfolio, UNDP supports the development of a more productive, competitive and inclusive economy by strengthening institutions, improving employment and skills-development systems, supporting enterprise growth and facilitating the transition towards greener, more digital and sustainable economic models. The portfolio combines policy and institutional support with practical interventions that expand economic opportunities, strengthen private-sector competitiveness and enable businesses and individuals—particularly those facing barriers to economic participation—to benefit from Albania’s economic transformation.

Within this framework, UNDP will support the Government of Albania’s ‘Dyfisho Sipërmarrjen Tënde’ programme. This national programme supports micro, small and medium-sized enterprises to grow by helping them access investment loans through a sovereign guarantee. The financing is provided by participating banks and enables viable businesses to invest, expand and become more competitive. However, many businesses—particularly smaller ones—also need technical assistance to prepare strong investment proposals and meet the banks’ application requirements.

To complement the financing mechanism, UNDP will establish and operate a dedicated Technical Assistance Facility to help eligible enterprises become investment-ready and better prepared to access finance. The Facility will provide structured and tailored assistance throughout the application process, including initial enterprise diagnostics, assessment of financing and business-development needs, preparation or improvement of business and investment plans, financial analysis and modelling, and compilation of the documentation required for loan appraisal. UNDP will also facilitate coordination among applicant enterprises, the Ministry of Economy and Innovation, participating financial institutions and other relevant stakeholders; maintain a systematic case-management process; monitor the progress of supported enterprises; and identify recurring constraints affecting access to finance. Through this work, UNDP will help improve the quality and readiness of enterprise applications, strengthen the referral and financing process, and generate evidence and lessons to inform future enterprise-support policies and programmes.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the direct supervision of the UNDP Programme Specialist responsible for the Inclusive Growth portfolio, the Project Coordinator is responsible for the day-to-day management and coordination of all project components, personnel, resources, partnerships and results. The incumbent will perform the following functions in accordance with UNDP rules, regulations, policies and procedures and the UNDP internal control framework.

Effectively manage a project team to ensure timely and quality delivery of project outputs

- Supervise and guide project staff and consultants to ensure timely achievement of project results and undertake credible performance assessment;

- Develop detailed project work plans for implementation of project activities, ensuring active engagement of all relevant stakeholders;

- Mobilize goods and services to implement project activities, including engaging responsible parties, drafting TORs and work specifications;

- Monitor regularly and collect different data during project implementation that will be valuable for preparation of progress report and present the impact of the project results;

- Prepare regular progress and annual reports of the project (progress against planned activities, targets set, financial expenditures etc.);

- Ensure timely submission of progress reports, prepare background documents and background documentation and ensure timely organization of Project Board meetings;

- Manage and monitor the delivery of the financial resources and ensure quality and timely financial reporting;

- Ensure appropriate filing and availability of required documentation for the audit purposes;

- Perform all tasks in Quantum Management Information System related to the Project Coordinator position.

Maintain and further enhance collaborative and productive working relations and partnership among key project partners and donors, through effective communication, consultation and reporting

- Maintain close working relations with the key national partners including the Ministry of Economy and Innovation and the Albanian Association of Banks;

- Prepare thematic reports, blogs, insights that analyse specific issues emerging from the project implementation;

- Maintain effective linkages with the international organizations, including by preparing project briefs presenting project results;

- Establish effective linkages with other UNDP programmes and projects and with other initiatives in the sector with a view to developing substantive partnerships and generating synergies;

- Provide critical data and insights in support of CO’s further scaling up and expansion efforts in the area of private sector development.

Ensure establishment of a robust oversight and monitoring system including data collection to facilitate smooth implementation of the project, communication, outreach, advocacy, reporting on results and impact, knowledge building and further scaling-up

- Set up a monitoring system for the project including data collection protocols and gender considerations for the project and for the partners including responsible parties and banks that will ensure monitoring of progress as per projects targets set and collections of evidence for the evaluation of results and impact;

- Take lead in creation and implementation of a system that will ensure lessons learnt, good practices and collective intelligence gathered during project implementation are documented and inform future programming and expansion;

- Provide substantive input by feeding back data from implementation and field monitoring of project activities, needs of project beneficiaries, target groups that will inform the development and fine tuning of the Project strategy and pipeline development.

Create synergies with other related initiatives in the UNDP and UN system initiatives in the country, regionally and globally, to maximize project impact and facilitate further expansion and scale-up

- Collaborate intensively with other UNDP, UN system and other related initiatives to maximise the impact of UNDP’s interventions that will contribute towards achievement of the expected outcome under the UNDP’s Country Programme Document 2026-2030 and UNSDCF 2026-2030.

Ensure Gender mainstreaming within the project focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Ensure gender is effectively mainstreamed throughout the project activities, work plans, budgets, reports, research, analyses and, where specifically relevant, analysed in detail.

- Ensure gender equality is mainstreamed throughout team, consultant and staff management activities.

- Ensure knowledge on gender equality is incorporated in setting up of the oversight and monitoring system, collection of data, project knowledge management activities and products.

Ensure quality communication of project results and impact using the established monitoring system and data collected to feed communication of results, as well as for further resource mobilization and new partnerships for scaling up.

- Ensure effective communication of the project results in close collaboration with UNDP and UN communication specialists;

- Use data collected and lessons learnt during project implementation to communicate results, advocate for change, inform future initiatives and guide further expansion of private sector development and related areas of UNDP/UN work.

- Participate in trainings and share knowledge about the project.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Project Coordinator will report to the Inclusive Growth Programme Specialist. The Project Coordinator will be located in Tirana.

jobs.title: Associado(a) de Certificação e Desenvolvimento de Competências em Cibersegurança (1 vaga) (Home Based) - [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Em 2025, o Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ) e o Programa das Nações Unidas para o Desenvolvimento (PNUD) firmaram uma parceria voltada à promoção da inovação em segurança cibernética para o Poder Judiciário. O projeto BRA/25/025 – “Fortalecimento da segurança cibernética e da transparência para governança e efetividade da atuação do Poder Judiciário” desenvolve e implementa ferramentas e estratégias para o fortalecimento da segurança cibernética, da preservação digital e da integridade da informação, ampliando a proteção dos sistemas e dos usuários do Judiciário.

A iniciativa fortalece a segurança institucional e promove a transparência, a boa governança e a eficiência dos processos judiciais, contribuindo para a economia de recursos e para uma atuação mais ágil da Justiça em benefício dos cidadãos e da sociedade.

Para isso, a governança do projeto está dividida nas seguintes frentes:

Quatro eixos transversais de coordenação:

- Coordenação Geral;

- Unidade de monitoramento e controle integrado;

- Unidade de gestão técnica e operacional;

- Unidade de formação e comunicação;

Quatro frentes de trabalho, focadas em:

- Compliance normativa;

- Conformidade operacional;

- Governança em rede;

- Fomento à cultura de segurança cibernética;

Por se tratar de uma vaga em regime remoto, espera-se que o(a) candidato(a) disponha de condições adequadas de trabalho, incluindo infraestrutura e equipamentos necessários para o pleno desempenho das atividades.

Deveres e responsabilidades

O(a) Associado(a) de Certificação e Desenvolvimento de Competências estará vinculado(a) ao Eixo 4 de Fomento à Cultura de Segurança Cibernética, com atuação voltada à estruturação e implementação de processos de certificação de competências em cibersegurança, incluindo definição de referenciais, critérios de avaliação e mecanismos de validação e reconhecimento. O(a) profissional atuará em articulação com as equipes do CNJ, PNUD e instituições parceiras.

As seguintes atividades indicativas estão previstas:

1. Estruturação do modelo de certificação em cibersegurança

• Estruturar modelos institucionais para certificação de competências em cibersegurança, definindo níveis, requisitos e critérios de reconhecimento.

• Definir os requisitos necessários para que servidores e equipes possam demonstrar e validar competências em diferentes áreas de cibersegurança.

• Estabelecer critérios de elegibilidade, evidências e mecanismos de concessão das certificações.

2. Avaliação e validação de competências

• Desenvolver critérios e instrumentos para avaliar e validar competências já adquiridas, considerando conhecimentos, habilidades, práticas e resultados demonstrados.

• Estruturar mecanismos de avaliação teórica e prática, quando aplicável, para aferição dos níveis de proficiência em cibersegurança.

• Analisar evidências de competência e recomendar a concessão, manutenção ou evolução das certificações.

3. Referenciais de competências em cibersegurança

• Desenvolver e manter matrizes de competências e referenciais de proficiência para diferentes funções e áreas de cibersegurança.

• Definir os conhecimentos, habilidades e comportamentos esperados para cada nível de proficiência.

• Mapear as competências que podem ser objeto de certificação, diferenciando-as das competências que demandam desenvolvimento por meio de capacitação.

4. Integração com programas de capacitação

• Estabelecer a relação entre capacitação e certificação, utilizando as trilhas de aprendizagem como mecanismos de preparação para os processos de avaliação e certificação.

• Integrar treinamentos, qualificações e experiências práticas às competências previstas nos referenciais de certificação, sem confundir a participação em capacitações com a comprovação da competência.

• Identificar lacunas de competências a partir dos resultados das avaliações e direcioná-las para iniciativas de capacitação e desenvolvimento.

5. Certificação baseada em evidências e práticas

• Trabalhar com Blue Teams, LabCiber, Campanhas e demais frentes técnicas para identificar práticas, experiências e resultados que possam constituir evidências de competência.

• Definir mecanismos para registro e validação de experiências práticas relevantes para os processos de certificação.

• Estabelecer critérios para reconhecimento de competências demonstradas em atividades reais de cibersegurança.

6. Governança, rastreabilidade da certificação e monitoramento e evolução do modelo de certificação

• Estruturar processos de governança para garantir padronização, imparcialidade, consistência e rastreabilidade das avaliações e certificações.

• Manter registros atualizados das certificações concedidas, níveis de proficiência, avaliações realizadas e respectivos ciclos de validade.

• Definir processos para renovação, atualização, revisão ou revalidação das certificações.

• Desenvolver indicadores para acompanhar a evolução da certificação de competências em cibersegurança nos tribunais.

• Analisar os resultados das certificações para identificar lacunas de competências e subsidiar o planejamento de ações de capacitação.

• Promover a melhoria contínua dos critérios, instrumentos e referenciais de certificação, considerando a evolução das necessidades de cibersegurança.

7. Facilitar a construção e o compartilhamento de conhecimento

• Apoiar o planejamento e a realização de treinamentos e capacitações relacionados aos projetos, destinados às equipes de programas, operações e parceiros relevantes.

• Sistematizar e documentar conhecimentos produzidos no âmbito dos projetos, incluindo aprendizados, boas práticas, lições aprendidas e evidências de implementação, organizando-os em formatos e repositórios que favoreçam sua consulta e reutilização.

• Promover a disseminação dos conhecimentos sistematizados no âmbito do projeto/unidade e contribuir para redes de conhecimento, comunidades de prática e plataformas institucionais, visando ao compartilhamento de experiências e ao fortalecimento da aprendizagem organizacional.

O(a) titular desempenha outras funções compatíveis com seu perfil funcional que considere necessárias ao bom funcionamento do projeto.

Arranjo Institucional

A pessoa contratada será supervisionada pela Analista de Gestão de Cultura de Segurança Cibernética.

Competências

- Alcançar Resultados - NÍVEL 1: Planeja e monitora seu próprio trabalho, presta atenção aos detalhes e entrega um trabalho de qualidade dentro do prazo.

- Pensar de forma Inovadora - NÍVEL 1: Aberto a ideias criativas e riscos conhecidos, é um solucionador de problemas prático e faz melhorias.

- Aprender Continuamente - NÍVEL 1: Mente aberta e curioso, compartilha conhecimento, aprende com os erros e pede feedback.

- Adaptar com Agilidade - NÍVEL 1: Adapta-se às mudanças, lida de forma construtiva com ambiguidades e incertezas, e é flexível..

- Agir com Determinação - NÍVEL 1: Demonstra determinação e motivação, mantém a calma diante da adversidade e tem confiança.

- Engajar e fazer Parcerias - NÍVEL 1: Demonstra compaixão e compreensão em relação aos outros, formando relacionamentos positivos.

- Promover a Diversidade e Inclusão - NÍVEL 1: Valoriza e respeita as diferenças, está consciente de vieses inconscientes e enfrenta a discriminação

Competências multifuncionais e técnicas

Direção e estratégia de negócios | Pensamento estratégico: Desenvolver estratégias eficazes e planos prioritários alinhados com a missão e os objetivos do PNUD,

baseando-se em uma análise sistêmica de desafios, oportunidades e riscos potenciais; conectar a visão geral à realidade no campo para criar soluções tangíveis e

direcionadas; aprender a partir de diversas fontes para antecipar e responder de forma eficaz às tendências atuais e futuras; demonstrar capacidade de previsão.

Direção e estratégia de negócios | Perspicácia Empresarial: Capacidade de compreender e lidar com situações de negócios de forma a alcançar bons resultados. Habilidade

para tomar boas decisões e fazer julgamentos rápidos dentro de tais contextos. Conhecimento e compreensão dos marcos operacionais da organização

Desenvolvimento de negócios | Design centrado no humano: Capacidade de desenvolver soluções para problemas envolvendo a perspectiva humana em todas as etapas do

processo de resolução. Conhecimento e compreensão dos princípios e práticas de design centrado no ser humano.

Gestão de negócios | Gestão de Projetos: Capacidade de planejar, organizar, priorizar e controlar recursos, procedimentos e protocolos para alcançar objetivos específicos.

Digital | Gerenciamento de riscos de segurança cibernética e privacidade de dados: Capacidade de antecipar, preparar e responder a riscos e problemas que possam resultar em violações de dados, afetando a reputação do PNUD e causando danos pessoais.

Agenda 2030: Paz | Estado de Direito, Segurança e Direitos Humanos: Instituições Eficazes do Setor de Justiça.

Agenda 2030: Paz | Estado de Direito, Segurança e Direitos Humanos: Acesso à Justiça

Habilidades e experiência necessárias

Requisitos mínimos de educação:

- Diploma do Ensino Médio completo é requerido.

- Diploma Universitário (Ensino Superior) em Direito, Ciência da Computação, Engenharia da Computação, Sistemas de Informação, Tecnologia da Informação, ou áreas afins será dada a devida consideração, mas não é um requisito.

Anos mínimos de experiência profissional relevante:

- Mínimo de 7 anos (para Ensino Médio) ou 4 anos (para Ensino Superior) em avaliação de competências e/ou processos de certificação profissional ou institucional em segurança cibernética.

Habilidades requeridas:

Habilidades desejadas, além das competências abordadas na seção Competências:

- Experiência na definição de níveis de maturidade, critérios de classificação ou referenciais de desempenho.

- Experiência no desenvolvimento de matrizes, frameworks ou referenciais de competências e níveis de proficiência.

- Experiência na estruturação de processos de governança, rastreabilidade e gestão de resultados de programas de avaliação ou certificação.

- Experiência na articulação com equipes técnicas e instituições para levantamento de requisitos, validação de critérios e implementação de modelos de avaliação;

jobs.title: Team Lead - Programme Specialist (Open to Internal and External Applicants)
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP’s Rule of Law Programme in Pakistan is working to strengthen the rule of law and to ensure equal access to justice and security services, particularly for women and marginalized groups across Pakistan in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) including the merged districts (MDs), Balochistan, and Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT). In close collaboration with a range of government, rule of law and justice sector institutions, the overall Programme aims to enhance and sustain peace and stability for the longer-term in Pakistan.

The Programme activities and interventions therefore directly correspond with the Government of Pakistan’s strategies and commitments to rule of law and justice reforms, as well as improving the efficiency and effectiveness of institutions to deliver accountable and affordable security and justice services to the public.

The Rule of Law Programme implementation is guided by the following four strategic objectives:

- Policy, legal and regulatory frameworks strengthened to warrant people-centered, equitable, timely, affordable justice and security delivery to all people with an emphasis on women, marginalized and vulnerable groups, and digital technologies.

- Capacity of justice and security stakeholders (duty bearers) enhanced to deliver inclusive, timely, and accessible services to all people with an emphasis on women and digital technologies.

- Capacity of women, and the most vulnerable and marginalized (rights holders) strengthened to access referral pathways to justice and security.

- Justice and security sector institutional facilities enhanced to deliver inclusive, timely, and accessible justice and security services, through women friendly and gender-responsive infrastructure development support with an emphasis on flood resilience and green energy.

Against this backdrop, UNDP actions and interventions are aimed at restoring public confidence and service delivery in the formal justice and rule of law sectors through a range of initiatives i.e. policy development and reform, fostering justice and security sector governance, as well as oversight and accountability at an institutional level with emphasis on inclusive and gender-responsive programming. The overall engagement strategy, therefore, involves both federal and local levels. The Programme is implemented in partnership with the Judiciary, Police, Prosecution, Prisons, Probation and Reclamation, Bar Associations, Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and academia both at federal and provincial levels.

The Team Lead /Programme Specialist will support the Chief Technical Advisor (CTA) in the implementation and achievement of programme results, liaising closely with key government and rule of law counterparts at federal and provincial levels, donor agencies, UN agencies and other international organizations. The Team Lead /Programme Specialist will provide technical leadership and advisory support to government counterparts and rule of law, security and justice-sector institutions and will supervise designated Rule of Law Programme personnel in accordance with the approved organigramme.

The incumbent will support the CTA in the strategic positioning of UNDP Rule of Law activities and provide policy and programme-management advice on rule of law, security and justice-sector issues. S/he will support donor coordination and resource-mobilization efforts, contribute to programme formulation, strategic direction and evaluation, and serve as a key technical focal point for major national and international stakeholders.

Duties and Responsibilities

The incumbent will report directly to the Chief Technical Advisor (CTA). S/he will provide day-to-day technical leadership and coordination for the Rule of Law Programme, support programme management and oversight, and provide substantive advice on rule of law, law enforcement, security-sector and institutional reform.

The role entails supervision of designated programme personnel and short-term consultants, in accordance with the approved organigramme and applicable UNDP policies and procedures. The incumbent will support the CTA in programme development, implementation, quality assurance and achievement of results.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams and projects in multidisciplinary teams to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

Provide technical leadership and advisory support on rule of law, law enforcement, security-sector and institutional reform.

- Provide day-to-day technical leadership, coordination, and advisory support to ensure effective implementation of programme interventions relating to security-sector and criminal justice reform, access to justice, and institutional strengthening

- Provide specialised technical advice to relevant institutions on institutional reform priorities affecting police, prosecution, prisons, probation and other security and criminal justice institutions, including institutional governance, operational effectiveness, accountability, coordination and service-delivery systems.

- Lead and coordinate institutional assessments and diagnostics to identify systemic gaps and recommend tailored solutions.

- Provide technical guidance on strengthening investigation and prosecution practices, institutional coordination, fair-trial safeguards, lawful and accountable service delivery, victim/survivor referral mechanisms and other priority criminal justice functions.

- Guide technical interventions aimed at strengthening citizen-responsive, accessible, inclusive and gender-sensitive law-enforcement and security services, including institutional systems and practices that improve services for women and vulnerable populations.

- Offer technical guidance to provincial and federal justice institutions on case management, investigation standards, and fair trial guarantees.

- Assist in the rollout of case management systems, and integrated data platforms.

- Provide substantive oversight and coordination for interventions involving law-enforcement and correctional institutions, ensuring coherence across institutional reform, capacity development, digital transformation, infrastructure and service-delivery initiatives.

- Coordinate communication and sharing knowledge with other regional Rule of Law Programmes.

- Provide advice to CTA on scaling up and sustainability of the Rule of Law Programme.

Provide technical leadership for gender-responsive institutional reform and women’s advancement across law-enforcement, security and criminal justice institutions.

- Provide technical leadership and advice on integrating gender equality, non-discrimination, accessibility and survivor-centred approaches into law-enforcement, security and criminal justice institutional reforms, policies, procedures and service-delivery systems.

- Guide diagnostics and institutional analysis of barriers affecting the recruitment, retention, participation, leadership and career progression of women within police, prosecution, prisons, probation and other relevant institutions.

- Support development and implementation of evidence-based institutional reform measures addressing gender-responsive human-resource policies, career progression pathways, safe and inclusive workplace standards and appropriate mechanisms for addressing harassment and discrimination.

- Provide substantive technical guidance on gender-responsive and survivor-centred institutional responses to gender-based violence and other cases involving vulnerable groups, including victim identification, trauma-informed approaches, referral pathways, confidentiality, informed consent and inter-institutional coordination.

- Guide the integration of gender-responsive approaches into law-enforcement and security-sector training systems, operational procedures, institutional policies, digital systems, facilities and service-delivery models.

- Support professional development, mentorship, leadership and pipeline-development approaches aimed at increasing the participation and advancement of women within law-enforcement, prosecution, correctional and other relevant institutions.

- Coordinate on reforms involving the judiciary, ADR, legal profession and access-to-justice institutions to ensure coherent gender-responsive programming while maintaining clear technical responsibilities.

Ensure programme management and oversight.

- Prepare annual and quarterly workplans aligned with programme outcomes, ensuring sequencing of interventions and resource allocation.

- Provide substantive and strategic support to the Rule of Law Programme, including supervision of programme team and several short- term consultants.

- Facilitate and manage Rule of Law Programme activities, and measure performance and report on project results and outcomes for CTA to present to the Project Review Board (PRB) and other forums, ensure reporting to donors is timely and maintains required standards.

- Support the establishment and functioning of the Rule of Law team and manage the recruitment of team and local consultants, as well as identifying short-term local experts as necessary.

- Coordinate and supervise the activities of the Rule of Law personnel , experts and consultants working as part oof the technical assistance team.

- Contribute toward Rule of Law work plans, progress reports, and terminal reports.

- Be responsible for the timely preparation and quality control of all substantive technical outputs, briefs and required documents, ensuring timely production and submission of outputs and reports by all members of the Rule of Law, contractors and partners.

- Support to organize PRB, donor coordination and project review meetings. Prepare background. documents, briefs, issues papers, and progress reports for the PRB meetings and for donor reporting. Follow-up on the implementation of PRB decisions and recommendations.

- Support process for the selection of suppliers, contractors, and partners. Supervise procurement of goods and services including preparation of equipment specifications, Terms of Reference (TORs) and Request for Proposals (RFPs) according to approved UNDP procedures.

- Conduct field visits to supervise, coordinate and monitor field-level activities of the Rule of Law Programme.

- Supervise outsourced research and dissemination of research findings.

- Provide support to the Rule of Law Programme’s infrastructure development projects.

- Conduct day-to-day meetings with Rule of Law personnel , providing feedback on performance and advice on way forward.

Strengthen coordination, partnerships and institutional engagement.

- Support CTA in coordination with UNDP country office, donors, government, and all other partners including other UN agencies for successful implementation of the Rule of Law Programme.

- Organize and document regular Criminal Justice Coordination Committee sessions at provincial and district levels to align police, prosecution, judiciary, and corrections.

- Develop and update SOPs for case referrals, evidence sharing, and victim/survivor support across institutions

- Link judicial academies, police training schools, and prosecution departments to harmonize curricula and embed reforms

- Facilitate structured dialogue with CSOs, bar associations, and academia to strengthen accountability and inclusion.

- Assist the CTA in building relationships with key government counterparts for achievement of results consistent with government priorities.

- Support in the delivery of the communications and visibility strategy, making use of a variety of technologies and information platforms;

Contribute to the results-based management, monitoring, reporting and knowledge management.

- Work closely with the designated team members to ensure that technical implementation is aligned with the programme results framework, indicators, baselines, targets and reporting requirements.

- Provide substantive inputs to progress reports, donor reports, programme reviews, briefing notes and other results-based documentation, ensuring that reported achievements accurately reflect implementation progress and institutional change.

- Support systematic use of evidence, monitoring findings, assessments and evaluation results to inform technical decision-making and programme adaptation.

- Capture lessons learned, promising practices and knowledge generated through programme implementation and support their dissemination and application across relevant institutions and programme locations.

- Contribute to quality assurance of research, assessments, diagnostics and knowledge products commissioned under the programme.

- Document programme achievements, challenges, and corrective actions, aligned with EU reporting requirements.

Facilitate Cross Cutting initiatives

- Mainstream gender equality, disability inclusion, and survivor-centred approaches across programme activities .

- Track participation of women and persons with disabilities in justice institutions and measure accessibility improvements.

- Integrate gender-sensitive approaches into all programme outputs, including survivor-centred justice for GBV cases and recruitment of women into justice institutions.

- Support ADR mechanism tailored to ethnic and religious minorities in remote areas.

- Expand digital case management systems with user-friendly interfaces for marginalized groups.

- Incorporate environmental crime awareness and enforcement into justice sector training, linking to SDG 16.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The incumbent will be based in the UNDP Pakistan Country Office in Islamabad, with travel to programme implementation locations, particularly Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, as required.

The incumbent will report directly to the Chief Technical Advisor (CTA) and will support the CTA in the overall technical leadership, programme management, strategic positioning, quality assurance and achievement of results of the Rule of Law Programme.

The incumbent will supervise designated programme personnel and consultants in accordance with the approved organigramme and will maintain effective working relationships with relevant government institutions, justice and security-sector stakeholders, development partners, UN entities, civil society and other partners. Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Management

Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management.

- Partnerships Management: Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

- Communication: Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. . Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Business Direction & Strategy

- System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

2030 Agenda: Peace

Required Skills and Experience

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience, will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

Desired Skills

Language Requirements :

Equal opportunity

jobs.description:
Background

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. Taking a ‘leave no one behind’ approach to our diversity efforts means increasing representation of underserved populations. People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Regional Bureau for Africa (RBA) provides strategic oversight, quality assurance, management support, and regional analysis across country offices and global initiatives.

The RBA Directorate seeks a highly motivated graduate student to support the establishment of a structured documentation and task-tracking system. The intern will contribute to improving coordination, workflow efficiency, and knowledge management within the Directorate.

The intern will report directly to the Special Advisor to the RBA Director.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Coordination & Task Management

- Maintain and update a centralized task-tracking system for Directorate activities

- Manage calendar coordination and support planning of strategic meetings and events

- Develop and maintain a comprehensive tasking log (deadlines, follow-ups, deliverables)

- Liaise with country offices and HQ units to ensure timely submissions and follow-ups

2. Documentation & Knowledge Management

- Take meeting minutes and upload within 24 hours to shared platforms

- Maintain organized document repositories (SharePoint and shared drives)

- Ensure documentation is accurate, accessible, and up to date

- Support document review processes and provide feedback when requested

3. Workflow Optimization & Digital Innovation

- Design and implement user-friendly tracking systems (dashboards, logs, reminders)

- Introduce automation solutions (e.g., Power Automate, task trackers)

- Identify inefficiencies and propose practical process improvements

- Support integration of AI-enabled tools for administrative and analytical tasks

4. Monitoring & Analysis

- Develop and maintain a qualitative monitoring system for Directorate activities

- Track progress of key initiatives and provide status updates

- Conduct research and contribute to briefing notes, speeches, and talking points

Expected Deliverables

- Provide minutes within 24 hours of meetings. Keep and maintain a ‘minutes’ folder on shared Directorate platform,

- Work with the Directorate Executive Assistant to maintain a color-coded calendar (separate from the one she directly handles for the Director) of events and meetings,

- Tasking log to keep track of deadlines, follow-ups, and general to-dos of Directorate requests and events. Populate and keep log up to date,

- Regularly follow up with teams on quarterly events. Circulate table and ensure it is completed and always updated,

- Stay in constant communication with and remain available to country offices/Headquarters units to ensure meeting of deadlines and submission of documents. Review the documents (if requested) and return with edits/feedback,

- Either grant personalized access to tasking logs or create a system checklist to make sure documents are getting drafted in a timely manner, sent to be edited, and submitted to the Special Advisor,

- Long term; conduct research on topics/events relating to briefing documents (speeches, talking points, etc.).

- Update and organize information on the RBA SharePoint to ensure documents are accurate and easy to access

- Design and maintain a simple, user‑friendly digital task‑tracking or monitoring system for Directorate activities, including automated reminders or visual status updates, and document lessons learned for sustainability.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Strong organizational and multitasking ability

- High level of integrity, discretion, and reliability

- Ability to work independently under pressure

- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills

Digital & Technical Skills

- Proficiency in Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Teams, Excel, SharePoint, Planner)

- Experience with task-tracking tools and dashboards

- Familiarity with workflow automation tools (e.g., Power Automate)

- Interest or experience with AI tools (e.g., Copilot, generative AI)

Communication & Teamwork

- Clear and effective written and verbal communication

- Ability to tailor messaging to different audiences

- Collaborative mindset and ability to work across diverse teams

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Applicants to the UNDP internship programme must at the time of application meet one of the following requirements:

- Be enrolled in a graduate school programme (second university degree or equivalent, or higher in Economics, African Studies, History, Social Science, International Development, Development Studies or other relevant fields),

- Have graduated with a university degree (as described above) and, if selected, must start the internship within one-year of graduation.

Experience:

- Have demonstrated ability to successfully interact with individuals of different cultural backgrounds and beliefs, which include willingness to try and understand and be tolerant of differing opinions and views.

- Preferably some relevant experience in international development or related area; Knowledge of the UN system is an advantage,

- Excellent analytical skills are required and experience designing infographics is an advantage.

- Experience in the use of computers and office software packages; experience with digital task management, process automation, or workflow optimization tools is a strong advantage.

Languages:

- Fluency in oral and written English is required,

- Knowledge of French is a major asset.

Intern conditions:

- UNDP internship programme does not provide a salary or remuneration for the internship,

- UNDP offers a modest monthly stipend to help cover basic daily expenses related to the internship, such as meals and transportation at the duty station,

- All other expenses connected with the internship will be borne by the intern, sponsoring Government, or institution,

- UNDP accepts no responsibility for costs arising from accidents and/or illness or death incurred during the internship,

- The intern is responsible for obtaining necessary visas and arranging travel to and from the duty station where the internship will be performed,

- Interns are not eligible to apply for, or be appointed to, any post in UNDP during the period of the internship,

- The intern must provide proof of enrollment in health insurance plan,

- Interns are not staff members and may not represent UNDP in any official capacity.

Disclaimer

Important information for US Permanent Residents ('Green Card' holders)

Under US immigration law, acceptance of a staff position with UNDP, an international organization, may have significant implications for US Permanent Residents. UNDP advises applicants for all professional level posts that they must relinquish their US Permanent Resident status and accept a G-4 visa, or have submitted a valid application for US citizenship prior to commencement of employment.

UNDP is not in a position to provide advice or assistance on applying for US citizenship and therefore applicants are advised to seek the advice of competent immigration lawyers regarding any applications.

Applicant information about UNDP rosters

Note: UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Non-discrimination

UNDP has a zero-tolerance policy towards sexual exploitation and misconduct, sexual harassment, and abuse of authority. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles.

UNDP is an equal opportunity and inclusive employer that does not discriminate based on race, sex, gender identity, religion, nationality, ethnic origin, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, age, language, social origin or other status.

Scam warning

The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. jobs.title: Grant Implementation Expert
jobs.description:
Terms of Reference (TOR) for functions under a National Personnel Service Agreement

Grant Implementation Expert

1. Position Information

Office/Unit/Project

Türkiye / Climate Change and Environment Portfolio / EU Partnership for Local Climate Action in Türkiye Project

Title

Grant Implementation Expert

Level

NPSA 9

Duty station (City and Country)

Ankara - Türkiye

Type (Regular or Short term)

Short-Term - Retainer

Office- or Home-based

Home-based

Expected starting date

01/11/2026

Expected Duration

Up to 130 days in 12 months

2. Office/Unit/Project Description

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN's global development network. It is an organization advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience, and resources to help people build better lives.

The Climate Change and Environment Portfolio’s strategy is focusing on promoting change at scale through investing in national capacity to respond in addition to piloting and prototyping development solutions that have the potential to lead to transformational change. Also, a key element of the strategy is to apply the integrated ecosystem approach, to help establish mechanisms to value ecosystem services with a view to address the market failures to fully reflect the true value of ecosystem services.

The portfolio strategy requires the establishment of programmatic partnerships, as a cross-cutting area, ‘with different ministries, international organizations (inter alia UNEP, EU, UNIDO, WB, EBRD and FAO), universities and CSOs, collaboratively adding value to the ongoing work of these stakeholders. The Climate Change and Environment (CCE) Portfolio focuses on three programmatic areas that complement each other: 1-Natural Resource Management contributing to sustainable environment management and conservation of natural resources in production landscapes, within the general framework of the ecosystems approach; 2- Climate Change and Disaster Resilience (including chemicals and waste) strengthening institutional capacities for analysis and risk management for resilience with a specific emphasis on climate change, and 3- Cooperation with relevant stakeholders to promote energy efficiency and renewable energy.

The overall objective of the EU Partnership for Local Climate Change Action in Türkiye (LCA) Project is to support Türkiye in its efforts to combat climate change through increased implementation capacity at the local level, which will ultimately contribute to sustainable, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development.

The overall outcome of the Project is the improvement of Türkiye’s local climate change mitigation and adaptation capacity, achieved through activities spanning five distinct components (Components A to E).

Component E focuses on providing Technical Assistance to the EU–Türkiye Climate Change Grant Programme (EU-TR CCGP). The Grant Programme is implemented directly by the Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change (MoEUCC), while UNDP provides technical assistance in support of its implementation.

Projects under the the Climate Change Grant Programme address at least one of these priority areas:

- In line with the priorities of the existing national adaptation and mitigation action plans between 2024-2030,

- Promoting resilient and low-carbon cities and sectors,

- Implementing adaptation and/or mitigation actions in line with existing local or national climate strategies.

As an additional element, all projects include a component (set of activities) on strengthening the communication between stakeholders and “raising awareness within the society”.

The approximate total amount allocated to the grant programme under Grant Component is EUR 15,114,913.23.

Minimum Grant Support* (EUR)

Maximum Grant Support* (EUR)

250,000

750,000

Any grant requested under this call for proposals fall between the following minimum and maximum percentages of total eligible costs of the action:

Minimum percentage: 50 % of the total eligible costs of the action

Maximum percentage: 90 % of the total eligible costs of the action A total of 25 grant projects has been contracted within the framework of the EU – Türkiye Climate Change Grant Programme. The projects are implemented across 15 cities in Türkiye, including Mersin, Çankırı, İzmir, Sinop, Konya, Ankara, Bursa, Çanakkale, Bolu, Malatya, İstanbul, Muğla, Isparta, Kahramanmaraş, and Diyarbakır, as well as in Warka (Poland).

Technical assistance under Component E supports the effective implementation and monitoring of the Grant Programme, including the operation of the Grant Management Information System (MIS), monitoring and evaluation arrangements, monitoring activities, reporting processes, capacity-building and consultative activities, follow-up of grant implementation processes, institutional learning, and the documentation and dissemination of programme results.

In this context, UNDP intends to engage a Grant Implementation Expert on a retainer basis to provide technical, analytical and operational support to the Grant Manager, Grant Expert and Project Team in relation to the implementation, monitoring, reporting and other related processes of the EU-TR CCGP, based on needs arising throughout the implementation period.

Beyond the LCA project, the Expert may also be requested to provide contributions to other projects as deemed relevant to his/her expertise.

3. Objective and Scope of Work

UNDP will engage a Grant Implementation - Expert to provide professional, technical, analytical and operational support to the implementation, monitoring, reporting and overall technical assistance provided to the EU–Türkiye Climate Change Grant Programme under Component E of the EU Partnership for Local Climate Action in Türkiye Project.

The Expert will work in support of the Grant Manager, Grant Expert and Project Team and will contribute to grant-related processes through review, analysis, preparation and consolidation of documentation and information, monitoring and reporting support, operational follow-up and other related activities. The Expert's functions will not include managerial, supervisory and/or representative functions.

The assignment will be implemented on a retainer basis. The Expert will be engaged on an as-needed basis through individual Service Requests issued by UNDP during the contract period. Each Service Request will define, as applicable, the specific assignment, scope of services, expected output(s), estimated level of effort, timeframe, reporting requirements, place of performance and any travel requirements.

The generic functions described below establish the overall areas within which services may be requested. They are indicative and not exhaustive and do not constitute a predetermined set of assignments or deliverables. Depending on the implementation needs of the Grant Programme, an individual Service Request may cover one or more of these functions.

Within the scope of the assignment, the Grant Implementation Expert may be requested to perform the following generic functions:

- Provide technical, analytical and operational support to the implementation, monitoring, reporting and follow-up of grant projects under the EU-TR CCGP.

- Support the Grant Manager, Grant Expert and Project Team in the preparation, review, consolidation and follow-up of grant-related documentation, information and implementation processes.

- Support the review and assessment of narrative, financial, progress, interim and final reports submitted by Grant Beneficiaries, together with relevant supporting documentation, through the MIS and/or other applicable reporting arrangements.

- Prepare and/or contribute to monitoring reports, programme progress reports, review notes, assessment notes, checklists, management summaries, briefing notes, presentations, trackers, analytical documents and other grant-related reporting and management outputs.

- Support the operation and use of the Grant MIS, including the review, recording, follow-up and consolidation of information and documentation submitted or generated during grant implementation.

- Support the operation of the Grant Programme's monitoring and evaluation arrangements, including the collection, review, consolidation and analysis of information relating to implementation progress, outputs, results, indicators, risks and other programme performance information.

- Support the tracking and consolidation of indicators and other quantitative and qualitative information reported by Grant Beneficiaries and contribute to programme-level analysis and reporting.

- Support desk-based and field-based monitoring of grant projects, including review of project documentation, preparation for monitoring visits, participation in site visits and meetings, documentation of findings, and preparation of monitoring reports, notes and follow-up recommendations.

- Support the review and follow-up of notifications, modification and amendment requests, implementation changes and other contractual or implementation-related matters submitted by Grant Beneficiaries, including preparation of technical observations, analyses and recommendations for consideration by the responsible parties.

- Identify gaps, inconsistencies, implementation risks, compliance issues and matters requiring clarification or follow-up in grant-related information and documentation and provide relevant inputs and recommendations to the Grant Manager, Grant Expert and Project Team.

- Support quality assurance of reports, documents, information and other materials produced or submitted in connection with Grant Programme implementation.

- Support communication, information exchange and coordination among UNDP, Grant Beneficiaries, the End Recipient, Contracting Authority and other relevant stakeholders concerning grant implementation, reporting, monitoring and related processes.

- Support the organization and delivery of meetings, consultations, trainings, workshops, guidance sessions and other capacity-building or information-exchange activities related to Grant Programme implementation.

- Prepare or contribute to guidance notes, presentations, training materials, templates, checklists and other tools intended to facilitate grant implementation, monitoring, reporting and compliance.

- Support the preparation, revision and application of grant implementation procedures, guidelines, reporting arrangements, monitoring tools, templates and other programme documentation, as required.

- Contribute to project- and programme-level reporting relating to Component E, including preparation and consolidation of inputs for progress reports, monitoring reports, donor reporting and other reporting requirements.

- Support the preparation and consolidation of information concerning Grant Programme achievements, results, challenges, risks and implementation progress for management, reporting and communication purposes.

- Support the identification, analysis and documentation of lessons learned, good practices, implementation experiences and programme achievements and contribute to the preparation of compendia, case studies, lessons learned reports, dissemination materials and other knowledge products.

- Support grant closure processes, including review and consolidation of relevant implementation, monitoring and reporting information and preparation of related documentation and programme-level inputs.

- Support the organization and implementation of Grant Programme events and related activities where technical or grant implementation input is required.

- Undertake other grant implementation support assignments falling within the overall scope and purpose of this ToR, as specified through individual Service Requests issued by UNDP.

The Expert may be requested to revise or further develop outputs prepared under individual Service Requests on the basis of comments provided by UNDP and/or relevant Grant Programme stakeholders.

Final approvals, formal contractual decisions, certifications and other functions vested in UNDP, the Contracting Authority, End Recipient or other authorized parties shall remain with the respective authorized entity and shall not be exercised by the Grant Implementation Expert.

If required by UNDP, the Grant Implementation Expert may be requested to provide additional consultancy services on topics related to her/his consultancies area.

5. Institutional Arrangement

UNDP will provide the Grant Implementation Expert with all relevant background documents and information required for the completion of assignments. UNDP is not required to provide any physical facility for the work of the Expert. However, depending on the availability of physical facilities and operational requirements, such facilities may be provided at the discretion of UNDP and/or in cooperation with MoEUCC. UNDP will facilitate meetings between the Expert and relevant stakeholders, when needed.

All documents, information and data provided to the Grant Implementation Expert are confidential and cannot be used for any other purposes or shared with a third party without prior written approval from UNDP.

The language of outputs will be specified in the relevant Service Request. Depending on the nature of the assignment, outputs may be required in English and/or Turkish.

The Grant Implementation Expert shall be responsible for the accuracy, consistency and reliability of the information and analysis provided under the assignment and for appropriately identifying the sources of information used.

The Grant Implementation Expert shall report to the Grant Manager of the EU Partnership for Local Climate Action in Türkiye Project under the overall supervision of the Project Manager and will work in close collaboration with the Grant Manager, Grant Expert, Project Team and other relevant stakeholders.

The specific technical focal point, expected outputs and reporting arrangements for each assignment may be further specified in the relevant Service Request.

Outputs prepared under a Service Request shall be submitted to UNDP for review and acceptance in accordance with the requirements and timeframe specified in the respective Service Request. Where revisions are requested, the Expert shall address the comments within the timeframe agreed for the respective assignment.

Place of work for the assignment is home-based and Ankara. Grant Implementation Expert will be expected to be present in MoEUCC (Grant Component Contracting Authority and Directorate of Climate Change) or UNDP premises at certain times when necessary. All travel, accommodation and living costs in duty station (home based and Ankara) will be covered by the Grant Implementation Expert. In case travels to other cities specified in the Projects DoA and/or other unforeseen travel out of the duty station is needed, the travel and accommodation costs of these missions will be borne by UNDP. The cost and terms of reimbursement of any travel authorized by UNDP for Expert must be negotiated prior to travel.

5. Competencies

Core

Achieve Results:

LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility:

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination:

LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:

LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Thematic Area

Name

Definition

Business direction and strategy

Strategic Thinking

Ability to develop effective strategies and prioritized plans in line with UNDP’s objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, potential risks, and opportunities, linking the vision to reality on the ground, and creating tangible solutions.

Business Development

Human-centered Design

Ability to develop solutions to problems by involving the human perspective in all steps of the problem-solving process.

Business Development

Knowledge generation

Ability to research and turn information into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need.

Business management

Working with Evidence and Data

Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions, and supporting decision-making.

Business management

Communication

Ability to communicate in a clear, concise, and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience.

Business management

Risk management

Ability to identify and organize action around mitigating and proactively managing risks.

6. Minimum Qualifications of the Successful NPSA

Min. Education requirements

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Economics/ Business Administration / Management/ Social Sciences/ Engineering, Environmental Sciences/ Natural Sciences/ Statistics/ Political sciences/ Law or related field is required, or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Min. years of relevant work experience

- Minimum 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience at the national or international level in providing management advisory services, and/or hands-on experience in design, monitoring and evaluation of development projects.

Required skills

- Excellent command of office software, such as word processors, spreadsheets, databases.

- Professional experience with government institutions in Türkiye.

- Specific professional experience in the design, implementation, and/or monitoring and evaluation of grant or similar programmes and/or contracts.

- Hands-on experience in EU grants or similar project implementation and/or its audit /verification.

- Specific professional experience in monitoring and evaluation and/or auditing, risk management and/or implementation of at least three (3) EU grant projects or similar programme financed by International Donors.

- Specific professional experience in preparation of training documents and execution of training covering the life cycle of grant projects such as tendering, implementation, monitoring, and financing.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

- Professional Certification in audit and/or risk management and /or accounting and financial management such as CIA, CMA, CPA or similar.

- Specific professional experience with UNDP Contracts and/or knowledge of contract management principles and /or audit/verification modalities of UNDP.

- Specific professional experience in EU-financed projects and contracts. Knowledge of general EU PRAG procedures related to Grants.

- Specific professional experience in monitoring, evaluation, auditing or implementation of at least one (1) grant or similar programme in the field of climate change.

-

- Fluency in Turkish and English

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

- Office/Unit/Project Description

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in São Tomé and Príncipe supports the Government in advancing sustainable development pathways that address poverty, inequality, and environmental sustainability. As a Small Island Developing State (SIDS), the country faces structural vulnerabilities linked to its size, remoteness, and exposure to external shocks, particularly climate change and environmental degradation. At the same time, São Tomé and Príncipe is endowed with exceptional natural capital, hosting rich terrestrial and marine biodiversity and functioning as a net carbon sink. The country’s global environmental significance is further reflected in its designation as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and the recognition of its traditional cocoa production system as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System (GIAHS/SIPAM), highlighting the intrinsic link between biodiversity conservation, sustainable livelihoods, and cultural heritage. UNDP works in close partnership with national institutions, civil society, and development partners to strengthen capacities, mobilize resources, and deliver integrated solutions aligned with national priorities and global commitments.

Within this framework, the Climate and Nature portfolio constitutes a core pillar of UNDP’s programme, focusing on supporting the implementation of the country’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), advancing climate resilience, and promoting the sustainable management of natural resources. The portfolio encompasses a growing pipeline of projects addressing climate mitigation and adaptation, biodiversity conservation, ecosystem restoration, disaster risk reduction, and the transition towards a low-carbon and climate-resilient economy. Key areas of intervention include strengthening climate governance systems—such as transparency, monitoring and reporting—supporting national adaptation planning and implementation, enhancing resilience to climate-related risks (including flooding and water insecurity), and advancing nature-based solutions and biodiversity finance mechanisms.

UNDP’s interventions are characterized by an integrated, cross-sectoral approach that combines policy advisory, institutional capacity development, and on-the-ground implementation. The portfolio places strong emphasis on stakeholder engagement—working closely with government entities, local communities, private sector actors, and development partners—and ensures that climate and environmental actions are inclusive, gender-responsive, and aligned with broader socio-economic priorities, including the promotion of green and blue economy opportunities. As the portfolio continues to expand in scope and complexity, there is a growing need for strengthened programme management and coordination capacity to ensure effective delivery, monitoring, and reporting across multiple projects and funding streams

The Global Environment Facility (GEF) Small Grants Programme (SGP) is implemented by UNDP on behalf of the GEF Partnership. UNDP oversees the Small Grants Programme (SGP) through the Vertical Hub and the Nature Hub of Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS). Funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF), the Small Grants Programme efficiently channels direct grants to non-governmental and community-based organizations to help them cope with climate change; conserve biodiversity; protect international waters; reduce the impact of Persistent Organic Pollutants; and prevent land degradation. Helping communities with their initiatives for sustainable livelihoods while generating global environmental benefits is the core inspiration of the Small Grants Programme.

Launched in 1992 as a corporate programme of the GEF, the GEF Small Grants Programme (GEF SGP) has supported local action for over thirty years to address global environmental concerns. SGP aims to deliver global environmental benefits in the GEF focal areas of biodiversity conservation, climate change mitigation, protection of international waters, prevention of land degradation, and elimination of persistent organic pollutants through community-based approaches. To date, SGP has funded over 29,000 community-based projects covering more than 120 countries. It has gained considerable experiences at the community level, including adapting to climate change while addressing issues of the GEF focal areas. Further information can be found at: https://sgp.undp.org/.

2. Scope of work

The National Coordinator will report through a matrixed structure to both the Resident Representative (or Deputy Resident Representative) and the SGP Regional Programme Specialist. The Coordinator will be responsible for overseeing the implementation of the SGP at the country level, including direct supervision of the SGP Programme Associate/Assistant and coordination of the National Steering Committee.

Ensure effective management of the SGP Country Programme team

- Supervise the SGP Country Programme Associate/ Assistant and provide necessary guidance and coaching;

- Promote and maintain effective teamwork within the SGP Country Programme team, the National Steering Committee members, and with the UNDP CO team;

- Prepare and implement annual work plan, including strategic and/or innovative initiatives, with set delivery and co-financing targets; draft annual SGP Country Office administrative and project operational budget proposal

- Set annual performance parameters and learning objectives for the SGP Country Programme team, assess their performance and provide feedback.

Ensure Programme/Portfolio Development and Management

- Keep abreast of national environmental concerns and priorities as well as the socio-economic conditions and trends as they relate to the SGP and assess their impact on SGP’s work and programme.

- Ensure formulation and implementation of the Country Programme Strategy (CPS), and its periodic review and update.

- Manage the SGP grant allocations and country operating budget, maintain the financial integrity of the programme by ensuring adherence to SGP Standard Operating Procedures as well as UNOPS rules and regulations, and ensure timely and effective use of SGP resources.

- Exercise quality control over the development of a portfolio of project ideas and concepts, and closely monitor the programme implementation progress and results.

- Organize periodic stakeholder workshops and project development sessions for civil society organizations (CSOs) and local communities, and potential applicants and other stakeholders to inform about SGP and its Strategic Initiatives.

- Work closely with Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and Community-based Organizations ( CBOs) in preparation of project concepts and proposals to ensure that projects fit with the SGP Strategic Initiatives, Country Programme Strategy, and technical guidance notes;

- Authorize and manage project planning grants as required.

- Oversee ongoing SGP grant projects and conduct periodic project monitoring field visits and provide technical and operational support and guidance to SGP grantees as required.

- Plan and serve as secretary to the National Steering Committee meetings. Support and closely coordinate with the National Steering Committee and Technical Advisory Group where relevant, in the process of project proposal review, selection and approval, especially the initial appraisal of proposals and assessment of eligibility.

- Foster programme, project, and policy linkages between the SGP and the full or medium-sized GEF projects, planned or underway in the country, as well as those of other government, donors and development partners.

- Report periodically to the Central Programme Management Team (CPMT) on programme implementation status, including annual monitoring reporting, financial reporting, audit, and update the relevant SGP databases.

- Undertake monitoring and evaluation of SGP Country Programme and projects, and grant maker initiatives, in coordination with National Steering Committee (NSC) and CPMT.

- Perform and coordinate administrative tasks (i.e. procurement, travel) adhering to SGP SOPs procurement rules and regulation, as required for programme implementation.

Resource Mobilization and Partnerships

- Establish and maintain close working relationships with stakeholders as well as promote the value, comparative advantages, and ensure visibility of the SGP.

- Assess interest and priorities of key donors and other development partners and develop/update and implement the resource mobilization and partnership strategy to mobilize resources from and develop partnerships with the government, donors and other partners to best leverage SGP resources and develop programme level partnerships.

- Support SGP grantees in securing co-financing and project level partnerships and assist in identifying opportunities and resources for sustaining and scaling up projects.

Facilitate Knowledge Management and Communication

- Document programme/project stories, lessons learned, and best practices in SGP programme/project development, implementation, and oversight.

- Access SGP and other global and regional knowledge, distill best practices and facilitate their dissemination and incorporation within SGP Country Programme and projects, UNDP CO, and to counterparts and partners;

- Support capacity building and networking of grantees to facilitate knowledge exchange, and promote uptake through Knowledge platforms, Knowledge fairs etc.

Ensure Monitoring and Progress Controls

- Sound SGP programme results and impacts, in alignment with national strategies and priorities and SGP strategy and approaches, that contribute to transformational change in society and economy to conserve the global environment and achieve the Sustainable Development Goals, Innovative, technically sound and socially inclusive grant portfolio is developed and implemented. Effective and efficient use of resources to create maximum project/programme impact. Increased trust by clients and donors and increased opportunities for visibility, partnerships and co-financing. The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

3. Institutional Arrangement

- The incumbent will be based in the UNDP São Tome e Principe CO office;

- The incumbent will have a matrixed reporting line to the Resident Representative (or Deputy Resident Representative) and to the SGP Regional Programme Specialist, in accordance with SGP Operational Guidelines;

- The incumbent will be responsible for the supervision and development of the SGP Programme Associate

- The incumbent will be given access to relevant information necessary for the execution of the tasks under this assignment;

- The incumbent will be provided with a workstation (i.e. laptop, internet, phone, scanner/printer, etc.) and access to reliable internet connection

4. Competencies

Expected Demonstration of Competencies

Core

Achieve Results LEVEL 2: Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work

Think Innovatively LEVEL 2: Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking

Learn Continuously LEVEL 2: Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning

Adapt with Agility LEVEL 2: Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process

Act with Determination LEVEL 2: Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously

Engage and Partner LEVEL 2: Is facilitator/integrator, bring people together, build/maintain coalitions/partnerships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion LEVEL 2: Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making

People Management

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies
