Small Grants Programme Coordinator [Open to internal and external candidates]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP Eswatini is initiating Eswatini Country Programme 2026–2030. As part of this programme UNDP will concentrate on two mutually reinforcing priorities: (1) good governance and social cohesion—strengthening accountable, transparent and people-centered institutions, expanding access to justice and human rights, bolstering anti-corruption and oversight, and improving public service delivery (including through digitalization and citizen feedback); and (2) sustainable and resilient economic development—advancing inclusive, green and digital growth by supporting MSME development, entrepreneurship and decent jobs (especially for youth, women and vulnerable groups), while building climate and environmental resilience through nature-positive development, circular economy approaches and a just energy transition, alongside efforts to mobilize innovative financing for implementation. Within the Sustainable and resilient development portfolio, UNDP will be executing the Global Environment Facility (GEF) Small Grants Programme (SGP).

The Global Environment Facility (GEF) Small Grants Programme (SGP) is implemented by UNDP on behalf of the GEF Partnership. UNDP oversees the Small Grants Programme (SGP) through the Vertical Hub and the Nature Hub of Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS). Funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF), the Small Grants Programme efficiently channels direct grants to non-governmental and community-based organizations to help them cope with climate change; conserve biodiversity; protect international waters; reduce the impact of Persistent Organic Pollutants; and prevent land degradation. Helping communities with their initiatives for sustainable livelihoods while generating global environmental benefits is the core inspiration of the Small Grants Programme.

Launched in 1992 as a corporate programme of the GEF, the GEF Small Grants Programme (GEF SGP) has supported local action for over thirty years to address global environmental concerns. SGP aims to deliver global environmental benefits in the GEF focal areas of biodiversity conservation, climate change mitigation, protection of international waters, prevention of land degradation, and elimination of persistent organic pollutants through community-based approaches. To date, SGP has funded over 29,000 community-based projects covering more than 120 countries. It has gained considerable experiences at the community level, including adapting to climate change while addressing issues of the GEF focal areas. Further information can be found at: https://sgp.undp.org/.

The SGP Programme in Eswatini has been implemented over the past 2 years under the oversight of UNOPS Regional Office, with 1 UNOPS contracted staff embedded within UNDP. As the Programme transitions to UNDP full oversight in 2026, UNDP Eswatini is recruiting a National Coordinator to coordinate the SGP in Eswatini.

Duties and Responsibilities

The National Coordinator will report through a matrixed structure to both the Deputy Resident Representative and the SGP Regional Programme Specialist. The coordinator will work on a day-to-day basis within the Sustainable Development Portfolio of UNDP under the oversight of the Sustainable Development Specialist to ensure synergies and coordination within the overall environment, climate and nature portfolio of UNDP. The Coordinator will be responsible for overseeing the implementation of the SGP at country level, while dedicating approximately 50% of their time to support implementation other country office locally-led initiative on adaptation and resilience, with particular focus on the grants element, including grant pipeline development, appraisal support, grantee capacity strengthening, milestone-based disbursement follow-up, grant monitoring, reporting and learning.

Ensure effective management of the SGP Country Programme team

- Liaise with the Sustainable Development/Environment Programme Assistant for administrative support in relation to SGP programming;

- Promote and maintain effective teamwork within the SGP Country Programme and wider Environment portfolio team, the National Steering Committee members, and with the UNDP CO team;

- Prepare and implement annual work plan, including strategic and/or innovative initiatives, with set delivery and co-financing targets; draft annual SGP Country Office administrative and project operational budget proposal;

- Set annual performance parameters and learning objectives for the SGP Country Programme team, assess their performance and provide feedback.

Ensure Programme/Portfolio Development and Management

- Keep abreast of national environmental concerns and priorities as well as the socio-economic conditions and trends as they relate to the SGP and assess their impact on SGP’s work and programme.

- Ensure formulation and implementation of the Country Programme Strategy (CPS), and its periodic review and update.

- Ensure the Country Programme Strategy (CPS) and annual workplans integrate gender analysis, clear gender equality actions, and measurable targets (including for women-led/women-benefiting initiatives), aligned to UNDP and national gender priorities.

- Manage the SGP grant allocations and country operating budget, maintain the financial integrity of the programme by ensuring adherence to SGP Standard Operating Procedures as well as UNDP rules and regulations, and ensure timely and effective use of SGP resources.

- Exercise quality control over the development of a portfolio of project ideas and concepts and closely monitor the programme implementation progress and results.

- Organize periodic stakeholder workshops and project development sessions for civil society organizations (CSOs) and local communities, and potential applicants and other stakeholders to inform about SGP and its Strategic Initiatives.

- Design and deliver capacity development and communications in gender-responsive ways (e.g., convenient timing/locations, accessible formats/languages, safe spaces), to enable meaningful participation of women and marginalized groups.

- Work closely with Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and Community-based Organizations (CBOs) in preparation of project concepts and proposals to ensure that projects fit with the SGP Strategic Initiatives, Country Programme Strategy, and technical guidance notes;

- Authorize and manage project planning grants as required.

- Oversee ongoing SGP grant projects and conduct periodic project monitoring field visits and provide technical and operational support and guidance to SGP grantees as required.

- During monitoring visits, assess gender-related results and risks, support corrective actions, and document lessons on what works to advance gender equality in community-based environmental action.

- Plan and serve as secretary to the National Steering Committee meetings. Support and closely coordinate with the National Steering Committee and Technical Advisory Group where relevant, in the process of project proposal review, selection and approval, especially the initial appraisal of proposals and assessment of eligibility.

- Promote gender-responsive grantmaking by applying gender considerations in calls for proposals, appraisal tools and selection processes, and by advising the National Steering Committee on gender equality gaps, risks and opportunities in the portfolio.

- Foster programme, project, and policy linkages between the SGP and the full or medium-sized GEF projects, planned or underway in the country, as well as those of other government, donors and development partners.

- Report periodically to the Central Programme Management Team (CPMT) on programme implementation status, including annual monitoring reporting, financial reporting, audit, and update the relevant SGP databases.

- Undertake monitoring and evaluation of SGP Country Programme and projects, and grant maker initiatives, in coordination with National Steering Committee (NSC) and CPMT.

- Perform and coordinate administrative tasks (i.e. procurement, travel) adhering to SGP SOPs procurement rules and regulation, as required for programme implementation.

Support implementation of grassroot level adaptation interventions under the Environment Portfolio (50% level of effort)

- Support the Sustainable Development Specialist and UNDP Country Office in the effective in-country implementation of adaptation grants, ensuring complementarity between the SGP grant portfolio and the UNDP’s other country initiatives on adaptation, catchment resilience, and nature-based solutions objectives.

- Support coordination of the grants pipeline for country adaptation and resilience grant, including targeted outreach to eligible community-based organizations, civil society organizations, cooperatives and other local entities; support preparation of concept notes and proposals aligned to Catchment Investment Programme priorities and agreed grant criteria.

- Provide technical and operational support to the review, appraisal and documentation of grant proposals, ensuring consistency with partner/donor requirements, UNDP Low-Value Grant procedures, social and environmental safeguards, gender and inclusion standards, and fiduciary due diligence.

- Strengthen grantee capacities in project design, financial management, procurement planning, safeguards, gender-responsive implementation, monitoring, reporting and verification, with particular attention to women, youth and vulnerable groups participating in locally led adaptation initiatives.

- Conduct field monitoring and quality assurance visits for country office initiatives on adaptation, catchment resilience, and nature-based solutions, document progress against agreed outputs and indicators, identify implementation risks and lessons learned, and support adaptive management by grantees and catchment-level stakeholders.

- Prepare timely inputs for donor/partner reporting, audits, knowledge products and regional learning processes, including evidence on grant results, beneficiary reach, safeguards compliance, gender-responsive outcomes, co-financing and sustainability prospects.

Gender mainstreaming (cross-cutting responsibility)

- Integrate gender equality and women’s empowerment considerations across SGP and other locally led adaptation and resilience initiatives’ planning, grantmaking, implementation, monitoring and reporting, in line with UNDP gender policies and the SGP strategic framework.

- Identify and address gender-related barriers to accessing SGP and in other locally-led Adaptation resources (e.g., information, land/asset access, time burdens, mobility, digital access), including through targeted outreach and capacity support for women-led organizations and groups.

- Ensure SGP and Locally Led Adaptation processes and partner engagements are risk-informed and safeguarding-sensitive, including attention to prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse/sexual harassment (SEA/SH) and appropriate referral pathways in line with UNDP requirements.

Resource Mobilization and Partnerships

- Establish and maintain close working relationships with stakeholders as well as promote the value, comparative advantages, and ensure visibility of the SGP.

- Assess interest and priorities of key donors and other development partners and develop/update and implement the resource mobilization and partnership strategy to mobilize resources from and develop partnerships with the government, donors and other partners to best leverage SGP resources and develop programme level partnerships.

- Support SGP grantees in securing co-financing and project level partnerships and assist in identifying opportunities and resources for sustaining and scaling up projects.

- Mobilize resources and partnerships that explicitly support gender-responsive community climate and biodiversity solutions, including engagement with women’s organizations and gender machinery where relevant.

Facilitate Knowledge Management and Communication

- Document programme/project stories, lessons learned, and best practices in SGP programme/project development, implementation, and oversight.

- Access SGP and other global and regional knowledge, distill best practices and facilitate their dissemination and incorporation within SGP Country Programme and projects, UNDP CO, and to counterparts and partners;

- Support capacity building and networking of grantees to facilitate knowledge exchange, and promote uptake through Knowledge platforms, Knowledge fairs etc.

- Ensure knowledge products and visibility materials reflect gender-responsive results (including women’s leadership and benefits), using inclusive language and ethically obtained stories/images/quotes with informed consent.

Ensure Monitoring and Progress Controls

- Sound SGP programme results and impacts, in alignment with national strategies and priorities and SGP strategy and approaches, that contribute to transformational change in society and economy to conserve the global environment and achieve the Sustainable Development Goals, Innovative, technically sound and socially inclusive grant portfolio is developed and implemented. Effective and efficient use of resources to create maximum project/programme impact. Increased trust by clients and donors and increased opportunities for visibility, partnerships and co-financing.

- Track, analyze and report gender-related results using appropriate indicators and sex-/age-disaggregated data where feasible; ensure findings inform adaptive management, learning and future grant cycles.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

- The incumbent will be based in the UNDP Eswatini offices;

- The incumbent will have a matrixed reporting line to the Deputy Resident Representative and to the SGP Regional Programme Specialist, in accordance with SGP Operational Guidelines;

- The Coordinator will work on a day-to-day basis under the oversight of the Sustainable Development Specialist to ensure synergies and coordination within the overall environment, climate and nature portfolio of UNDP;

- The incumbent will be given access to relevant information necessary for the execution of the tasks under this assignment;

- The incumbent will be provided with a workstation (i.e. laptop, internet, phone, access to scanner/printer, etc.) and access to reliable internet connection.

Competencies

Core competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 2: Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 2: Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 2: Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 2: Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 2: Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 2: Is facilitator/integrator, bring people together, build/maintain coalitions/partnerships

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 2: Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making.

Business Direction & Strategy

- Strategic Thinking Develop effective strategies and prioritized plans in line with UNDP’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight.

Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Partnership management

- Strategic engagement Ability to capture and sustain attention, interest and agreement of high-level, influential policy and decision makers and secure their buy-in of high-level vision and objectives.

Background

The Spotlight Initiative is a global partnership between the United Nations (UN) and the European Union (EU) to eliminate all forms of violence against women and girls in support of the 2030 Agenda on Sustainable Development. It was launched in September 2017 by the UN Secretary General and the EU High Representative and Vice President as a model for partnerships with donors, civil society, and the UN to deliver on SDGs in a comprehensive manner. SDG 5 and the achievement of gender equality are placed at the center of efforts (alongside Goal 16) with the aim to provide an enabling environment for the implementation of all goals. Within the UN, the Initiative helps operationalize the UN development system reforms and model a new way of delivering on SDGs in an integrated way, leveraging stakeholders’ diverse comparative expertise and collaborative advantages.

In Liberia, the Spotlight Initiative ran from 2019 to 2023 and focused on addressing the root causes of sexual and gender-based violence, harmful practices, and violations of women's rights, including SRHR. Building on the knowledge and lessons from the first phase (2019-2023), Spotlight Initiative 2.0 is being implemented to consolidate the achievements and further galvanize crucial efforts to eliminate violence against women and girls.

To support this implementation, multi-stakeholder, and multi-year programme, a dedicated Programme Coordination and Management Unit (PMCU) has been established within the UN Resident Coordinator’s Office. In this context, the Resident Coordinator’s Office is seeking to recruit an Programme Associate to provide programme implementation support, stakeholder engagement, advocacy, knowledge management, reporting, and results tracking. The Programme Associate position has been created to strengthen support for programme delivery and achievement of results to support services to the Spotlight team based in the Resident Coordinator’s office, and as needed, to the Spotlight RUNOs technical team based in UNDP, UNFPA and UN Women.

Duties and Responsibilities

- Scope of Work (5 to 7 items only)

a. Programme implementation Support

- Support implementation follow-up of programme workplans, activities, decisions, commitments, and agreed actions to ensure timely delivery of results.

- Support programme implementation tracking, programme planning , and programme management review processes

- Support organization of meetings, preparation of agendas, briefing materials, presentations, participant lists, minutes, and action trackers.

- Support tracking of decisions from programme meetings and governance mechanisms.

- Support field missions’ preparations, and stakeholder engagements.

- Maintain a repository of programme decisions, commitments, action points, and key implementation documents to support institutional memory and accountability.

b. Stakeholder Engagement, Advocacy and Partnership Support

- Support efforts for stakeholder engagements

- Assist in organizing advocacy initiatives, dialogues, consultations, campaigns and various activities that advance Spotlight Initiative objectives.

- Support communication and information-sharing on spotlight initiative among stakeholders and beyond

- Support preparation of advocacy materials, briefing notes, talking points, presentations, position papers, and engagement packages.

- Document stakeholder commitments, recommendations, and agreed actions and monitor follow-up implementation.

- Support donor missions, visits, programme reviews, and other relevant engagements.

- Maintain stakeholder databases and partnership records to facilitate effective engagement and communication.

- Support efforts in preparation of stakeholder mapping and engagement updates to inform programme planning and partnership management.

c. Knowledge Management, Reporting and Learning

- Support documentation and dissemination of programme achievements, lessons learned, good practices, innovations, and success stories.

- Maintain programme knowledge repositories and ensure systematic filing and accessibility of programme information and documentation.

- Compile initial information and inputs from RUNOs for programme reporting purposes.

- Assist in preparation of progress reports, implementation updates, briefing notes, donor reports, and management information products.

- Contribute to the preparation of knowledge products highlighting programme results, impact, and emerging evidence.

- Contribute to programme advocacy through support in preparation of success stories, human-interest stories, event summaries, and other results-focused communication products, ensuring compliance with applicable UN and donor visibility requirements

d. Administrative Support

- Provide logistical and administrative support for programme activities, workshops, consultations, trainings, meetings, missions, and other stakeholder engagements.

- Support travel arrangements, mission planning, procurement requests, and other operational requirements in accordance with UN regulations and procedures.

- Maintain programme records and support documentation required for programme implementation, reporting, and audits.

- Facilitate coordination between the PMCU and relevant support units within participating UN agencies.

- Assist in tracking and maintaining programme documentation necessary for accountability and reporting purposes.

- Support organization of meetings, missions, programme reviews, and consultations, including preparation of logistical and administrative arrangements.

- Maintain accurate records of correspondence, official communications, meeting documentation, and programme files in accordance with UN records management requirements.

e. Event Management Support

- Support in coordination and management of programme events, including workshops, trainings, conferences, launches, consultations, and meetings, ensuring effective planning and implementation.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization

jobs.title: Associado de Pesquisa em Cibersegurança (1 vaga) (Home Based) - [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Em 2025, o Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ) e o Programa das Nações Unidas para o Desenvolvimento (PNUD) firmaram uma parceria voltada à promoção da inovação em segurança cibernética para o Poder Judiciário. O projeto BRA/25/025 – “Fortalecimento da segurança cibernética e da transparência para governança e efetividade da atuação do Poder Judiciário” desenvolve e implementa ferramentas e estratégias para o fortalecimento da segurança cibernética, da preservação digital e da integridade da informação, ampliando a proteção dos sistemas e dos usuários do Judiciário.

A iniciativa fortalece a segurança institucional e promove a transparência, a boa governança e a eficiência dos processos judiciais, contribuindo para a economia de recursos e para uma atuação mais ágil da Justiça em benefício dos cidadãos e da sociedade.

Para isso, a governança do projeto está dividida nas seguintes frentes:

Quatro eixos transversais de coordenação:

- Coordenação Geral;

- Unidade de monitoramento e controle integrado;

- Unidade de gestão técnica e operacional;

- Unidade de formação e comunicação;

Quatro frentes de trabalho, focadas em:

- Compliance normativa;

- Conformidade operacional;

- Governança em rede;

- Fomento à cultura de segurança cibernética;

Por se tratar de uma vaga em regime remoto, espera-se que o(a) candidato(a) disponha de condições adequadas de trabalho, incluindo infraestrutura e equipamentos necessários para o pleno desempenho das atividades.

Deveres e responsabilidades

O(a) Associado(a) de Pesquisa em Cibersegurança estará vinculado(a) ao Eixo 4 – Fomento à Cultura de Segurança Cibernética, com atuação voltada à pesquisa aplicada para identificar desafios concretos, desenvolver e testar abordagens e soluções e apoiar sua adoção pelas instituições do sistema de Justiça. Desenvolverá estudos, provas de conceito e soluções inovadoras, incluindo o uso de inteligência artificial e outras tecnologias emergentes, com foco na geração de resultados aplicáveis e na sua validação em contextos institucionais reais.

As seguintes atividades indicativas estão previstas:

1. Pesquisa Aplicada e Prospecção Tecnológica

a. Conduzir pesquisas aplicadas em cibersegurança, identificando tendências, novas tecnologias e práticas emergentes. b. Avaliar tecnologias, metodologias e abordagens inovadoras que possam fortalecer a postura de segurança institucional. c. Acompanhar a evolução do cenário tecnológico e suas possíveis aplicações no contexto do Laboratório de Cibersegurança do Poder Judiciário.

2. Experimentação, Prototipagem e Desenvolvimento de Soluções

a. Desenvolver estudos, provas de conceito, protótipos e soluções inovadoras em parceria com o Blue Team e demais áreas técnicas. b. Planejar e executar experimentações e testes para avaliar a viabilidade, a eficácia e a aplicabilidade das soluções propostas. c. Colaborar na criação e no aprimoramento de ambientes de simulação, laboratórios virtuais e testbeds.

3. Inovação e Agenda de Pesquisa

a. Participar da definição de desafios, programas de inovação e agendas de pesquisa para o Laboratório de Cibersegurança do Poder Judiciário. b. Identificar oportunidades de pesquisa e desenvolvimento experimental alinhadas às necessidades institucionais. c. Contribuir para a priorização de iniciativas de inovação em cibersegurança.

4. Gestão do Conhecimento e Disseminação de Resultados

a. Documentar experimentações, testes, metodologias e resultados, consolidando conhecimento estruturado e replicável. b. Produzir relatórios técnicos, manuais, estudos e materiais de referência relacionados às pesquisas desenvolvidas. c. Promover a disseminação dos aprendizados, resultados e boas práticas para outras frentes e equipes.

5. Cooperação Técnica e Parcerias Institucionais

a. Estabelecer e fortalecer parcerias com instituições acadêmicas, órgãos públicos e grupos especializados. b. Apoiar a realização de iniciativas conjuntas de pesquisa, inovação e intercâmbio de conhecimentos. c. Articular a participação de especialistas e instituições parceiras em projetos e programas do Laboratório de Cibersegurança do Poder Judiciário.

6. Aplicação Institucional e Transferência de Inovações

a. Acompanhar a transição de inovações bem-sucedidas para ambientes produtivos ou programas internos. b. Apoiar as áreas técnicas na incorporação e aplicação dos resultados das pesquisas. c. Contribuir com insumos técnicos para campanhas de conscientização, critérios de certificação e outras iniciativas institucionais.

7. Internalização da Pesquisa em Cibersegurança

a. Promover o desenvolvimento de pesquisas técnico-científicas em cibersegurança, incluindo estudos sobre inteligência artificial, aprendizado de máquina e demais tecnologias emergentes. b. Incentivar a produção e a divulgação de artigos científicos, publicações técnicas e estudos especializados. c. Articular iniciativas de cooperação técnica e científica com instituições acadêmicas, centros de pesquisa, organismos internacionais e entidades especializadas estrangeiras. d. Viabilizar o intercâmbio de conhecimentos, metodologias e boas práticas em inovação em cibersegurança.

O(a) titular desempenha outras funções compatíveis com seu perfil funcional que considere necessárias ao bom funcionamento do projeto.

Arranjo Institucional

A pessoa contratada será supervisionada pela Analista de Gestão de Cultura de Segurança Cibernética.

Competências

- Alcançar Resultados - NÍVEL 1: Planeja e monitora seu próprio trabalho, presta atenção aos detalhes e entrega um trabalho de qualidade dentro do prazo.

- Pensar de forma Inovadora - NÍVEL 1: Aberto a ideias criativas e riscos conhecidos, é um solucionador de problemas prático e faz melhorias.

- Aprender Continuamente - NÍVEL 1: Mente aberta e curioso, compartilha conhecimento, aprende com os erros e pede feedback.

- Adaptar com Agilidade - NÍVEL 1: Adapta-se às mudanças, lida de forma construtiva com ambiguidades e incertezas, e é flexível..

- Agir com Determinação - NÍVEL 1: Demonstra determinação e motivação, mantém a calma diante da adversidade e tem confiança.

- Engajar e fazer Parcerias - NÍVEL 1: Demonstra compaixão e compreensão em relação aos outros, formando relacionamentos positivos.

- Promover a Diversidade e Inclusão - NÍVEL 1: Valoriza e respeita as diferenças, está consciente de vieses inconscientes e enfrenta a discriminação

Competências multifuncionais e técnicas

Direção e estratégia de negócios | Pensamento estratégico: Desenvolver estratégias eficazes e planos prioritários alinhados com a missão e os objetivos do PNUD, baseando-se em uma análise sistêmica de desafios, oportunidades e riscos potenciais; conectar a visão geral à realidade no campo para criar soluções tangíveis e direcionadas; aprender a partir de diversas fontes para antecipar e responder de forma eficaz às tendências atuais e futuras; demonstrar capacidade de previsão.

Direção e estratégia de negócios | Perspicácia Empresarial: Capacidade de compreender e lidar com situações de negócios de forma a alcançar bons resultados. Habilidade para tomar boas decisões e fazer julgamentos rápidos dentro de tais contextos. Conhecimento e compreensão dos marcos operacionais da organização.

Desenvolvimento de negócios | Design centrado no humano: Capacidade de desenvolver soluções para problemas envolvendo a perspectiva humana em todas as etapas do processo de resolução. Conhecimento e compreensão dos princípios e práticas de design centrado no ser humano.

Gestão de negócios | Gestão de Projetos: Capacidade de planejar, organizar, priorizar e controlar recursos, procedimentos e protocolos para alcançar objetivos específicos.

Digital | Gerenciamento de riscos de segurança cibernética e privacidade de dados: Capacidade de antecipar, preparar e responder a riscos e problemas que possam resultar em violações de dados, afetando a reputação do PNUD e causando danos pessoais.

Agenda 2030: Paz | Estado de Direito, Segurança e Direitos Humanos: Instituições Eficazes do Setor de Justiça.

Agenda 2030: Paz | Estado de Direito, Segurança e Direitos Humanos: Acesso à Justiça.

Habilidades e experiência necessárias

Requisitos mínimos de educação:

- Diploma do Ensino Médio completo é requerido.

- Diploma Universitário (Ensino Superior) em Direito, Ciência de Dados, Estatística, Tecnologia da Informação, Relações Internacionais e Segurança da Informação ou áreas afins será dada a devida consideração, mas não é um requisito.

Anos mínimos de experiência profissional relevante:

- Mínimo de 7 anos (para Ensino Médio) ou 4 anos (para Ensino Superior) de experiência profissional relevante em inovação e pesquisa aplicada em cibersegurança.

Habilidades requeridas:

- Experiência no uso do Pacote Microsoft Office e de ferramentas de tecnologia da informação;

Habilidades desejadas, além das competências abordadas na seção Competências:

- Experiência em inovação tecnológica, provas de conceito, ambientes de simulação, laboratórios virtuais, testbeds ou desenvolvimento experimental na área de cibersegurança.

- Experiência em projetos relacionados à inteligência artificial, aprendizado de máquina ou análise de dados aplicados à segurança cibernética.

- Experiência na elaboração de estudos, relatórios técnicos, artigos científicos ou outras publicações especializadas.

- Experiência em projetos de cooperação técnica ou científica com instituições acadêmicas, centros de pesquisa, órgãos públicos, organismos internacionais ou entidades estrangeiras

- Experiência profissional em na implementação, avaliação ou monitoramento de programas de conformidade com a LGPD, ou GDPR, ou outros referenciais internacionais.

Idiomas exigidos:

- Fluência em português é requerida.

- Nível intermediário de inglês é desejável.

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, and culture. Individuals from minority groups, indigenous groups and persons with disabilities are equally encouraged to apply. All applications will be treated with the strictest confidence.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization in fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and planet. Learn more at undp.org or follow at @UNDP

Iraq is recognized as one of the most affected countries by the harmful effects of climate change. Iraq ratified the Paris Agreement on January 14, 2021. In October 2021, the Government of Iraq (GoI) signed their first National Determined Contribution (NDC), which has been presented at the COP26. The Government of Iraq has requested UNDP support in implementation of the NDC, including through capacity development, advisory for sectoral planning and formulation of related strategies, frameworks, and instruments.

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP's policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels offers a spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in UNDP's Strategic Plan.

UNDP is an accredited Implementing Agency for the Global Environment Facility (GEF) Trust Fund and the family of funds such as the Least Developed Countries Fund (LDCF), the Special Climate Change Fund (SCCF), and the Global Biodiversity Framework Fund (GBBF). As an Implementing Agency, UNDP offers countries highly specialized services for eligibility assessment, project formulation and due diligence, co-financing mobilization, implementation oversight, results management and evaluation, and knowledge management.

Iraq faces significant environmental and public health risks associated with persistent organic pollutants (POPs), hazardous chemicals, obsolete pesticides, polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), unintentional POPs (UPOPs), industrial POPs (IPOPs), and chemically contaminated sites. Previous assessments identified substantial quantities of obsolete pesticides and potentially PCB-contaminated electrical equipment and highlighted significant technical and institutional capacity gaps in chemicals and contaminated-sites management.

The Government of Iraq is a Party to major international chemicals and waste conventions, including the Stockholm, Basel, Rotterdam and Minamata Conventions. Iraq has previously developed a National Implementation Plan (NIP) under the Stockholm Convention; however, the existing NIP requires updating to reflect newly listed POPs, improved inventories, updated risk information, institutional developments and current national priorities.

The Integrated Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs) and Chemical Hotspots Management Project, therefore adopts an integrated approach combining:

- strengthening the national framework for POPs and hazardous chemicals management;

- updating the national POPs inventories and National Implementation Plan;

- strengthening laboratory, inspection, monitoring and institutional capacities;

- environmentally sound management and disposal of obsolete pesticides;

- management and disposal/phase-out of PCB-contaminated equipment, oils and waste; and

- assessment and remediation planning for priority chemical pollution hotspots.

The project comprises three components. Component 1 focuses on improved management of POPs and hazardous chemicals; Component 2 focuses on high-risk POPs in the agriculture and power sectors; and Component 3 addresses chemical pollution hotspots and contaminated sites.

Implementation will require extensive technical assistance, consultancy services, procurement of laboratory and field equipment, hazardous waste management services, capacity building, site assessments, remediation planning and policy/regulatory development.

The project will be implemented by UNDP through an Output Agreement with the Ministry of Environment. The Project Manager will therefore be the principal day-to-day focal point for implementation and coordination within the project management structure.

Institutional Arrangement

The Project Manager will directly report to the Programme Specilaist with matrix reporting to the chief technical specialist of the Environment, Energy and Climate Change (EECC), UNDP Iraq. The position holder will be part of a dynamic team of national and international experts working on policy advocacy, capacity building, innovation and sharing best practices with national stakeholders on climate change, environmental management and POPs and Chemical Hotspots Management.

Duties and Responsibilities

Provide Strategic Technical Direction and Leadership

- Lead strategic planning for the project as well as formulation and periodic revisions of the project’s annual work plan (AWP), including plans for budget, HR and procurement that are developed in close coordination with UNDP’s Country Office Programme, HR, and Procurement teams. Lead development of detailed implementation plans.

- Lead the provision of high-level strategic and technical guidance to the project, ensuring alignment with UNDP corporate priorities, donor requirements, national development frameworks, and relevant international commitments.

- Advise UNDP management and project stakeholders on emerging technical issues, risks, opportunities, and strategic approaches to enhance project impact, sustainability, and policy relevance.

- Oversee the overall technical quality of project outputs, deliverables, studies, assessments, and knowledge products to ensure compliance with international standards and best practices.

- Provide leadership in the identification, design, and implementation of innovative technical solutions and approaches that support the achievement of project objectives and intended outcomes.

- Guide the integration of cross-cutting issues, including gender equality, environmental sustainability, social inclusion, human rights, and capacity development, into project planning and implementation.

- Support adaptive management by recommending strategic adjustments based on implementation progress, lessons learned, and changing contextual circumstances.

- Provide direction, guidance, and direct supervision to UNDP project personnel. Undertake technical review of project documents produced by the project team and partners, and ensure high technical standards are met.

- Ensure proper execution of all administrative activities associated with project implementation, including mobilizing goods and services, preparing Terms of Reference, completing contracting processes, recruiting/selecting consultants and experts, and managing financial arrangements/transactions and their correct authorization.

- Identify opportunities for synergies with other projects within UNDP and beyond, to advance the key objectives and grow its focus.

Lead Technical Quality Assurance and Programme Oversight

- Provide technical review and quality assurance of project work plans, technical reports, procurement specifications, Terms of Reference, training materials, policy products, and other project deliverables.

- Ensure that project activities are implemented in accordance with approved project documents, UNDP rules and regulations, donor requirements, and national priorities.

- Support the technical teams in maintaining high standards of project delivery, timeliness, and cost-effectiveness.

- Review technical outputs developed by consultants, contractors, service providers, and implementing partners and provide recommendations for improvement where necessary.

- Ensure consistency and coherence across project components and interventions to maximise results and avoid duplication of efforts.

- Provide technical support to the implementing partners and act as a liaison between UNDP and the partners.

- Support resource mobilization efforts and project development.

Support Strategic Partnerships and Stakeholder Engagement

- Facilitate technical dialogue and collaboration between UNDP, government institutions, development partners, academia, civil society organisations, and private sector stakeholders.

- Provide technical advice and support to implementing partners to strengthen ownership, coordination, and effective project implementation.

- Identify opportunities for strategic partnerships, resource mobilisation, and collaboration that can enhance project sustainability and scale-up successful interventions.

- Represent the project and provide technical inputs during meetings, workshops, consultations, conferences, and policy dialogues as required.

Monitor and report on progress in implementing project activities and achieving the targets set.

- Provide leadership and technical advice to the project in developing baselines and indicators for project monitoring and evaluation and coordinate the finalization of detailed results framework. Develop clear strategies and an effective system for data collection, means of verification, and information sharing and reporting.

- Lead the implementation of project monitoring, evaluation, and results framework to identify plan deviations and other problems; and make needed course corrections within agreed upon tolerances to achieve results. Conduct field visits as required to verify project activities relative to stated targets and provide regular field updates to UNDP management.

- Lead the development and conduct of mid-term and annual reviews, and end line assessment; and coordinate the conduct of independent evaluations. Organize project review and evaluation meetings. Follow up on the implementation of decisions, recommendations, and course corrections.

- Manage and monitor project risks, including social and environmental risks, initially identified and submit new risks to appropriate project governing bodies for consideration and decision on possible actions.

- Coordinate the preparation of corporate, donor and government reports in line with the reporting schedule and UNDP and donor requirements. Ensure provision of ad hoc reports and information requested by relevant entities.

- Ensure proper operational and financial closure of the project.

Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing, and advocacy relevant to the assigned thematic areas.

- Provide technical guidance for the development and refinement of project indicators, monitoring frameworks, and reporting tools.

- Review project progress and results regularly and provide recommendations to address implementation challenges and improve performance.

- Contribute to the documentation of lessons learned, good practices, case studies, and knowledge products to support institutional learning and replication of successful approaches.

- Lead and support capacity-building initiatives, technical trainings, workshops, and knowledge-sharing activities for project staff, government counterparts, and stakeholders.

- Promote knowledge exchange and contribute to relevant communities of practice, technical networks, and learning platforms.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

- People Management: UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site .

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy

- System Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

2030 Agenda: Planet

- Nature Environmental Governance: Global Environmental Governance

Finance

- Budget Management Ability to support budgetary aspects of work planning process, drawing and management of team budgets.

Business Direction & Strategy

- Effective Decision Making Take decisions in a timely and efficient manner in line with one’s authority, area of expertise and resources.

- Negotiation and influence Reach an understanding, persuade others, resolve points of difference, gain advantage in the outcome of dialogue, negotiate mutually acceptable solutions through compromise, and create win-win situations.

Business Management

- Project management Ability to plan, organize, prioritize, and control resources, procedures, and protocols to achieve specific goals.

- Risk management Identify and organize action around mitigating and proactively managing risks

Minimum Qualifications of the Successful NPSA

Minimum Education requirements

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Environmental Management, Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Natural Resources Management, Development Studies, Project Management or a relevant related field is required, OR

Background

The United Nations Volunteers (UNV) programme contributes to peace and development through volunteerism worldwide. We work with partners to integrate qualified, highly motivated and well supported UN Volunteers into development programming and promote the value and global recognition of volunteerism. UNV is active in 160 countries every year. UNV is administered by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). UNV is headquartered in Bonn, Germany, with a field presence comprising 6 regional offices and 50+ field units.

The Human Resources Section (HRS) provides a full range of HR services to the organization and its workforce. As part of the Human Resources Section, the Capacity Development Team (CDT) designs capacity development and learning programmes for UN Volunteers. The team supports the implementation of the UNV Learning Portfolio which consists of five comprehensive learning experiences: 1. onboarding 2. skills surge 3. empowerment for change 4. connect and learn 5. career craft.

Scope of Work

- Plan and design virtual and onsite learning activities

- Perform the full cycle of project management, including communication, timeline management, budget oversight, and scope control.

- Prepare terms of reference and procure professional services from vendors and consultants for volunteer learning activities and projects.

- Coordinate logistics, and administrative arrangements for the timely delivery of the thematic workshops.

- Organize and monitor the delivery of services by external consultants and vendors in line with project plans, timelines and budgets.

- Conduct a thorough review to capture lessons learned and best practices for future projects.

- Provide technical guidance and supervision to designated personnel supporting assigned learning portfolio activities.

2. Deliver virtual and onsite learning activities

- Facilitate in-person, virtual, and blended learning activities in collaboration with stakeholders and domain experts, and the capacity development team using appropriate platforms.

- Adapt learning delivery methods to meet the needs of diverse volunteer categories, incorporating interactive and participatory techniques to increase engagement and retention.

- Build and maintain relationships with key stakeholders to expand co-delivery of volunteer learning initiatives.

- Engage with facilitators to ensure understanding and finalization of learning content and methods for effective program delivery.

- Coordinate or provide technical and learner support for virtual, blended, and onsite learning activities.

- Monitor volunteer engagement during sessions, making real-time improvements to optimize learning outcomes.

- Conduct pre- and post-workshop evaluations, recommending data-driven improvements.

3. Design and maintain e-courses on Learning Management System

- Ensure catalogue e-courses are current, relevant and accessible on UNV Learning Management System (e-Campus);

- Track completion of e-courses, including mandatory ones in collaboration with relevant UNV sections;

- Stay abreast of the status of mutual recognition of mandatory learning programmes completion through the UN Inter-Agency Group;

- Design, develop, update or maintain priority digital and blended learning products on eCampus, using learning technologies and authoring tools, including storyboards, instructional scripts, interactive activities and multimedia resources..

- Liaise with external vendors to resolve technical issues with accessing and completing courses, while improving user experience and interface.

- Support the administration and continuous improvement of learning platforms and digital learning environments to strengthen learner access, usability, engagement and reporting.

4. Support the revision of and delivery of learning programmes

- Collaborate with stakeholders and domain experts to revise learning programme content and delivery, aligning with identified learning needs and corporate goals.

- Analyze learning evaluation data to identify areas of improvement and incorporate changes into learning programmes and products.

- Apply agreed quality standards, templates and review processes to learning products, digital content, facilitator materials and learner resources.

- Maintain version control, communicate updated/revised programme to stakeholders, and conduct Training of Trainers for relevant workshops.

5. Coordinate learning outreach, communications and engagement

- Plan and coordinate communications and learner-engagement activities for assigned learning portfolio and UNV region, using appropriate communication channels and digital platforms.

- Develop and implement programme information, guidance and stakeholder updates to support awareness, access to and participation in learning opportunities.

- Draft relevant reports on learning activities, outcomes and impact as required.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the section and the organization.

The Learning Specialist reports to the Team Leader, Capacity Development and Learning, and works closely with the rest of the CDT and as a member of the Human Resources Section.

Core Competencies

Achieve Results

Learn Continuously

Adapt with Agility

- Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Act with Determination

Engage and Partner

Enable Diversity and Inclusion

People Management: The position has no direct supervisory responsibilities. The role is intended to provide technical leadership and vendor/resource oversight through subject matter expertise, architecture guidance, quality assurance, and management of vendor-delivered outputs, not through line management of UNV staff.

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

For six decades, UNDP has shaped the progress of human development, working with its partners to lift millions from poverty and increase opportunities for all. Empowered by Member States with a mandate to work across the spectrum of human development, UNDP provides integrated support at scale to improve people’s lives worldwide. UNDP’s Strategic Plan 2026-2029 is grounded in the determination of UNDP to eradicate poverty, the greatest global challenge, indispensable to the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals. Through the Strategic Plan, UNDP will continue to support countries’ progress towards high human development, while protecting the planet. Four strategic objectives – prosperity for all, effective governance, crisis resilience, and healthy planet – define its strategic direction, powered by three accelerators: digital and artificial intelligence (AI) transformation; gender equality; and sustainable finance. All are underpinned by a commitment to human rights and to leaving no one behind, and rest on the recognition of UNDP as a trusted and transparent development partner.

Within UNDP, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) unites world-class policy expertise, flagship global programmes, and collaborative innovation and learning networks so UNDP is not only ready for the future— but helps build it with governments and partners. BPPS is where policy meets practice - for impact. From development to crisis contexts, BPPS helps countries navigate complexity, scale what works, and advance a more just, resilient, and sustainable future. The position of Director, Quality and Impact Hub is a member of the BPPS senior leadership team.

The Quality and Impact Hub aim to expand UNDP’s value position as an accountable, transparent and therefore trusted and neutral development partner. The Impact Hub serves as the corporate custodian and strategist driving continual improvement of UNDP’s institutional architecture that guides UNDP programming. The Impact Hub leads changes in UNDP policy instruments and quality assurance approaches to enable UNDP programming - spanning all funding sources, including core, non-core, and Vertical Funds (VFs) - that is risk-informed, agile, results focused and integrates social and environmental risks and opportunities. The Impact Hub brings together two existing units in BPPS: the Vertical Fund Hub (VF Hub), and the Quality Programming Team (QPT - including the Social and Environmental Team (SES) Team) to be the central pillar of trust and transparency in UNDP.

By consolidating policy custodianship, quality assurance, risk management, and results oversight, the Impact Hub will be better able to support UNDP in achieving higher accountability, fostering greater trust with partners, reduce fiduciary risks, be more adaptable, and achieve greater developmental quality and impact. A renewed focus on fit-for-purpose and relevant policies will enable and steer UNDP into new partnerships with the private sector, with IFIs, and with the VFs. The Impact Hub will also institutionalize quality assurance and oversight into UNDP, where risk management, results assurance, and policy coherence operate seamlessly through digital systems, enabling evidence-based decision-making and learning across all UNDP programming. The Impact Hub will drive continuous improvement internally while learning from external engagements with the UNDP Executive Board and Boards of the Vertical Funds amongst others to ensure UNDP remains fit-for purpose, dynamic, agile and relevant in an ever-changing international development landscape. The Quality and Impact Hub will continue to lead UNDP’s accountability and engagement with the VFs and ensure UNDP VF programming complies with VF policies and requirements, as well as continue to provide financial oversight of VF programming to ensure VF funds are used for their intended purpose as required by the VFs and VF fiduciary management, reporting and auditing as mandated by the VFs.

Position Purpose

The Director of the Quality and Impact Hub guides and informs areas within the Hub, drawing on their deep technical expertise, political acumen, and demonstrated leadership and managerial capacities. The Director leads cross-cutting efforts in UNDP programming policy reform, and accountability, thereby contributing to UNDP’s reputation as a trusted and transparent. The Director also provides advice and technical expertise for high level decision makers seeking UNDP’s support. Further, the position engages across multilateral processes and partners to position UNDP as a partner of choice in support of developing countries. The role also interfaces with the broader BPPS (other Hubs, Teams) UNDP’s other Bureaus and Offices, and with UN system and related offices, entities, agencies/programmes/funds. The Director is responsible for creating a culture and enabling systems and processes that motivate, engage, and build a coherent team across multiple geographies. The Director will be supported by a Deputy Director.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Lead UNDPs engagement with the Vertical Funds including Policy alignment, Project Oversight and Compliance and Financial Oversight

- Develop political, technical, operational and financial strategy for UNDP’s engagement with the Environmental Vertical Funds (Global Environment Facility, Green Climate Fund and Adaptation Fund) and provide the substantive technical and managerial leadership required to implement it;

- Ensure effective collaboration and relationship management with the Secretariats of the Environment Funds.

- Represent UNDP in the Vertical fund partnerships engaging with the Governing Bodies of each Fund; the technical and advisory bodies of each Fund, and the Accredited Entities under each Fund;

- Prepare, implement, and monitor annual VF Fee budgeting and planning in close collaboration with the Director of the Planet Hub and technical teams, as well as Regional Team Leads to ensure organizational alignment;

- Develop and continuously enhance the internal UNDP VF oversight and compliance procedures to ensure VF policies are met in UNDP VF programming;

- Deliver on project and portfolio level VF monitoring, reporting and evaluation requirements;

- Provide dedicated financial oversight for each VF project, including nationally implement projects and specific global projects, as well as annual portfolio level Fund specific audits, as required by VF policy and procedures;

- Regularly engage with other UNDP Bureaus to ensure consistent application of oversight and compliance procedures across VF programming, and on policy, legal, risk and other strategic VF issues;

- Proactively monitor project and program level VF specific risks connected with UNDP’s relationship with the Vertical Funds and regularly engages with Planet Hub teams including at regional level to ensure efficient and effective oversight and risk management of VF programming.

2. Lead development of UNDP Programme, Portfolio and Project Management standards, approaches, and prescriptive content (PPM)

- Represent UNDP in relevant UNSDG programming working mechanisms, inter-agency task forces and other UN reform initiatives and provide strategic analysis and advice on emerging issues across the UN related to programme and project management, and programming standards, approaches and modalities (e.g. on QCPR, UNSDCF, UNSDG guidelines and programming principles); help establish programme-related priorities, positions and action;

- Lead and develop new and revised programme, portfolio and project standards, approaches, policies and procedures to improve the quality of UNDP programming, facilitate evidence-based decision making/feedback loops, reduce unnecessary transaction costs, respond to evaluation and audit recommendations, and maintain coherence with operational content;

- Lead on the roll-out, review and revision of programming and portfolio approaches to enhance programme effectiveness for achieving results;

- Lead the review of specific quality assurance tools and standards including Partner Capacity Assessment Tool (PCAT) and Private Sector Due Diligence (PSDD) to facilitate flexible, innovative and impactful programming in UNDP;

- Monitor implementation of policies, methods and tools and compliance by relevant UNDP units, and analyze performance to identify lessons learned and steps needed to incentivize improved organizational performance, compliance, and effectiveness;

- Manage and contribute to development of PPM-related capacity building guidance, training modules and other resources for staff.

3. Provide management leadership on quality country programming, SES, Transparency, and Risk Management to increase value add of UNDP programming

- Develop and update guidance and Standard Operating Procedures for the corporate HQ Programme Appraisal Committee (HQ PAC) for new country and regional programmes (CPDs and RPDs);

- Manage the nomination, appointment and orientation process of HQ PAC members and chairs;

- Oversee the quality assurance processes and oversight of the regional bureau cleared CPDs/RPDs, for onward submission to the Executive Board based on its adherence to the Programme Quality Appraisal recommendations;

- Leads the development of standard operating procedures, guidance and systems (VF and non-VF) to ensure UNDP provides high-quality oversight services and remains compliant with policies and procedures;

- Monitor project-level appraisal and VF pipeline development processes and quality assurance, including the implementation of the Quality Standards for Programming and the Social and Environmental Standards;

- In partnership with other Bureaus, update UNDP tools to embed risk management into UNDP programming and the escalation of implementation risks for enhanced oversight as needed;

- Lead UNDP’s transparency initiative by integrating and implementing the International Aid Transparency Initiative (IATI) standard in programme and project management;

- Lead enhancement of and application of UNDP Social and Environmental Standards across all UNDP programming.

4. Promote and lead innovation and substantive knowledge management

- Create an environment of creative and innovative thinking; and culture receptive to change to drive the development of future UNDP programming policy and procedures;

- Lead the evolution and adoption of digital tools to support the efficiency and efficacy of the work of the Quality and Impact Hub;

- Advise on the enhancement of organizational management information systems and digital tools (e.g. Quantum, PIMS +) to advance the integration and effective application of policies and procedures to meet strategic management needs;

- Position accountability and transparency and quality assurance as a key aspect of UNDP’s value proposition to its partners;

- Analyze data on the performance of programmes and projects, including quality assurance data, to advise management of programming reforms that would help to lift performance, using evidence-based approaches.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Hub, Bureau, and the Organisation.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Background

In 2025, the National Council of Justice (CNJ) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) established a partnership aimed at promoting innovation in cybersecurity for the Brazilian Judiciary. Project BRA/25/025 develops and implements tools and strategies to strengthen cybersecurity, digital preservation and information integrity, expanding the protection of the Judiciary’s systems and users.

The initiative strengthens institutional security and promotes transparency, good governance and the efficiency of judicial processes, contributing to resource savings and to a more agile Justice system for the benefit of citizens and society.

To this end, the project governance is organized into the following fronts:

Four cross-cutting coordination axes:

- General Coordination;

- Integrated Monitoring and Control Unit;

- Technical and Operational Management Unit;

- Training and Communication Unit;

Four workstreams, focused on:

- Regulatory compliance;

- Operational conformity;

- Network governance;

- Promotion of a cybersecurity culture;

As this is a home-based position, the candidate is expected to have adequate working conditions, including the infrastructure and equipment necessary for the full performance of the activities.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst will be assigned to the Network Governance axis and will be responsible for leading the collection, analysis and dissemination of cyber threat intelligence, with the aim of anticipating risks, enriching the understanding of incidents and threat actors, and strengthening the resilience of Judiciary institutions within the context of project BRA/25/025.

The incumbent will work in close coordination with the CNJ and UNDP teams, and the following indicative activities are foreseen:

Cyber Intelligence Coordination and Dissemination

a. Engage in the threat information-sharing network among Judiciary bodies, ensuring the smooth flow of tactical and operational data.

b. Produce intelligence inputs for operational alerts, threat advisories, and rapid dissemination bulletins for technical teams and managers.

c. Facilitate cooperation with national and international Computer Security Incident Response Teams (CSIRTs) and public sector cooperation networks.

d. Contribute to a proactive, forward-looking cyber defense posture for the Judiciary, anticipating threats based on the intelligence produced and shared.

e. Support the operation and curation of intelligence-sharing platforms (e.g., MISP, OpenCTI), using standards such as STIX/TAXII and the Traffic Light Protocol (TLP) for the classification and dissemination of information.

Intelligence Production and Threat Analysis

a. Conduct advanced analyses of threat actors, their motivations, capabilities and TTPs (Tactics, Techniques and Procedures), applying analytical models such as the Diamond Model and the Cyber Kill Chain.

b. Transform raw data from technical, open and internal sources into actionable intelligence to support proactive defense and improve incident containment, observing operational security (OPSEC) best practices in collection activities.

c. Support vulnerability prioritization based on the actual likelihood of exploitation in the current threat landscape.

d. Monitor open sources, forums, deep and dark web channels, and national and international technical reports to identify campaigns, data leaks and threats targeting the public sector and the Judiciary.

e. Define, maintain and periodically review Priority Intelligence Requirements (PIRs), ensuring intelligence production remains aligned with organizational risks, priorities and the evolving threat landscape.

Strengthening Proactive Detection

a. Produce and provide indicators of compromise (IoCs), behavioral patterns and detection signatures/rules (e.g., YARA, Sigma, Snort/Suricata) to feed monitoring systems (SIEM, EDR, IDS/IPS, etc.).

b. Collaborate with Blue Team, Threat Hunting and Incident Response teams to validate intrusion hypotheses based on threat intelligence.

c. Assess the effectiveness of security coverage against techniques mapped in frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK, identifying detection gaps and proposing adjustments.

d. Support the automation and orchestration of intelligence workflows (collection, enrichment, correlation and distribution), integrating CTI platforms with SOAR and monitoring tools.

e. Support the analysis of incident-related artifacts, logs and relevant technical evidence to extract relevant IoCs and TTPs.

Strategic Risk Management and Security Posture

a. Contribute to periodic security posture reviews with an external view of threats specifically targeting the public sector and the Judiciary.

b. Identify long-term cyberattack trends to guide investments and changes in the defense architecture.

c. Propose improvements to technical controls based on the evolution of identified threats.

d. Support External Attack Surface Management (EASM) activities by identifying exposed assets, leaked credentials and indicators of organizational exposure.

Integration with Capacity Building and Innovation

a. Integrate real-world threat intelligence into Situational Awareness programs to raise user maturity against targeted attacks.

b. Promote the use of CTI frameworks (e.g., MITRE ATT&CK, Diamond Model, Cyber Kill Chain), OPSEC best practices and security data analysis.

Continuity, Reporting and Simulations

a. Participate in the development of realistic threat scenarios for crisis simulation exercises and continuity plans.

b. Produce technical intelligence reports, threat assessments, and executive summaries tailored to technical teams and senior management.

c. Conduct workshops and training on intelligence analysis for local teams.

Knowledge Management

a. Document analysis methodologies and lessons learned from relevant incidents, and keep the knowledge base on sector adversaries up to date.

b. Develop and maintain analytical templates, reporting standards and intelligence production guidelines to ensure consistency across the intelligence lifecycle.

c. Promote the reuse of intelligence products across Incident Response, Threat Hunting, Vulnerability Management and Security Operations teams

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Project.

The incumbent will be supervised by the Governance and Network Management Analyst.

Business Direction & Strategy | Business Acumen:

Ability to understand and deal with a business situation in a manner that is likely to lead to a good outcome. Ability to make good judgments and quick decisions within such frameworks in the organization. Knowledge and understanding of the operational frameworks in the organization.

Business Development | Human-centered Design:

Ability to develop solutions to problems by involving the human perspective in all steps of the problem-solving process. Knowledge and understanding of human-centered design principles and practices.

Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management.

Effective Justice Sector Institutions

Access to Justice
